entry.summary: This work integrates stochastic manipulation skills into sampling-based multi-robot planning by formulating the problem as an MDP over a multi-modal composite roadmap, enabling concurrent motion planning with uncertain execution times and trajectories. It addresses a real gap where existing planners assume single robots, open-loop paths, or static post-hoc scheduling.

entry.title: VOMMI: Collecting and Leveraging Portable Demonstrations for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Yutian Zhang, Xingrui Xiong, Siyuan Ma, Yang Li, Jiawen Wen, Jiaqi Zhai, Liwen Yang, Ce Hao, Haozhen Chi, Yangkun Zhu, Yifan Zhu, Xiaowen Chu, Dong Wei, Qiaojun Yu, Dibo Hou

entry.summary: VOMMI is a framework for collecting low-cost, robot-free mobile manipulation demonstrations using portable RGB cameras, connecting them to VLA post-training through offline trajectory reconstruction. It tackles the drift and inconsistency problems of raw visual odometry trajectories to produce reliable motion supervision without teleoperation or specialized sensing hardware. This helps alleviate the data scarcity bottleneck for embodied intelligence.

entry.title: Safe Multi-Robot Collaborative Transport Using Density Functions

author.name: Jagannath Prasad Sahoo, Sriram S. K. S. Narayanan, Umesh Vaidya

entry.summary: The authors present a hierarchical density-based MPC framework enabling multiple quadrupedal robots to collaboratively push a shared object to a desired pose using only initial and goal poses. A centralized box-level MPC optimizes contact forces under control-density constraints for convergence and obstacle avoidance, while each robot solves a distributed whole-body MPC to track its contact location.

entry.title: NMPP: Nonlinear Model Predictive Planning for Agile UAV Flight in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Ond\v{r}ej Proch\'azka, Juraj Pauko, Robert P\v{e}ni\v{c}ka, Martin Saska

entry.summary: NMPP imposes perceived obstacles as hard geometric constraints within a nonlinear model predictive planner and passes a full-state reference to an obstacle-blind SE(3) controller for agile quadrotor flight in clutter. It achieves 58-67% lower position RMSE than linear MPC trajectory tracking baselines while preserving dynamic feasibility.

entry.title: Network Intervention by Polling Strategic Agents

author.name: Chenyu Zhang, Rohit Parasnis, Saurabh Amin

entry.summary: The paper studies a planner setting prices in multi-activity network games where agents hold private information and may misreport. It derives a centrality-based decomposition of optimal prices and proposes Poll, a sampling-based algorithm that queries agents locally, with provable properties addressing incentive and scalability challenges.

entry.title: Measuring Chain-of-Thought Necessity and the Effect of Reasoning Constraints

author.name: jeffk

entry.summary: The author extends Lanham-style chain-of-thought corruption interventions from factual tasks to ethical reasoning, measuring CoT necessity as a component of faithfulness. Findings show larger models depend far less on CoT for ethical questions, and constraining CoT with format templates may increase dependence by narrowing the reasoning space, with implications for CoT-based safety monitoring.

entry.title: Training Numerical Intelligence via Auto-Diagnosis and Skill Discovery

author.name: Peter Chen, Wotao Yin

entry.summary: This paper introduces ADSD, a framework that improves numerical solvers by first diagnosing why a solver performs poorly from execution feedback, then using that diagnosis to discover appropriate numerical methods, packaged as reusable solver skills. It reframes AI-driven solver improvement from trial-and-error code editing into a structured diagnosis-first process.

entry.title: Language-Conditioned Token and Reasoning Efficiency in Large Language Models: A Paired Cross-Lingual Study Protocol

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: This paper specifies a prospective, preregistered paired protocol to separate input language, trace language, and answer realization effects on token and reasoning costs, instantiating 240 scored items in English plus seven languages across three open-weight checkpoints and 47,520 initial core runs. It addresses confounding in cross-lingual cost comparisons.

entry.title: Asking Earns Nothing: Scoring the Decision to Act in BFCL Multi-Turn

author.name: Yangze Liu, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: A critical audit of the BFCL multi-turn agent leaderboard showing that its scorer never examines the turn on which a model is supposed to ask for missing information: asking earns nothing, guessing costs nothing, and asking twice loses the item. The paper leverages matched should-ask versus base items as a built-in control experiment. This exposes a meaningful measurement flaw in a widely used agent benchmark.

entry.title: Autonomous Structuring of Radiology Reports Across Modalities at Archive Scale Using an Open-Weight Large Language Model

author.name: Friedrich Puttkammer, Fabian Drexel, Marlene Fritzsche, Era Stambollxhiu, Miriam Kumpf, Lena Schmitzer, Lea Schumann, Lina Xu, Johannes Moll, Jannik L\"ubberstedt, Zeineb Ben Chaaben, Anirudh Narayanan, Hartmut H\"antze, Renato Cuocolo, Antonios Billis, Alexander L\"oser, Jawed Nawabi, Marcus R. Makowski, Cosmin I. Bercea, Shahrooz Faghihroohi, Lisa C. Adams, Keno K. Bressem

entry.summary: A retrospective clinical study developing and evaluating an open-weight LLM pipeline (gpt-oss-120B, an existing open-weight model) that converts an entire radiology report archive into structured reports without human oversight, using 150 hierarchical templates selected via constrained decoding on a single local GPU. Template selection was scored against expert labels on 914 sampled reports across five modalities, with structuring quality assessed field by field on 920 reports by five residents. Demonstrates practical, privacy-preserving, archive-scale clinical NLP.

entry.title: $\mathrm{TRIZ}^{a}$: Guiding Agent Evolution from Pattern Recognition to Solution Invention

author.name: Wenyin Liu (Guangdong University of Technology), Yiheng Huang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Kai Wang (Beijing Denglu Technology Ltd)

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces TRIZ^a, a paradigm for automating R&D that combines the classical TRIZ inventive theory (40 inventive principles and contradiction matrix) with LLM-driven agent evolutionary search, replacing random mutation with theory-guided, explainable ideation. It operationalizes functional information and TRIZ Ideality on a common information scale, with hard gates separating true promotion from mere metric improvement. The approach is validated in cybersecurity on benchmarks including PowerDuck GOOSE and CICIoT2023.

entry.title: RAGStress: A controlled benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation under knowledge-base degradation

author.name: Shiqi Yang, Jiekai Ma, Gaoyuan Du

entry.summary: RAGStress stress-tests retrieval-augmented generation under systematic knowledge-base corruption, pairing four naturalistic corruption types with three severity levels across 57 MMLU subjects and 182,546 documents, totaling 52,500 evaluations. It characterizes how clean-KB evaluation assumptions break down, revealing retrieval behavior under realistic degradation.

entry.title: CIPO: Counterfactual Imagination Policy Optimization for Adaptive Tool Granularity Selection

author.name: Yu Li, Yunlu Wan, Zijian Zhu, Han Luo, Chao Ren, Long-Fei Li, Lei Feng

entry.summary: CIPO frames skill use in LLM agents as adaptive tool granularity selection: deciding whether a state requires atomic fine control or skill-level abstraction. It trains this policy with counterfactual imagination, comparing consequences of atomic versus skill choices from the same state. This is a clean formulation of a real problem that emerges as agents build composite skills alongside primitive tools.

entry.title: Toward AI Trustworthiness: Finding Analytically Proven Forward-Invariant Sets for AI-Controlled Systems

author.name: Haoyang Song, Xikun Yang, Qixin Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for certifying safety of neural-network controllers by finding analytically proven forward-invariant sets (FIS) — regions of state space that trajectories cannot leave. It uses an invertible neural network to map the original state space into a latent space where a regular-shape invariant set can be found and then transformed back with formal guarantees. This enables safety certification for AI-controlled nonlinear systems.

entry.title: Bridging the Evidence-to-Execution Gap:A Reflective Agent for Multi-Objective Peptide Design

author.name: Haosen Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: EASER is a reflective agent that bridges scientific literature reasoning and biological sequence generation by steering a diffusion generator through a learned property interface of fixed low-rank matrices. The agent proposes intervention hypotheses such as anchors and editable positions to close the evidence-to-execution gap in multi-objective peptide design.

entry.title: RollPlace: Improving Macro Placement via Monte Carlo Rollout Search

author.name: Qi Zhou, Guojun Liu, Guangzhi Qi, Ming Lu, Jiechu Liu, Zhongli Liu, Jianqun Yang, Xingji Li

entry.summary: RollPlace is a two-stage macro placement framework for chip design that first generates initial layouts via ML or heuristics, then refines them by adjusting specific macros using Monte Carlo rollout search rather than generating a single one-shot solution. This addresses a common weakness of RL-based EDA placement methods whose outputs typically require later refinement.

entry.title: The Pushback Paradox: A Two-Probe Diagnostic for Language Model Compliance

author.name: Stefan B\"uhler, David Exler, Markus Reischl, Mark Schutera

entry.summary: This paper introduces an open two-probe benchmark that places language models on a spectrum between exploitable compliance and uncooperative resistance. An active probe measures exploitability (following instructions that lower payoff) while a passive probe measures stoppability (waiting when instructed to give up a higher payoff), combined into a compliance index kappa. Applied to twelve language models, seven mostly complied in both probes by deferring to the instruction.

entry.title: Do Motion Tokenizers for Co-Speech Gesture Generation Encode Gesture Semantics?

author.name: Varsha Suresh, Divij Jain, Jia Liu, M. Hamza Mughal, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: This work probes discrete motion tokenizers used in co-speech gesture generation to determine which motion properties are recoverable from their codebooks. Using 19 gesture descriptors ranging from raw motion to abstract communicative function, the authors find that geometry and handedness decode well while semantic motion categories decode only weakly. The result shows reconstruction objectives alone do not guarantee gesture semantics are captured.

entry.title: Streaming Multi-Track Timeline Control for 3D Human Motion Generation

author.name: Yangsong Zhang, Anujith Muraleedharan, Rikhat Akizhanov, G\"ul Varol, Fabio Pizzati, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: TimelineControl enables text-driven 3D human motion generation where new instructions arrive during synthesis and must be combined with ongoing, independently timed overlapping actions. The method uses interval-aware conditioning to preserve instruction timing plus causal part-structured representations and part-aware denoising to coordinate concurrent actions. This targets interactive applications rather than batch text-to-motion generation.

entry.title: CurveCodec 2: Skeleton-agnostic animation compression with a learned entropy model

author.name: Mingyi Shi, Huancheng Lin, Xuelin Chen, Taku Komura

entry.summary: This paper presents a learned codec for skeletal animation data that works across arbitrary skeleton rigs with stated error bounds, improving on the authors' earlier CurveCodec by matching the worst-case error of the industry-standard ACL library while counting payload in bits rather than floats. It analyzes where redundancy in skeletal motion actually lies and identifies which codec components benefit most from a learned entropy model. This matters for game engines, robotics, and motion datasets where animation storage is a production bottleneck.

entry.title: AgroGround: Multi-Granularity Grounded Recognition in Agriculture

author.name: Abdulla Alshehhi, Zongyan Han, Rao Anwer

entry.summary: Introduces AgroGround, a large-scale dataset for grounded agricultural recognition that links plant-disease labels to image regions. An automated pipeline converts labels from eight agricultural VQA datasets into lesion and whole-object annotations, yielding roughly 795,000 instruction examples with negative supervision from healthy images. This addresses the costly manual annotation bottleneck for diagnosis models that must both recognize and localize evidence.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Solar Image Synthesis: Adapting the Surya Foundation Model from He I 10830 {\AA} to EUV Translation and Coronal Hole Segmentation

author.name: Marco Marena, Andr\'es Mu\~noz Jaramillo, Qin Li, Haodi Jiang, Jinghao Cao, Wen He, Ziyang Zhang, Chenxi Yuan, Chao Wang, Haimin Wang, Bo Shen

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Surya solar foundation model to translate full-disk helium (He I 10830 Angstrom) observations into SDO/AIA extreme-ultraviolet images at 94, 193, and 304 Angstrom channels, plus coronal hole probability maps. Using a convolutional input adapter, low-rank backbone fine-tuning, and dedicated output decoders trained on temporally paired, registered observations with SPOCA catalog supervision, the approach enables studying solar morphology from historical helium records that predate modern EUV imaging.

entry.title: Coupling Noisy Pairwise Knowledge to the DAG Posterior for Causal Discovery

author.name: Guoliang Xu, James E Corter

entry.summary: Introduces HB-NoisyKG, a Bayesian framework combining observational data with noisy causal reports from sources such as LLMs for causal structure learning. A feature-conditioned Beta prior pools reliability information per variable pair and a shared error matrix captures systematic source mistakes, with alternating inference refining reliability and graph estimates. This makes heterogeneous external knowledge safely usable for causal discovery.

entry.title: Knossos and Ariadne: Benchmarking and Learning Complete Diagram Topology Extraction with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bangwei Guo, Xujiang Zhao, Shengyu Chen, Yanchi Liu, Wei Cheng, Xi Zhu, Guoning Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces diagram-to-graph topology extraction as a task, along with Knossos, a benchmark of 19,200 symbolic diagrams across six domains containing over 245K nodes and 439K edges. The accompanying Ariadne model/method targets complete entity and relation extraction from structural diagrams with VLMs. This fills a real gap, since existing VLM benchmarks rarely evaluate full relational structure rather than isolated element recognition.

entry.title: TempoBridge: Source-Conditioned Flow Matching with Optimal Transport Couplings for Single-Cell Population Transitions

author.name: Bowen Han, Lingbei Meng, Shihuan Luo, Yupeng Zang, Wenlin LI, Peize He, Yaodi Luo, Lian Zhang, Jianqing Zhu, Jinchao Xu

entry.summary: TempoBridge is a unified source-conditioned flow matching framework for modeling temporal, genetic, and chemical cell population transitions from unpaired single-cell snapshots. It uses minibatch optimal transport couplings for training paths and a fixed empirical population summary, requiring no target examples at inference.

entry.title: Tracing a Sparse Emotion-Control Circuit in LLM-Based Text-to-Speech

author.name: Hongfei Du, Jiacheng Shi, Yanfu Zhang, Ye Gao

entry.summary: Using activation patching with two new emotion-sensitive metrics, the authors identify a sparse circuit of 23-27 attention heads and MLPs (about 5% of components) that recovers or suppresses 74-88% of the late emotion-readout shift in LLM-based TTS. The circuit combines a shared backbone with emotion-specific components.

entry.title: MGPO: Manifold-Guided Diffusion Alignment for Task-Aware Dataset Distillation

author.name: Yunyi Chen, Chenru Wang, Xinyi Ye, Zexin Zheng, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: MGPO reformulates diffusion-based dataset distillation as a multi-objective reinforcement learning problem, aligning generated samples to downstream task needs via a pixel-space discriminative reward and a latent-space geometric reward based on class-wise minimum spanning trees. This counters the objective mismatch where density-focused diffusion fails to preserve decision boundaries and manifold coverage. The result is distilled datasets better suited for discriminative downstream training.

entry.title: Does Explainability Survive Data Drift?

author.name: Samuel Ozechi

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether model explanations decay under data drift even when the feature-target relationship remains stable, and whether pre-drift explanations stay faithful to the replacement model. It highlights that explanation fidelity is rarely monitored in regulated domains like finance and healthcare despite governance requirements.

entry.title: TasteRoute: Personalized Routing for Video Generation

author.name: Zhi Rui Tam, Chao-Chung Wu, Sin-Han Yang, Peyton Ku, Brendan Kuang, Tzu-Ting Hsieh, Min-Fang Hsu, Fang-Ling Tsai, Yun-Nung Chen, Wei-Chiu Ma, Chieh-Yen Lin

entry.summary: TasteRoute is a personalized router for video generation that selects among available text-to-video and image-to-video models based on the request, user preferences, and budget. The paper motivates this by showing annotators agree with a consensus oracle only 34-55% of the time, suggesting preferences are genuinely individual. It matches strong baselines on preference routing while lowering average generation cost.

entry.title: ROT: Rotating Hidden States towards Contextual Vectors for Hallucination Mitigation in LVLMs

author.name: Yijing Du, Xiangcheng Zhan, Shuo Yang

entry.summary: ROT is a training-free method against object hallucination in large vision-language models that detects anomalous contextual deviation of hallucinated tokens in intermediate layers, where they show low similarity to both textual and visual contexts. It then rotates hidden state vectors toward contextual vectors in a layer-specific manner, acting on deep semantics more directly than attention-weight interventions. The empirical analysis of where hallucination manifests in hidden states is itself informative.

entry.title: Where Did the Repair First Go Wrong? Localizing the Origins of Silent Failures in Agentic Vulnerability Repair

author.name: Wenji Bai, Muhammad Waseem, Zeeshan Rasheed, Jaakko Peltonen, Pekka Abrahamsson

entry.summary: The paper proposes SAGE, a trace-based method that localizes the earliest point where an LLM-based coding agent diverges from a task's security intent during vulnerability repair, targeting silent failures that pass syntactic and functional tests but remain insecure. It combines security reasoning assessment at each turn with reconstructed code history. This fills a gap in failure attribution for agentic software engineering with security implications.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence and the New Science of Culture

author.name: Douglas R. Guilbeault, Bhargav Srinivasa Desikan, James A. Evans

entry.summary: This position/theory paper argues that cognition and culture are co-constituted and now empirically measurable, proposing that subjectivities be modeled as local trajectories through a high-dimensional cultural field formed by aggregating those trajectories. It claims embedding methods and generative models provide the first general framework for measuring this co-constitution from individual conceptual structure to large-scale ideologies. It outlines testable predictions for a computational science of culture.

entry.title: Agentic schema-guided extraction of materials process knowledge from scientific literature

author.name: Sameer Sadruddin, Jennifer D'Souza

entry.summary: SciKGExtract combines LLM extraction, chemical normalization via PubChem, and agent-based evaluation and refinement to build knowledge graphs of materials synthesis procedures. Evaluation on 176 atomic-layer-deposition papers with expert annotation shows normalization consistently improves extraction F1 across models.

entry.title: Better Call Reward: Reward Hacking as Strategic Abstention in Legal Reasoning Models

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Justin Shenk

entry.summary: Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with GRPO against a proxy of surface features (citation count, legalese density, length) causes the model to stop committing to answers: formatted-answer rates collapse from 0.900 to 0.109 while accuracy on committed answers actually rises. The result reframes reward hacking as strategic abstention rather than capability loss.

entry.title: Odyssey: A Closed-Loop Benchmark for Long-Horizon Real-World Driving with Explicit Navigation Routes

author.name: Jungho Kim, Hongjae Shin, Seunghoon Yu, Heecheol Yoo, Myeongjun Kim, Jiyong Oh, Donghyuk Kwak, Seunghyeop Nam, Haesung Oh, Hyunju Kim, Hyungchan Cho, Jaehyun Park, Soo Won Seo, Jun Won Choi

entry.summary: Odyssey is a closed-loop end-to-end driving benchmark of 100 scenarios reconstructed from 100-second nuPlan logs, replacing ambiguous directional commands with explicit SD-map routes so the navigation objective is consistent. It enables evaluation of how earlier decisions affect subsequent long-horizon driving, which short-segment benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Harmful Content Generation in Text-to-Image Models: Capabilities and Moderation Limitations

author.name: Paschalis Giakoumoglou, Manos Schinas, Symeon Papadopoulos

entry.summary: A systematic evaluation of harmful content generation across five open text-to-image models using an automated pipeline converting legitimate news captions into unsafe prompts across five harm categories, including built-in safety mechanisms and community fine-tuned bypass variants. Human evaluation of 1,500 images shows high harmful generation rates and exposes moderation limitations.

entry.title: AffordCraft: Scalable Construction of Task-Ready Simulation Assets from Single Images

author.name: Haoyun Yang, Xueyang Zhou, Ziyi Xie, Yongchao Chen

entry.summary: AffordCraft builds simulation-ready articulated objects from a single RGB image and task instruction via retrieval rather than generation: it locates the object and target part, selects a matching articulated asset from a library, and fits it to the image while preserving parts, joints, and physical validity. This avoids the common failure of generative approaches whose predicted parts and joints fail to settle or move in physics simulation. It enables scalable robot learning environments from photos.

entry.title: Learning When to Refine: Long-Horizon Reinforcement Learning for Budgeted Neural-Operator PDE Solvers

author.name: Ange Tong

entry.summary: Formulates budgeted adaptive refinement for neural-operator PDE solving, combining a global Fourier neural operator, a local patch-wise corrector, a set-aware selector, and a macro policy that allocates a finite refinement budget over a trajectory. It introduces rollout-verified policy improvement (RV-PI), which evaluates feasible refinement counts through actual continuation rollouts of the learned solver.

entry.title: Shaping the Wind: Nested Potentials for Kinematically Admissible Urban Wind Prediction

author.name: Yidi Wang, Yunhe Zhang, Jiawei Gu, Ziyue Qiao, Pengyang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a neural surrogate for transient urban wind prediction whose outputs are constrained by construction to satisfy mass conservation and wall impermeability, using a nested-potential output representation. This guarantees kinematically admissible velocity fields that plain velocity-regression surrogates cannot ensure.

entry.title: The Implicit Bias of Hyperbolic Representation Learning for Multiclass Data: A Busemann Risk Perspective

author.name: Xingrun Li, Sho Kuno, Yusuke Mukuta, Xin Yang, Tatsuya Harada

entry.summary: Provides theory for Riemannian gradient flow in hyperbolic multiclass classification with fixed prototypes, covering general permutation-invariant relative margin losses. A radial/directional decomposition via Busemann functions yields a dichotomy governing whether representation radius diverges toward the ideal boundary or recedes inward.

entry.title: Constant-Curvature Sliced Gromov-Wasserstein for Heterogeneous Cross-Curvature Alignment

author.name: Shanglin Li, Wenjing Lu, Muyang Li, Nicu Sebe, Ziheng Chen

entry.summary: This paper extends Gromov-Wasserstein distances to compare probability distributions living on mixed-curvature spaces (combining hyperbolic, spherical, and Euclidean components), which previously lacked a unified metric for alignment. It introduces a sliced formulation for tractable cross-curvature alignment and adds explicit geometric consistency mechanisms across component spaces. This matters because mixed-curvature representations are increasingly used for hierarchical and complex data, and distribution comparison across them was an open problem.

entry.title: RELACE: retrospective likelihood-based action credit estimation for long-horizon language agents

author.name: Sayak Chakrabarti, Sathish Reddy Indurthi

entry.summary: RELACE is a critic-free framework for multi-turn LLM agents that combines retrospective action assessment (teacher-forced likelihood scoring of executed actions) with state-conditioned advantage estimation, improving on GRPO's coarse trajectory-level credit and GiGPO's outcome-sensitive estimates. The goal is more precise localization of errors in long-horizon agentic tasks. This contributes to the fast-moving area of credit assignment for agent RL.

entry.title: AlignQuant: Tile-Aligned Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient LLM Generation

author.name: Hanzhi Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Qinglei Cao, Heng Fan, Yan Huang, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: AlignQuant is a post-training mixed-precision quantization method that uses GPU-compatible 2D weight tiles as the shared unit for precision allocation, storage, and execution, resolving the mismatch between fine-grained precision choices and hardware units. It scores precision reductions using projection-output perturbations weighted by loss gradients under quantized activations, with joint prefill/decode calibration.

entry.title: Learning a Mixture of GFlowNets

author.name: Tiago da Silva, Amauri H. Souza, Salem Lahlou

entry.summary: The paper provides a general theoretical framework for mixtures of GFlowNets, specialized into continuously and discretely indexed collections. It shows continuously indexed mixtures relate to random-features expansions, provably boosting expressivity and reducing instability via sparsity, while ensembling improves exploration over monolithic samplers with lower overhead than prior methods.

entry.title: WASD: Wasserstein-based Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models

author.name: Byeonghu Na, Donghyeok Shin, Yeongmin Kim, Mina Kang, Il-Chul Moon

entry.summary: WASD introduces knowledge distillation for LLMs using a Wasserstein distance over output distributions with a token-embedding-based ground cost, explicitly leveraging token-level semantic similarity rather than per-vocabulary-index divergences. This should better transfer semantic structure from teacher to student.

entry.title: $\alpha$Transfer: Coefficient Transfer for Efficient Model Merging

author.name: Shih-Cheng Huang, Zhi Rui Tam, Chieh-Yen Lin, Yun-Nung Chen, Hung-yi Lee, Shao-Hua Sun

entry.summary: The paper shows that within a model family, performance distributions over model-merging coefficients are highly congruent across model sizes, enabling alphaTransfer: search for optimal merging coefficients on a small proxy model and transfer them directly to larger target models. This avoids prohibitively expensive coefficient searches at scale.

entry.title: CANDLE: Cortical Null-Space Decomposition for Noninvasive Brain Source Imaging

author.name: Shuntaro Suzuki, Yuiga Wada, Komei Sugiura

entry.summary: This paper proposes CANDLE, a learning-based electrophysiological source imaging model that estimates cortical source activity from EEG while handling the ill-posedness of the inverse problem. It leverages a null-space prior derived from subject-specific cortical geometry from T1-weighted MRI, improving generalization across individual brain anatomies.

entry.title: A Riemannian Geometry for Low-rank Adaptation

author.name: Shoichiro Takeda, Shin'ya Yamaguchi, Satoshi Suzuki, Yasunori Akagi

entry.summary: The paper observes that LoRA's BA-transpose parameterization induces an equivalence relation on (B, A) pairs, forming a quotient manifold of redundant directions. It endows this quotient with an invariant Riemannian metric so optimization respects the geometry, removing redundancy in low-rank fine-tuning.

entry.title: Symphony for Text Generation: Benchmarking Clinical Note Generation

author.name: Daniel Varab, Victor Petr\'en Bach Hansen, Asbj{\o}rn W. Helge, Kevin Pelgrims, Mathias Baltzersen, Adrian Young-San Roessler, Vanessa Klungtvedt, Maximilian Brand, Lasse Krogsb{\o}ll, Henrik Cullen, Lars Maal{\o}e

entry.summary: The authors introduce MedConv, a 300-encounter multilingual clinical dataset in English, Danish, and German, and evaluate the Corti clinical AI platform against two commercial ambient scribes using entailment metrics and LLM-judged comparisons across eight PDSQI-9 dimensions. Results show Corti matches or outperforms leading commercial scribes. The work provides a structured, multilingual evaluation framework for a rapidly growing clinical documentation area.

entry.title: Evolutionary One-Step Generators: Fast and Diverse Sampling for Discrete Design

author.name: Marcus Vukojevic, Erik Nielsen, Veronica Lachi, Andrea Passerini, Giovanni Iacca

entry.summary: EGO trains compact one-step discrete generators using antithetic low-rank evolution strategies combined with distribution matching, structural constraints, and diversity or history-dependent rewards, targeting design tasks like molecular discovery where repeated identical structures waste capacity. The framework handles criteria only computable after hard decoding. It offers a fast alternative to autoregressive or diffusion samplers for discrete design.

entry.title: Climbing the Design Ladder: Sequential Knowledge Distillation for Early-Stage Circuit Timing Prediction

author.name: Reza Moravej, Fahad Rahman Amik, Zhanguang Zhang, Didier Ch\'etelat, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: STEP-KD uses intermediate chip design stages (synthesis, floorplanning, placement) as stepping stones for progressive knowledge distillation to predict post-routing timing from early-stage data, avoiding expensive late-stage iteration loops in IC design. The approach bridges the large abstraction gap between logical descriptions and physical layouts. It targets a costly, well-known pain point in EDA workflows.

entry.title: FlowCF: Sparse Counterfactual Explanations for Mixed-Type Tabular Data using Flow Matching

author.name: Emmanouil Panagiotou, Eirini Ntoutsi

entry.summary: FlowCF frames counterfactual explanation generation for mixed-type tabular data as sparse transport from a factual point to a target class, solved with an extended flow matching procedure. The model-agnostic method targets the practical desiderata of sparsity and proximity, which the authors show existing amortized and gradient-based methods handle poorly.

entry.title: On the Computational Tractability of Robust Bandits

author.name: Vanessa Kosoy, Vinayak Pathak

entry.summary: For robust (imprecise) bandits, a learning setting for when the environment is outside the hypothesis class, the authors identify a special case admitting a polynomial-time learner with O-tilde(sqrt(T)) regret and prove that several small generalizations are NP-hard. This delineates the computational frontier of unrealizable bandit learning beyond agnostic guarantees.

entry.title: Axiom Satisfiability of Linear Rewards in Alignment

author.name: Soumya Nasipuri, Sayak Ray Chowdhury, Sanjukta Roy

entry.summary: Building on impossibility results showing that fitting linear rewards from preference data with convex losses violates Pareto optimality and other social choice axioms, this paper asks what it costs to enforce those axioms. It relaxes the linear reward model with per-candidate slack and computes the minimum-slack relaxed reward satisfying the axioms with a margin.

entry.title: sHAIL-Causal: A Sequential Staircase Procedure for Invariant Causal Predictor Discovery

author.name: Ernest Fokou\'e

entry.summary: Introduces sHAIL-Causal, a sequential staircase procedure that climbs a nested hierarchy of hypothesis classes once a joint saturation criterion of goodness-of-fit and cross-environment invariance is met. The paper shows theoretically and via simulation that complexity-only staircases select confounded predictors, while the invariance criterion recovers stable causal structure.

entry.title: DeepAJM: Deep Association Joint Model for Irregularly Sampled data

author.name: Barsha Halder, Jeffrey A. Thompson

entry.summary: DeepAJM is a deep joint model for simultaneously modeling longitudinal and survival outcomes from irregularly sampled patient data, using an encoder-decoder architecture to learn latent structure in time-varying covariate trajectories without parametric assumptions. It retains a partially interpretable per-outcome association structure linking longitudinal processes to survival prediction. This addresses a real weakness of classical parametric joint models, which are biased under model misspecification and small samples.

entry.title: Explicit Asymptotic Bounds for Sequential Calibration Beyond $T^{2/3}$

author.name: Eric Dai, Maxwell Fishelson

entry.summary: The paper improves on the classical O(T^(2/3)) bound for sequential binary forecasting calibration, introducing a two-phase recursive labeling strategy for the sign-preservation-with-reuse game yielding explicit O(n^alpha t^beta) bounds across space-time trade-offs. It sharpens the reduction from sign-preservation upper bounds to calibration error bounds, building on the recent progress by Dagan et al.

entry.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Empirical Risk Minimization on Entry-wise i.i.d. Heavy-Tailed Data

author.name: Kaito Takanami, Takashi Takahashi, Yoshiyuki Kabashima

entry.summary: This paper provides the first precise asymptotic characterization of prediction error for empirical risk minimization in linear regression with entry-wise i.i.d. symmetric alpha-stable heavy-tailed data, using a functional order parameter and the replica method. It addresses the gap between Gaussian theory and real-world data with frequent extreme values.

entry.title: Scen-Opt: A Scenario Optimization Toolbox for Data-Driven Convex Programming

author.name: Ben Wooding, Simone Garatti, Marco C. Campi, Abolfazl Lavaei

entry.summary: Introduces Scen-Opt, the first open-source software toolbox for data-driven convex optimization within the scenario approach, a statistical framework that provides certifiable out-of-sample constraint-satisfaction guarantees. It bridges a long-standing gap between mature theory and practical usability in data-driven decision-making.

entry.title: Making COMET Comparable Across Scripts: Diagnosis and Correction of Tokeniser-Induced Script Bias in Indic MT Evaluation

author.name: G. L. John Salvin (Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad), Swapnil Hingmire (Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad)

entry.summary: Demonstrates that COMET translation-quality scores are biased by target-script identity, with script accounting for 22.9% of score variance on IndicMT Eval when only orthography is changed. The paper traces the bias to the tokeniser, provides label-free diagnostics, and proposes corrections to make cross-script score comparisons valid.

entry.title: Two-Sample Testing via Generative Processes

author.name: Eshant English, Kenji Fukumizu, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-sample test built on stochastic interpolants between two samples: for a symmetric schedule, the interpolant law is time-reflection invariant if and only if the two distributions coincide. The test compares marginals at times t and 1-t via Jensen-Shannon divergence and uses permutation calibration for exact finite-sample validity, with no learning required.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Paths and Flows via Path-Flow Alignment

author.name: Zeyu Michael Li, William Xingxu Chen, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: The authors propose jointly training an interpolation path network and a velocity field for flow matching under a shared alignment loss, rather than fixing paths in advance. They identify and analyze a failure mode called path overfitting, where the alignment loss decreases while sample quality degrades, linked to low-entropy bottlenecks in the induced probability path. This advances the theoretical understanding of adaptive-path flow matching.

entry.title: One Step at a Time: Trading LLM Autonomy for Process Predictability

author.name: Hans Schabert, Christoph Peters

entry.summary: This paper introduces a design pattern for LLM agents executing business processes: an MCP server releases process steps one at a time and receives structured outputs after each, rather than giving the agent a full procedure and waiting for a final answer. This trades agent autonomy for guaranteed process predictability, auditability, and step-by-step inspectability.

entry.title: Foresight-over-Graph: Reasoning Beyond Local Horizons for Knowledge Base Question Answering

author.name: Yang Hong, Yajun Yang, Xin Wang, Liping Jing, Qinghua Hu

entry.summary: The paper addresses hallucination in knowledge-intensive QA by grounding LLM reasoning in knowledge graphs, identifying that standard hop-wise greedy or beam pruning is myopic and discards evidence branches that only become relevant deeper in the graph. It proposes a foresight-oriented reasoning approach that looks beyond local horizons during evidence retrieval. This is relevant to improving reliability of retrieval-augmented reasoning over structured knowledge.

entry.title: Auditable Claims about AI Agents

author.name: Yue Zhao, Jiate Li, Li Li, Yi Nian, Jinbo Liu, Xiaolin Zhou, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: This position paper argues that a claim about an AI agent (such as a human approves every external email) is only checkable if it names its policy, scope, the records that would settle it, and who writes them, adapting assurance-engagement preconditions to AI agents. It connects this to Article 12 of the EU AI Act and extends the authors' Auditable Agents framework. It matters for making agent-safety and compliance claims verifiable in practice.

entry.title: POLAR: Ontology-Guided Risk Prevention for Tool-Calling LLM Agents

author.name: Yunju Kang, Seonghyeon Cho, Irene Li, Yeo-Chan Yoon, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: POLAR is a guardrail framework for small tool-calling agents that assesses action reversibility through a structured two-layer ontology, deriving candidate inverse action sequences to assign graded reversibility scores and pruning risky actions before execution. Evaluated on tau-squared-bench across six agent models, it improves task success while preventing irreversible mistakes. It matters for pre-emptive, auditable agent safety.

entry.title: A Systematic Study of Semantic ID Spaces for Generative Information Retrieval

author.name: Alexia Allal, Hicham Randrianarivo, Sylvain Lamprier

entry.summary: This companion paper presents a comprehensive study of the properties, metrics, and trade-offs that define effective numerical document identifiers in generative retrieval, aiming to replace expensive downstream evaluations with cheaper analyses. It addresses the under-explored question of what makes a good DocID. It matters by enabling faster iteration in generative information retrieval design.

entry.title: Visual-Invariance-Augmented Feature Optimal Alignment for Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Closed-Source MLLMs

author.name: Xiaojun Jia, Simeng Qin, Yiming Li, Jie Liao, Sensen Gao, Ke Ma, Yang Liu, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: IAU-FOA improves targeted transferability of adversarial attacks against closed-source multimodal LLMs by aligning adversarial and target samples at both global and patch-level features using optimal transport with adaptive unbalanced weighting, rather than coarse encoder-level alignment alone. The work highlights persistent vulnerability of deployed MLLMs to black-box attacks.

entry.title: MoonGS: High-quality Representation of the Lunar Surface via Gaussian Splatting Using Robust Depth Features from Image Pairs

author.name: Yun Jiang, Bo Zheng, Yingying Zhang, Xueming Xiao, Tao Hu, Hutao Cui, Zhiguo Meng, Ke Gao, Yang Gao, Meibao Yao

entry.summary: MoonGS is the first feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework tailored to lunar scenes, predicting pixel-aligned Gaussian primitives from just two rover images in a single forward pass without per-scene optimization, using foundation-model depth features and semantic priors. It targets autonomous lunar exploration where sparse viewpoints and weak textures defeat standard reconstruction.

entry.title: ElasticFit: Fit-Aware 3D Object Insertion via VLM Reasoning and Generative Adaptation

author.name: Tzu-Hsin Hsieh, Ricardo Marroquim

entry.summary: ElasticFit combines VLM reasoning with generative adaptation to insert objects into existing 3D scenes such that they fit local geometry while preserving semantic intent and physical plausibility. It infers structured fitting cues from language instructions and rendered scene observations to ground placement, volume, and shape constraints. This advances scene editing and 3D content creation, an active area for AR/VR and design tools.

entry.title: Comprehensive Evaluation and Fine-Tuning of Foundational Cell Nuclei Segmentation Models in Renal Pathology

author.name: Ruijie Wu, Junlin Guo, Ruining Deng, Yu Wang, Shilin Zhao, Haichun Yang, Yuankai Huo

entry.summary: This study builds a difficulty-stratified annotation resource for renal pathology nuclei segmentation, combining 5,901 foundation-model pseudo-labels, 860 expert-annotated challenging cases, and 198 consensus failure cases. It systematically evaluates seven fine-tuning strategies across nine cell segmentation model configurations, finding fine-tuning improves all models. The resource and evaluation protocol support foundation-model adaptation in digital pathology.

entry.title: Revar3r: gauge-aware perturbation uncertainty for feed-forward 3d reconstruction

author.name: Sammam Mahdi, Fariha Binta Salim, Rakin Bin Rabbani, Aniqua Nusrat Zereen

entry.summary: This paper identifies a fundamental flaw in training-free perturbation-based uncertainty estimation for feed-forward 3D reconstruction models like VGGT: output frame rotations act as unobserved gauge symmetries, causing run-to-run variation that reflects symmetry rather than actual error. The authors derive a closed-form, error-independent variance term that grows with scene extent and propose Revar3r, a gauge-aware correction. Experiments on 30 real VGGT view-sets validate the phenomenon and the proposed fix.

entry.title: MacJEPA: Missingness-Robust Audio-Visual Recognition from Untrimmed Egocentric Videos

author.name: Souptik Sen, Zahra Ahmadi

entry.summary: MacJEPA redefines egocentric modality missingness as temporally localized sensor outages within untrimmed, multi-event audio-visual observations, rather than whole-stream absence in trimmed clips. It proposes a missing-modality-robust masked-context query JEPA that recognizes visual actions and acoustic events from interval queries over audio-visual context. This better matches real-world sensor failure patterns in egocentric video.

entry.title: Digital Twin-Driven Real2Sim2Real: Simulator-Conditioned Generation via Paired Driving-Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Hojun Lim, Hyeongseok Jeon, Donghyun Kim, Soonyoung Jung, Heecheol Yoo

entry.summary: This work proposes DT-R2S2R, a pipeline that reconstructs recorded driving clips inside a georeferenced digital twin to condition generative augmentation, yielding simulator-derived annotations grounded in real environments. It aims to substitute for costly target-region data collection and annotation for camera-based 3D perception in autonomous driving.

entry.title: Knowing When to Trust a Prior: Reliability-Gated Cue Fusion for Video Gaze Prediction

author.name: Lichen Zhu, Yueqian Lin, Yiheng Wang, Hai "Helen" Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: FocusGate is a gated ensemble that fuses gaze-free priors into gaze-trained video gaze predictors, with a per-frame gate reading defocus-map statistics to decide when the prior is trustworthy; rejected frames fall back to the base model exactly. It improves all sixteen model-dataset combinations tested, including atop the NTIRE 2026 champion.

entry.title: PDB: Point-Based Deformation Blending for Facial Animation Retargeting

author.name: Sihun Cha, Hyeonseung Shin, Suah Yu, Junyong Noh

entry.summary: PDB is a mesh-agnostic facial animation retargeting method that predicts a compact set of deformed control points and blending weights, reconstructing target meshes via simple matrix multiplication without preprocessing. Weights with ReLU-enforced non-negativity and exact zeros are computed once per target and reused across frames. This enables efficient expression transfer across topologically different face meshes.

entry.title: ReGraph: A Computational Account of Emergent Generalization in the "what" and "where" Dual Visual Streams

author.name: Hyewon Kang, Jungmin Lee, Ilgyu Lee, Seok-Jun Hong

entry.summary: ReGraph offers a computational model of where context-invariant generalization emerges in the brain, building on the dissociation between dorsal (where) and ventral (what) visual streams upstream of the entorhinal cortex. It investigates how grid-like, context-invariant representations arise in neocortical regions before the MEC, connecting neuroscience theory to representation learning in AI.

entry.title: Synapse Loss Estimation for the BrainScaleS Wafer-scale Neuromorphic System

author.name: Bernhard Vogginger, Christian Mayr

entry.summary: This paper addresses the BrainScaleS wafer-scale neuromorphic system, which co-locates memory and computation to avoid the von Neumann bottleneck and supports flexible dense or sparse network connectivity through configurable neurosynaptic cores. The authors develop methods for estimating synapse loss, a practical constraint that arises when mapping desired network connectivity onto the hardware's finite routing resources. This matters because accurate estimation tools are key to reliably deploying large-scale neural network simulations and AI workloads on neuromorphic substrates.

entry.title: ScanSTL: Parallel Robustness Evaluation for Signal Temporal Logic

author.name: Gokhan Alcan

entry.summary: ScanSTL reformulates signal temporal logic robustness computation using associative temporal aggregation and parallel scans, achieving linear work and logarithmic parallel depth for operators like Always, Eventually, and Until. This removes the sequential bottleneck and memory overhead that limit STL evaluation in robot planning and control.

entry.title: EigenDEXplore: Structured Exploration for Dexterous Manipulation with Human Priors

author.name: Harsh Gupta, Tyler Ga Wei Lum, Changhao Wang, Chuer Pan, C. Karen Liu, Jeannette Bohg, Shuran Song

entry.summary: The paper studies how low-dimensional, human-prior-derived subspaces of coordinated hand joint motions affect exploration in RL and trajectory optimization for dexterous manipulation, analyzing tradeoffs between expressivity and dimensionality across diverse manipulation settings. It proposes structured exploration balancing human-derived coordination with joint-space flexibility.

entry.title: Navigation with RF Cues: Embodied Perception Action under Multipath Uncertainty

author.name: Wenlihan Lu, Tianshun Li, Liuqing Yang, Shijian Gao

entry.summary: The authors build a Habitat-Sionna RT benchmark that generates aligned visual and radio-frequency observations for robot navigation toward RF-emitting targets in smart factories, where occlusion and poor lighting hamper vision. They also propose an uncertainty-aware multimodal navigation approach that handles multipath propagation distortions of RF directional cues. This opens a novel sensing modality for embodied navigation research.

entry.title: Communication-Free Obstacle Localization from Aggregate Wrench Measurements in Leader--Follower Cooperative Transport

author.name: Amin Kashiri, Aditya Mohan, Yasin Yaz{\i}c{\i}o\u{g}lu

entry.summary: This paper addresses obstacle localization for teams of robots cooperatively transporting a rigid payload without explicit inter-robot communication. The authors design a follower control law that produces a piecewise-linear relationship between payload motion and aggregate wrench, allowing the leader robot to recover obstacle locations from combined force and torque measurements alone.

entry.title: Pareto-Optimal Entropy-Regularized Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Dimitrios S. Georgiou, Augustinos D. Saravanos, Evangelos A. Theodorou

entry.summary: PER-DDP is an entropy-regularized population-based extension of differential dynamic programming for trajectory optimization under nonlinear dynamics and collision constraints. By selecting samples based on Pareto optimality rather than cost alone, it broadens stochastic exploration and mitigates DDP's vulnerability to suboptimal local basins.

entry.title: Towards an Extensible Benchmark for Spoken Dialogue with Social Robots

author.name: Casey Kennington, Ross Mead, Saad Elbeleidy, Jesse Thomason

entry.summary: This paper proposes a community benchmark for spoken human-robot dialogue that targets artifacts unique to embodied speech interaction, such as clarification requests, interruptions, embodied signals like head nods, and real-time constraints. It also introduces Retico, a real-time communication framework designed to meet the technical requirements for running such benchmarks on robots.

entry.title: Multi-Task Active Learning with Efficient Resource Allocation

author.name: Hanwen Ye, Jiuchen Zhang, Annie Qu

entry.summary: ALCATRAs is a unified framework for multi-task active learning under a deployment asymmetry where costly auxiliary variables are acquired only during labeling under a budget but are systematically missing at prediction time. The framework couples data acquisition, surrogate construction, and downstream prediction for this missing-by-design setting common in scientific studies.

entry.title: Qualitative impressions from creating AI honeypots for six months

author.name: Dean Valentine

entry.summary: Reflections from six months of building alignment honeypot benchmarks, discussing how eval awareness, task ambiguity, and the simulated setting complicate fair alignment evaluation. The author notes the difficulty of avoiding over-fitting evals to specific models like OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol and Anthropic's Fable 5.

entry.title: Agent Policy-Value Audit: Separating Transition Composition from Event Selection in Financial LLM Agents

author.name: Mingyang (Alex), Chen (Andrew), Yida (Andrew), Xu (Aurora), Huiwen (Aurora), Chen, Yiming Lu, Wei Jin

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard paired-return evaluation of financial LLM agents conflates position-transition composition with genuine event-selection skill: an agent that frequently goes from flat to long earns positive returns in an upward-drifting pool even when selecting randomly. The proposed audit holds action-change counts fixed and randomly reassigns them across events, defining selection skill as the excess over this composition benchmark.

entry.title: Action-Consequence Alignment for Reliable Planning and Self-Improving in Latent World Models

author.name: Jinping Wang1, Zhiqiang Gao, Xiantong Zhen, Ling Shao

entry.summary: Identifies a concrete planning mismatch in latent world models: nearby action alternatives can receive lower prediction error while producing outcomes farther from the recorded target, so the model assigns lower cost to less accurate actions. Inspired by neuroscience tickling experiments, the authors introduce Action-Consequence Alignment (ACA) to preserve action-consequence correspondence and improve planning reliability and self-improvement. A conceptually neat diagnosis with a targeted fix for world-model-based planning.

entry.title: Decide, Ask, or Defer: Clinical LLMs under Incomplete Evidence

author.name: Mingzhan Yang, Weili Wu

entry.summary: Introduces a DECIDE/ASK/DEFER formulation for clinical LLMs that separates information acquisition and deferral from binary decide/abstain choices, plus a blinded protocol preventing models from using evidence-completeness metadata. Evaluating Qwen, Gemini, and GPT on 200 matched clinical evidence states from DDXPlus reveals substantial disagreement (137 of 200 states) in action selection under identical evidence. Highlights underexamined decision-making behavior of clinical LLMs beyond diagnosis accuracy.

entry.title: A Tropical Geometry View of Forgetting: A Per-Unit Projector for Knowledge-Preserving Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Xiaoyin Chen, Chunlin Ren, Qihuang Zhang

entry.summary: Using tropical geometry of ReLU layers, the authors show why shared-subspace projectors (Adam-NSCL, GPM) are too coarse for preventing forgetting during fine-tuning, deriving an exact decomposition of output change into per-unit terms tied to which tokens each unit fires on. This yields a per-unit projector that preserves prior knowledge more precisely than layer-wide subspace constraints.

entry.title: Do More Modalities Always Help? A Geometric Perspective on Missing-Modality Robustness

author.name: Songyuan Sui, Zhen Tan, Mohan Zhang, Rana Muhammad Shahroz Khan, Xia Hu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: The paper systematically characterizes a counterintuitive failure mode: multimodal models trained on full modalities can underperform unimodal models when a modality is missing at inference, across fusion models, CLIP-style two-tower models, and vision-language models. It links the degradation to learned cross-modal dependencies in principal parameter subspaces, offering a geometric explanation.

entry.title: Why, Where, How: Taxonomy-guided Error Grounding for Code Repair in NL2SQL

author.name: Suchan Lee, Woomin Song, Hwanjo Yu, Sangwoo Mo

entry.summary: TEG improves NL2SQL correction by turning error diagnoses into structured correction inputs: type-specific rules map each error type to constructs to reconsider and an edit operation to request, with masking of selected query constructs. This addresses the gap that execution success does not reveal what to fix and that taxonomies alone say why but not where or how. Text-to-SQL remains an active benchmark area where such targeted correction matters.

entry.title: CASE: Cost-Aware Stopping for Efficient Long-Video Agents

author.name: Yiming Du, Chenghao Liu, Zhiyuan Liu, Fangxing Zheng, Zhao Wang, Junnan Nie, Songfang Huang

entry.summary: CASE is a plug-in termination framework for long-video agents that frames the question of when enough evidence has been gathered as policy-conditioned sequential stopping. It combines auxiliary multiple-choice evidence assessment with the host agent's execution state at causal checkpoints, training a lightweight Ridge regressor on cost-aware targets that jointly weigh answer correctness and continued reasoning cost.

entry.title: Second-Order Problem Solving for Recursive Self-Improvement in Formal Verification

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Aditya Vempaty, Ashish Jagmohan

entry.summary: SO-RSI is a framework that upgrades recursive self-improvement from first-order patching of failure symptoms to second-order diagnostic inquiry that investigates why failures occur before structural intervention. It passively monitors execution traces for three structural anomalies (recurrence, opposing edits, expectation mismatch) to trigger targeted mechanism investigations, applied to formal verification workflows. This reduces trial-and-error thrashing in agent self-improvement loops.

entry.title: Dependable AI-Assisted Engineering: A Formal Framework for AI Participation and Assurance in Safety-Critical Workflows

author.name: Puxue Tan

entry.summary: This paper develops a formal framework for deciding how and whether AI-generated engineering artifacts should enter safety-critical workflows, assigning participation and assurance records at the level of individual workflow units. Each record covers the engineering requirement, approved operational formalization, mechanism, fallback, evidence obligations, guarantee, and deployment-readiness status. The framework distinguishes deterministic verification, statistically calibrated admission, human judgement with AI advice, and human adjudication of AI output.

entry.title: Dual-Scale Relational Graph Transformers for Ecosystem-Aware Fraud Detection

author.name: Mohsen Nayebi Kerdabadi, Xinrou Li, Yao Xiao, Zijun Yao, Xin Sun

entry.summary: The paper presents HERMES, a dual-scale heterogeneous relational graph transformer for account-takeover fraud detection in digital banking. Unlike production tabular models that score sessions in isolation or graph models that only reason over local neighborhoods, HERMES jointly models local relational structure around a session and the evolving global state of the fraud ecosystem. This reduces friction for legitimate customers while improving detection.

entry.title: GlitchPatch: Repairing Glitch Tokens in Frozen Language Models via Local Retokenization

author.name: Kunsheng Tang, Peigui Qi, Yide Song, Peijun Huang, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: GlitchPatch repairs glitch tokens, anomalous vocabulary entries causing LLM outputs inconsistent with inputs, without access to model internals by optimizing the input tokenization, e.g., through local retokenization guided by an empirical study of BPE merge-rule deletion. The study shows naive merge-rule deletion fixes some failures but raises the overall glitch rate by disrupting normal tokens, motivating a more careful local approach. This offers a practical repair path for frozen deployed checkpoints.

entry.title: ConEx: Human-Interpretable Saliency Maps via Concept-Aware Attribution

author.name: Yehonatan Elisha, Oren Barkan, Ziv Weiss Haddad, Noam Koenigstein

entry.summary: Presents ConEx, a framework bridging pixel-level saliency visualization with concept-based reasoning by automatically discovering class-specific concepts represented as concept activation vectors, learned without manual supervision via a masking mechanism that improves concept purity. The resulting saliency maps indicate where each concept applies, providing both faithfulness and interpretability. This addresses the low-level nature of standard attribution methods.

entry.title: Greedy Local Learning for Language Model Pretraining: Gaps and Objective Design

author.name: Jihwan Moon, Sheir A. Zaheer, Jinmyoung Lee, Gunhee Kim, Chan Y. Park

entry.summary: The paper presents a token-budget-matched empirical study of greedy block-wise local learning for autoregressive language model pretraining at 125M and 400M parameters, measuring how the loss gap to end-to-end backpropagation behaves at scale. Local learning deletes inter-block backward passes, enabling forward-only communication and independent per-block optimization, which is attractive for decentralized model-parallel training. The work identifies which auxiliary objective designs reduce the gap.

entry.title: DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Seongheon Park, Heecheol Kim, Shulin Tian, Lilika Makabe, Namiko Saito, Katsushi Ikeuchi, Sharon Li, Yasuyuki Matsushita

entry.summary: DiVeR improves verifier-guided test-time scaling for vision-language-action robot policies by training verifiers to focus on decision-critical states where plausible candidate actions differ meaningfully, rather than treating all trajectory states equally. Sampling multiple action candidates and selecting via the verifier offers an efficient alternative to scaling robot data or model capacity. The targeted verifier learning makes better use of scarce robotic training signal.

entry.title: Operational Abstractions of Neural Network Concepts via Topological Representations

author.name: Mathieu Pont, Christoph Garth

entry.summary: The paper introduces Topological Concept Representations (TCR), a post-hoc abstraction that encodes the concepts in a learned representation and their relationships using topology, built from concept recoverability and interaction scores. Interventions on the abstraction propagate back to the underlying model, giving a common editable representation of concept organization.

entry.title: On Semi-Markov Suboptimality in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bingyun Liu, Yuheng Jing

entry.summary: This theory paper separates execution suboptimality from policy suboptimality in hierarchical reinforcement learning with temporally extended subtasks, introducing task and execution trees plus a Unified Value Function and a four-stage Generalized Hierarchical Bellman Equation. Under bounded rewards and uniform termination it establishes hierarchical policy and execution improvement results and characterizes when Markovian structure is preserved. The work provides a common analytical foundation for HRL guarantees.

entry.title: LightMTP: Lightweight Latent Multi-Token Prediction

author.name: Tamara Czinczoll, Julie Kallini, Gerard de Melo, Chen Shani

entry.summary: LightMTP is a parameter-efficient multi-token prediction objective for LLM pretraining that encodes future tokens into latent representations without external helper models, unlike prior latent MTP approaches. It aims to capture longer-range structure beyond the immediate next token while avoiding the large parameter overhead of existing MTP methods. This targets better pretraining signal at low cost.

entry.title: Boosting Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zexin Li, Ruili Yao, Yiming Zeng, Xiaoxue Gao

entry.summary: This work studies transfer-based black-box adversarial attacks on deep RL policies, formulating attack as return minimization under a per-step perturbation budget. It shows that transplanted image-classification attacks are no stronger than random noise and proposes a trajectory-level attack optimized over a receding horizon via differentiation. The findings expose real-world vulnerability of DRL systems where white-box access assumptions fail.

entry.title: Mind the Accent Gap: British Accent Robustness in Speech-Driven Financial Voice Assistants

author.name: Aadam Haq, Oggi Rudovic, Malcolm Chadwick, Jay Rainey, Shucong Zhang, Ricardo Guerrero, Sourav Bhattacharya, Maja Pantic

entry.summary: The paper introduces CavaBench, an internally collected benchmark of spoken financial queries, to evaluate ASR model robustness to regional British accents (Scottish, Irish, Welsh) within end-to-end ASR-LLM voice assistant pipelines. It examines how ASR errors propagate into LLM tool-call arguments, which is especially costly in finance, under realistic latency and memory constraints. The work highlights a systematic gap since most ASR training data is American English.

entry.title: DART-ES: Difficulty-Aware Reweighting and Targeted Replay for Fine-Tuning LLMs with Evolution Strategies

author.name: Zhishen Sun, Hongzhan Wang, Sizhe Dang, Guang Dai, Haishan Ye

entry.summary: Proposes DART-ES, an improvement to evolution-strategies fine-tuning of LLMs that estimates per-problem local solvability from pass rates across the perturbation population and maintains a dynamic difficulty state guiding continuous reweighting and targeted replay. This addresses standard ES's weakness of uniformly averaging rewards into a single scalar that ignores how problem learning value changes with model capability.

entry.title: Few-Shot Bioactivity Prediction with Meta-Learning under Assay Heterogeneity

author.name: Michal Kmicikiewicz, Tommy Rochussen, Vincent Fortuin, Ewa Szczurek

entry.summary: Shows that meta-learning performance for few-shot bioactivity prediction degrades as meta-training tasks become more heterogeneous, and introduces MetaHeta, a framework that conditions predictions on auxiliary data from related assays using linear attention. The work quantifies a real limitation of naive meta-learning in drug discovery settings.

entry.title: ATLAS-AL: Adaptive Trust-Region for Latent Adversarial Searches via Active Learning

author.name: Marsalis Gibson, Claire Tomlin, Shankar Sastry

entry.summary: ATLAS is a query-based framework that discovers sets of adversarial inputs for black-box learning systems by casting attack generation as active level-set estimation, combining calibrated approximations with local-global sampling in trust regions. Unlike fixed attack suites, it adaptively maps regions of failure. This strengthens security evaluation of learned systems, particularly safety-critical control settings implied by the authors' backgrounds.

entry.title: Dynamic Budget Allocation for LLM Evaluation under Hard Resource Constraints

author.name: Shai Feldman, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: HARP addresses evaluating LLMs in multi-turn interactions via time-to-event metrics (e.g., steps to a jailbreak or task completion) under hard compute budgets, where censored event times complicate calibration. Unlike prior allocation methods that satisfy budgets only in expectation, HARP enforces hard budget constraints with predictive calibration via a reflow procedure. This matters for jailbreak evaluation and agentic benchmarking under real compute limits.

entry.title: Efficient Multimodal Inference through Adaptive Acquisition and Sequential Fusion

author.name: Payal Mohapatra, Haodong Yang, Yueyuan Sui, Stephen Xia, Benjamin Lundell, Qi Zhu

entry.summary: SemARC couples a Sequential Modality Aggregator with an Adaptive Runtime Controller to decide which modality to encode next and when to stop, using acquired evidence to select each modality before its encoder runs. It executes only selected encoder and fusion branches and handles order-dependence of sequential fusion with a fixed-size state, reducing inference cost.

entry.title: Cite What You Explore: Budget-Aware LLM Reasoning over Medical KGs with Verifiable Evidence

author.name: Chen Chen, Dongjie Wang, Mei Liu, Zijun Yao

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-based framework for post-discharge risk prediction that explores medical knowledge graphs under three constraints: cost-bounded exploration, source-quality-aware evidence weighting, and citable rationales for retrospective review. It targets missing dependencies in EHRs such as comorbidity cascades and drug-disease interactions.

entry.title: Retrieval Is Not Enough: Refreshing Memory for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters

author.name: Chao He, Jianyu Xu, Xinyi Guo, Ruiqi Liu, Haobin Ding, Ruiqi He, Dongqing Song

entry.summary: The paper identifies that retrieval-augmented time-series forecasting degrades when the retrieval memory becomes stale after deployment, and that the influence of retrieved references on a frozen forecaster needs calibration. It proposes FreshCast, a plug-in method that refreshes memory and modulates retrieved information, addressing the mismatch between validation and deployment behavior.

entry.title: MemFLoRA: Memory-Floor LoRA for CNN Adaptation at the Edge

author.name: Mehmet Emre Akbulut, Johannes Geier, Ulf Schlichtmann

entry.summary: MemFLoRA is a low-rank CNN adapter designed around activation memory rather than trainable parameter count, defining a memory-floor criterion so trainable bases avoid retaining large activations until the backward pass. This targets on-device learning where activation state, not parameter count, is the binding resource for edge CNN adaptation.

entry.title: Hierarchy-GBP: Accelerating Factor Graph Inference via Abstraction and Recovery

author.name: Yuzhou Cheng, Tom Yates, Ignacio Alzugaray, Danyal Akarca, Pedro A. M. Mediano, Andrew J. Davison

entry.summary: The authors observe that Gaussian belief propagation is fast at smoothing local errors but slow at correcting global errors, and propose H-GBP, a two-stage method that first solves global errors on a coarse graph abstraction, projects results back, then refines locally with GBP. They prove convergence to the optimum and target scalable spatial perception applications.

entry.title: HyperNSDE: Personalized Neural SDEs for Joint Static-Longitudinal Clinical Data Generation

author.name: Perrine Chassat, Agathe Guilloux

entry.summary: Proposes HyperNSDE, a continuous-time generative model for synthetic patient data that conditions a latent Neural SDE on static patient representations via a hypernetwork, jointly modeling static covariates, irregular longitudinal trajectories, and informative observation times. Stochastic latent dynamics capture realistic variability without a trajectory encoder.

entry.title: Learning to Retrieve via Reinforcement Learning in Embedding Space

author.name: Qi Liu, Fengming Liang, Yiqun Chen, Erhan Zhang, Jiaxin Mao

entry.summary: RELER is an RL framework that trains embedding models to directly optimize retrieval metrics and downstream task rewards by sampling query and document embeddings from von Mises-Fisher distributions and updating with REINFORCE and a leave-one-out baseline. This moves beyond contrastive objectives that do not optimize retrieval outcomes directly.

entry.title: Agentic AutoRAG: RAG Pipeline Optimization through Reasoning-Driven Agents

author.name: Lasse B. Strand, Robert Jakob, Kevin O'Sullivan, Markus Kreft

entry.summary: Agentic AutoRAG uses LLM agents for multi-objective optimization of RAG pipelines, exploiting the fact that retrieved chunks reveal whether failures occur during retrieval or generation, unlike prior optimizers that reduce each trial to an aggregate score. The agent reasons over failure evidence to guide configuration choices such as chunking, embedding, reranking, and generation.

entry.title: Large Language Model Orchestration under Heterogeneous Preferences via Explicit Persona Inference

author.name: Shuqing Shi, Ziyan Wang, Milind Tambe, Yali Du

entry.summary: The paper proposes HARP, an LLM orchestrator that maintains explicit probabilistic beliefs over each heterogeneous agent's private preference with a principled update rule, rather than carrying beliefs as unstructured prompt text where early errors persist. Drawing on game theory and multi-agent systems, it coordinates autonomous agents toward collective goals. This brings formal preference inference into LLM-based orchestration.

entry.title: Memory Depth and Reconstructed Context Width: A Controlled Evaluation of Hierarchical Retrieval

author.name: Michael Andreev

entry.summary: Using EverMemBench, this paper experimentally disentangles two parameters of long-term conversational memory systems: structural depth of hierarchical organization and context width supplied to the answer model. Increasing width from 1K to 4K tokens improves accuracy by 10-18 percentage points while depth provides no monotonic gain, and production performance plateaus beyond 8-16K context.

entry.title: Learning to Curate What You Generate for Generalizable Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Junhui Yin, Yuchen Yang, Yilin Yin, Shuai Na, Haoran Xi, Jianhua Yang, Muyi Sun, Man Zhang, Shengfeng He

entry.summary: The paper defines Generalizable FSCIL, a realistic setting where both base and incremental sessions have scarce data, and proposes curating trustworthy synthetic knowledge instead of naively mixing generated samples that introduce semantic noise and old-new boundary conflicts. The framework improves initial representations and class boundary stability.

entry.title: CueRator: Agentic Search for Symbolic Rules to Adapt Frozen Multimodal Encoders

author.name: Sunchan Park, Beomkwon Cho, Kyeongbo Kong

entry.summary: CueRator is an agentic framework that uses LLM-driven search over symbolic decision rules to adapt frozen contrastive multimodal encoders, converting cross-modal similarities into predictions. Validated on open-vocabulary audio-visual event perception, it pairs a symbolic formulation that preserves generalization to unseen categories with a lightweight per-video policy for adaptivity. This connects agentic LLM search with parameter-efficient multimodal adaptation.

entry.title: PIE-PS: Photometric Stereo from Physical Irradiance Event Streams

author.name: Xiangze Meng, Guangyu Li, Jing Li, Di Mei, Songchen Ma, Mingkun Xu, Rui Ma

entry.summary: PIE-PS reconstructs dense surface normals from raw event-camera streams under known moving lighting, deriving a physical relation between adjacent events, light motion, and surface normals from the event trigger model. It introduces Physical Irradiance Events (PIEs) by pairing events to overcome sparsity and unknown contrast thresholds, combining a physics-only solver with a learning framework. This exploits the microsecond latency and high dynamic range of event cameras for photometric stereo.

entry.title: UniCounting: Instance-Aware Proposal Consolidation for Image-Query-Free Multi-Category Counting

author.name: Jinshi Liu, Pan Liu, Lei He, Weichao Luo, Rui Qian

entry.summary: UniCounting formulates multi-category visual counting without exemplars or text queries: given only an RGB image and a fixed vocabulary, the model outputs a complete category-count vector. It casts counting as instance-aware structural inference over an over-complete proposal set from frozen SAM, consolidating duplicate and partial masks into coherent instance counts.

entry.title: MedCORE: Criteria-Grounded Clinical Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis

author.name: Asim Khan, Samee Ullah Khan, Dwarikanath Mahapatra

entry.summary: MedCORE operationalizes clinical reasoning in a vision-language architecture by decomposing diagnosis into clinically defined criteria, spatially localizing evidence for each criterion, and aggregating into structured diagnoses. The framework aims for transparent, criteria-grounded medical image diagnosis rather than direct image-to-label mapping.

entry.title: Distribution-Transfer Safe-Horizon MPC under Mode Uncertainty

author.name: Stephen Crawford, Nora Ayanian

entry.summary: This paper addresses distribution mismatch in scenario-based chance-constrained MPC with obstacles governed by switching dynamic modes, constructing a confidence set for the unknown categorical mode law from finite observations. It derives a multiplicative domination bound that transfers Safe-Horizon collision-risk certificates from a chosen sampling distribution to every law in the confidence set, regularized with Wasserstein geometry.

entry.title: Beyond Task Reward: A Controller-Restriction Protocol for Evaluating Embodiment-Dependent Competence

author.name: Siyuan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes evaluating robot morphologies by restricting the controller complexity and measuring retained task competence, showing on EvoGym that task reward explains only 10-39% of the variance in this metric and geometric descriptors fail to predict it. The measurement is reliable across optimizer restarts.

entry.title: Seeing Through the Displaced Frame: Privileged Noise Distillation for Vision-Force Precision Assembly

author.name: Ching-Hsiang Chang, Tzu-Yu Chuang, Yi-Hsiu Lee, Yi-Ting Chen, Yuan-Fu Yang, Min Sun

entry.summary: The paper identifies that pose estimation noise in precision assembly corrupts both observations and the action coordinate frame, and supplies the missing offset information during training via a privileged simulation teacher and closed-form demonstration relabeling. The deployed student, trained with BC plus a final RL phase, uses vision and force inputs.

entry.title: Sensor-Layout-Agnostic Navigation via Geometric Observation Canonicalization

author.name: Welf Rehberg, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: The authors present an embodiment-informed visual navigation policy that generalizes across diverse depth sensor configurations on an aerial platform, overcoming the fixed-camera limitation of existing policies. Depth measurements from arbitrary sensor payloads are explicitly unprojected into a shared robot-centric frame and stitched into a unified spherical range image with a binary validity mask distinguishing gaps from unobserved regions. This enables zero-shot deployment across heterogeneous sensor layouts.

entry.title: Feeling Through the Load: Compliant Quadruped Locomotion under Payload Interactions

author.name: Shaunak A. Mehta, Mayank Mishra, Prajit KrisshnaKumar, Sebastian Scherer, Koichiro Niinuma

entry.summary: This work develops a force-aware locomotion framework for quadrupeds carrying unrestrained payloads, enabling robots to distinguish intentional external interactions on the payload from ordinary load motion using only onboard measurements. It separates learning of force-aware locomotion from force estimation and treats payload interactions as commands shaping the combined robot-payload system.

entry.title: Federated Bayesian Surveillance of Mechanical Thrombectomy Adverse Events: A Population Risk Layer for Surgical Digital Twins

author.name: Damini Rijhwani

entry.summary: This work proposes treating population-scale adverse-event surveillance as a belief layer within surgical digital twins, using a federated Bayesian protocol where sites maintain Gamma-Poisson posteriors and share only Renyi-differentially-private updates. It benchmarks on the full FDA MAUDE cohort for thrombectomy catheters, covering 8,617 reports.

entry.title: SGAnalog: An End-to-End Circuit Benchmark from Open-Source Silicon Tapeouts

author.name: Yueting Li, Weihang Ding

entry.summary: SGAnalog is a benchmark of 273 topologically distinct human-designed analog circuit designs drawn from Tiny Tapeout manufacturing shuttles, with schematics, SPICE netlists, and commit metadata processed in a fixed containerized environment. It enables testing whether models learn transferable circuit design skills and whether outputs work under defined process and test conditions.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning VLM for Enhancing AI's Spatial Intelligence: Understanding 3D and 2D Rotations

author.name: Uttamasha Monjoree, Wei Yan

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune Google DeepMind's Gemma-4 models (GA April 2026) on multiple object-rotation datasets, showing that mixture-of-experts variants substantially outperform generalist variants at predicting rotations defined by axes and angles. The work targets spatial intelligence gaps relevant to STEM, medicine, architecture, and construction.

entry.title: CORE-RL: Confidence-Oriented Reliability Evaluation of Black-Box Reinforcement Learning Policies
