entry.summary: Proposes COVER, a method for the first stage of classifier cascades in sleep staging that maximizes coverage of a fixed primary model's predictions under a prescribed accepted-risk target. It replaces maximum softmax probability with an auxiliary-informed learned error score and applies fixed-scale scorer refinement.

entry.title: Learning under Localized Minority Imbalance

author.name: Amin Hosseininasab, Steven M. Shugan

entry.summary: The paper identifies localized minority imbalance (LMI), where minority instances are disproportionately under-observed in specific regions of feature space rather than uniformly undersampled, and shows existing class-imbalance techniques can fit observation-induced bias and generalize poorly. It includes a motivating example of small business bankruptcy records and presumably proposes mitigations.

entry.title: Loopy: Low-Bit Quantization Framework for Looped Language Models

author.name: Zeyu LI, Yipu ZHANG, Jintao Chen, Xin LI, Wei ZHANG

entry.summary: Loopy addresses post-training quantization of looped language models, where errors in a quantized shared core compound across recurrent steps. It finds that quantization configuration rankings change with recurrent depth, motivating depth-targeted selection, and proposes methods to avoid costly full-calibration evaluation at deployment depth.

entry.title: TIGER: Time-Series Classification with In-Context-Learning Gated Ensemble of Representations

author.name: Johann Faouzi

entry.summary: TIGER improves time series classification by replacing the bespoke-per-representation design of ensembles like HIVE-COTE 2.0 with a shared portfolio of three general-purpose classifiers applied to four representation families, stacked with an in-context-learning-based gating mechanism. This simplifies the architecture while adaptively combining predictions. Ensemble methods remain the most accurate approach for time series classification, so this is a meaningful architectural simplification.

entry.title: dIon: Fragmentation-Based Invariance for Self-Supervised Learning of Tandem Mass Spectra

author.name: Alfred Nilsson, Joel Lapin, Samuel H. Payne, Mathias Wilhelm, Lukas K\"all

entry.summary: dIon adapts the DINO self-supervised framework to tandem mass spectrometry using a novel domain-specific invariance linking precursor properties (mass, charge) to fragment-ion evidence, requiring no peptide sequence labels. Two latent prediction tasks recover a clean teacher representation, one associating precursor information with fragments and one preventing collapse onto precursor alone. The learned representations improve de novo peptide sequencing.

entry.title: Spacecraft Rendezvous Trajectory Generation with Modular Constraints via Diffusion Model Composition

author.name: Mariko A. Storey-Matsutani, Richard Linares

entry.summary: The paper presents a diffusion-based trajectory generation method for spacecraft rendezvous and proximity operations, training separate energy-based diffusion models for individual constraints like approach cones and sensor line-of-sight, then composing them at inference time with each other or analytic energy fields. This enables flexible constraint combinations for on-orbit servicing, inspection, and debris removal missions. It demonstrates compositional generative modeling applied to aerospace control.

entry.title: IREA: Intermediate Representation-based Embedding Alignment for Normative RAG

author.name: Mirae Han, Sihyeong Yeom, Harksoo Kim

entry.summary: The paper introduces normative RAG, a retrieval-augmented approach supporting LLM ethical judgment with external normative knowledge, and proposes IREA to align narrative-style queries with generalized normative statements via intermediate representations, addressing the retrieval asymmetry that breaks factual retrieval methods. A novel application area for RAG with clear motivation. Early-stage but interesting direction.

entry.title: The Hidden States Cookbook: A Large-Scale Ablation Study for Noise-Robust Conversational Intent Classification in Industry

author.name: Bogdan Bogachov, Nikita Letov, Yaoyao Fiona Zhao

entry.summary: This industrial ablation study runs 360 controlled experiments on hidden-state pooling strategies (mean, max, last-token, attention, FFT-augmented) for noise-robust conversational intent classification using Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on BANKING77 and CLINC150 under clean and noisy conditions. It answers a practical production question: which pooling strategy best handles user queries embedded in conversational noise. The cookbook-style findings are directly actionable for building conversational database interfaces.

entry.title: Do Speech Representations Preserve Regional Accent Across Read and Spontaneous Speech?

author.name: Paula A. Perez-Toro, Tomas Arias-Vergara, Annette Schwarz, Abner Hernandez, Andreas Horr, Cornelia Kristen, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: Using 500 German speakers from nine regions, this study compares ten speech representations on regional accent classification and geolocation under matched versus read-to-spontaneous transfer conditions. Whisper representations perform best in-domain (0.489 UAR, 148 km median error) but degrade sharply across transfer, while speaker embeddings are less discriminative but more robust. The findings expose a generalization gap relevant to accent-aware speech applications.

entry.title: Multimodal Dual-Encoder Retrieval for Automated ICD Coding

author.name: Abhinav Bohra, Anuj Bohra

entry.summary: This work proposes a two-stage ICD coding framework that first retrieves codes with a multimodal dual-encoder over structured EHR data and clinical notes, then applies a reranker, addressing scalability to 9K+ codes, rare-code generalization, and transparency. Retrieval framing avoids dense classifier heads and supports long-tail codes.

entry.title: Sparse-View 4D Gaussian Splatting via Spatiotemporal Priors and Generative Assistance

author.name: Shengqi Wang, Zhengxian Yang, Kaiwen Tian, Yang Liu, Bowen Liu, Hua Du, Taicheng Huang, Jiamin Wu, Tao Yu

entry.summary: This paper describes a 4D Gaussian Splatting framework for the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Volumetric Video Challenge's sparse-view track, reconstructing dynamic scenes from six wide-baseline cameras. It combines region-adaptive spatial priors, motion-consistent temporal priors via interpolation and metric-scale monocular depth, and generative assistance.

entry.title: FreeLoc: Online Floorplan Localization via Diffusion-Aided Pose Refinement

author.name: Haocheng Peng, Boyang Zhou, Jiarui Hu, Xiyue Guo, Ziyang Zhang, Boming Zhao, Yifan Gao, Xiao Li, Hujun Bao, Zhaopeng Cui

entry.summary: FreeLoc performs online RGB-based indoor localization directly against floorplans, avoiding dense scene-specific offline databases. It queries plausible pose anchors via on-the-fly floorplan ray querying and refines them into continuous poses with a diffusion-aided refinement scheme, plus an online likelihood construction for sequential localization.

entry.title: A Biomimetic Gaze Control to Restore Head-Neck Movements

author.name: Colin Rubow, Haohan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces an eye-tracking controller for powered neck exoskeletons that leverages the vestibulo-ocular reflex to emulate natural eye-head coordination, replacing unintuitive hand-held input devices for users with neck muscle weakness. It includes personalization of the control behavior to produce more natural head-neck movements.

entry.title: Towards Quadruped-Provided Localization and Active Tracking for Micro-UAVs

author.name: Alejandro Lorite Mora, Andr\'es Fa\'i\~na

entry.summary: This system moves the entire localization stack for a 27-42 gram micro-UAV onto a quadruped robot with a 7-DOF arm, which tracks AprilTag fiducials on the drone with an end-effector camera and fuses that with its own self-localization to place the drone in a shared map frame. The arm acts as an actively controlled gimballed tracker. This enables autonomous micro-UAV flight in confined spaces without heavy onboard sensing or compute.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Goal Exploration

author.name: Jean Tarbouriech, Omar Darwiche Domingues, Pierre M\'enard, Matteo Pirotta, Michal Valko, Alessandro Lazaric

entry.summary: This paper presents AdaGoal, a goal-selection scheme for provably efficient multi-goal exploration that adaptively targets goals of intermediate difficulty based on state-reaching uncertainty. It achieves near-minimax-optimal sample complexity for learning epsilon-optimal goal-conditioned policies in reward-free MDPs, with extensions to linear function approximation. The work is a notable contribution to reward-free and exploration-focused RL theory.

entry.title: Half-Hop: A graph upsampling approach for slowing down message passing

author.name: Mehdi Azabou, Venkataramana Ganesh, Shantanu Thakoor, Chi-Heng Lin, Lakshmi Sathidevi, Ran Liu, Michal Valko, Petar Veli\v{c}kovi\'c, Eva L. Dyer

entry.summary: Half-Hop addresses over-smoothing and failures in message passing neural networks by upsampling edges with added slow nodes that mediate communication between source and target nodes. The method only modifies the input graph, making it plug-and-play with existing GNN architectures, supported by theoretical and empirical analysis. It is a simple, general improvement to graph learning.

entry.title: An analysis of Mirror-Descent Soft Actor-Critic

author.name: Denis Zorba, Michal Valko

entry.summary: This paper provides finite-time convergence guarantees for Soft Actor-Critic when the target policy arises from policy mirror descent rather than the classical Gibbs target, deriving conditions for strong convexity and smoothness of the actor objective characterized through the Legendre differential operator. It establishes an O(N^{-1/5}) best-iterate convergence rate up to approximation errors. This brings theory closer to how SAC is actually implemented in practice, where only a few actor steps are taken.

entry.title: REACT: Physically and Chemically Consistent Reconstruction of Marine Active Tracers

author.name: Wenbin Dai, Hao Zheng, Shiyu Liang, Chaofan Sun, Xueying Zhang, Hanbo Huang, Xuan Gong, Yiran Zhang, Enhui Liao

entry.summary: REACT reconstructs global sea surface pH while enforcing carbonate chemistry consistency, addressing the mismatch between passive-tracer AI models and active tracers like pH where dissolved inorganic carbon is the conserved quantity. This matters for trustworthy AI in climate and ocean acidification monitoring.

entry.title: Towards Safer Autonomous Driving in an Open World: A Dual-Process Approach

author.name: Simon Janssen, Michiel Braat, Chris van der Ploeg, Serge Thill, Jan-Pieter Paardekooper

entry.summary: The paper combines a neural network planner for routine driving with model predictive control for unfamiliar situations, switching between them via a meta-cognitive component that reasons about contextual risk using a knowledge graph, inspired by Dual Process Theory. The goal is safety-standard compliance in open-world conditions.

entry.title: Semantic Causal-Factor Inference from Aviation Incident Narratives Using A Variational Autoencoder with Cosine-Similarity-Based Reconstruction

author.name: AZIIDA NANYONGA1, HASSAN WASSWA, UGUR TURHAN, KEITH FRANCIS JOINER, GRAHAM WILD

entry.summary: This work proposes a framework combining NLP with a variational autoencoder to infer causal factors from long, unstructured aviation accident and incident investigation narratives, mapping narrative embeddings to expert-reported probable causes via cosine-similarity-based reconstruction. It targets automation of safety investigations where causal evidence is scattered across lengthy documents.

entry.title: Efficient Neural Surrogates for Linear Radiation Transport on the Lattice and Hohlraum benchmarks

author.name: Carmelo Gonzales, Steffen Schotth\"ofer, Cory D. Hauck

entry.summary: This paper studies neural surrogates for linear radiation transport equations, which underpin simulations in nuclear engineering, inertial confinement fusion, and medical imaging, with the goal of amortizing expensive solver costs for design optimization and uncertainty quantification. It benchmarks architectural choices and inductive biases across model families on lattice and hohlraum problems, addressing when surrogate accuracy transfers between transport problem types.

entry.title: R1A-PC: Physics-Guided Electromagnetic Inversion of Three-Dimensional Human Point Clouds in Complex Static Environments

author.name: Xudong Yuan, Ruyun Xu, Jingtai Yang, Xianzheng Sun

entry.summary: R1A-PC is a physics-guided method that reconstructs 2048-point 3D human geometry from paired electromagnetic measurements with and without the target, using background subtraction and a frequency-balanced discrete Born adjoint to produce spatial knowledge maps in cluttered static environments. It handles multipath interference from walls and floors via deformation-stage decoding conditioned on the background field.

entry.title: Learning from imperfect teachers for low-resource acoustic generalization

author.name: Shuanglin Li, Ruxiao Qian, Jian Liu, Haijun Lin, Wenwu Wang, Siyang Song

entry.summary: The paper proposes BA-MPD, a logit-based knowledge distillation objective for low-resource acoustic modeling that corrects for biases in imperfect teachers. It combines Boundary-Anchored Correction and Mass-Partitioned Distillation so the student avoids transferring teacher-induced distortions while still benefiting from softened supervision.

entry.title: FreSia: Frequency-Semantic Instantiation and Alignment for Multivariate Time Series Analysis

author.name: Yubo Wang, Hui He, Hezhe Qiao, Guoqing Ji, Zhendong Niu

entry.summary: FreSia aligns the semantic space of LLMs with the frequency space of time series, using a Frequency-Guided Prompt mechanism that distills seasonal and trend structure lost in discrete numerical tokenization. It targets multivariate forecasting and anomaly detection with LLMs.

entry.title: Agentic-ZTA: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Autonomous Zero Trust Enforcement

author.name: Shovan Roy, Lopamudra Praharaj, Maanak Gupta, Bhavani Thuraisingham

entry.summary: Agentic-ZTA operationalizes the NIST SP 800-207 zero trust control loop with a multi-agent decision pipeline, embedding policy knowledge in a retrieval-augmented pipeline and intercepting access requests at a Policy Enforcement Point with contextual enrichment routed to a policy engine agent. It explores agentic AI for automating zero trust cybersecurity decisions.

entry.title: MS-Exam-Gen: Source-Grounded Benchmark Construction for Evaluating LLMs on Textual Multiple Sclerosis MRI Knowledge

author.name: Abdul Basit, Muhammad Abdullah Hanif, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MS-Exam-Gen is a reproducible framework for constructing and auditing source-grounded multiple-choice benchmarks testing LLM knowledge of multiple sclerosis MRI criteria, protocols, reporting, and differential diagnosis, explicitly scoped to textual rather than image interpretation. It targets auditable assessment of narrow, evolving subspecialty biomedical knowledge.

entry.title: CRAFTER: Causality-based Self-adaptation for Autonomous IoT Systems

author.name: Houssam Hajj Hassan (IP Paris, SAMOVAR), Ajay Kattepur (IP Paris, TSP - INF, ACMES-SAMOVAR), Denis Conan (IP Paris, TSP - INF, ACMES-SAMOVAR), Georgios Bouloukakis (IP Paris, TSP - INF, ACMES-SAMOVAR, ECE)

entry.summary: CRAFTER is an automated framework for designing and deploying self-adaptive IoT systems using causal reinforcement learning, aiming to maintain QoS under fluctuating workloads and evolving demands. It targets reusability across multiple IoT verticals, addressing a limitation of domain-specific self-adaptation techniques.

entry.title: Using Process Mining to Generate AI Agents from Software Engineering Process Records

author.name: Saimir Bala, Fabiana Fournier, Lior Limonad, Andreas Metzger

entry.summary: This paper combines object-centric, imperative, and declarative process mining on event logs from software repositories to discover project-specific agent structures, addressing how to specify AI agents for hybrid human-AI software engineering teams. It tackles the granularity problem between coarse-grained agents (complexity) and micro-agents (coordination overhead) that predefined role-based frameworks ignore.

entry.title: An Executable Benchmark for LLM-Based HLS Repair:Design Complexity and Repair Underconstraint

author.name: Maisha Mastora, Dean Sullivan

entry.summary: The authors present the first comprehensive, executable benchmark for LLM-based repair of High-Level Synthesis (HLS) designs, evaluating four models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5.4, and Claude Opus 4.6, all established models) on 125 instances spanning eight logic bug types across three open-source HLS suites. Prior work reported only 10.5% repair accuracy for GPT-4 with no failure analysis. The benchmark provides suite-specific functional checks and analyzes what drives repair difficulty.

entry.title: PB-GRPO: Learning Socially Adaptive LLM Agents from Persona-Driven Simulation with Preference-Batched GRPO

author.name: Jingquan Wang, Jun Yin, Xu Han, Yongsheng Mei, Jie Hao, Bin Guo

entry.summary: PB-GRPO trains socially adaptive LLM agents using a persona-driven social simulation environment with LLM-based user simulators and user-satisfaction scoring. The method introduces preference-batched GRPO to optimize multi-turn social behaviors, such as inferring unstated user goals and adapting to latent preferences, where real interaction data is scarce. This extends RL post-training beyond locally helpful responses toward socially competent conversation.

entry.title: AI-Enabled Quality Assurance for Multiple-Choice Assessment Items

author.name: Steven Moore, Nicholas Diana

entry.summary: This narrative review surveys automated detection of flaws in multiple-choice assessment items, covering item-writing flaw detection, revision, psychometric screening, and NLP benchmark auditing across fourteen studies. It maps a 19-criterion rubric to detection methods and finds that high label-level accuracy often coexists with weak detection of positive cases and inconsistent reference standards.

entry.title: System One Models for Wireless Decision-Making:Applications and Performance Evaluation

author.name: Masoud Rahimi, S. M. Matin Alemohammad, Hamid Behroozi, Mahdi Nouri

entry.summary: The paper investigates System-One models that directly learn probability distributions over explicitly defined decision spaces as lightweight alternatives to LLMs for latency-constrained wireless control tasks. It formalizes their decision structure and learning objective, maps applicability across physical-layer control, RRM, mobility, slicing, and network operations, and evaluates performance.

entry.title: Variational Quantum Attention for Molecular Graph Learning

author.name: Yu-Cheng Lin, Yu-Chao Hsu, Tai-Yue Li, Nan-Yow Chen, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces QGAT, an edge-aware variational quantum attention mechanism for molecular graphs in which the receiving atom, neighboring atom, and bond jointly determine the quantum attention state. Across five molecular property prediction tasks it performs competitively with GATv2, with consistent improvement on BBBP.

entry.title: Separating Decision Time from Decision Quality in the Real-Time Gap of Distilled Deciders: Evidence from a Game and a Conveyor Simulator

author.name: Chihoon Shin, Junyeong Lee, Kihyeok Jeong, Wonok Kwon

entry.summary: The paper dissects why learned real-time deciders underperform when evaluated asynchronously versus in wall-clock play, splitting the gap into decision-time and decision-quality components. Preregistered experiments in ViDoom-style settings quantify both components at roughly 6-9 percentage points each, showing tick-based evaluation masks substantial real-time losses.

entry.title: A Graph-Based Inspection and Intervention Tool for Assessing Mechanistic Learning in PINNs

author.name: Adwait Patkhedkar, Alifaraz Lakhani, Prathmesh Mohite, Abhijeet Salunke

entry.summary: GIIT maps the physics dependency graph of a modeled system onto internal components of a trained physics-informed neural network using sensitivity and trend analysis, then probes the mapping via targeted interventions. The authors find that under temporal extrapolation out-of-distribution, layer-wise correspondence drifts and functional correspondence degrades even when physics residuals remain low. This cautions that apparently physically-grounded networks may not retain meaningful internal structure beyond training conditions.

entry.title: Kapture: Capturing Cardiac Dynamics with Koopman-Governed Learning for Efficient Radar-Based Electrocardiogram Recovery

author.name: Tong Wu, Jing Peng, Ziqi Feng, Yuanyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Kapture reconstructs contactless ECG from millimeter-wave radar by projecting radar hidden states into a low-dimensional observable space where a regularized Koopman linear evolution operator is identified, with predicted observables refining subsequent hidden states. A temporal contrastive objective suppresses predictable interference such as respiration and motion. The approach is parameter-efficient compared to large spectrogram backbones.

entry.title: Revisiting Ground-Truth Synthesis from High-Speed Video: Exact Validity Conditions and an Audited Consumer Capture Corpus

author.name: Abdullah Al Shafi, Sumaiya Rahim Suma

entry.summary: The paper derives exact validity conditions for synthesizing motion-deblurring ground truth by averaging consecutive high-frame-rate frames, showing the central-frame label is unbiased only for odd windows with equal sample durations. Auditing 51 smartphone clips at nominal 240 fps, the authors find 19 actually captured near 176 fps, a flaw visible only in container timing metadata, and release an audited consumer capture corpus.

entry.title: Hierarchical Time-aware Bootstrapping for Off-Policy Subgoal Value Learning

author.name: Bingyun Liu, Yuheng Jing

entry.summary: The paper identifies a bias in HIRO-style off-policy hierarchical RL where subgoal relabeling corrupts high-level value targets, and proposes Hierarchical Time-aware Bootstrapping (HTB). HTB evaluates specified subgoals under the current low-level policy while using remaining execution time to distinguish subgoal continuation from new high-level decisions, enabling sounder off-policy Bellman updates.

entry.title: Reflecting on Creative-Boundaries with an AI Co-Doodler

author.name: Samia Menon, Samyukta Jayaram, Chetan Goenka, Shm Garanganao Almeda

entry.summary: This pictorial (research-through-design paper) explores how users negotiate creative boundaries when collaborating with an AI co-creative drawing tool. The authors present Froggi-Draw, a single-initiative co-doodling system where users control when and how much the AI contributes, and report findings from a 1-week pilot study with eight novice and experienced artists. Participants navigated creative risk and uncertainty, and at times perceived the AI as encroaching on their creative territory, prompting design implications for supportive co-creative AI.

entry.title: When the Cross-Silo Federation Goes Offline: Continual Learning for Site Onboarding with Limited Unlabeled Data

author.name: Ahmadreza Eslaminia, Klara Nahrstedt, Chenhui Shao

entry.summary: The paper addresses a practical federated learning gap: onboarding a new site after established participants have gone offline, using only unlabeled data that mixes known and unseen conditions. It presents an autonomous three-stage procedure for continual learning in this setting without access to the original federation.

entry.title: Nexus: An Execution Fabric for AI Agents Across Cloud, Edge, and Devices

author.name: Cary Chang, Jialin Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Nexus, a cloud-edge platform treating each agent invocation as a persistent task with unified execution abstractions, permission control, and lifecycle management across failures, recovery, usage, and settlement. It uses an OpenWrt-based runtime to span computers, mobile devices, and edge environments, addressing cost, scaling, and fault-impact limitations of cloud-centric agent designs. Relevant as systems infrastructure for long-running, multi-device agents.

entry.title: Who Keeps the Gains from Personal AI Assistants? Seller Adaptation and the Unassisted in a Language-Model Market Simulation

author.name: Haonan Huang, Joey Xiao

entry.summary: Builds an agent-based rental market simulation where LLMs play consumers, personal assistants, and six adaptive sellers with algorithmic pricing, examining whether consumer savings from AI assistants persist once sellers adapt and what happens to unassisted consumers. Early evidence suggests savings depend heavily on seller response and assistant mandate type. Timely agent-based economics on the distributional effects of shopping assistants.

entry.title: UltraDub: Towards Authentic Dubbing by Unifying Visually-Steered Flow Learning and Trajectory Guidance

author.name: Gaoxiang Cong, Liang Li, Jianwei Wen, Zhedong Zhang, Zheng-Jun Zha, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: UltraDub is a visual voice cloning framework for authentic video dubbing that uses visual information both as continuous motion context and as structural rhythm guidance for speech generation. It introduces a Motion-guided Dual-context Retrieving module to keep linguistic and speaker-style cues consistent while maintaining lip synchronization. The work addresses the tension between intelligibility, speaker consistency, and audiovisual sync.

entry.title: Representation Disentanglement for Fair Chest X-Ray Diagnosis

author.name: Yujie Sun, Ruizhe Li, Xiaowu Sun

entry.summary: The paper proposes a single-encoder framework using dual-level decorrelation and prototype-guided cross-group contrastive learning to reduce demographic dependence in chest X-ray representations, plus a new metric called Demographic Representation Alignment Reduction. Evaluation covers four tasks on 34,809 CheXpert test images across eight intersectional groups by age, sex, and ethnicity. The goal is reducing performance disparities from biased learned representations.

entry.title: Machine learning for journal entry testing: A type-aware evaluation of anomaly detectors under a review budget

author.name: Jan Gronewald, Michel Scherer, Nijat Mehdiyev

entry.summary: This paper proposes a type-aware evaluation for journal-entry anomaly detection in auditing, introducing fair-share type recall, type coverage, and first-hit rank metrics that respect realistic review budgets. It benchmarks nine unsupervised detectors, a supervised reference, and feedback-driven DeepSAD on real client ledgers and a synthetic ledger. The work improves evaluation realism for an applied detection domain.

entry.title: Joint Class-Time Learning for Video Classification with Multi-Instance Partial-Label Learning

author.name: Lingyu Shen, Wei Tang, Fakhri Karray, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a method coupling label disambiguation with temporal evidence allocation for multi-instance partial-label video classification, using occupancy-regularized spherical matching and candidate-restricted inference with a dual-marginal KL teacher. This jointly determines which candidate classes correspond to which time segments. It addresses inexact supervision in both instance and label spaces.

entry.title: Toward Reliable Infant Pose Estimation: A Training-Dynamics Approach to Noisy Annotation Detection

author.name: Emanuele Cardinale, Sara Moccia, Alessandro Cacciatore, Lucia Migliorelli

entry.summary: The paper adapts small-loss and training-dynamics-based noisy-label detection to markerless infant pose estimation, proposing a framework for detecting mislocalized keypoints whose errors propagate into clinically relevant motion biomarkers for preterm infants. This improves data quality for a sensitive medical imaging application.

entry.title: Mind the Accent Gap: British Accent Robustness in Speech-Driven Financial Voice Assistants

author.name: Aadam Haq, Oggi Rudovic, Malcolm Chadwick, Jay Rainey, Shucong Zhang, Ricardo Guerrero, Sourav Bhattacharya, Maja Pantic

entry.summary: The paper introduces CavaBench, an internally collected benchmark of spoken financial queries, and evaluates ASR models and full ASR-LLM pipelines for robustness to regional British accents under latency and memory constraints. It shows how ASR errors on Scottish, Irish, and Welsh accents propagate into LLM tool-call arguments, causing wrong or missing financial responses. This highlights an equity and reliability gap in deployed voice assistants.

entry.title: Closing the Context Gap: Activation Alignment for Tabular In-Context Learning

author.name: Yoel Zeldes

entry.summary: The paper proposes activation alignment for tabular foundation models, which must reprocess all labeled training examples at every inference. Instead of discarding context, a lightweight linear transformation trained on synthetic unlabeled data maps a data-constrained student model's intermediate activations to match a full-context teacher, recovering much of the performance at lower cost. This tackles a real inference-cost problem for the TabPFN-style model family.

entry.title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing

author.name: David Serrano-Lozano, Duygu Ceylan, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Iliyan Georgiev, Javier Vazquez-Corral, Anna Fr\"uhst\"uck

entry.summary: UniSlider decouples the editing slider from a generative model's strength parameter, requiring perceptual distance from the input to grow linearly with slider value, and introduces a framework enforcing monotone, perceptually uniform trajectories for continuous image editing. This fixes common failures where images partially revert, long ranges produce no visible change, or short ranges transform abruptly. It improves the usability of diffusion-based interactive editing tools.

entry.title: Least Squares for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Weiu-qiou Ciang, Yuzhou Hong, Sherry Chen

entry.summary: Analyzes the relationship between forecast losses and representation losses that regress next latents, showing that for scalar targets with linear decoders, latent ranks of at least one reduce to ordinary least squares and isotropy constraints are mere rescalings. The paper identifies failure cases for rank-limited whole-vector fits via constructed autoregressive examples.

entry.title: DePICT: Decision-Preserving Interface for Constrained Downstream Tasks

author.name: Utkarsh Grover, Ravi Ranjan, Agoritsa Polyzou, Wyatt T. Mackey, J. Morris Chang, Leonardo Bobadilla, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: Introduces DePICT, a procedure for constructing decision-preserving interfaces that rank context directions by the sensitivity of a constrained optimizer's solution and aggregate them across an operating regime, answering which inputs a decision system truly depends on. The paper provides theoretical guarantees for locally regular constrained programs in high-dimensional settings.

entry.title: One-Step Curvature Probes Miss the Fitting Operator: Retained Capacity and Terminal Null-Space Correction for Continual Learning

author.name: Abu Sa-Adat Mohamed Moon-Im Al Ahsan, Ibne Farabi Shihab, Md Najmus Swaqeeb

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of continual learning in overparameterized linearizations, showing that one-step curvature probes misestimate forgetting because learners are judged after reaching new-task fit. It derives exact factorizations of terminal old-task quadratic ratios in terms of retained fitting capacity and endpoint curvature, separating a fitting floor from algorithm-dependent null-space effects.

entry.title: A Hand-Checkable Proof That Two Hidden ReLU Layers Compute the Maximum of Six Numbers

author.name: Dimitrios Myrisiotis

entry.summary: Gives an explicit hexagon identity, found by computer-assisted search but provable by hand via explicit cancellations, that yields a self-contained analytical proof that two hidden ReLU layers suffice to compute the max of six inputs. The resulting network has widths 17 and 41, zero biases, and rational weights. A neat, verifiable contribution to depth-separation theory.

entry.title: PhaseGate: Phase-Aware CPU Retrieval Scheduling for On-Device LLMs on Unified Memory

author.name: Seoyoon Yum, Sehoon Kim

entry.summary: PhaseGate studies contention between GPU-based LLM inference and CPU retrieval on unified-memory devices, showing concurrent retrieval workers raise p95 decode latency by about 60 percent while prefill is barely affected. It uses LLM inference phase (prefill vs decode) as an admission signal, calibrating separate concurrency limits per phase and achieving 2x aggregate retrieval throughput while keeping latency near no-retrieval baselines. A practical systems result for on-device LLM assistants.

entry.title: Revisiting the Generalization of Neural Graph Edit Distance Models

author.name: Zhouyang Liu, Ning Liu, Yixin Chen, Jiezhong He, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates neural graph edit distance (GED) models under exact supervision across diverse graph datasets, revealing a pronounced gap between within-collection performance and cross-collection transfer. Training on multiple source collections substantially improves zero-shot transfer and provides better initialization under limited supervision. It highlights an overestimated notion of progress in neural GED under standard within-dataset evaluation.

entry.title: DASH: Fast, Valid Counterfactuals for Deep Networks via Batched Directional Search

author.name: Shraman Pal, Gabriel Medeiros, Clayton Escouper das Chagas, Can Li

entry.summary: DASH is a batched heuristic search method for generating close, valid, and actionable counterfactual explanations for deep neural networks under l1, l2, and linf objectives, using directional Lipschitz bounds and local affine models to guide the search. It aims to combine the speed of heuristic methods with the validity guarantees more typical of exact solvers.

entry.title: MAGIC: Topology-Aware Analytic Graph Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Junlin Chen, Yuhan Wang, Xuefei Wang, Xiao Wang, Ruijie Wang, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: MAGIC is a replay-free framework for graph few-shot class-incremental learning that addresses overfitting from scarce novel-class labels and representation drift caused by cross-session edges altering historical propagation neighborhoods. It combines a frozen graph representation backbone with topology-aware analytic components to preserve prior knowledge while learning new classes from few labeled nodes.

entry.title: Ranking Bandits for Carousel Interfaces with Observable Browsing Depth

author.name: Takuma Yasuda, Atsuyoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: The paper formulates a ranking-bandit problem where the learner observes a user's maximum browsing depth on carousel interfaces, distinguishing displayed-but-unclicked items from never-displayed items. It proposes UCB, Thompson Sampling, and DMED algorithms with provable updates under unknown item attractiveness and browsing-depth distributions.

entry.title: Efficient Graph Generation via Direct Prediction and Flow Matching

author.name: Susie Lu

entry.summary: The paper argues that noise-prediction diffusion is suboptimal for graph generation because it does not explicitly learn topological properties like connectivity and degree distribution, and proposes combining direct prediction with flow matching. The approach targets applications such as drug discovery and social network simulation.

entry.title: An equality condition for the Dobrushin bound on attention rollout and how often it holds in trained transformers

author.name: Przemys{\l}aw Rola

entry.summary: Characterizes exactly when the layerwise Dobrushin coefficient bound for attention rollout is tight, showing equality holds if and only if a mutually self-dominant token pair exists. Empirically, the condition holds far less often in trained transformers than random matrices would suggest, informing interpretability analyses based on attention rollout.

entry.title: Graph Data Augmentation via Contrastive Generator Inversion ($\texttt{DCBA}$)

author.name: Mateusz Stolarski, Micha{\l} Czuba, \L{}ukasz Krai\'{n}ski, Katarzyna Musial, Pawe\l{} Pra\l{}at, Bogumi\l{} Kami\'{n}ski, Piotr Br\'{o}dka

entry.summary: Introduces DCBA, a graph data augmentation method that infers the configuration of a synthetic graph generator (the ABCD scale-free community generator) from an observed network. It learns a joint representation of graphs and generator parameters via a multi-positive contrastive objective with soft negative weighting, enabling generation of new synthetic graphs for training graph ML models.

entry.title: Image resolution enhancement for advanced semiconductor nodes

author.name: Lucas Rencker, Omid Tajalizadehkhoob, Khalid Elsayed, Artem Khachaturiants, Helda Pahlavani, Yan Guo, Jakob van de Laar, Erik Simons, Niranjan Saikumar, Hamed Sadeghian

entry.summary: Presents a machine learning framework for enhancing resolution of high-throughput scanning probe microscopy images used in semiconductor metrology, targeting sub-nanometer feature measurement without sacrificing throughput for in-line process control. It establishes the general framework under which ML enhancement can reduce imaging time at advanced nodes.

entry.title: Beyond Transport Cost: Routing Differences between Flow Matching and Optimal Transport

author.name: Eungyeol Han, Jong-Seok Lee

entry.summary: The paper separates transport cost from routing in noise-data couplings for generative flow matching, showing numerically that FM and OT can produce different routings at nearly equal cost. Using exact FM routing as an oracle, the authors construct a routing-aware training coupling that yields directionally consistent generation improvements over a cost-matched, cost-only alternative. This demonstrates that cost alone is insufficient for coupling design.

entry.title: GO-Based Clustering for Learning Cluster-Level Causal Gene Regulatory Networks

author.name: Azlaan Mustafa Samad, Wei Zhang, Ad\`ele H Ribeiro

entry.summary: This work introduces GO4CD, an algorithm that uses Gene Ontology to construct biologically meaningful gene partitions at multiple granularities for cluster-level causal discovery in gene regulatory networks. The approach avoids the need for predefined admissible acyclic partitions, improving tractability and interpretability of high-dimensional causal GRN inference.

entry.title: Mind the Drift: Diagonal Linear Networks Under Large Learning Rates

author.name: Aniket Sanyal, Tom Jacobs, Rebekka Burkholz

entry.summary: This theory paper studies gradient descent with large learning rates in diagonal linear networks through the Edge of Stability lens, uncovering a competition between two implicit biases that jointly determine sparsity of recovered regression solutions. It introduces the Drift, a quantity related to but distinct from the Gain, characterizing imbalance effects of discretization error at scale. The work deepens understanding of why large learning rates change training trajectories.

entry.title: SimAuthor: Harnessing Foundation Models for Persistent Scientific Simulator Authoring

author.name: Yishan Wang, Ran Piao, Mathias Funk, Aaqib Saeed

entry.summary: SimAuthor is a harness that uses foundation models to author scientific simulators executable programs encoding mechanistic hypotheses under weak empirical feedback from limited real observations. It retains and iteratively revises executable simulators, separating scalar search scores from richer structural evaluation signals since scientific adequacy admits no exact test. This formalizes an underexplored use of LLMs beyond one-shot code generation.

entry.title: Multimodal Deep Survival Analysis for Sinkhole Susceptibility

author.name: Lucas Yuan, Minhee Kim, Zihan Li, Chunli Dai, Sanduni S. Disanayaka Mudiyanselage, Ming Ye, Kani Fu

entry.summary: The authors propose a multimodal Cox proportional hazards framework for predicting sinkhole susceptibility in Florida, addressing the challenge that non-sinkhole locations cannot be labeled as true negatives and that risk factors span heterogeneous data modalities. The work extends survival analysis methodology to a real geohazard problem. It matters for both geoscience applications and positive-unlabeled learning methodology.

entry.title: Sharp Deviations Bounds for Dirichlet Weighted Sums with Application to analysis of Bayesian algorithms

author.name: Denis Belomestny, Pierre Menard, Alexey Naumov, Daniil Tiapkin, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper derives sharp non-asymptotic deviation bounds for weighted sums of Dirichlet random variables via a novel integral representation of the density, yielding Gaussian-like approximations using geometry and complex analysis. Applications include new deviation bounds for Dirichlet process posterior means relevant to the analysis of Bayesian algorithms.

entry.title: Deep Learning Denoising of Real SWOT Sea Surface Height Observations

author.name: Ga\'etan Meis, Ana\"elle Tr\'eboutte, Maxime Ballarotta, Marie-Isabelle Pujol, G\'erald Dibarboure

entry.summary: This paper evaluates and extends a U-Net CNN approach, originally developed on simulated SWOT satellite measurements, to denoise real Surface Water and Ocean Topography sea surface height observations, where instrumental noise corrupts fine-scale ocean dynamics signals. It demonstrates the transition from simulation-validated denoising to operational real-data application.

entry.title: OncoNoteBERT: A Foundation Representation Model for Natural Language Processing of Real-World Outpatient Oncology Notes

author.name: Wuraola Oyewusi, Eliana Vasquez Osorio, Goran Nenadic, Gareth Price

entry.summary: The paper introduces oncology-specific BERT-style encoders trained on 290,026 UK outpatient notes from over 21,000 cancer patients, comparing continued pretraining of RadBERT against training OncoNoteBERT from scratch with a domain tokenizer. Domain-specific clinical language models can capture oncology terminology, staging, and de-identification markers that general biomedical models miss. This supports downstream extraction from real-world oncology records for research and care.

entry.title: Exact Optimal Transport by Matching

author.name: Dmitry Kamenetsky

entry.summary: The paper observes that balanced discrete optimal transport between equal-size unit-mass sets is exactly minimum-cost bipartite matching, and shows that exact matching engines beat entropic Sinkhorn and Greenkhorn in speed and accuracy throughout the moderate-n regime on dense 2D instances. A textbook LP dual-feasibility clip certifies the exact solutions. This offers a practical correction to the default habit of using approximate OT solvers.

entry.title: FLAT: Smoothing the Rugged Landscape for Learnable, Sample-Efficient Traffic Calibration

author.name: Haopeng Deng, Shuo He, Dayuan Wang

entry.summary: Presents FLAT, a method for calibrating microscopic traffic simulation models for digital twins under tight simulation budgets. It replaces rugged trajectory-matching objectives with an eight-dimensional behavioral fingerprint that smooths the optimization landscape, combined with annealed lower-confidence-bound acquisition for efficient Bayesian optimization. This makes sequential calibration learnable from a few dozen samples.

entry.title: Exploiting Hierarchical Controller Structure in Contextual Parameter Learning for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Sebastian Hirt, Lukas Theiner, Jan Peters, Rolf Findeisen

entry.summary: Proposes a contextual Bayesian optimization framework for joint parameter learning across hierarchical humanoid control architectures, retaining structured observations across levels rather than treating closed-loop performance as a scalar black box. This captures cross-layer parameter interactions that independent per-level tuning neglects. Relevant to coordinating planning, whole-body motion, and low-level control in humanoid robots.

entry.title: Hypergraph Representation Learning with Hyperlink Random Effects

author.name: Zimeng Li, Shihao Wu, Gongjun Xu, Ji Zhu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a method for learning representations from hypergraph data that exploits low-rank structure while handling hyperlinks of non-uniform sizes and heterogeneous generating mechanisms through hyperlink random effects. This addresses key limitations of existing tensor-based and deep hypergraph approaches.

entry.title: Optimal Oracle Complexity for Finite-Sum Monotone Inclusions

author.name: Qihao Zhou

entry.summary: The author presents a switching regularization method for finite-sum monotone inclusions that achieves the optimal O(n + sqrt(n)LR/epsilon) oracle complexity, removing the additive n log n cost of per-stage restarting. A matching lower bound is proven for randomized linearly convergent algorithms.

entry.title: TIRMamba: A Thermal-Prior-Modulated State-Space Network for Sub-Million-Parameter Infrared Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Chun-An Lin, Tsung-Jung Liu, Yen-Chieh Ouyang

entry.summary: TIRMamba achieves infrared image super-resolution with roughly 900K parameters versus 26-37M for prior Mamba-based leaders, using a thermal prior highway to modulate a weight-tied bidirectional state-space trunk. The paper also notes and addresses benchmark limitations from the tiny standard training set and evaluation on fusion products.

entry.title: Synergizing Drone Delivery Order Pooling and Road Network Monitoring through Monitoring-Task Orderization

author.name: Yulong Hu, Meng Xu, Sen Li, Nikolas Geroliminis

entry.summary: This paper studies real-time dispatch of a shared drone fleet that both delivers on-demand food orders and collects road-network traffic data. It introduces monitoring-task orderization to convert monitoring objectives into a form compatible with order pooling and routing, addressing a joint matching, routing, and scheduling problem under uncertainty. The work matters because it formalizes dual-use urban drone operations, a growing real-world application domain.

entry.title: Gaussian Limits for SGD Without Stationary Moments

author.name: Xiaoli Li, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: The authors construct least-squares SGD instances where temporal dependence gives stationary errors with infinite moments of every positive order, while independent data with identical marginals yields finite variance, yet Gaussian small-step limits persist in both regimes. They develop a general theory via pathwise contraction, score cancellation, and localization to obtain stationary Gaussian and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck limits. This clarifies when Gaussian approximations of SGD remain valid without moment assumptions.

entry.title: Quantum data loading from the learned shared structure of real signals

author.name: Pablo Herrero G\'omez, Antonio Jimeno Morenilla, David Mu\~noz-Hern\'andez, Higinio Mora Mora

entry.summary: The paper shows that classical signals in a dataset share learnable structure that a quantum-native loader can capture once and reuse, preparing every signal with a fixed small circuit parameterized by a few numbers. Across seven views of five public datasets it matches the strongest structured loader at equal gate cost with several times fewer parameters, and a preregistered blind replication validates inference from random subsets. This tackles the often-overlooked cost bottleneck of quantum data loading.

entry.title: From Abusive Language Classification to Sequence Labeling Identification

author.name: Nicolas Zampieri, Ignacio Lopez, Manon Girard, Jeremy Auguste

entry.summary: The paper reformulates abusive language detection as sequence labeling, jointly extracting abusive spans and target mentions rather than doing sentence-level classification, for industrial moderation under latency constraints. On a production moderation corpus, this approach remains competitive with classification while providing localized outputs for moderators. It bridges NLP research and operational content moderation needs.

entry.title: Revisiting Label-Free Speaker Embedding Enhancement with vMF Profile Likelihood

author.name: Seunghwan Kim, Jinyong Kim, Sooyoung Yang, Youngjin Ko, Myungjoo Kang

entry.summary: The paper models label-free speaker embedding enhancement as matching on the unit hypersphere, using a von Mises-Fisher likelihood with a profiled concentration parameter to derive a simple closed-form objective with adaptive weighting. It preserves baseline performance across VoxCeleb1, VoxSRC23, CN-Celeb, VOiACES, and VC-Mix while giving clearer gains on acoustically mismatched sets.

entry.title: Boundaries Agree, Labels Do Not: Intra-Annotator Dynamics as a Kind of Training Data

author.name: Marharyta Shvets

entry.summary: This study examines intra-annotator consistency — how reliably a single reader reproduces their own interpretation over time — as an alternative lens on annotation quality, using one expert human and three LLM families to segment three Sumerian myths and label causal functions of segments across runs months apart. It finds an interesting dissociation: boundary decisions (segmentation) agree across time while labels do not, suggesting self-consistency dynamics could themselves serve as a kind of training signal. The work is relevant because data quality increasingly rivals compute as a bottleneck for language model training.

entry.title: Understanding Errors in LLM-Based Question Answering over Imperfect Tables

author.name: Baowen Zhang, Wei Fan, Ruman Wang, Hangting Ye

entry.summary: Controlled studies across three LLMs on table QA over imperfect tables show that error discovery is sensitive to row order and layout: errors placed at the back or in compact layouts are found more often, and providing error locations is not always sufficient for accurate answering. The paper systematically characterizes a robustness gap in structured-data QA. Solid empirical analysis of an underexamined setting.

entry.title: Inductive Claims Extraction at Scale

author.name: Sandrine Chausson, Bj\"orn Ross

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-based pipeline that inductively extracts and catalogues claims from large social media corpora, treating claims as a unit of analysis for studying political phenomena like echo chambers and polarisation, potentially combined with Social Network Analysis. It is applied to two different corpora, demonstrating how computational tools can capture recurring interpretive statements in political discourse. The work bridges NLP and computational political science.

entry.title: Atomic Visual Entailment: Enhancing Zero-Shot Vision-Language Reasoning through Atomic Fact Decomposition and Learned Selection

author.name: Nallathambi Vethiappan, Derya Soydaner, Gijs Wijnholds

entry.summary: AVE improves zero-shot visual entailment by decomposing a hypothesis into atomic visual facts, producing candidate predictions from both the full hypothesis and its atomic facts with frozen vision-language models, and training a lightweight classifier on candidate behavior for the final label. The paper finds decomposition helps only when hypothesis context is preserved. It narrows the gap between zero-shot and fine-tuned approaches on visual entailment.

entry.title: Introducing Code-Switched Contexts to Cognitively-Inspired Bilingual Model Training

author.name: Zhuojing Huang, Luise Pohlmann, Lisa Beinborn

entry.summary: Inspired by bilingual children who use code-switched input as a cognitive scaffold, this paper studies how synthetic code-switched pretraining data improves cross-lingual alignment, controlling structural location and developmental timing variables across two typologically distinct language pairs. It maps which parameters govern success of this strategy. The findings inform more efficient bilingual pretraining recipes.

entry.title: Large Language Models and Augmented Democracy

author.name: Jairo Gudi\~no-Rosero

entry.summary: This thesis examines LLM-based digital twins as intermediaries in augmented democracy, testing whether personalized twins predict Brazilian citizens' policy preferences, extending the framework to political organizations via Swiss parliamentary data, and analyzing vulnerability of these representations to attacks. It spans preference representation, collective modeling, and security.

entry.title: Dynamic Time Step Prediction in Inverse Heat Dissipation for Blur-Like Image Restoration Tasks

author.name: Cap Dang Xuan Kiet, Tat-Jen Cham

entry.summary: This work improves diffusion-based image restoration by predicting the inversion time step per image rather than using a fixed intermediate step, since degradation severity varies. It also adapts the inversion process for blur-like degradations where standard DDIM Gaussian noise corruption is mismatched.

entry.title: A Theory of Shape Reconstruction from Heat Conduction and Shading

author.name: Akihiko Oharazawa, Sriram Narayanan, Mani Ramanagopal, Srinivasa G. Narasimhan

entry.summary: The paper develops a theory combining shape-from-shading and shape-from-heat-conduction cues to resolve classical ambiguities in single-image Lambertian shape recovery, including the normal cone ambiguity and the convex/concave ambiguity in Shape-Laplacian estimation. The method resolves local shape ambiguities without priors like smoothness, except for a few degeneracies.

entry.title: Diagnosis-Conditioned Spatial Gating and Decoder-Level Supervised Contrastive Learning for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Md Mustafizur Rahman, Mylene C. Q. Farias

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Position-Aware Gate that uses predicted finding representations to spatially modulate visual patch features without region supervision, plus a decoder-level supervised contrastive loss for radiology report generation. On MIMIC-CXR, the combined method improves clinical efficacy F1 from 0.484, addressing finding-level accuracy beyond fluent text.

entry.title: Synthetic-to-Real ViT-Based Pose Estimation of a Noncooperative UAV

author.name: Krishnanujam Srinivas, Hanish Acharla, Brij Agrawal, Leonardo Herrera

entry.summary: The work examines how well a ViT-based monocular pose estimator with a self-supervised DINOv2 backbone, trained purely on synthetic imagery, generalizes to real imagery of noncooperative UAVs. It addresses the synthetic-to-real domain gap, a key barrier since labeled real-world pose data is costly to collect.

entry.title: Task-Sensitive Geometry of Representation Transfer for Object Detection under Image Degradation

author.name: Van Vung Pham

entry.summary: Using paired clean and Gaussian-degraded BDD100K images, this study shows clean-teacher distillation improves degraded-image detection while producing heterogeneous object-level transfer. It isolates a complementary representation component, maps it into the student space via an orthogonal bridge, and uses controlled interventions to rescue a reported fraction of objects.

entry.title: TRACE: Time-Adaptive Residual Attention Control with Content-Style Decomposition for Training-Free Diffusion Style Transfer

author.name: Duc Khoan Le, Kim Ngoc Tran, Minh Nhat Le, Thanh An Tran, Viet Toan Nguyen, Khanh An Lay, Tran Thai Son, Hoang Pham Minh

entry.summary: TRACE is a training-free diffusion style-transfer framework that uses time-adaptive residual attention control and content-style decomposition to balance style fidelity, content preservation, and content leakage during sampling. It addresses weaknesses of fixed guidance schedules by making style injection depend on the diffusion timestep and state. The approach improves reference-guided stylization without additional training.

entry.title: PCLM: Small-target localization with frozen CLIP via prototype contrast and local magnification

author.name: Zhipeng Ye, Feng Jiang, Qiufeng Wang, Hao Li

entry.summary: PCLM is a support-conditioned localization method using a frozen CLIP encoder for small-target detection, building foreground and background prototypes from masked support images and using their difference as a shared scoring direction for query patches. Overlapping enlarged query windows sample small targets more densely, with reprojection and coverage averaging producing a continuous localization map. It adapts vision-language encoders to a regime where targets occupy few patches.

entry.title: WILLIE: A Unified Framework and Benchmark for Wound Classification, Segmentation, and Localization

author.name: Gopi Trinadh Maddikunta, Shannan Hamlin, Hsin-Mei Chen, Kimaya Barnes, Peizhu Qian

entry.summary: WILLIE presents a unified multi-task framework and harmonized benchmark for wound classification, segmentation, and localization, addressing chronic wound assessment that affects over 8.2 million US patients. Existing approaches handle these coupled tasks with separate models; WILLIE harmonizes three public datasets under a common protocol for systematic multi-task evaluation. This could streamline clinical wound care workflows.

entry.title: Controllable Road Marking Generation

author.name: Zhiyu (Joey), Cai, Yufan Zhang, Ruichen Tan, Zengxiang Lei, Satish Ukkusuri

entry.summary: Introduces a controllable generative pipeline that synthesizes bird's-eye-view road marking layouts from a drivable-area mask, outer-ring markings, and text, using a text-conditioned latent rectified-flow DiT with a topology-aware auxiliary loss and Gaussian-blurred targets. Provides a benchmark with deterministic metadata-derived prompts across lane dividers, road dividers, and pedestrian crossings.

entry.title: fMRI-TAMCL: Text-Anchored Supervised Multimodal Contrastive Learning for fMRI-Based Brain Disorder Classification

author.name: Juliana Mantebea Danso, Enoch Opanin Gyamfi, Mylene C. Q. Farias

entry.summary: Proposes fMRI-TAMCL, a text-anchored multimodal contrastive learning framework combining fMRI images, sparse functional connectivity, and generated subject-specific text for brain disorder classification. A Subject-Adaptive Threshold Derivation module addresses multisite heterogeneity that plagues rs-fMRI datasets.

entry.title: Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Guidance for Non-Blind Image Deblurring

author.name: Sihan Wang, Jinshu Huang, Haibin Su, Yunhua Xue

entry.summary: The authors propose frequency-decoupled posterior guidance for training-free diffusion-based deblurring, explicitly separating frequency activation scheduling from attenuation-aware spectral regularization. This improves on prior frequency-aware guidance methods that conflate the two effects.

entry.title: Multi-Task Partially Supervised Learning for Super-Resolution and Semantic Segmentation on Earth Observation data

author.name: Ho\`ang-\^An L\^e, Minh-Tan Pham, Solange Lemai-Chenevier, Daniel Greslou

entry.summary: The paper studies joint super-resolution and semantic segmentation when each training example has only a single-task annotation, examining sequential, shared, and a proposed hybrid architecture with a re-projection loss. Experiments show favorable results against SOTA on Earth observation data.

entry.title: Talk Like You: Imitating How You Speak in Real-Time Talking Head Generation

author.name: Baiqin Wang, Zhixing Ding, Jijie Li, Jiankuo Zhao, Zhen Lei, Xiangyu Zhu

entry.summary: This paper introduces TalkLikeYou, a framework for real-time talking head generation that captures person-specific lip motion patterns and speaking habits rather than producing uniform facial animations. It addresses the fine-grained, individual-level articulation variations that existing high-fidelity methods overlook.

entry.title: Robust Surgical Robotic Instrument Tracking via Sequential Multi-Cue Fusion and Sim-to-Real Self-Training

author.name: Hanyang Hu, Zekai Liang, Florian Richter, Michael C. Yip

entry.summary: The paper presents a tracker-guided self-training framework that adapts keypoint-based instrument trackers from synthetic to unlabeled real surgical videos, using robot joint states and an uncertainty-aware EKF to correct instrument poses. The approach overcomes the cost of real-world annotation for surgical instrument tracking.

entry.title: Structural Foundations of Nonlinear Systems with Unknown Inputs: The UID-Induced Normal Form and Minimal-Sensing Structure-from-Motion

author.name: Agostino Martinelli

entry.summary: The paper establishes a general structural solution to state estimation for nonlinear systems driven by unknown inputs, introducing the UID-induced normal form that decomposes unknown-input information into decoupled directions and observable quantities. It applies this theory to minimal-sensing structure-from-motion in a unified way.

entry.title: Visual Swarm Navigation via Deep Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Hybrid Design

author.name: \'{A}lvaro D\'{i}ez (Department of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, University of Alicante), Fidel Aznar (Department of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, University of Alicante)

entry.summary: The authors propose a hybrid AI methodology for automatically synthesizing decentralized swarm robot controllers for visual navigation, combining multi-agent reinforcement learning with neuro-evolutionary strategies including the cross-entropy method and CMA-ES to refine pre-trained policies. This targets emergent collective behaviors for applications such as search and rescue and environmental monitoring.

entry.title: Autoware in Construction: Gap Analysis and LiDAR Perception Toward Off-Road Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yu Otsuki, Teja Emmey, Sena Matsushita, Akiro Harada, Takeshi Miura

entry.summary: The paper documents lessons from extending the open-source Autoware autonomous driving platform to construction sites, presenting a gap analysis against unstructured terrain, dust, evolving conditions, and construction-specific objects, plus LiDAR perception work for large dump trucks. It provides a practical roadmap for off-road autonomy on an established open platform.

entry.title: Nudge Before You Push: Physics-Aware Navigation via Tactile Probing

author.name: Xianyao Li, Fang Xu, Ruitong Tian, Bowen Sun, Xiao Hu, Yang Ye, Jing Du

entry.summary: TANav uses a brief tactile nudge and a TacPhys model that reads force sequences (with optional RGB-D and kinematics) to estimate mass and authorize pushes under site-defined handling boundaries, distinguishing visually identical containers with different loads. A repeated-patrol planner weighs probe versus route costs, reducing missed pushes from 28.7% to 5.5% versus peak-force thresholding and recovering 90% of an oracle's path savings.

entry.title: RMMBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Robotic Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Huapeng Li, Fuxiang Feng, Jinqiu Fan, Shuo Yang, Fengjiao Chen, Xuezhi Cao, Ran Song, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: RMMBench is an evaluation benchmark for robotic mobile manipulation in which robots must understand language instructions and complete long-horizon tasks in continuous spaces, integrating high- and low-level embodied evaluation of VLM-driven capabilities. It addresses gaps in existing benchmarks' task diversity and metric granularity.

entry.title: Human-in-the-Loop Neuro-Symbolic Drift Anticipation for Reliable Visual SLAM

author.name: Junhyun Nam, Wonse Jo

entry.summary: Hybrid DeepSEE is a human-in-the-loop neuro-symbolic framework for proactive drift anticipation in visual SLAM, combining neural drift risk estimation with symbolic constraint reasoning. An LLM serves as a reasoning bridge, translating qualitative human context into interpretable symbolic constraints that regularize the neural predictions in out-of-distribution environments.

entry.title: From Social Reasoning to Embodied Interaction: An Agentic Framework for Social Robots

author.name: Ziyu Cheng, Yuewen Guo, Zhirui Liu, Dong Zhang, Haotao Lu, Jingyi Yu, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: ARISE is a unified framework bridging agentic reasoning and interactive social embodiment on the Sophia humanoid robot, integrating multimodal context understanding, long-term memory, and reasoning-driven decisions about when to engage with coordinated physical expressive behavior. It closes the loop between foundation-model social reasoning and embodied expression, which existing systems address only partially.

entry.title: Talk, Render, Act: Integrating Social Gesture and Digital Face with Synchronized Speech for Conversational Humanoid Robot

author.name: Jin Jiang, Kun Li, Jiancong Ma, Shengcai Liao

entry.summary: TRABot is an agent-based framework for expressive humanoid conversation that coordinates specialized agents for motion-atom construction, dialogue generation, motion planning, and facial animation. It builds Robot-Ready Semantic Motion Atoms by segmenting retargeted motion data into units with natural gesture boundaries and verified communicative functions, synchronizing speech, facial animation, and body gesture. This integrates two usually separate research threads: talking-face animation and robot gesture generation.

entry.title: Nonlinear Density-Driven Optimal Control (D2OC) for Multi-Agent Spatial Coverage via Sequential Convex Programming

author.name: Julian Martinez, Kooktae Lee

entry.summary: This paper extends Density-Driven Optimal Control to multi-step finite-horizon control of discrete-time control-affine nonlinear systems for multi-agent spatial coverage, driving the collective agent distribution toward a target density via a Wasserstein-based objective. Sequential convex programming with horizon-local linearization yields strictly convex QPs that preserve the Wasserstein barycentric structure while handling input constraints, with some convergence characterization. This enables prescribed-density coverage for nonlinear agents.

entry.title: On the Sequentially Semiseparable Structure of SDE-Induced Kernels and Efficient Algorithms for Kernel-Based Estimation Problems

author.name: Mikkel Paltorp, Luigi Caglio, Tianshi Chen, Evangelos Katsanos, Martin S. Andersen

entry.summary: The paper studies kernels induced by linear time-invariant stochastic differential equations, covering Matern and spline kernels used in Gaussian process regression and system identification. It exploits sequentially semiseparable structure to derive efficient algorithms for kernel-based estimation. This provides computational speedups for kernel methods across statistics, ML, and control.

entry.title: Taylor Expansion of Discount Factors

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Mark Rowland, R\'emi Munos, Michal Valko

entry.summary: This work studies the effect of using different discount factors for value estimation versus objective definition during learning, discovering a family of objectives interpolating between value functions of distinct discount factors. The analysis yields new value estimation and policy optimization methods with empirical gains, plus explanations of common deep RL heuristics. It connects discounting theory to practical algorithm design.

entry.title: DoMo-AC: Doubly Multi-step Off-policy Actor-Critic Algorithm

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Tadashi Kozuno, Mark Rowland, Anna Harutyunyan, R\'emi Munos, Bernardo \'Avila Pires, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper introduces DoMo-VI/DoMo-AC, an algorithm combining multi-step policy improvements and multi-step policy evaluation for off-policy control, addressing why multi-step methods have had limited impact in optimal control. It provides guaranteed convergence speed-ups to the optimal policy and works with general off-policy learning. The work clarifies theoretical obstacles to multi-step control methods.

entry.title: Optimal last-iterate convergence in matrix games with bandit feedback using the log-barrier

author.name: Come Fiegel, Pierre Menard, Tadashi Kozuno, Michal Valko, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: This work resolves how to achieve optimal last-iterate convergence for learning minimax policies in zero-sum matrix games with bandit feedback, showing that log-barrier regularization plus a dual analysis achieves the Omega(t^{-1/4}) exploitability rate that was previously only a lower bound. The approach extends to extensive-form games with the same rate. This closes a gap between lower bounds and achievable rates in adversarial game learning.

entry.title: Quantitative Universality of Approximate Message Passing for Rank-One Quadratic Sensing

author.name: Duy Thuc Nguyen, Yue M. Lu, Subhabrata Sen

entry.summary: The paper establishes quantitative universality for approximate message passing (AMP) with centered rank-one quadratic sensing matrices, which arise in quadratic regression and quadratic neural networks. It shows AMP behavior governed by the state-evolution recursion holds when rank-one sensing is compared against covariance-matched Gaussian designs, for smooth bounded spectral denoisers. This rigorously justifies Gaussian universality heuristics for structured sensing models.

entry.title: How Would We Know? Reflections on trying to make AI go well amid deep uncertainty

author.name: mikey jm

entry.summary: A wide-ranging essay arguing that given deep uncertainty in AI safety debates, the community's capacity to test and update its core assumptions matters as much as any single intervention. The author assigns roughly 30-40% probability to transformative AI within 1-3 years, argues capabilities are outpacing assessment and control, and explores how epistemics in AI safety connect to power. It is a macrostrategy and epistemics reflection rather than empirical research.

entry.title: Agent Policy-Value Audit: Separating Transition Composition from Event Selection in Financial LLM Agents

author.name: Mingyang (Alex), Chen (Andrew), Yida (Andrew), Xu (Aurora), Huiwen (Aurora), Chen, Yiming Lu, Wei Jin

entry.summary: The paper proposes an audit method that separates genuine event-selection skill from drift-driven returns in financial LLM agents, by holding action-change counts fixed and randomly reassigning them to build a composition benchmark. The gap between deployed value and this benchmark isolates selection ability.

entry.title: MedImageOSWorld: Benchmarking GUI Agents for Medical Image Consoles

author.name: Ziyang Long, Xinqi Li, Lujing Xing, Hsin-Jung Yang

entry.summary: MedImageOSWorld is a benchmark evaluating GUI agents on simulated CT, MR, and ultrasound consoles, where agents configure protocols, plan acquisitions, inspect images, and make corrective adjustments via screenshots and mouse-and-keyboard actions across seven capability levels. Evaluation combines workflow checks with hidden anatomical ground truth, targeting the link between on-screen anatomy and acquisition decisions.

entry.title: Learning Field Reconstruction from Incomplete Data by Globally Correcting Local Estimates

author.name: Renhao Zhong, Zihan Zhou, Chiyuan Ma, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: The paper tackles physical field reconstruction when every training field is incomplete, proposing a locally constructed, globally revisable estimator that learns local field estimates and substructures and then corrects them globally. The approach uses local spatial relationships as a structural prior to avoid averaged predictions that attenuate sharp transitions and localized detail.

entry.title: ProsaBuddy: Assisting Mechanized Real-Time Schedulability Analysis with LLM-based Agents

author.name: Junyi Liu, Tianchi Ren, Fei Guan, Xu Jiang, Zhe Jiang, Wang Yi, Nan Guan

entry.summary: ProsaBuddy is an LLM agent system that lowers the barrier to constructing machine-checkable schedulability analysis proofs in the Rocq proof assistant within the Prosa framework. It uses a ReAct loop with retrieval over the Prosa codebase, Rocq tool access, optional human hints, and subgoal delegation to automate parts of formal verification for hard real-time systems.

entry.title: Population Scaling or Data Dilution? Dynamics of Local Topology Evolution in Decentralized Learning

author.name: Yin-Kuan Liang, Yan Gao, Yang Long

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how scaling client count in decentralized learning interacts with data allocation, topology mixing, and communication capacity, comparing Ring, Static Random, and LFHE topologies on CIFAR-10. It provides an analytical failure mode for the Ring topology whose spectral gap decays as Theta(N^-2), implying slower consensus as scale grows.

entry.title: CLARA: Can AI Assess Developmental Appropriateness in Children's Stories?

author.name: Sijing Yin, Zirui Wang, Qian Liu, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: Introduces CLARA, a cognitively grounded framework for assessing children's narrative developmental appropriateness across cognitive, language, and social-emotional dimensions, plus a bilingual Chinese-English benchmark of 1,107 stories with structured annotations. It tests whether AI systems can approximate human developmental judgments at scale, relevant to educational recommendation and literacy research. A well-scoped application of AI to child development assessment.

entry.title: Parallelism or Concession? Concurrency-Aware Procurement Negotiation for Agentic Commerce

author.name: Xiaolin Xu, Donghao Zhu

entry.summary: This paper models a one-unit post-order sourcing problem where an agentic buyer forges parallel negotiations with sellers, jointly choosing the number of negotiators and a price cap under a hard deadline. The model captures per-thread costs, fulfillment loss, and excess-commitment risk from simultaneous agreements, and derives structural results including a geometrically decaying marginal value of extra negotiators. It provides theory for resource-rational concurrent agent negotiation.

entry.title: Few-Shot Prototype Head Adaptation for On-Device ECG Personalization on PSoC~6

author.name: Guilherme Silva, Pedro Silva, Gladston Moreira, Eduardo Luz

entry.summary: The paper proposes prototype-only head adaptation as a lightweight personalization primitive for TinyML ECG arrhythmia detection on microcontrollers, avoiding backpropagation through convolutional layers and optimizer state. A 1-D CNN with about 1,300 parameters adapts via few-shot prototype updates on a PSoC 6 device. This enables patient-specific on-device adaptation under severe resource constraints.

entry.title: MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents

author.name: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Tao Feng, Bohan Liu, Weida Liang, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: MemPilot is a flexible framework that orchestrates on-demand multimodal memory curation for LLM agents under explicit performance-cost-latency preferences, moving away from query-agnostic memory construction. It optimizes when and how memory operations run at runtime, offering control over the tradeoffs that fixed memory schemes ignore. This addresses growing costs and information loss in agent memory systems.

entry.title: Gated Target Propagation for Compositional Generalization in Continual Learning

author.name: Abdel Mfougouon Njupoun, Colin Bredenberg, Blake Aaron Richards, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: GaTaP is a continual learning algorithm using task-specific gating variables learned via a closed-form inner-loop update to selectively suppress or enhance network modules, with parameters trained on a slower outer loop using local difference target propagation signals. Beyond avoiding catastrophic forgetting, it supports recombination of prior knowledge for novel task compositions. Experiments cover class-incremental learning on multilayer networks.

entry.title: KALEIDO: Input-Space Adaptation of a Vision Model for Time-Series Forecasting Through Gated Fold Geometries

author.name: Xiangyu Shi, Qinghua Liu, Sam Heshmati, Zubin Abraham

entry.summary: KALEIDO repurposes an ImageNet-pretrained masked autoencoder for zero-shot time-series forecasting by rendering series as images, and adapts the rendering geometry itself by detecting dominant periods and generating multiple fold geometries. A convex per-position gate fit on validation data combines the inpaintings with the zero-shot output, requiring no temporal pretraining.

entry.title: Usefulness of Quantile-Aware Diffusion Modeling for Highly Imbalanced Tabular Data

author.name: Abu Talha, Peng Liu, Souradyuti Paul

entry.summary: Proposes a quantile-aware diffusion modeling approach for generating synthetic data in highly imbalanced classification settings such as FinTech and healthcare, arguing standard diffusion models with quadratic loss lack sensitivity to rare, extreme values in skewed or heavy-tailed tabular distributions. The method captures tail structure to better augment minority classes.

entry.title: Reachability-Aware Diffusion Policy Optimization

author.name: Hikmet Simsir, Kutay Demiray, Ozgur S. Oguz

entry.summary: RADPO is a model-free method for safety-aware online optimization of diffusion policies, combining predictive first-hit reachability estimation with cumulative-cost budget feedback. It learns a discounted first-hit reachability value that weights sooner cost events more heavily, uses this to shape rewards, and adjusts shaping strength via a dual-like multiplier based on realized costs. No explicit dynamics model is required.

entry.title: Gated Graph Neural Networks for Learning Hidden Independent Cascade Dynamics

author.name: Anubha Goel, Illia Oleksiienko, Mateusz Wilinski, Alexandros Iosifidis, Juho Kanniainen

entry.summary: The paper tackles the inverse problem of estimating per-node spreading probabilities in the Hidden Independent Cascade model from noisy proxy observations, without access to per-node activation times. Gated graph neural networks are used to infer node-level parameters whose count scales with the graph, marginalizing over unobserved spreading outcomes. Applications include modeling information and disease spread on social networks.

entry.title: Bounded Reasoning: Cognitive Hierarchy in Human-versus-AI Cyber Defense

author.name: Zahra Aref, Sheng Wei, Narayan B. Mandayam

entry.summary: The paper studies a sequential cyber-defense game where human or RL defenders face a DQN attacker, comparing human play under reward-only versus reward-plus-transition information structures aligned with Cognitive Hierarchy Theory-driven DQN. It critiques single-score human-agent evaluations by examining how human and automated policies adapt differently over time.

entry.title: Transporting Unsecured Stacked Payloads with a Quadrupedal Robot via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nobuo Namura, Masayuki Hiromoto, Kento Uemura, Hironobu Sasaki, Kanata Suzuki

entry.summary: PAMORT trains a quadrupedal robot to carry unsecured stacked boxes on a torso-mounted board without payload sensors, using a multi-objective RL base policy conditioned on a preference vector over locomotion and payload-stability rewards, with an online weight adjuster adapting preferences from proprioception. This addresses the real trade-off between aggressive locomotion and payload stability on uneven terrain. It is a practical legged-robotics contribution with a clean preference-conditioned design.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Optimization of Workload-Aware Power Delivery Networks
