entry.summary: This paper addresses social sycophancy in language models, where models over-affirm users in personal advice settings like relationship guidance, potentially making people overconfident. Unlike prior work focused on factual sycophancy with ground-truth answers, the authors identify that social sycophancy stems from models over-centering the user's perspective and propose pluralistic preference optimization to incorporate other stakeholders' viewpoints.

entry.title: MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0

author.name: Carsten Maple (Victor), Cagatay Yucel (Victor), Isaac Holeman (Victor), Chris Knotz (Victor), Peter Mattson (Victor), James Goel (Victor), Jonathan Petit (Victor), Sean McGregor (Victor), James Ezick (Victor), Abhishek Kumar (Victor), Alicia Parrish (Victor), Murali Emani (Victor), Kashyap Iyer (Victor), Faiza Khan Khattak (Victor), Washington Mbonu (Victor), Daniel Machlab (Victor), Eileen Long (Victor), Shaona Ghosh (Victor), Jibin Varghese (Victor), Roman Lutz (Victor), Andrew Gruen (Victor), Bennett Hillenbrand (Victor), Prabal Gupta (Victor), Mohammed Serrhini (Victor), Dhivya Nagasubramanian (Victor), Aakash Gupta (Victor), Jun (Victor), Lu, Kurt Bollacker, Chang Liu, Jonathan Petit, Cong Chen, Jean-Philippe Monteuuis, Brent Miller, Apurv Verma, Roman Eng, Armstrong Foundjem, Mohammed Serrhini

entry.summary: The MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0 provides an end-to-end, standardized pipeline for evaluating LLM robustness to single-turn text jailbreaks, combining criteria-driven attack selection, paired baseline and adversarial evaluation, human annotation, evaluator calibration, and risk-calibrated disclosure. It evaluates eight open-weight systems against 264 seed prompts across eleven hazard categories.

entry.title: hacktrace: behavior-supervised detection of reward hacking during code generation

author.name: Hao Jiang, Xin Li, Annan Wang, Yichi Zhang, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: HACKTRACE is a monitor for detecting reward hacking in coding agents, trained on 173,561 annotated multi-turn trajectories from Qwen3-8B, supervising shortcut behavior regardless of whether exploits succeed. It reads internal states the agent already computes, enabling detection before a turn completes without extra tokens, achieving a mean per-problem AUC of 0.997. This addresses a core AI safety concern as coding agents deploy widely.

entry.title: Reasoning Models Are Accurate but Unsound on Identification

author.name: Arman Behnam, Binghui Wang

entry.summary: The paper examines whether reasoning models can correctly decide if a causal effect is identifiable from observational data, showing they are accurate but unsound: they sometimes answer non-identifiable queries, which cannot be validated by any data. The authors build CERTID, a formal pipeline using the sound and complete ID algorithm to certify identifiability and verify returned formulas against structural criteria, enabling rigorous evaluation beyond string matching.

entry.title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies

author.name: Jungkyu Park, Dhruva Biswas, Joseph Cappadona, Cerise Tang, Ken G. Zeng, Bartosz Machura, Chuwen Liu, Paolo Tarantino, Coral Omene, Francisco J. Esteva, Rohit Bhargava, Marcin Braun, Kamila Pa\'zdzierz, Jakub Czerwi\'nski, Hanna Roma\'nska-Knight, Albert Grinshpun, Bareket Daniel, Michele Buchinger, Frederick Howard, Piotr Wysocki, Brie Chun, Freya Schnabel, Rich Caruana, Jan Witowski, Krzysztof J. Geras

entry.summary: A two-stage model first learns to infer transcriptomic profiles from histopathology using 8,742 patients across 32 cancer types, then predicts pathological complete response to neoadjuvant breast cancer therapy from inferred expression plus clinical variables. Trained on 1,080 patients and validated on 1,412 across nine cohorts, it achieves pooled AUROC 0.79 and outperforms histopathological biomarkers, including within molecular subtypes.

entry.title: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in LLMs with Whiteout

author.name: Anna Yoo Jeong Ha, Ronik Bhaskar, Haitao Zheng, Ben Y. Zhao

entry.summary: Presents Whiteout, a practical tool that selectively prevents LLMs from regurgitating personally sensitive information (birth dates, phone numbers, addresses) upon individual requests, as an alternative to machine unlearning which removes too much information and degrades utility. From a well-known privacy/security group (Zhao and Zhao, UChicago).

entry.title: OpenGameEval: Benchmarking Agentic Programming and Exploration in a Stateful Game Engine

author.name: Eray Turkel, Mengsha Sun, Kartik Ayyar, Sean Dunigan, Jack Lu, Vlad Shcherban, Hsiang-Shun Shih, Xin Wang, Tiantian Zhang

entry.summary: OpenGameEval is a benchmark and evaluation framework that runs language models as agents inside Roblox Studio, scoring agentic game development via executable checks on both edited scenes and simulated play sessions in reproducible, stateful environments. It uniquely separates observation tools from editing tools in an eight-tool action space so exploration behavior can be measured directly, and evaluates 13 frontier models on 84 human-curated tasks, finding tasks remain hard - the best model solves only 51.7% on a single attempt.

entry.title: Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhihan Yang, Wei Guo, Jean-Marie Lemercier, Simon Welker, Yonggan Fu, Mohammad Mahdi Kamani, Sajad Norouzi, Julius Berner, Tomas Geffner, Karsten Kreis, Yongxin Chen, Molei Tao, John Thickstun, Pavlo Molchanov, Ante Juki\'c, Arash Vahdat, Morteza Mardani

entry.summary: This paper introduces Sigma, described as the first large-scale (3B/8B parameter) continuous diffusion language model, built on smooth ODE/SDE latent trajectories in contrast to discrete diffusion models. It trains blockwise via likelihood optimization, warm-starts from pretrained autoregressive weights, and identifies classifier-free guidance and score temperature as key inference techniques for reasoning and coding quality. Continuous diffusion trajectories could enable better inference-time steering and acceleration than discrete approaches.

entry.title: OPD Before RL: Warm-Starting Rubric-Based RL with On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xinpeng Wang, Wei Shi, Yu-Chia Chen, Maria Zontak, Yun He, Richard Yuanzhe Pang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage framework for tasks that lack verifiable outcomes: rubric-privileged on-policy distillation first uses rubrics as teacher context to give dense token-level supervision, then rubric-based RL refines the policy with outcome-level rewards. This addresses the credit-assignment weakness of rubric-based RL where rewards arrive only after full responses.

entry.title: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time

author.name: Changxiu Ji, Amy Lu, Qizheng Zhang, Kunle Olukotun

entry.summary: Sentry is a failure-management layer that runs alongside LLM agents, detecting mid-task failures such as invalid tool calls and repeatedly looping actions, and exposing conditional failure knowledge only when relevant. The key insight is that failure lessons misfire when kept permanently in context, so they should be conditionally retrieved at test time rather than baked into a static playbook.

entry.title: Not Until the Evidence Says So: Teaching LLM Investigators When to Close a Case

author.name: Tingzhu Bi, Ping Wang, Meng Ma

entry.summary: This paper studies a decision LLM investigators face in accident, defect, and outage investigations: whether the collected evidence suffices to close a case. The authors show that even frontier models that identify correct causes in most cases routinely overstate their evidence and prematurely close cases whose official finding is cause undetermined. They propose training and evaluation methods for calibrated case-closure judgments.

entry.title: Detect and Suppress: A Mechanistic Defense against Adversarial Patches in VLA Models

author.name: Yukiya Horiba, Koshiro Aoki, Shunsuke Yasuki, Bum Jun Kim, Taiki Miyanishi

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how adversarial visual patches disrupt Vision-Language-Action models used for robot control, using sparse autoencoders to identify an internal feature that correlates with attack presence. The authors suppress this feature at inference time only when a linear probe flags an attack, improving robustness without fine-tuning. It matters because it offers a cheap, mechanistically grounded defense for safety-critical embodied AI.

entry.title: Trained Agentic Context Management

author.name: Bryce Sandlund

entry.summary: Instead of training native long context, this paper finetunes Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on a synthetic dataset over a minimal harness of self-call and context-reading tools. With only 8,000 tokens of context, the small model matches GPT-5.4 with 1M tokens on OOLONG-synth for documents over 40K tokens. This suggests trained agentic strategies can substitute for massive context windows at far lower cost, using existing models rather than new releases.

entry.title: All Work And No Play Makes Jack a Dull Boy: Understanding and Preventing Catastrophic Strategy Collapse in RLVR

author.name: Qiyuan Huang, Tianshi Xu, Meng Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies and characterizes late-stage strategy collapse in GRPO-style RLVR post-training of LLMs, showing it is a harmful contraction of strategy capacity rather than benign pruning. It develops a unified optimization-plus-information-theoretic framework proving that major RLVR objectives progressively concentrate probability mass on a single strategy, and proposes mitigations.

entry.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation

author.name: Nicolas Zucchet, Scott W. Linderman

entry.summary: Taking an entropic perspective on distillation, the authors prove that forward KL inflates student entropy above the teacher's, yielding a quantitative identity verified in pretraining and supervised finetuning, while reverse KL deflates entropy until the student-teacher gap grows too large. The work explains how the choice of divergence determines student diversity, a core concern for LLM training pipelines.

entry.title: Autonomous Robotic Navigation for Endovascular Brain-Computer Interface Access

author.name: Harry Robertshaw, Weijie Qi, Nikola Fischer, Alejandro Granados, Thomas C. Booth, Sam E. John

entry.summary: This paper presents the first demonstration of in vitro autonomous robotic navigation for endovascular BCI access in the cerebral venous system, using Soft Actor-Critic controllers trained in silico with geometric augmentation across anatomies. Navigation was validated over 1,000 simulated episodes and 20 physical fluoroscopy-guided runs across training and unseen anatomies. It advances a less invasive BCI delivery paradigm with real translational potential.

entry.title: Emergent Structure in the Marginal Attention Space of Language Models

author.name: Valentino Maiorca, Walter Nelson, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: This work maps post-softmax attention weights into a joint token-head marginal attention space across more than 60 diverse LLMs, finding text-intrinsic signals robustly conserved across independently trained models. The authors empirically connect marginal attention to the input-output Jacobian and provide theoretical justification, contributing to the growing literature on cross-model mechanistic structure (e.g., platonic representations).

entry.title: SCOPE-4D: Endoscopic 4D Geometry Foundation Models

author.name: Chaoyi Zhou, Zhongpai Gao, Anwesa Choudhuri, Meng Zheng, Benjamin Planche, Run Wang, Terrence Chen, Siyu Huang, Ziyan Wu

entry.summary: Presents SCOPE-4D, a foundation model jointly predicting camera parameters, dense geometry, and 3D tissue trajectories from monocular endoscopic video in a single forward pass, addressing scarce geometric supervision and the camera-motion versus tissue-deformation ambiguity. It also contributes SCOPE-5K, a curated dataset of roughly 5,000 real and synthetic gastrointestinal and laparoscopy clips with evaluation sets.

entry.title: Seeing, Saying, but Not Using: From Reportable Spatial Facts to Usable States in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jinchang Zhang, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces SpaceConflict, a 23,196-input benchmark showing that multimodal LLMs can correctly report spatial facts yet fail to use them in downstream reasoning, an availability-utilization gap. It probes four levels of spatial state construction, from local fact binding to state judgment under transformation.

entry.title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models

author.name: Zhaochong An, Fei Zhang, Menglin Jia, Duncan Frost, Zijian Zhou, Yikai Wang, Xudong Wang, Aditya Patel, Belinda Zeng, Tao Xiang, Serge Belongie, Amir Bar, Sen He

entry.summary: NAVA-WAM introduces native action-prior learning, directly pretraining robot action policies from observation-only videos without action annotations, avoiding indirect representation-to-control transfer or separate latent-action models. The two-stage training first pretrains on observation-only video and then grounds the learned action priors for robot control, improving scalability of world action models.

entry.title: PointWAM: 3D World Action Modeling for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Chunghyun Park, Beomjun Kim, Seungcheol Park, Heeseung Kwon, Yashu Shukla, Seunghoon Sim, Jinwoo Shin, Minsu Cho

entry.summary: Introduces PointWAM, a 3D world action model that decomposes the world into scene and hands and jointly forecasts both as 3D point trajectories in a shared space-time frame. This explicit disentangled representation captures contact geometry central to dexterous manipulation and enables effective pre-training for robot control.

entry.title: KungfuAthleteBot: learning high-dynamic humanoid motion from video with unified robust recovery

author.name: Zhongxiang Lei, Lulu Cao, Xuyang Wang, Tianyi Qian, Jinyan Liu, Xuesong Li

entry.summary: KungfuAthleteBot (KAB) is a framework for learning high-dynamic humanoid motion from video of national-level martial artists, addressing physics inconsistency, missing actuation information, and absent failure/recovery behavior. It contributes the KungfuAthlete dataset plus physics-guided trajectory correction and unified robust recovery mechanisms.

entry.title: Dynamic LLM Routers are Often Misguided

author.name: Sam Wang, Julia White, Sahibzada Allahyar, Dhruv Atreja, Urchade Zaratiana, Kelton Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzing six commercial LLM routers across 14 settings, the authors find none outperforms random selection between two well-chosen models at matched cost, with some underperforming by more than 10 percentage points. They trace the gap to four patterns including difficulty blindness and length reversal, and show these are what the standard cost-accuracy Pareto objective itself rewards.

entry.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses

author.name: Zekai Wang, Yingqiang Ge, Zekun Wang, Hai Wang, Yuhui Xu, Joshua Frandsen, Shancong Fu, Ashia C. Wilson, Chandan K. Reddy

entry.summary: VERSE is a self-evolving optimizer that improves LLM agent harnesses by also improving its own diagnostic, editing, and testing procedures, building tools for failure analysis, verification, training audits, and workflow control. The authors show in controlled studies that optimizer self-evolution fails without execution-based verification but achieves the best results when verification is available, validating the approach across five executors.

entry.title: Depth as Time in One-Step Generative Models

author.name: Arnold Caleb Asiimwe, William Yang, Sanghyuk Chun, Esin Tureci, Olga Russakovsky

entry.summary: The authors offer an empirical observation, depth as time: when multi-step diffusion is compressed into a single forward pass via distillation or flow maps, the denoising computation appears to unfold across network depth and can be recovered by decoding intermediate layers with the model's own output head. This connects layer-wise computation in one-step generators to the diffusion sampling trajectory.

entry.title: IGNITE Tokamak World Model Architecture

author.name: Peter Steiner, Azarakhsh Jalalvand, Nathaniel Chen, Kouroche Bouchiat, Ricardo Shousha, SangKyeun Kim, Egemen Kolemen

entry.summary: Introduces IGNITE, a generative world foundation model for fusion plasma behavior trained self-supervised on over a decade of unlabeled DIII-D experimental data, simulating tokamak discharges from actuator trajectories supplied directly or generated from text prompts or target outcomes. Uses multiple spatio-temporal tokenizers for heterogeneous modalities at vastly different time scales.

entry.title: Pincer: Resource Authorization for Agents using a Digital Twin

author.name: Mayank Rathee, Alexander Stepanov, Shalin Madabhavi, Jinhao Zhu, Raluca Ada Popa, Ion Stoica

entry.summary: Proposes Pincer, a resource authorization system for autonomous coding agents built around a digital twin, defending long-horizon shell-using agents with persistent memory without sacrificing the generality that typed tools or information-flow control give up. Addresses weaknesses of current user-mediated sandboxing (policy decay, permission fatigue) and auto-mode classifiers, from a strong security/systems team including Popa and Stoica.

entry.title: Misinformation Without Triggers: From Factual Answers to Downstream Decisions

author.name: Lin Tian, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: This safety study traces false web content in training data past a model's factual answers into downstream decisions, revealing an audit gap between what direct probes report and what the model actually does. Using a controlled decision task with matched truthful controls, the authors show that untriggered false training documents can propagate into scored decisions in ways that direct factual probes fail to predict.

entry.title: Training-Loss Guarantees for Muon with Finite-Step Newton--Schulz Orthogonalization

author.name: Amartya Roy, Souvik Chakraborty

entry.summary: The paper provides the first finite-time training-loss guarantee for the Muon optimizer that accounts for both momentum accumulation and its tuned five-step Newton-Schulz orthogonalization. For wide two-layer ReLU networks with a positive-definite limiting NTK, Muon provably reaches any target empirical squared loss with high probability.

entry.title: Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity in Agent-Security Benchmarks

author.name: Neeraj Karamchandani, Piyush Nagasubramaniam, Xinhong Xie, Sencun Zhu, Dinghao Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity (TPRS), a metric for how much attack success rates change when surface representations (like tool names) are altered while the underlying threat, policy, and evaluation stay fixed. Experiments on Agent Security Bench show ASR varies substantially with superficial representation changes. The finding challenges the validity of comparing agent security via single-benchmark ASR scores.

entry.title: Harnessing LLMs as Agents: What Does It Cost?

author.name: Zelin Zhao (Georgia Institute of Technology), Xinyu Guo (Georgia Institute of Technology), Jingyuan Zhang (Georgia Institute of Technology), Yuxuan Zhang (Etude AI), Yongxin Chen (Georgia Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Language Model Agent Machine (LAM), a resource-bounded abstraction that quantifies the computational costs of agent harnesses such as context management, memory, tools, and verification. It establishes formal results including equivalence to red-blue pebbling under call-transfer budgets and asymptotic separations induced by memory interfaces. This provides a first rigorous theory of what agent scaffolding costs in computational resources.

entry.title: Iterating Consistency Models: Stability, Error Bounds and Noise Schedules

author.name: Alessio Spagnoletti, Abdul-Lateef Haji-Ali, Andr\'es Almansa, Alain Oliviero Durmus, Eric Moulines, Marcelo Pereyra

entry.summary: This paper provides the first non-asymptotic error analysis of multistep consistency model sampling, decomposing error into initialization-error contraction and approximation-error accumulation under verifiable stability assumptions. The theory explains why adding sampling steps can help or hurt depending on the noise schedule, assigning contraction to large early noise levels and residual control to small late levels. This gives principled guidance for CM sampler and schedule design.

entry.title: Asterism: Exploring and Synthesizing Scattered Observations into Literature-Grounded Hypotheses and Theories

author.name: Joseph Chee Chang, Michael D'Arcy, Amy X. Zhang, Pao Siangliulue, Sangho Suh, Aakanksha Naik, Jena D. Hwang, Javier Ramos Benitez, Stella Wroblewski, Matt Latzke, Michael Cuoco, Ruben Lozano-Aguilera, Kris Ganjam, Joel Chan, Doug Downey, Peter Jansen, Kyle J. Travaglini, Daniel S. Weld

entry.summary: Asterism is a system that extracts observations from hundreds of papers as concept-relation triples unified in a hierarchical ontology, letting researchers curate evidence graphs and aggregate observations at different granularities to ground theory formation. Unlike fully automated LLM theory synthesis, it keeps researcher choices and intuitions central to hypothesis generation.

entry.title: SpectralCache: Accelerating Diffusion-Based World Models via Spectral Feature Caching

author.name: Zhendong Mi, Pu Zhao, Ziyu Hu, Xiaodong Yu, Yanzhi Wang, Grace Li Zhang, Shaoyi Huang

entry.summary: Reveals that world-model diffusion features exhibit highly stable singular subspaces across nearby denoising steps with predictable singular-value evolution, and exploits this via SpectralCache, a training-free caching framework that reuses subspaces and estimates only low-dimensional singular values. This substantially reduces inference overhead for interactive diffusion-based world models.

entry.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens

author.name: Ruiyang Si, Jianxin Bi, Shunyu Yang, Rui Ni, Wenbo Huang, Qiang Wang, Shulong Jiang, Duomin Wang, Xiuyu Li, Haiwen Feng, Zhen Dong, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: PyRUA-Lean is an interactive code-execution framework in which a VLM agent composes robot primitives and learned VLA policies into Python cells with conditional checks and local retries, returning only explicitly requested observations for replanning. Across 700 tasks in LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, it achieves a 14 percent higher success rate with 65 percent fewer tokens than a matched tool-calling baseline using the same GPT-6 Astra planner.

entry.title: On the Chain-of-Thought Monitorability of Looped Language Models

author.name: Han Wang, Ishwar B Balappanawar, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides the first systematic evaluation of whether chain-of-thought monitoring remains effective for looped language models, which repeatedly apply shared transformer layers to gain latent computation without increasing size. The authors study loop depth effects within a LoopLM family and compare looped versus non-looped models matched by parameter, layer, or effective-depth budgets.

entry.title: Gains and Collapse in On-Policy Distillation:A Reinforcement Learning Perspective

author.name: Han Cui, Jianhao Yan, Yun Luo, Hongbo Zhang, Zhizhang Fu, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: This paper explains why on-policy distillation sometimes improves student models and sometimes collapses into long repetitive generation, framing the teacher as an implicit reward model over student behaviors. When the implicit reward aligns with quality, OPD helps; when misaligned, reward hacking drives collapse. The analysis also shows OPD improves performance without expanding student capabilities.

entry.title: EyeRobot 2.0: Active Gaze for Precise Manipulation without Wrist Cameras

author.name: Kush Hari, Justin Kerr, Nidhya Shivakumar, Samarth Mahapatra, Carmelo Sferrazza, Jiahui Lei, Jitendra Malik, C. Karen Liu, Ken Goldberg, Angjoo Kanazawa

entry.summary: EyeRobot 2.0 enables fine-grained bimanual robot manipulation with a single stereo camera by actively swiveling eye viewpoints to fixate a 3D point and processing images foveally with more visual tokens at centers. A hierarchy of an RL-trained gaze servoing policy and a target selector coordinates Active Visual Fixation during tasks. This bio-inspired design removes the need for wrist cameras while achieving precise manipulation.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Huijuan Wang, Chufan Shi, Cheng Yang, Yaokang Wu, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Xuezhe Ma

entry.summary: The paper proposes recursive cross-capability self-improvement (RSI), a loop in which a unified text-and-image model uses its own understanding and generation abilities to produce training data for one another: it generates images, critiques them, writes programs targeting shortcomings, and uses execution-verified results to improve both image generation and visual understanding. Verified renders and correct programs become training signals.

entry.title: GRAFT: Growing Agglomerative Foundation Models via Continual Teacher Distillation

author.name: Zhenghao Zhao, Chi Zhang, Qingshuang Chen, Yelin Kim

entry.summary: Introduces GRAFT, a continual multi-teacher distillation framework allowing a single vision backbone to progressively absorb capabilities from an open-ended sequence of foundation models such as DINOv2, SigLIP2, and MASt3R. When a new teacher arrives, the previously trained backbone serves as a scaffold, avoiding repeated joint distillation over the full teacher set.

entry.title: Parasitic Co-Denoising: Unlocking 3D Human Motion Generation in a Frozen Video Diffusion Model

author.name: Yunjiao Zhou, Junlang Qian, Lihua Xie, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: The paper shows that a frozen text-to-video diffusion model (Wan2.1) contains recoverable 3D motion signals in its intermediate denoising states, and introduces parasitic co-denoising, where a lightweight flow-matching motion decoder extracts explicit 3D motion along the host model's schedule. This avoids training a separate motion generation model.

entry.title: Right Order, Wrong Scale: Auditing LLM Judges for Occupational AI Measurement

author.name: Harry Lyu, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: The paper introduces O*NET-BENCH, an audit suite built from 45,796 worker ratings, and evaluates 33 LLM judge configurations across six model families on 4,501 test ratings. Judges agree with workers on response ordering but wildly overestimate acceptance rates (3.0-97.9% versus a 61.1% human baseline), and a simple TF-IDF baseline nearly matches the best judge. This exposes a ranking-versus-calibration gap with implications for AI-in-the-workplace measurement.

entry.title: Open-Endedness Bench: Measuring Epistemic Process from Agent Records

author.name: Chengyang Shi, Xianglin Ji, Jintao Huang, Jicheng Wang, Yifeng He, Jiachen Liu

entry.summary: OEB introduces a benchmark-agnostic methodology for evaluating open-ended research agents by reading their execution logs and assessing how they form, test, and revise hypotheses, without requiring reference answers or outcome scores. This addresses the gap where open-ended agent runs are judged only by outcome, which cannot establish whether claims follow from executed experiments.

entry.title: Continual Graph Memory for Mathematical Research Agents

author.name: Junyi Zhang, Jinxi Yu, Eric Hanchen Jiang, Jiachen Lu, Zhi Zhang, Xinjie He, Hyunsik Chae, Ethan Ji, Alexander K Taylor, Vigyan Sahai, Yiwen Kou, Kai-Wei Chang, Raghu Meka, Nanyun Peng, Amit Sahai, Terence Tao, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Ansatz is a mathematical research agent built around Continual Graph Memory, a graph-based, evolvable cross-problem memory that organizes intermediate proof results from massive parallel long-horizon proof searches and reuses knowledge across explorations. It targets frontier mathematical research problems requiring extended multi-agent proof construction.

entry.title: Peer Influence across Heterogeneous AI Models

author.name: Frida N{\o}hr Laustsen, Marie Haahr Petersen, Victoria Popa, Ariel Flint, Romualdo Pastor-Satorras, Andrea Baronchelli, Luca Maria Aiello

entry.summary: Testing seven open-weight models across three language understanding tasks, this paper measures persuasion as probabilistic decision shift after a single dissenting exchange between AI agents. It finds persuasion is strong but that neither standalone certainty nor model scale reliably predicts who persuades whom - consistently correct models can be highly susceptible. These results matter for multi-agent system design and epistemic reliability.

entry.title: A Near-Zero Monitor Readout Is Not Evidence of Behavioral Control

author.name: Zhe Zhou, Tianhua Tao

entry.summary: This paper shows that low monitor readouts during RLVR training do not demonstrate that a monitor-based intervention controls reward hacking behavior. In a code-generation environment, three monitors passing the same offline gate produce probe scores at their numerical floor from early training, so near-zero readouts cannot distinguish monitoring success from the absence of the behavior being monitored.

entry.title: Counterfactual Predictions in Scientific Emulators Without Controlled Experiments

author.name: Dingling Yao, Kahaan Gandhi, Valentin Duruisseaux, Boris Bonev, Francesco Locatello, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: ReRoute is a framework for scientific what-if (counterfactual) prediction that combines factual data with partial mechanistic knowledge, avoiding the need for controlled simulation data in which confounded factors are disentangled. It fixes the queried input of a pretrained emulator and reroutes computations to answer unobserved interventions. Authored by Anima Anandkumar and Caltech collaborators, it addresses a fundamental limitation of neural scientific emulators.

entry.title: Compound AI System Reliability: A Failure Taxonomy and Resilience Pattern Catalog from 150 Production Incidents

author.name: Rudrendu Kumar Paul, Sourav Nandy

entry.summary: Analyzes 150 production incident reports from open-source compound AI projects and enterprise deployments to build a taxonomy of 23 failure modes across retrieval, generation, tool, orchestration, and integration failures, and proposes resilience patterns validated with measured effectiveness from controlled experiments. Focuses on failures at component boundaries rather than within individual models.

entry.title: FastOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Lightweight VLA Deployment

author.name: Yoojin Oh, Jeongsol Kim, Yeonwoo Seo, Jangho Park, Seonghyun Jin, Sunwoo Park, Youngmin Kim, Youngjun Jun, Kyumin Choi, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: FastOPD is a foundation-to-lightweight distillation framework for vision-language-action robot models, combining flow-map-based single-state teacher supervision with a self-consistency objective to build compact students that preserve teacher dynamics. It aims to make large-scale VLA models practical for real-world robot deployment without architecture redesign or reduced denoising steps.

entry.title: Discriminating Fixture Coverage in Agent-Infrastructure Verification Suites

author.name: Xin Xu, Siru Tao

entry.summary: The authors apply mutation analysis to an invariant suite gating LLM agent deployment and show that the standard practice of passing a correct implementation and failing a broken one certifies suites that miss serious bugs, including a mutant removing event deduplication that survives all checks. They quantify suite quality by measuring kill rates against adversarially designed mutants, exposing how little evidence a single pass/fail observation provides.

entry.title: D2K-Bench: Can LLM Agents Turn Expert Designs into Efficient GPU Kernels?

author.name: Daifeng Li, Huiqiang Jiang, Chengruidong Zhang, Wei Wu, Xudong Guo, Jianhong Tu, Jianwei Zhang, Binhang Yuan, Dayiheng Liu

entry.summary: D2K-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark with 26 tasks and 85 workloads measuring how well LLM agents translate expert design guidance at three abstraction levels (algorithmic insight, dataflow design, low-level optimization) into efficient GPU kernels. Controlled pairwise runs with and without guidance, plus a 350-turn budget, isolate where agent performance gaps originate.

entry.title: OptiSelect: How does the Optimizer Shape Data Curriculum?

author.name: Simin Fan, Alireza Abdollahpoorrostam, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: OptiSelect formalizes optimizer-aware online data selection for LLM pretraining, arguing that selection should account for how the optimizer reshapes gradients before parameter updates. The authors prove a selection-gain principle tied to discriminability of optimizer-induced utility scores and show sign-based preconditioners of Lion and Muon yield distinctive selection behavior.

entry.title: Beyond Trained Models: Compiling GNNs for a Sound Explainer Benchmark

author.name: Steve Azzolin, Francesco Paolo Nerini, Stefano Teso, Francesco Bonchi, Bruno Lepri, Andr\'e Panisson, Andrea Passerini

entry.summary: This work shows that standard GNN explainability benchmarks are confounded: on widely used datasets, trivial features like degree statistics suffice, so plausibility-based evaluation of explainers is unsound. The authors introduce Gracr, a compiler that translates graded modal logic formulas directly into GNN weights, producing models guaranteed to rely on the intended motifs. This enables a clean, assumption-free benchmark for GNN explainers.

entry.title: PowerBench: Measuring Language Model Bias in Power-shifting Requests

author.name: Nicolas Martorell, Wendy Brau, Gonzalo A. Heredia, Tom\'as Pablo Korenblit, Gaspar Labasti\'e, Tom\'as Gimenez Molina

entry.summary: PowerBench evaluates whether language models systematically differ in whom they assist with power-shifting requests, distinguishing self-empowerment, disempowerment, and power grabbing against refusal-inducing controls. The authors open-source a curated dataset varying power domain, context, affected-party scale, and user standing, and evaluate 24 models from US and Chinese developers under reciprocal nationality conditions. This is a novel and socially significant axis of bias: unequal assistance could shift real-world power distribution at scale.

entry.title: Fisher-Guided Submodular Data Selection for Continual Pre-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Zhenghao Zhao, Gaowen Liu, Zhiling Lan, Yan Yan

entry.summary: The paper frames data selection for continual pre-training as a forgetting-control problem and shows that loss-based selection degrades the Fisher diagonal precisely on high-Fisher coordinates the pretrained model relies on. It proposes Fisher-guided submodular selection that asks how training on a candidate will move model parameters, avoiding expensive general-domain replay. This offers a principled alternative to perplexity-based selection for domain-adaptive pre-training.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Bayesian Data Assimilation with Generative Models and Observation Interpolants

author.name: Nikolaj T. M\"ucke, Benjamin Sanderse

entry.summary: The authors introduce an observation-interpolant framework that converts pretrained stochastic interpolant, flow matching, and diffusion models into posterior samplers without retraining, via a shared likelihood-score correction to the drift or velocity. A closed-form Gaussian surrogate with bias correction enables practical computation, unifying stochastic and deterministic posterior sampling.

entry.title: Planning to Learn

author.name: Ian Osband

entry.summary: Ian Osband's solo paper analyzes why exact policy gradients lose to cross-entropy even in classification, where gradients are exact and smooth. The key insight is that exact gradients are myopic: each update changes where the next update starts, so an update's value depends on how much learning remains, and cross-entropy embodies a patient, lookahead-style accuracy objective. This reframing has implications for policy-gradient methods central to RL and LLM post-training.

entry.title: Does Physics Live in the Activations? Localizing Physical Quantities in Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Jonas Kneifl, Jakub Skalski, Bart{\l}omiej Twardowski, Kamil Deja

entry.summary: This paper probes internal representations of video diffusion transformers for simulator-derived physical quantities such as kinematic motion and rigid-body dynamics. It finds these quantities are linearly decodable with high accuracy early in the denoising process, outperforming decoding from noised latents, suggesting video models do internalize some physical structure. This bears directly on the debate about whether generative video models can serve as world models.

entry.title: DAWIS: Data Assimilation with Windowed Inverse Sampling via Multitask Interpolants

author.name: Erik Wikingsson, Martin Andrae, Tomas Landelius, Fredrik Lindsten

entry.summary: DAWIS is a unified data assimilation method using flow/diffusion generative models with inference-time guidance that can revise past states when new observations arrive, unlike existing filters that only assimilate the latest observation conditioned on a fixed history. Using multitask interpolants, it covers filtering, fixed-lag smoothing, and related regimes within one framework. This addresses error accumulation in high-dimensional non-Gaussian data assimilation for dynamical systems.

entry.title: Finding the Move Is Not Winning the Game: XiangqiBench for Closed-Loop Evaluation of LLM Agents

author.name: Yekun Chai, Qiwei Peng, Haoyi Xiong

entry.summary: XiangqiBench is an executable benchmark in which LLM agents must convert 119 forced-mate Xiangqi endgames into actual checkmates against an engine opponent via an interactive REPL, with 8,568 trajectories from 12 frontier LLMs. It exposes a conversion gap: models that can identify the correct first move frequently fail to execute the full plan under adversarial response.

entry.title: Source Preference in the Wild: How LLM Agents Favor Items by Source, and How to Reduce It

author.name: Jonghyun Song, Haewon Park, Jeonghoon Shim, Woojung Song, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Studying 12 LLM agent models across three domains, this paper shows that agents systematically favor items from certain sources even when a preferred-source item satisfies fewer requirements, selecting the worse item about two-thirds of the time. The work quantifies a consequential bias in agentic search and proposes mitigation strategies, with implications for fairness and market exposure as agents increasingly act on users' behalf.

entry.title: World Embedding Benchmark

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Ruifeng Yuan, Yang Wang, Long Li, Fengyu Cai, Hou Pong Chan, Jialin Yu, Hao Zhang, Chenghua Lin, Chenghao Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces the World Embedding Benchmark with 8,000 controlled simulation cases across 80 families in fluid mechanics, solid mechanics, dynamics, and optics and electromagnetism, pairing rendered videos with simulation-derived physical annotations. It supports text-video retrieval, physical-property regression, and video-description classification to probe how video representations encode physical information.

entry.title: Imagine the Future, Internalize the Gist: Efficient VLA Reasoning via Internalized Spatiotemporal Imagination

author.name: Shenglan Li, Zhendong Mi, Hengyi Zhu, Jingwu Luo, Chun Kit Chan, Geng Yuan, Yanzhi Wang, Pu Zhao, Shaoyi Huang

entry.summary: Proposes IG-VLA, a framework where vision-language-action models imagine task-relevant future scene evolution directly in latent visual representation space rather than through costly pixel-level video rollouts, plus a Scene Gist Memory to reduce inference overhead. This adds anticipatory reasoning to robotic manipulation at much lower computational cost.

entry.title: Found but Not Read: When Extracted Text Closes the Retrieval-Reading Gap in Document Vision-Language Models

author.name: Qingtao Xia, Siyao Cheng, Jiahua Bao, Jiaxing Du, Jie Liu

entry.summary: The authors identify a retrieval-reading gap in retrieval-augmented document QA: VLMs often find the correct evidence page but fail to read it. Adding CPU-OCR extracted text to page images raises strict accuracy by 13-16 points on their FoveDoc-Bench, with an exact text layer roughly doubling the gain across six VLMs.

entry.title: COSMI: COmpositional Synthesis of Multi-object Interactions

author.name: Daniel Eskandar, Ilya A. Petrov, Gerard Pons-Moll

entry.summary: COSMI composes contact-consistent single-object interaction captures into multi-object human-object interaction sequences, using hand mirroring, body transfer, and language-model plus geometric plausibility checks for filtering. The resulting dataset contains 222k sequences and 275 hours with up to five concurrent objects, growing combinatorially without extra recording.

entry.title: Reliability Stress Tests and Decision-Time Routing for Chest X-ray Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xinye Yang, Zhusi Zhong, Scott Collins, Grayson Baird, Xuyu Wang, Zhicheng Jiao

entry.summary: Introduces a reliability stress-test framework for chest X-ray VLMs, evaluating three medical VLMs (including MedGemma variants) across 36 configurations of prompt styles, single- versus multi-agent workflows, and two balanced datasets. It shows exact-match accuracy can overstate reliability for conservative models that default to Normal predictions, and proposes decision-time routing based on the findings.

entry.title: Rethinking World-Action Model for Compositional and In-Context Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Shukai Gong, Xuanran Zhai, Yintianrun Zhang, Ruopeng Cui, Ye Huang, Yiyang Fu, Dexuan Lyu, Chaojie Li, Xinyi Song, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Mingyuan Jia, Yufan Deng, Jiaxin Fang, Bo Liang, Jiaxin Li, Yuxiang Gao, Hao Liu, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes ViGAR, a hierarchical world-action framework factorizing long-horizon compositional manipulation into a visual subgoal planner and a subgoal executor that jointly generates future visual trajectories and actions conditioned on predicted subgoals, with shared pre-training. This adds explicit subtask-level reasoning to world-action models for real-world deployment.

entry.title: DeltaWorld: Physically Consistent Interactive World Simulators via Action-Conditioned Latent Increment Learning

author.name: Boyuan Hou, Xiaoge Cao, Chaofan Zhang, Shuo Wang, Shaowei Cui

entry.summary: DeltaWorld is an interactive world simulator that predicts action-conditioned latent increments rather than full next latent states, capturing subtle action-induced changes and preserving robot-object interaction dynamics over long horizons. This mitigates physically implausible artifacts like object interpenetration and excessive deformation in existing world models. It targets scalable environments for robot planning, policy training, and evaluation.

entry.title: Beyond Reward Hacking: Proxy Divergence Across Four Layers of a Staged Humanoid Learning Pipeline

author.name: Arunabh Bora

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that reward hacking is only one instance of a broader specification problem in legged-robot RL pipelines. It identifies four proxy layers — reward, curriculum gate, evaluation statistic, and reference motion — each with its own divergence mechanism and a proposed reformulation (e.g., first-order/L1-based corrections) to close the gap with the intended target.

entry.title: Large language models exhibit unreliable updating of clinical judgment as patient evidence evolves

author.name: Min Zeng, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: Using matched ICU trajectories from electronic health records, this study finds that across diverse LLMs, conditioning on a preceding judgment more often increases than reduces prediction error as patient evidence evolves. Controlled interventions reveal asymmetric sensitivity to worsening versus improving respiratory evidence and other systematic belief-updating failures with direct patient-safety implications.

entry.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers

author.name: Giovanni Monea, Keshav Ramji, Yousef El-Kurdi, Luis A. Lastras, Yoav Artzi, Nathan Godey, Ram\'on Fernandez Astudillo

entry.summary: This paper pretrains looped transformers to share memory across recursions: only the first recursion writes a KV cache while later recursions read it plus a short local window. Surprisingly, sharing memory improves rather than degrades quality, and at 150M-1B scale the Looped Prediction Transformer and its hybrid variant set a new quality-memory frontier for looped models, lowering perplexity with five recursions. This is a notable result for compute-flexible, memory-efficient architectures.

entry.title: The Fragility of Trigger-Tag Mechanisms for Misuse Detection in Open-Weight LLMs

author.name: Toluwani Aremu, Manit Baser, Mohan Gurusamy, Nils Lukas, Dinil Mon Divakaran

entry.summary: This paper formalizes trigger-tag mechanisms that emit detectable signals when open-weight LLMs are used under target misuse conditions, distinguishing token-level and activation-level variants, and systematically evaluates their robustness under adversarial attack. The findings show these mechanisms are fragile in open-weight settings where models can be modified beyond developer control.

entry.title: Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT

author.name: Joery Ari\"en de Vries, Neil David Lawrence, Zhenwen Dai

entry.summary: FTW adapts the cross-entropy method to critic-free reinforcement fine-tuning of agentic LLMs, replacing GRPO-style group rollouts with an ordinal filter over replay-buffer samples, which suits stateful environments where repeated rollouts are impractical. The authors provide polynomial concentration guarantees on order statistics of returns and derive the method through conservative policy improvement.

entry.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Ruihong Shen, \v{Z}iga Kova\v{c}i\v{c}, Peter Kulits, Xingrui Wang, Zizhang Li, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Alan Yuille, Jieneng Chen, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: 4DCodeBench evaluates whether AI agents can reconstruct dynamic 4D scenes from video as executable graphics programs, spanning phenomena like deformation, fluid flow, and fracture using real and synthetic scenes. Benchmarking frontier models reveals that strong static reconstruction does not translate into reliable reconstruction of complex dynamics. The benchmark exposes a clear capability gap in programmatic physical scene understanding.

entry.title: SDECast: Probabilistic Weather Forecasting in Continuous Time with Neural SDEs

author.name: Maria Marchenko, Martin Andrae, Fredrik Lindsten, Christian A. Naesseth

entry.summary: SDECast is a neural stochastic differential equation framework for continuous-time probabilistic weather forecasting, extending SDE matching to learn stochastic atmospheric dynamics directly in physical space without repeated SDE simulation during training. This avoids the error accumulation of autoregressive rollouts at fixed temporal resolutions and respects the temporal continuity of atmospheric dynamics. Results on simulated geophysical flows demonstrate the approach's promise.

entry.title: Octrees as an Explicit 3D Language

author.name: Ran Dan, Si-Tong Wei, Pengfei Xiong, Wei Zhang, Yadong Mu, Peng-Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Proposes OctLLM, which feeds geometry to a large language model as explicit sparse-octree occupancy token sequences instead of latent codebook indices, and trains via position-aware mask modeling rather than fine-tuning that erodes general language ability. Randomized emptying of penultimate-level nodes keeps sequence length manageable while preserving shape.

entry.title: Behavior Pack Optimization for Video MLLM Post-Training

author.name: Zhaolu Kang, Shiyu Liu, Tailong Luo, Wei Zhang, Yingjie He, Lei Wei, Guansu Wang, Liang He, Siheng Wang, Guangyuan Dong, Jiaqi Su, Shuang Chen, Haoyu Ji, Qishi Zhan, Kaiyue Zhou

entry.summary: The paper shows video MLLMs ignore temporal evidence, since shuffling frames or masking the answer-supporting segment barely changes predictions, tracing this to post-training rewards computed on single responses. Behavior Pack Optimization scores joint outputs across counterfactual views chosen by question type, rewarding consistency under intervention.

entry.title: FlowHMR: Physically Plausible Motion Capture from Video

author.name: Zhanke Wang, Chengfeng Zhao, Qing Shuai, Jingzhong Lin, Heng Li, Zeyu Ling, Yuxin Wen, Jing Li, Di Kang, Chunchao Guo, Linchao Bao

entry.summary: FlowHMR recovers physically plausible global 3D human motion from monocular video by formulating video motion capture as video-conditioned motion generation, pretraining a flow matching model that generates diverse motion hypotheses to resolve depth ambiguity. Generated hypotheses are then physically tracked, avoiding the averaged-solution collapse of direct regression and improving physics-based tracking success.

entry.title: Filter-Aware Fine-Tuning for Safe Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking

author.name: Pranit Mohnot, Christian Helten, Daniele Gammelli, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: Shows that independently treating a humanoid tracking RL policy and runtime safety filters like control barrier functions induces fundamental mismatches, since filtering alters executed actions and the induced state distribution. The paper studies this policy-filter interaction and proposes filter-aware fine-tuning for safe humanoid whole-body motion.

entry.title: ManiPhysicsBench: Physics-Based Assessment of Object Preservation in VLA Manipulation

author.name: Sangwu Park, Yeonjun In, Wonjoong Kim, Sungwon Kim, Sein Kim, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: ManiPhysicsBench evaluates whether VLA manipulation policies preserve objects, not just complete tasks, using a consolidated asset library (ManiPhysicsZoo) with literature-supported material properties and 3D meshes. A solver-based assessment computes grasp-specific damage thresholds from geometry, material, and recorded contact forces to assess deformation and fracture risk. It benchmarks policies on LIBERO and SimplerEnv across three physics axes and difficulty levels.

entry.title: AVL-JEPA: Preventing Causal Dynamics Information Collapse In Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture World Models

author.name: Yikang Qiao, Ling Zhang, Ziying Song, Duan Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in JEPA world models called causal dynamics information collapse, where visual information is preserved but the physical consequences of actions are discarded. It proposes action-grounded vision-invariance latent (AVL) objectives that anchor dynamics using executed actions and align perturbed and clean latent predictions without destroying dynamics information.

entry.title: When Terminal-Agent Training Stalls: Demystifying Data Generation and Verification Challenge

author.name: Xi Qin, Isabel Kurth, Xin Cui, Elin Park, Alexander Schaefer, Yaad Oren

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses failure modes in pipelines that use frontier models like Claude Opus as meta-agents to generate terminal-agent RL training tasks and verifiers, identifying benchmark invalidity, harness brittleness, and reward misalignment. It shows a 9B model saturates at 81.3% pass@2 on Opus-generated tasks, and adding genuinely hard tasks drops this to 20.6%, evidence that solvability bands are model-specific. This exposes quality issues in synthetic RL environments.

entry.title: Answering clinicians' questions over trial evidence tables with verifiable, feedback-driven language models

author.name: Manan Roy Choudhury, Suparno Roy Chowdhury, Swastik Sahoo, Muhammad Ali Khan, Kaneez Zahra Rubab Khakwani, Mohamad Bassam Sonbol, Irbaz Bin Riaz, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: FD-SCoPE is a language-model framework that lets clinicians ask questions over systematic review evidence tables, including questions about attributes not recorded in the tables, while exposing the query, selected trials, and derivation rule behind every answer. On an oncology evidence table of 159 immune checkpoint inhibitor trials, it completed all 140 clinician-style tasks with strong precision and retrieves 99.3% of relevant trial records.

entry.title: PAPER2LLM++: Continual Self-Evolution of LLMs from Research Papers

author.name: Hongji Pu, Yilun Zhao, Wenpeng Yin

entry.summary: PAPER2LLM++ is a framework for continual self-evolution of LLMs using research papers as a stream of evidence and supervision: it extracts evidence-grounded findings, tests whether reported limitations persist in the current model, and converts findings into candidate learning signals via a try-evaluate-commit procedure. This connects the literature on model failures directly to model improvement.

entry.title: Scaling Trajectories for Complex Tasks through Recursive Self-Rewrite

author.name: Zongxia Li, Yucheng Shi, Zhongzhi Li, Junyao Yang, Ruhan Wang, Chengsong Huang, Fuxiao Liu, Haitao Mi, Jordan Boyd-Graber, LeoweiLiang

entry.summary: Recursive Self-Rewrite (RSR) uses a single base model, Qwen-3.8-27B, to discover successful solutions under diverse task harnesses and reconstruct them as training trajectories under a general harness, using a planner-critic-executor loop with leakage screening. Across roughly 3K self-curated terminal tasks, three harnesses jointly solved 759 tasks, 34.3% more than the strongest individual harness.

entry.title: Predictor-Guided Latent Space Codon Optimization for Maximizing Protein Expression

author.name: Alberto Caron, Tianyu Cui, Dmytro S. Lituiev, Mangal Prakash, Artem Moskalev, Amina Mollaysa, Bo Zhai, Hirsh Nanda, Daniel M. Poole, Zhongyin Liu, Iman Farasat, Robert Davidson, Nikolay V. Manyakov, Tommaso Mansi, Scott Oloff, Rui Liao

entry.summary: LSCO recasts codon optimization - a discrete, combinatorially large problem central to therapeutic proteins and mRNA vaccines - as continuous optimization in the latent space of a pretrained mRNA language model, enabling gradient-based search. It combines a data-driven expression objective with predictor guidance rather than relying on weak heuristics like codon adaptation index. This has direct pharmaceutical relevance.

entry.title: Preserving Mathematical Reasoning in Compressed Diffusion Language Models via Trajectory-Aware Low-Rank Approximation

author.name: Tian Liang, Zishan Shao, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: This paper addresses a gap in compressing diffusion language models, where calibration on clean activations mismatches the partially masked states seen at inference. The authors formulate a trajectory-aware low-rank objective over corruption levels and masking realizations, and propose Traj-MC to efficiently estimate the trajectory second moment, showing improved preservation of mathematical reasoning after compression.

entry.title: Multilingual GSM-Symbolic: What determines capability transfer across languages?

author.name: Kenneth Enevoldsen, Riley Herchert, Sofie Mosegaard, Dan Saattrup Smart, Simon Enni, Isaac Chung, Sofie Bruun, Ayush Sunil Munot, Max M\"uller-Eberstein, Adnan El-Assadi, Elisa Bassignana, Gianluca Barmina, Hafsteinn Einarsson, Iben Nyholm Debess, Linda Freienthal, Lukas Galke Poech, Mike Zhang, Nicolas Legrand, Vladimir Salnikov, Yevhen Kostiuk, Zafar Hussain, Sagandeep Kaur, Agnes Toftg{\aa}rd, Marie Mattson, Kristoffer Nielbo

entry.summary: This paper introduces Multilingual GSM-Symbolic, an extensible benchmark of 30,000 item-matched math question-answer pairs across 15 languages built on symbolic templates to prevent overfitting. It uses the benchmark to jointly study what factors determine how capabilities learned in one language transfer to another, aiming to reduce the need for exhaustive evaluation of every language pair and to guide improvements for low-resource languages. It matters because cross-lingual transfer is poorly understood and existing evaluations are incomparable and saturation-prone.

entry.title: Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents

author.name: Yu Li, Guangfeng Cai, Long-Fei Li, Shuo Han, Shengtian Yang, Han Luo, Kaibing Yang, Lei Feng

entry.summary: The paper proposes DepGPO, which improves credit assignment for terminal-using RL agents by explicitly tracing read-write dependencies between commands rather than using trajectory-level or step-level signals. By building a command dependency structure, training signals are concentrated on operations that actually affect the final outcome in multi-step coding and debugging tasks.

entry.title: GlanceWAM: Sparse Test-Time Imagination for World-Action Models

author.name: Linhan Wang, Zijian An, Mingyuan Zhang, Chen Dai, Yi Xu, Can Cui, Jiayan Wang, Zichong Yang, Yinlin Chen, Lifeng Zhou, Chang-Tien Lu

entry.summary: GlanceWAM decouples visual imagination from robot control in world-action models by asynchronously generating a single lookahead frame seconds into the future in latent space, off the critical control path. This achieves both real-time inference and improved task success, resolving a fundamental latency-versus-success trade-off in video-based robot learning. The work is significant for scaling generative-model priors into practical real-time robotic systems.

entry.title: APDMem: Agent-Controlled Progressive Disclosure for Query-Adaptive Long-Term Memory

author.name: Chin-Lun Fu, Anagha Kulkarni, Hong Ni, Behrouz Madahian

entry.summary: This paper introduces APDMem, a hierarchical long-term memory architecture for personalized LLM assistants that organizes conversation history into four layers of increasing detail: thematic summaries, personalized key facts, turn-level evidence notes, and raw messages. An agent-controlled retrieval process applies progressive disclosure, reading coarse summaries first and drilling into fine-grained evidence only when a query demands it, yielding adaptive cost-quality tradeoffs compared to flat memory stores or fixed retrieval granularity.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Scaling of Terminal Environments for Scientific Domains

author.name: Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Junyao Yang, Ruhan Wang, Yu Wang, Jingyuan Huang, Jichao Yu, Ninghao Liu, Haitao Mi, Leowei Liang

entry.summary: The paper presents software-in-the-loop reconstruction, a self-supervised framework that automatically builds training environments for terminal agents in scientific domains by deriving reference outputs and verifiers from existing executable software workflows. Multiple input configurations are run and partitioned into public observations and hidden evaluations, avoiding manual per-task authoring of environments and verifiers. This addresses a key bottleneck in scaling RL-style agent training beyond software engineering into specialized domains.

entry.title: Prospective Hindsight: Self-Calibrating Reinforcement Learning via Prediction-Reality Gaps

author.name: Jiaxin Zhang, Xiangyu Peng, Qinglin Chen, Yu Li, Hiroaki Hayashi, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Prospective Hindsight, a self-calibrating RL training signal that weights advantage updates by the gap between the agent's pre-action prediction and post-hoc evaluation, amplifying gradient contribution on rollouts where the agent's self-model is most inaccurate. The method augments arbitrary retrospective base RL methods using a stop-gradient surprise-weighted scheme.

entry.title: When History Fails to Become Experience: Action Calibration in Language Agents

author.name: Jingyu Liu, Zhiwen Wang, Yuxin Jing, Huanyu Zhou, Yong Liu

entry.summary: This paper investigates why language agents often fail to benefit from interaction history within a task, finding that much of the apparent benefit of history persists even when past actions are shuffled, indicating agents do not reliably link actions to their outcomes. The authors introduce the notion of action calibration to explicitly test and improve how agents connect prior actions with environmental feedback.

entry.title: Beyond Predefined Sinks: Security-Aware Dependency Analysis for LLM Agents

author.name: Hang Cui

entry.summary: AgentSecGraph is a static analysis framework that builds candidate-centered security-aware dependency graphs for each security-sensitive agent operation, augmenting operation identity with agent relevance, trust-boundary context, guard evidence, and external-effect semantics rather than relying on predefined sensitive-operation anchors. It enables more accurate identification of when agent decisions reach dangerous capabilities like command execution or filesystem access.

entry.title: S2S-JEPA: Predicting the Predictable at Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Timescales

author.name: Chenyu Dong, Gianmarco Mengaldo

entry.summary: S2S-JEPA applies the JEPA principle to subseasonal-to-seasonal weather forecasting, arguing that AI weather models fail beyond two weeks because they predict unpredictable fine-scale details, and instead forecasts only slowly varying predictable components in latent space. This connects a computer-vision architectural insight to a well-known predictability gap with real societal value.

entry.title: Contextual Flow Matching: Adaptive Step Selection in Flow Models for Efficient Visual Generation

author.name: Divya Jyoti Bajpai, Arun Verma, Manjesh Kumar Hanawal

entry.summary: COFLOW is an inference-time, plug-and-play method that adaptively selects the number of function evaluation steps for flow-matching visual generation based on prompt features. It is trained online with an unsupervised reward balancing efficiency and fidelity, requiring no retraining of the underlying generative model. It generalizes to both image and video generation.

entry.title: Cephalonauts One: A deep fMRI dataset for decoding naturalistic speech in the human brain

author.name: Antoine Collas, Louis Jalouzot, G\'eraud Ilinca, Corentin Caris, Romain Valabr\`egue, Ahmed Hassayoune, David Goncalves, Madeleine Hueber, Thadd\'ee Delebarre, Julien Savatovsky, Clara Fonteneau, Charles Maussion, Bertrand Thirion, Alexis Thual

entry.summary: Cephalonauts One releases roughly 30 hours of whole-brain 3T fMRI data per subject across three subjects listening to naturalistic podcasts, with audio, transcripts, and stimulus embeddings, making it the deepest naturalistic-speech fMRI dataset available. The authors also propose an audio-retrieval decoding benchmark based on held-out sessions. This resource enables substantial progress in neural encoding and decoding research.

entry.title: Drive vs. Decay: On the Training Dynamics of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

author.name: Jos\'e Lucas De Melo Costa, Seong Woo Ahn, Fabrice Popineau, Arpad Rimmel, Bich-Li\^en Doan

entry.summary: This paper develops an early-training stability theory for JEPAs that unifies empirical anti-collapse heuristics by linearizing the coupled gradient flow around the trivial fixed point. It identifies a driving force and a decay effect whose per-mode ratio predicts which modes become unstable and hence the achievable representation rank. A predicted phase boundary is confirmed empirically across more than 800 Tabular-JEPA configurations.

entry.title: Test-time Multi-agent Coordination by Decomposed Value Gradient Flow

author.name: Dongsu Lee, Haoran Xu, Amy Zhang

entry.summary: SCOUT addresses offline multi-agent RL's tradeoff between expressive generative policies that cannot identify high-value modes and value-optimized policies that collapse multi-modal coordination. It combines a flow-matching generative foundation model with a learned value function through test-time action refinement. This avoids single-agent mode collapse and joint drift into unseen action regions during coordination.

entry.title: Muon Learns Facts Better: Understanding the Role of Spectral Orthogonalization

author.name: Xuheng Li, Qiwei Di, Yuan Cao, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: This theory paper explains why the Muon optimizer's spectral orthogonalization aids feature learning, using a tractable factual-recall model with a linear transformer trained under gradient flow, spectral GF, and Sign GF (continuous limits of GD, Muon, and Adam). It characterizes how orthogonalization changes the sample requirements and dynamics of fact learning.

entry.title: AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xin Wang, Wenhao Wu, Menghao Zhang, Zhi Wang, Kun Shao, Jian Luan

entry.summary: AdaStep addresses step-level credit assignment for long-horizon LLM agents trained with sparse outcome rewards. It formulates per-step advantage weighting as an MSE estimation problem, deriving optimal per-state shrinkage coefficients that control how strongly group-derived local advantages modify trajectory-level signals.

entry.title: Beyond Random Splits: Evaluating Drug-Target Affinity Models Under Chemically and Biologically Motivated Distribution Shifts Copy

author.name: Minjae Chung, Clara Li, Malar Paavai Muthukumaran, Shaunna Wang, Aniket Ramkrishnan Iyer, Shaun Qien Yeau Tan, Harinishree Sathu, Micky C. Nnamdi, J. Ben Tamo, Benoit Louis Marteau, May Dongmei Wang

entry.summary: This work evaluates drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction models under chemically and biologically motivated distribution shifts rather than standard random splits, asking whether the choice of evaluation split changes which architecture appears best. The authors curate 718,800 unique drug-protein pairs from ChEMBL and BindingDB and compare a fingerprint plus protein-CNN baseline against 12 controlled architectures combining four drug representations with three ESM-2-based interaction modes. Results show substantial performance degradation under scaffold and fingerprint-cluster out-of-distribution splits, with RMSE rising from roughly 0.95 to over 1.3 under harder shift conditions.

entry.title: Mastering Atari 2600 Games with Discovered Options

author.name: Erik M. Lintunen, Marlos C. Machado

entry.summary: The authors present Wayfarer, a domain-agnostic online deep RL agent that discovers options via Laplacian representation learning from high-dimensional observations. It demonstrates that temporal abstraction can deliver real gains at scale, achieving strong performance on the Atari 2600 benchmark where prior option-discovery methods were confined to simple domains or handcrafted representations. This is a notable step toward general-purpose hierarchical RL.

entry.title: Intent-Hiding Jailbreaks: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Compositional Attacks

author.name: Fengwei Tian, Ravi Tandon

entry.summary: This paper develops an information-theoretic framework for understanding compositional jailbreak attacks against LLMs, where harmful requests are hidden inside bundles of benign tasks that the model would otherwise refuse. The authors model each task with an estimated harmfulness probability, treating the average over all tasks as a prior and the average over a selected bundle as a posterior, and show that choosing auxiliary tasks so prior and posterior align (a prior-posterior matching condition) can obscure harmful intent from safety filters. This formalizes a growing class of attacks and offers a principled basis for designing detection and defense mechanisms.

entry.title: Safe Streaming Flow Planning by Aligning Sampling Dynamics with Execution Dynamics

author.name: Seunghwan Jang, Jeongyong Yang, Siddharth Ancha, SooJean Han

entry.summary: SafeStreamingFlow is a goal-conditioned flow-matching planner for robot control that aligns the generative model's sampling dynamics with the physical system's execution dynamics, enabling fast streaming replanning with safety constraints enforced during execution. This addresses a key weakness of prior safe diffusion planners, which generate full trajectories at once and suffer distribution shift and computational cost. The approach is relevant to deploying generative planners in real-time robotic settings.

entry.title: Silent Dissent: LLM Agents That Yield to the Majority Still Represent Their Original Premise

author.name: Ziang Ni, Peng Zou

entry.summary: Using two-hop factual questions and scripted unanimous peers in an Asch-conformity setup, this study reads intermediate bridge entities from models' residual streams via a J-lens while agents outwardly yield to a wrong majority. Pre-registered tests on four open-weight models suggest that conforming agents may still internally represent their original premise, distinguishing changed answers from changed beliefs.

entry.title: SecJev: Bringing Security Expertise to System One Decision Models

author.name: Zheng Chen, Fei Yu, Haohao Huang, Yang Li, Anlong Chen, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SecJev, reportedly the first family of Jev-style System One decision models specialized for security, spanning 0.8B to 9B parameters and producing typed Boolean, choice, and ordered predictions from text, telemetry, and observation histories. The work also contributes SecJev-Corpus, a benchmark unifying source-label prediction and policy evaluation across 14 tasks and eight data sources relevant to security workflows.

entry.title: SCION: Scene Composition with Instanced Neural Primitives

author.name: William Koch, Amogh Joshi, Cyrus Vachha, Cheng Zheng, Felix Heide

entry.summary: This paper introduces SCION, a hierarchical compositional scene representation for 3D vision that replaces the millions of independent Gaussians used in typical 3D Gaussian Splatting with a compact vocabulary of reusable neural primitives. By recognizing that real-world elements like bricks, leaves, and pebbles recur across scenes, the approach reduces redundant stored parameters and provides better manipulation handles for downstream editing tasks, unlike prior template-fitting methods that required manual element selection.

entry.title: CHASE-VLA: Post-Training Quantization Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models with Chunk-Aware Scale Estimation

author.name: Jin Hyun, Jung Gyu Min, Gyuhyun Jung, Youngjoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes CHASE-VLA, a chunk-aware post-training quantization method for VLA models that uses the generated action chunk, including its unexecuted future suffix, as causal context to calibrate activation scales of the diffusion action expert across denoising steps. This addresses scale mismatch that fixed calibration suffers in repeated policy invocations.

entry.title: TerrainForge: Physics-Grounded road geometry Editing for Counterfactual Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yang Chen, Yicheng Zhu, zhenning Li, Tao Li, Zilin Bian

entry.summary: TerrainForge generates counterfactual driving videos by editing road geometry and surface conditions (crests, sags, speed humps, friction changes) with a unified road model coupled to four-wheel vehicle dynamics. Road edits propagate consistently to vehicle motion, camera viewpoint, and clearance, enabling physically plausible what-if simulation for autonomous driving.

entry.title: T3lescope: Arbitrary-Resolution High-Fidelity Generative Surface Reconstruction from Images

author.name: Atsuhiro Noguchi, Tianhan Xu, Yiming Liang, Yuta Kikuchi, Masahiro Ishiyama, Shintaro Takagi, Hitoshi Murai, Eiichi Matsumoto

entry.summary: T3lescope reconstructs high-fidelity 3D scene meshes from posed multi-view images without per-scene optimization, scaling from single objects to large outdoor scenes. It uses learned 3D priors to handle sparse or glossy/transparent observations while avoiding the fixed-resolution tradeoff of prior generative methods, maintaining global geometric consistency across large extents.

entry.title: I2CD: Direct Image-to-Convex Decomposition for Simulation-Ready Collision Geometry

author.name: Qian Wang, Liam Merz Hoffmeister, Brian Scassellati, Daniel Rakita

entry.summary: Presents I2CD, which predicts a convex decomposition directly from a single RGB image by freezing pretrained Hunyuan3D-2 and training only a lightweight 38M-parameter cross-attention head whose convex-slot tokens emit parameters of K convex polytopes. This replaces slow reconstruct-then-decompose pipelines for producing simulation-ready collision geometry.

entry.title: Keep the Effect, Drop the Actor: Programmable Effect-to-Execution World-Action Models

author.name: Junyi Hu, Zhewen He, Zhenhua Li, Yi Fang

entry.summary: PEWAM is a 71.5M-parameter world-action model that compiles a single robot demonstration into an effect program capturing object keypoint trajectories and grasp points, decoupled from the specific demonstrator arm. Four generation streams with independent flow-matching times allow clamping the effect and re-sampling execution, turning inference into programming and re-solving actions closed loop from the live scene. It completes 40 of 90 held-out LIBERO-Goal episodes from one demonstration's program.

entry.title: DexJoCo-X: Benchmarking Action Representations for Multi-Hand Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Xiangwei Jiang, Yao Mu, Lixin Duan, Wen Li

entry.summary: DexJoCo-X is a benchmark and toolkit for controlled comparison of action representations in cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation, spanning seven dexterous hands, six single-arm and bimanual tasks, and 2,100 balanced demonstrations with matched scenes and success criteria. It enables isolation of representation, pretraining, and architecture effects that prior confounded studies could not separate.

entry.title: Bridging Frontier Reasoning and Robot Execution: From Autonomous Demonstration Generation to Dense Language Supervision

author.name: Bosung Kim, Alexander Trevithick, Ruiyi Wang, Prithviraj Ammanabrolu

entry.summary: This robotics paper tackles the gap between powerful but slow frontier models and the low-latency requirements of real-time robot control. It explores two complementary approaches: using a frontier model to autonomously generate corrective-rich demonstrations for training a fast local policy, and providing dense language supervision at deployment through a harness. The self-improving demonstration generation loop, where cost falls as successful examples accumulate in context, is a notable efficiency contribution.

entry.title: World Editing: Intervening on Executable Worlds at Increasing Depth

author.name: Max Ku, Nok-Kan Law, Yu-Chien Tang, Shih-Ying Yeh, Ping Nie, Andy Zheng, Tat Hei Lai, Fei-Yueh Chen, Nikko Yu, Wei-Chieh Sun, Suzy Huang, Chiao-Wei Hsu, Chih-Chuan Huang, Chak-Wing Mak, Ho Yin Sam Ng, Edisy Kin Wai Chan, Min-Hung Chen, Ho Kei Cheng

entry.summary: The paper formulates world editing as intervening on existing executable world models while preserving invariant properties, introducing intervention depth as an axis from property edits to system-level changes. It contributes IGMWorld and IGMBench, a 110-task benchmark with over 1,100 executable criteria built via industry-grade game modding in Minecraft and Terraria. This opens a new evaluation axis for interactive world models beyond generation.

entry.title: Coherence-Driven Belief Formation and Population Dynamics of Contagion in LLM Agents

author.name: Tathagata Banerjee, Nima Moghaddas

entry.summary: The authors empirically measure belief adoption in LLM agent populations, finding a sigmoid adoption kernel characteristic of complex contagion with thresholds sensitive to claim plausibility, source reliability, and agent disposition. These three factors collapse onto a single effective dimension interpretable as coherence of the incoming belief with the agent's priors, with implications for multi-agent population dynamics.

entry.title: LUMOS: Tracing Parametric Knowledge from Training Data to Behavioral Outputs in LLMs

author.name: Seoyeon Ye, Gayoung Kim, Jiyoung Hong, Sookyung Kim, Hyunsoo Cho

entry.summary: LUMOS traces knowledge along the causal chain from training-data exposure to behavior, using OLMo 2 with its fully transparent corpus to distinguish genuine generalization from memorization. It finds models internally encode rare facts with high separability (84%) yet fail to express them behaviorally (54%), quantifying a knowledge-expression gap.

entry.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Frontier Reasoning Data Synthesis

author.name: Wenlong Zhang, Zhengbo Jiao, Chenxu Zhang, Lekang Jiang, SiYuan Ma, Qituan Zhang, Guo Chen, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose task-harness co-evolution, a framework in which the data-synthesis harness itself improves recursively: converting solver failures into reusable skills online and revising skills, prompts, and workflows after each batch, while model weights and verifiers stay fixed. Across mathematics, coding, and science, the framework generates progressively harder valid tasks under bounded cost increases.

entry.title: Coco: An Agentic Copilot for the Hardware--Software Co-Design Lifecycle

author.name: Samuel Kushnir, Kavya Sreedhar, Yeshwanth Reddy Pogula, Amir Yazdanbakhsh, Narges Shahidi, Ming Liu, Varun Gohil, Ravi Iyer, Parthasarathy Ranganathan, Christina Delimitrou, Suvinay Subramanian

entry.summary: Coco is an agentic platform deployed with real TPU architects that accelerates ML-hardware co-design by managing fresh simulation-sweep evidence absent from any LLM pretraining corpus, spanning experiment setup, analysis, and decision support. It explicitly avoids hallucination-prone chat-with-your-data patterns where correctness matters most. Authorship includes Google systems leaders (Ranganathan, Delimitrou, Subramanian), indicating serious industrial deployment.

entry.title: Counterexample Generation via Per-Theorem Symbolic Verifiers: When Imitation Hurts and Reinforcement Repairs

author.name: Omar Farouk Zouak, Houssam Eddine Boukhalfa, Soumaya Lakehal, Shiv Katiyar, Samia Nefti-Meziani

entry.summary: Frames counterexample generation for false mathematical conjectures as constrained witness emission against per-theorem Python verifiers, and releases SymCE, a corpus of 4,707 false algebra and real-analysis conjectures with executable verifiers usable as RL reward. Finds an imitation trap: counterexample-only SFT collapses true-theorem recognition, while GRPO with sparse outcome rewards repairs it.

entry.title: Tailoring the Quantization Space for 1-Bit KV Cache Compression

author.name: Minsoo Cheong, Donghyun Son, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: TaSQ tackles the failure of vector quantization for KV caches at extreme 1-bit compression by tailoring the VQ target space through query-guided channel weighting, cross-head normalization, and covariance-aware channel grouping. This makes codebook capacity more effectively used so aggressive compression no longer degrades model quality as severely.

entry.title: EvoRiskBench: An Evolving Benchmark for Runtime Security Risks in Workspace Agents

author.name: Shiyi Kuang, Xuemei Luo, Kun Liu, Junhai Li, Rui Tian, Feng Shi, Bo Shen, Nianyu Li, Dehui Li, Ping Chen

entry.summary: EvoRiskBench is an evolving benchmark for runtime security risks of workspace agents, organized around an EP-Path-EF framework linking risk entry points to technical effects through agent-mediated paths, with nine entry-point and five effect categories validated in a 20-participant human study.
