The framework performs reasoning analysis and token-level inference optimization for quantized reasoning models, avoiding brittle predefined overthinking markers.

entry.title: RainAtlas: A Multi-Continental Dataset for Precipitation Downscaling

author.name: Pierre-Louis Lemaire, Luca Schmidt, Wietze Suijker, Alex Hernandez-Garcia, David Rolnick

entry.summary: RainAtlas is a large-scale, ML-ready, multi-continental dataset for precipitation downscaling designed to lower engineering barriers and improve cross-region generalization of ML models. It addresses the scarcity of high-resolution precipitation observations, particularly in under-resourced regions vulnerable to extreme rainfall.

entry.title: DynaFlow: Transparent and Flexible Intra-Device Parallelism via Programmable Operator Scheduling

author.name: Yi Pan, Yile Gu, Jinbin Luo, Yibo Wu, Ziren Wang, Hongtao Zhang, Ziyi Xu, Shengkai Lin, Baris Kasikci, Stephanie Wang

entry.summary: DynaFlow is a systems framework enabling transparent integration of intra-device parallelism into ML workloads via programmable operator scheduling, removing the need for invasive model-specific code overhauls. It overlaps operators with complementary resource usage during inference and training while remaining robust across workloads, architectures, and hardware. This addresses a major engineering barrier to adopting overlap-based utilization improvements.

entry.title: Training LLM Judges from Language Feedback via Position-Selective Self-Distillation

author.name: Ilgee Hong, Changlong Yu, Zhenghao Xu, Xin Liu, Yuwei Zhang, Qin Lu, Bing Yin, Tuo Zhao

entry.summary: The paper proposes training LLM judges from natural language feedback using position-selective self-distillation: a self-conditioned teacher provides dense, position-level supervision from preference rationales, avoiding the coarse scalar credit of outcome-supervised RL like GRPO. Selectivity ensures only trustworthy positions receive distillation, with an industry team (Amazon-affiliated authors) targeting subjective evaluation tasks.

entry.title: PrivCert: Certifying Statement Support under Differential Privacy

author.name: Tsubasa Takahashi, Takumi Hiraoka

entry.summary: PrivCert addresses the evidence gap in differentially private text generation, where released statements may be plausible but unverified, by introducing privacy-preserving certificates and emit-or-abstain decisions. Its Proposal-and-Filter instantiation separates data-independent candidate discovery from private support certification, with formal guarantees on emitted statements.

entry.title: Amortized Bayesian Inference on Multilevel Models of Arbitrary Structure

author.name: Daniel Habermann, Andreas Bulling, Stefan T. Radev, Paul-Christian B\"urkner

entry.summary: The paper presents a general method for amortized Bayesian inference on arbitrarily structured multilevel models: given a generative model as a DAG, the method automatically derives valid posterior factorizations and matching neural network architectures via graph expansion and inversion. Unlike prior work, it preserves all conditional independence and exchangeability assumptions while amortizing over group and observation counts. This extends simulation-based inference to a much broader model class.

entry.title: Reliable but Design-Sensitive: Instrument Uncertainty in LLM Annotation

author.name: Thomas Reiter, Christoph Kern, Fedor Miasnikov, Sofiia Nikolenko, Rob Chew, Stephanie Eckman, Frauke Kreuter

entry.summary: Testing seven LLMs across 12 task designs and 3,000 tweets for offensive language and hate speech, this study finds high repeatability within a fixed design (median Fleiss' kappa 0.91) but large label shifts and prevalence variance inflation (up to 110x sampling variance) when task designs change. LLM annotation reliability is therefore heavily design-sensitive.

entry.title: Distilling What Matters: Confidence-Aware Selective Distillation for Large Language Models

author.name: Ayan Sengupta, Vaibhav Seth, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: CaRE-KD is a confidence-gated distillation framework that adapts to unreliable teacher signals in LLMs by switching between forward and reverse KL divergence at the token level based on teacher-student confidence, plus a batch-level epistemic rejection mechanism. This counters the assumption that teachers are reliable oracles and preserves well-calibrated student behavior.

entry.title: From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuhao Wang, Ruiyang Ren, Yinan Zhang, Ruiqing Zhang, Jing Liu, Chunyan Miao

entry.summary: Controlled study of on-policy distillation showing that rollout quality alone is an incomplete criterion for allocating teacher guidance, since deeper intervention yields diminishing accuracy gains while increasing off-policy load. Proposes MAESTRO, which uses local policy disagreement between teacher and student to adaptively schedule when and how strongly the teacher intervenes.

entry.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention

author.name: Cutter Dawes, Nick Alonso, Tom Figliolia, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: The paper explains how hybrid transformer models that interleave local mixing layers (sliding window attention, gated linear attention) with global attention lacking explicit position encodings (NoPE) can implicitly encode relative position. The authors develop a mechanistic account of how local mixing injects positional information usable by global NoPE layers, explaining the success of such architectures at scale. This addresses a poorly understood but practically important architectural pattern.

entry.title: Fractional State Space Transition for Long Sequence Modeling

author.name: Ivan Kobyzev, Abbas Ghaddar, Ali Nasiri-Sarvi, Lifeng Shang, Yufei Cui

entry.summary: FRAC is a selective state space model architecture derived from fractional dynamics that replaces the exponential forgetting of ODE-based SSMs with power-law long memory, approximating the heavy-tailed kernel with a finite log-spaced sum of exponential modes. This yields an efficient recurrent module with parallel training and prefill while retaining long-range information. The work addresses a core architectural choice for long-context modeling, where memory decay laws directly determine how much history models retain.

entry.title: $S^3$: Spectral Null-Space Swap Makes Reasoning Models Efficient

author.name: Hongbo Ma, Sansheng Cao, Jiajun Fan, Bangji Yang, Ge Liu

entry.summary: The paper finds that a reasoning model's thinking capacity resides in weight components within the null space of the corresponding non-thinking model's dominant singular directions, and proposes S3, a training-free swap that exploits this to reduce excessive chain-of-thought token cost without losing post-training accuracy gains. This is claimed as the first use of the null space for reasoning-model optimization. It offers a cheap way to make thinking models more efficient.

entry.title: Mitigating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models via False Discovery Controlled Visual Data Splitting

author.name: Chang Liu, Yu Tian, Rui Xie

entry.summary: Proposes CORAL, a training-free framework that mitigates multiple object hallucination in large vision-language models by modeling visual uncertainty via uncertainty-aware data splitting and mirror statistics computed from symmetrically perturbed visual inputs. This provides principled false-discovery-rate control over spurious object predictions during decoding, unlike heuristic contrastive methods.

entry.title: When Can Text Replace Vision? Structural Bottlenecks in Diagram Reasoning

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Janet Wang, Jihun Hamm, Chandan K Reddy

entry.summary: This paper introduces a diagnostic protocol to determine whether VLM failures on diagram reasoning after textualization stem from information omission in the text representation or solver failure to use present information. Using matched solver settings across image, question-blind structure, and gold-structure conditions, it applies validity-triggered recovery, question-relevant fidelity, and matched edge intervention tests.

entry.title: MCD: Causal Distillation of Multimodal In-Context Learning in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yanshu Li, Jiaqian Li, Canran Xiao, Xi Xiao, Tianyang Wang, Yongtai Liu

entry.summary: MCD transfers multimodal in-context learning ability from large to small LVLMs by distilling which evidence in context causally supports the teacher's prediction, rather than only matching outputs or hidden states. This prevents students from imitating answers while relying on spurious cues like language priors or prompt structure.

entry.title: Looking Back to Move Forward: Temporal Verification for Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Haoxuan Wang, Wayne Wu, Yan Yan, Bolei Zhou

entry.summary: This paper proposes temporal verification as a test-time scaling strategy for generative robot policies: instead of myopically scoring candidate action chunks from the current observation alone, a verifier accounts for trajectory continuity and history when selecting among sampled candidates. This mitigates error compounding in heterogeneous demonstrations that drives robots into hard-to-recover out-of-distribution states.

entry.title: Concurrent Semantic Search and Mission Execution for LTL Missions in Unknown Environments

author.name: Fernando Salanova Gaspar, David Morilla Cabello, Cristian Mahulea Poleuca, Eduardo Montijano Mu\~noz

entry.summary: The authors present an adaptive high-level planning method that interleaves task-driven semantic search with execution of Linear Temporal Logic missions in unknown environments, rather than separating exploration from mission execution. It builds a metric-semantic scene graph online using a Vision-Language Model, advancing both search and mission non-myopically. This matters because it bridges formal mission planning with open-world semantic perception.

entry.title: Beyond Policy Alignment: Closing the Planning-Learning Loop for Robot Control with Learned World Models

author.name: Kowndinya Boyalakuntla, Yuhan Liu, Abdeslam Boularias

entry.summary: PL-MPC extends TD-MPC-style model-based control by modifying both critic supervision and planner terminal-value estimation, using hybrid multi-step TD targets and disagreement-aware components to close the feedback loop between planning and learning rather than only aligning the policy with planner behavior. This treats planning and learning as mutually dependent processes in high-dimensional control. The work offers a principled advance over recent policy-constrained world-model variants.

entry.title: AI Agents are Vulnerable to Radicalization

author.name: Ozgur Can Seckin, Shalmoli Ghosh, Alessandro Flammini, Kristina Lerman, Maria Elizabeth Grabe, Filippo Menczer

entry.summary: This study simulates conversations between an influencer LLM and a target LLM role-playing a human persona, testing whether agents can radicalize other agents. It distinguishes resonance (reinforcing existing beliefs) from persuasion (shifting attention to previously unimportant beliefs) and finds both radicalize targets, with resonance producing consistently stronger effects across affective and behavioral metrics.

entry.title: ArgGYM: A Procedural, Engine-Verified Benchmark for Structured Defeasible Reasoning

author.name: \.Ibrahim Ethem Deveci, Funda Tan \c{C}al{\i}k, Bar{\i}\c{s} Deniz Sa\u{g}lam, Duygu Ataman

entry.summary: ArgGYM is a benchmark and RL environment with engine-verified rewards for defeasible reasoning, where conclusions can be provisionally supported, defeated, reinstated, or revised. It extends the verifiable-reward paradigm, successful in math and code, to argumentation under incomplete and revisable information.

entry.title: Code to Control: Synthesizing Parameterized Reactive Controllers

author.name: Zergham Ahmed, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Chris Bates, Samuel J. Gershman

entry.summary: Code to Control has an LLM synthesize the structure of a Python controller while derivative-free search fits its parameters, producing policies that execute without LLM inference or planning at decision time. This enables real-time gameplay with faster action selection than a PPO policy under their timing protocol. It offers a compelling middle ground between LLM action selection and amortized world-model planning.

entry.title: Whose Voice Survives the Summary? A Voice-Retention Audit of LLM Employee Listening

author.name: Thilo Tamme, Anton Hantel, Bijan Khosrawi-Rad

entry.summary: This audit introduces a Voice Retention / Representation Ratio metric for representational bias in LLM summarization of employee feedback, applied to 2,586 bilingual free-text responses and 45 leader-summaries from a global professional service firm. It finds summaries filter by popularity not sentiment: single-voiced concerns are dropped 86% of the time, and short and German-only content is disproportionately lost. This reveals a systematic silencing layer in AI-mediated organizational communication.

entry.title: Routing Probes Can Improve Without New Information: An Exact-Null Audit of Uncertainty Beyond Model Outputs

author.name: Wenhao Liang, Lin Yue, Wei Emma Zhang, Mingyu Guo, Olaf Maennel, Weitong Chen

entry.summary: The authors audit claims that routing signals in vision transformers (expert gates, attention weights, halting scores) carry error information beyond model outputs, using an exact label null where correctness labels are redrawn from a frozen output-only generator. Under this null, MLP comparisons still report routing gains in 51.3% of confidence-only evaluations while linear comparisons do not, implicating estimation artifacts.

entry.title: Effective Does Not Mean Useful: Conditional Functional Substitutability for Redundancy and Scaling in Transformers

author.name: Jiaheng Chen, Jiaxing Li, Yucheng Xiao, Xinyong Cai, Juncheng Bu, Lan Yu, Tinghe Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Conditional Functional Substitutability (CFS), a direct measure of functional redundancy defined by whether intermediate states induce similar downstream responses, replacing indirect importance- and similarity-based proxies. Across modalities and Transformer families, CFS reveals systematic functional reorganization with scale, with implications for model reduction.

entry.title: Autoresearch in Mixed-Integer Linear and Nonlinear Programming

author.name: Yuwei Gu, Yaoxin Wu, Tong Guo, Wen Song, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: AutoMIP is an agent skill for long-horizon autonomous research on NP-hard mixed-integer programming problems, using idea pooling and algorithm tree search to manage competing hypotheses and experimental trajectories. It enables agents to preserve unexplored ideas, refine promising algorithms, and backtrack to alternative methodological directions.

entry.title: ChronoGraph: Functional 4D Scene Graphs with Vision-Language Models for Interaction Understanding and Grounded Planning

author.name: Chenyangguang Zhang, Malgorzata Gwiazda, Guanlong Jiao, Yuanchen Ju, Federico Tombari, Koushil Sreenath, Marc Pollefeys, Sunghwan Hong

entry.summary: ChronoGraph introduces functional 4D scene graphs that link actions on affordance parts to semantic and geometric state changes, unifying the representation of observed and anticipated transitions. This shared representation supports both explaining how past actions changed a scene and planning future grounded actions, with an accompanying benchmark (ChronoGraphBench) built via an automatic data engine from human-interaction videos. The author list includes established researchers such as Marc Pollefeys.

entry.title: Who Verifies the Graph? Misspecification Attacks on Causal Action Verification for Language Agents

author.name: Fabio Rovai

entry.summary: The paper red-teams CIVeX, a causal action verifier that gates agent tool calls against a committed action-state graph, by corrupting only the committed graph. Omitting a single bidirected edge raises false executions from zero to 15.3% (91% harmful), and reversing one arrowhead yields 48.9% false executions, showing that certificates are only as trustworthy as the committed causal model.

entry.title: ContextAdapt: Evaluating Contextual Adaptation and Value Alignment in LLMs

author.name: Olivia Macmillan-Scott, Mirco Musolesi

entry.summary: ContextAdapt is an evaluation framework testing whether LLMs appropriately adapt the application of values such as honesty, autonomy, and confidentiality across professional domains (medicine, law, finance, national security), while staying consistent when context changes are normatively irrelevant. It is grounded in primary-source professional and regulatory documents. The work probes a subtle dimension of alignment beyond blanket value adherence.

entry.title: Aegis: Generative Gradient Masking for Privacy-Preserving Medical Federated Learning

author.name: Chaoyu Zhang, Shanghao Shi, Heng Jin, Ning Wang, Y. Thomas Hou, Wenjing Lou

entry.summary: Aegis defends medical federated learning against model inversion attacks that reconstruct patient images from shared gradient updates, addressing attacks that defeat secure aggregation at realistic batch sizes. Instead of accuracy-degrading perturbation or heavy cryptography, it uses generative gradient masking to sanitize updates while preserving diagnostic performance.

entry.title: Which Tasks Survive Self-Supervised Learning?

author.name: Achleshwar Luthra, Lucas Bryant, Tracy Zhu, Tomer Galanti

entry.summary: The paper studies which downstream tasks remain recoverable from same-instance self-supervised representations via the notion of semantic recoverability, showing that for centered and whitened representations it exactly determines the directional class-distance-normalized variance and controls few-shot nearest-centroid classification. This gives a theoretical account of what information SSL preserves and destroys.

entry.title: PANDA: A Decentralized Architecture with Flexible Orchestration for Scalable, Fault-Tolerant Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Matthew D. Laws, Cristina Nita-Rotaru

entry.summary: PANDA is a decentralized architecture for LLM-based multi-agent systems in which large collectives of heterogeneous, independently administered agents discover each other's capabilities and self-organize into specialized teams per task. It scales by decoupling collective from team communication, supporting concurrent tasks, fault tolerance, and multi-team participation.

entry.title: TERRA: Terrain-Aware Reconstruction, Retargeting and Control for Musculoskeletal Locomotion

author.name: Merkourios Simos, Chengkun Li, Bianca Ziliotto, Alexander Mathis

entry.summary: Presents TERRA, an end-to-end pipeline that extends muscle-actuated reinforcement learning locomotion from flat ground to terrain by reconstructing task-relevant support geometry from kinematic trajectories using terrain priors, contact estimation, and negative free-space evidence. It enforces anatomical and tendon-continuity constraints during retargeting to enable terrain-aware musculoskeletal control.

entry.title: Adaptive-GEPA: Make Your Harness Fit Heterogeneous Requests

author.name: Tianyu Chen, Yasi Zhang, Ruiyi Wang, Xinran Zhao, Taoran Li, Mingyuan Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Adaptive-GEPA, an extension of reflective prompt optimizers like GEPA that learns both how to divide heterogeneous incoming requests and how to solve each family, evolving a router plus a library of specialist programs under one search budget. This avoids the trade-off between optimizing one shared program implicitly and pre-fixing request partitions.

entry.title: SkillSeek: Revisiting Agent Skill Retrieval at Marketplace Scale

author.name: Guanqun Yang, Wenlong Zhang, Tian Shi, Ping Wang

entry.summary: SkillSeek is an open-source two-stage skill retriever (BGE-base bi-encoder plus a small cross-encoder exposed over MCP) for Anthropic-style Agent Skills repositories that have grown past 230,000 skills. It achieves parity with LLM-mediated retrieval loops on the 89-task SkillsBench benchmark while avoiding per-task LLM token costs.

entry.title: Unmerge: Efficient Machine Unlearning via Task Arithmetic

author.name: Haoran Tang, Andrew Tan, Rajiv Khanna

entry.summary: The paper recasts machine unlearning as the inverse of task arithmetic: given a merged task vector combining forget and retain learning, unlearning subtracts a learned forget component to recover the retain vector. The authors observe the forget signal is concentrated in low-rank subspaces spanned by dominant directions, enabling efficient unlearning without data-dependent hyperparameter search.

entry.title: Make Code as Policy Great Again: Frontier Agents Write, Call, and Evolve Robot Tools

author.name: Shijia Ge, Alex Zhou, Jianshu Zeng, Yexing Wan, Di Wu, Zelin Zheng, Yazhe Wang, Zhiqi Jia, Xuan Shangguan, Jay Zhu, Yijun Liu, Lingyu He, Sihang Wu, Xiao He, Hongcheng Gao

entry.summary: The paper introduces URAI (Universal Robot-Agent Interface), which pairs a programming agent that writes and refines reusable robot tools with an execution agent that selects and parameterizes those tools from observations, so code handles multi-phase motions while the model handles decisions. This division of labor reduces token cost and latency versus step-by-step reasoning through every motion.

entry.title: Association profile conditioning in a set-temporal transformer for cross-session intracortical motor decoding

author.name: Xinyuan Zhang, Handong Mo, Pengfei Wen, Shuang Liang, Jichang Yang, Yan Zeng, Zhongrui Wang, Han Wang

entry.summary: APST is a set-temporal transformer for intracortical motor decoding that adapts to new sessions with all network weights frozen, by summarizing each unit's firing-behavior relationship in a closed-form four-dimensional association profile from a few calibration trials. These profiles condition a set-attention encoder that accepts arbitrary numbers and orderings of units, followed by a causal transformer for streaming decoding. It addresses the critical day-to-day stability problem for brain-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Blackout vs. Freeze: Analyzing Physical Failure Modes of VLAs under Camera Faults

author.name: Heejae Suh, Jongwook Han, Zahra Gholami, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: This work analyzes how vision-language-action models pi0.5 and GR00T behave under camera faults, finding that blackouts and freezing produce distinct physical failure modes even at similar low success rates, with freezing causing extreme joint behavior and blackouts causing object drops. It shows proprioception partially compensates for lost visual input but cannot restore success when wrist-view objects are missing, with direct implications for VLA safety.

entry.title: From Imitation to Reward Discovery: On-Policy Warmup for Agentic RL

author.name: Yitong Qiao, Tiantian He, Lei Liu, Yue Shen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Zhixuan Chu

entry.summary: The paper identifies an On-Policy Acceleration Phenomenon: initializing RLVR with on-policy distillation lets language-model agents reach high performance earlier and achieve both higher average and final performance. It proposes On-Policy Warmup, where a student trains with teacher supervision on its own interaction trajectories before transitioning to RLVR.

entry.title: Steering Fields: Adaptive Vector Fields for Safe Image Generation and Beyond

author.name: Simone Facchiano, Jan Eric Lenssen, Bernt Schiele, Wolfgang Stammer, Fabio Galasso, Jonas Fischer

entry.summary: Steering Fields generalize activation steering vectors for text-to-image flow models by adaptively re-estimating the steering direction at each step of generation on noisy states, with a continuous trajectory-level formulation. This avoids the unintended global changes caused by fixed, example-agnostic vectors, enabling suppression of harmful content while promoting benign alternatives.

entry.title: Free Everywhere, Exact on Trees: PPO's Dropped Correction Buys Sample Efficiency Under Aggressive Reuse

author.name: Nima H. Siboni

entry.summary: The paper shows that under history-injective dynamics, the state-visitation correction dropped in TRPO, PPO, and GRPO can be restored exactly from per-step log-probabilities PPO already computes. This enables aggressive off-policy batch reuse with sample-efficiency gains at no extra cost, and is exact on tree-structured (history-injective) environments.

entry.title: Synthetic Pre-pretraining Survives Scale, but Not as a Grammatical Prior

author.name: Atsuki Yamaguchi, Tatsuro Inaba, Joel Niklaus, Michal \v{S}tef\'anik, Aline Villavicencio, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: This comprehensive study tests synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) at up to 7B parameters and 100B-token pre-training budgets across five tasks and four data mixtures. It confirms PPT's token-efficiency benefits survive scale but overturns the grammatical-prior explanation, showing the mechanism is not a transferable structural inductive bias about natural language grammar.

entry.title: Do Better Goal Representations Improve Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning?

author.name: Syed Nazmus Sakib, Abdul Monaf Chowdhury, Nafiul Haque, Shifat E Arman, Md Mehedi Hasan

entry.summary: This paper examines offline goal-conditioned RL by constructing an exact temporal-distance goal representation in deterministic mazes and systematically degrading its geometric quality while holding the downstream learner fixed. Surprisingly, large changes in goal representation quality barely affect performance, while analogous interventions on the agent's current state representation more than double success, suggesting prior work conflates state and goal representation effects.

entry.title: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Pranjal Aggarwal, Lawrence Keunho Jang, Sean Welleck, Daniel Fried, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Jing Yu Koh

entry.summary: cua-speedrun provides a standardized, reproducible benchmark for measuring the execution speed and cost of computer-use agents, whose evaluation is currently confounded by heterogeneous infrastructure. With CUAs surpassing human accuracy on many benchmarks, the paper argues speed and cost are the key adoption barriers. Strong academic author list including Salakhutdinov, Fried, and Welleck.

entry.title: Linguistic Loopholes in LLM Unlearning: From a 174-Language Benchmark to Coverage-Aware Unlearning

author.name: Tyler Skow, Shravan Chaudhari, Rama Chellappa, Abhay Yadav

entry.summary: The paper shows that unlearning a fact in one language does not remove it in others, introducing language-budgeted multilingual unlearning: selecting a subset of languages to maximize cross-lingual erasure without damaging unrelated capabilities. It contributes the Cross-Lingual Unlearning Tensor benchmark spanning 174 language-script pairs and 25 paraphrase types. Relevant to safety and privacy of deployed multilingual models.

entry.title: Learning-Enabled Estimation: Tight Characterizations under Sample Selection Biases

author.name: Vikram Kher, Jane H. Lee, Anay Mehrotra, Manolis Zampetakis

entry.summary: The paper studies regression when outcomes are observed only after selection filters depending on both covariates and outcomes, spanning clinical dropout, labor-market self-selection, and strategic auction entry. Building on Heckman's tradition, it appears to provide the first complete characterization of when such regression is learnable, moving beyond scattered sufficient conditions.

entry.title: QATFactory: A Versatile, Deployment-Aligned Framework for Quantization-aware Training and Distillation of LLMs

author.name: Weili Xu, Jisen Li, Yuqing Jian, Chenxi Li, Zhizhou Sha, Yifan Yu, Qingyang Wu, Chenfeng Xu, Zhongzhu Zhou, Tianyi Zhang, Ben Athiwaratkun

entry.summary: QATFactory is an open-source framework for quantization-aware distillation and RL that simulates deployment-time quantization (NVFP4, MXFP4, Q4_K) while computing matmuls in BF16, enabling FP4 training on hardware lacking FP4 tensor cores. It supports dense and MoE LLMs, aligning training with real inference formats.

entry.title: When, Not How Much: Evaluating Time-Series Foundation Models on Sparse Events

author.name: Daniel Schoess, Florian von Wangenheim

entry.summary: This evaluation study assesses time-series foundation models on predicting which future periods contain activity rather than point values, across five sparse datasets and 12 TSFMs. It finds released TSFM forecasts barely improve on training-free references in chance-corrected average precision, and that simple linear probes on frozen backbones beat their own point forecasts in 29 of 30 pairs.

entry.title: Self-Repulsive Sampling for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Michael Helcig, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: Self-Repulsion is a training-free sampler for masked diffusion language models that diversifies parallel sampled paths by penalizing tokens already committed by peers during denoising steps. Paths share a batched forward pass and commit sequentially, improving answer diversity without extra forward/backward passes or added compute.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Prefix-Invariant Realizations of Low-Precision Fast Matrix Multiplication

author.name: Shuxiao Xie, Shuyang Xie, Yuan Cao, Dezhi Ran, Wei Yang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: This work shows that fast FP8 matrix multiplication realizations can break prefix invariance in language models, changing multiple-choice likelihood answers on OpenBookQA even when accuracy looks normal. On Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, two repaired fast kernels altered chosen answers on 5.83% and 10.00% of items while bf16 and deployed FP8 baselines changed none.

entry.title: Replay on Demand: An Emergent Curriculum for Balancing Adaptation and Forgetting in Continued Pretraining

author.name: Lukas Thede, Shengzhuang Chen, Stefan Winzeck, Matthias Bethge, Zeynep Akata, Jonathan Richard Schwarz

entry.summary: Replay on Demand derives replay allocation from model learning dynamics, prioritizing adaptation samples by remaining learning potential and replay samples by observed forgetting, letting competition for a shared budget yield an online curriculum. Across scales and domains it matches or improves the adaptation-forgetting trade-off versus fixed replay mixtures.

entry.title: From Spectra to Joint Schedules in LLM Pre-training: 3+3(+2) Scaling-Law Regimes

author.name: Yichen Wang, Fanghui Liu, Yudong Chen

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes how learning-rate and batch-size schedules alter observed power-law learning curves in noisy online SGD with linear random features, using an exact Volterra equation separating forcing and memory components. It proves power-law behavior is tied to cumulative weighted spectral mass rather than coordinatewise power laws, and characterizes regimes under joint schedules via intrinsic time. The results inform the design of scaling-law-aware pre-training schedules for LLMs.

entry.title: MedKIT: Evaluating Knowledge Integration and Generalization in Large Language Models

author.name: Lukas Thede, Yash Kumar Atri, David Chen, Danielle Bitterman, Matthias Bethge, Tom Hartvigsen, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: MedKIT is a benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can actually use newly integrated medical knowledge under realistic sequences of clinical updates, probing transfer across lexical variation, relational transformations, compositional reasoning, and more. It goes beyond factual recall, addressing safety risks from outdated clinical knowledge in medicine.

entry.title: Optimal VC Dimension of Contrastive Learning with Margin

author.name: Dionysis Arvanitakis, Vaggos Chatziafratis, Yiyuan Luo, Konstantin Makarychev

entry.summary: This theoretical work resolves an open question from Alon et al. by establishing the optimal VC dimension for PAC-learning d-dimensional Euclidean representations from margin-based anchor-positive-negative triplets. The result tightens the sample-complexity understanding of why contrastive learning generalizes well beyond pessimistic PAC predictions.

entry.title: Steepest Guidance: A Practical and Principled Approach to Inference-Time Alignment of Flow and Diffusion-based Models

author.name: Shokichi Takakura, Akifumi Wachi, Rei Higuchi, Kohei Miyaguchi, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: The paper reframes inference-time alignment of flow and diffusion models as a sequential optimization problem over probability measures, proposing Steepest Guidance, which maximizes local improvement in the objective rather than estimating Doob h-transform guidance. The method comes with theoretical analysis and strong empirical performance.

entry.title: Security Properties of Neural Networks as Decision Problems

author.name: Adrian Wurm

entry.summary: The paper formalizes eight security-relevant decision problems for deployed neural networks, including backdoor presence, unsafe parameter faults, and privacy leakage of inputs, and classifies their complexity. The key observation is that a piecewise-linear network's computation is definable by a quantifier-free formula of real addition, placing network properties in the polynomial hierarchy via Sontag's theorem. This provides the first complexity-theoretic classification for several neural network security questions.

entry.title: SEAR: Spoofing Evidence-Grounded Audio Reasoning Benchmark for Audio Language Models

author.name: Rong Wan, Suliu Qin, Jiaxi Li, Wei Xie, Wenwu Wang, Xiaolong Han, Lu Yin, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: SEAR is a four-task benchmark evaluating whether audio language models used for deepfake detection can actually identify and quantify acoustic evidence rather than just produce plausible-sounding rationales. The authors also propose BAEA, an agent that equips a frozen ALM with controlled acoustic forensic tools under fixed or adaptive evidence-acquisition policies. Experiments across six ALMs reveal a gap between plausible rationales and verified acoustic grounding.

entry.title: Lookahead-R: Budget-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution-Centric Planning

author.name: Zongze Wu, Yani Guo, Runnan Li

entry.summary: Lookahead-R reformulates tool retrieval for LLM agents as resource-constrained sequential decision-making, using a lightweight surrogate world model that predicts execution success, latency, and semantic utility without real API calls. A cost-sensitive, uncertainty-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search then selects tools, bridging the speed-precision trade-off between semantic and execution-based retrieval.

entry.title: Causal and Interpretable Structures in LLM Compositional Tasks

author.name: Gurbir Arora, Toni J. B. Liu, Jiajun Bao, Rapha\"el Sarfati, Christopher J. Earls

entry.summary: Studying activations on cyclic-concept tasks (months, hours, weekdays, musical notes) across Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral, the paper finds a consistent layerwise progression in how joint dependence among tokens is geometrically organized and causally used, moving from pairwise-inferred relations toward joint representations. It combines geometric and causal interpretability analysis.

entry.title: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety

author.name: Jianxing Chen, Xiao Yu, Shipra Agrawal, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: SCOUT is a two-stage agentic safety verifier for computer-use agents that performs task-specific reasoning and actively investigates environment state rather than relying solely on screenshots, since screenshots may not reveal what actually changed. This addresses the challenge of detecting subtle harms from agents operating computers even under benign instructions. The approach is notable for combining LLM-as-judge verification with active tool use.

entry.title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind: Systematically Erasing LLM's Memories

author.name: Olga Ohrimenko

entry.summary: The paper studies whether persistent LLMs with external memory stores can actually delete user-requested information, finding that current LLMs fail to forget even when they claim to have done so and even with limited context. Naive message removal is insufficient, motivating a new research direction the authors call Deletion of LLM Memories. This has direct privacy and compliance implications as memory-enabled assistants proliferate.

entry.title: Grounded Revision vs. Prior Injection: Probing Retrieval-Augmented Patent Claim Amendment

author.name: Josepha Michiko Leo, Hyun-seok Min, Yehoon Jang, Irvan Zidny, Jin-Woo Chung, Sungchul Choi

entry.summary: Using patent claim amendment as a testbed where correctness is definable, the authors release a corpus of 7,385 USPTO prosecution cases, a seven-probe battery comparing retrieval policies, and a deterministic five-channel metric that avoids LLM-based judging. Across 9,600 pre-registered evaluation calls, they probe whether retrieval genuinely grounds document revision or merely injects templated prior knowledge.

entry.title: Can Language Models Learn to Forecast Stock Prices

author.name: Jiacheng Guo, Suozhi Huang, Shuzhen Li, Yunlong Gao, Zerui Cheng, Jason Ge, Shushu Liang, Zihao Li, Hao Lu, Ming Yin, Shilong Liu, Jiashuo Liu, Xu Kuang, Mengdi Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies whether post-training on verifiable outcomes, successful in math and code, can improve financial forecasting, using a chronological stock-price sandbox where models gather price, volume, and market context before committing to numerical predictions. It highlights the added challenges of noisy realized returns and the model needing to decide its own information-gathering strategy.

entry.title: CypherTurn: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Conversational Text-to-Cypher Evaluation and the Autonomy Divergence

author.name: Yuzhe Zhang, Weijie Zhu, Haolin Yang, Ziyun Zhang, Xianwei Xue, Mengke Chen, Qiutong Pan, Huaqian Cai

entry.summary: CypherTurn is the first benchmark for multi-turn conversational Text-to-Cypher evaluation, with 721 sessions, 5,927 turns, 7 knowledge graphs, and 13 conversational phenomena, evaluated under both guided and autonomous agentic protocols. Results show the best model reaches only 64.7% execution accuracy with session-level correctness below 5%, and frontier model rankings reorder under autonomy.

entry.title: Relevance Is Not Sufficient Evidence: Detecting Evidence Gaps Before Generation in RAG

author.name: Suting Chen, Peichun Hua, Yunming Xiao

entry.summary: This paper shows that RAG generators answer 40.0-99.3% of insufficient-evidence questions even when instructed to abstain, and argues sufficiency should be judged from question and evidence alone before generation. It identifies label-leakage pitfalls in constructing insufficient-evidence test sets, such as lexical overlap and evidence-position cues.

entry.title: Learning What to Remember: Long-horizon Counterfactual Memory Optimization

author.name: Jiaming Tang, Mingyan Liu, Armin Sarabi

entry.summary: The paper introduces Memory Gain Policy Optimization (MGPO), a method that treats deciding what a language model should persistently remember as a credit-assignment problem. MGPO credits each memory rewrite only for its marginal contribution to current and future downstream utility, converting delayed memory usefulness into a direct learning signal. Demonstrated on document-level information extraction, it addresses a core challenge for long-horizon agents with persistent memory.

entry.title: What Makes Recurrence Effective in Looped Language Models?

author.name: Xinlin Zhuang, Siyuan Wang, Imran Razzak, Weiyang Liu

entry.summary: Through controlled experiments across knowledge and reasoning tasks and inference budgets below, within, and beyond the training horizon, this paper systematically examines when recurrence helps in looped language models, where it should be applied, and how conditioning affects performance. Key findings include that recurrence can improve reasoning beyond the training horizon while degrading knowledge performance, and that harder reasoning instances are not consistently better served. It provides practical guidance for parameter-sharing architectures that scale inference compute without parameters.

entry.title: SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Zhenrui Yue, Huimin Zeng, Yueqi Wang, Yaokun Liu, Fengran Mo, Jinghan Zhang, Mung Yao Jia, Gyuseok Lee, Yang Zhang, Na Wei, Dong Wang

entry.summary: SIPO combines RL with verifiable rewards and on-policy self-distillation by introducing a contrastive self-teacher that provides dense token-level credit, addressing the sparse-reward credit assignment problem in RLVR and the overconfidence and long-trajectory penalties that make prior OPSD unstable. At each iteration it samples multiple rollouts per prompt and constructs privileged-context teacher signals. This unifies two active paradigms for improving LLM reasoning and should be practically useful for post-training.

entry.title: On-Policy Visual Evidence Distillation

author.name: Shaohang Wei, Feifan Song, Guangyue Peng, Wenhao Yu, Wei Li, Wen Luo, Yang Xu, Yufan Shen, Luke Mao, Yang Du, Asher Qin, Houfeng Wang

entry.summary: The paper extends on-policy distillation to visual agents that interleave reasoning with image operations, noting that errors in acquiring, reading, or grounding visual evidence propagate through interaction trajectories. The method explicitly models the connection between student actions, resulting observations, and subsequent reasoning so the teacher can provide trajectory-aware corrections. This addresses a gap where prior multimodal OPD methods only augment supervision with auxiliary image views.

entry.title: VACE: Validation-Gated Alternating Co-Evolution of Agent Models and Harnesses

author.name: Jiexing Qi, Yu He, Jun Liu, Qichen Huang, Shaohua Hu, Zhan Dang, Guohua Chen, Rui Yang, Wen Jiang, Yang Liu, Tao Lyu, Fangming Li

entry.summary: VACE alternates agentic reinforcement learning on model weights with trajectory-driven harness refinement, gating each candidate harness revision on validation improvement with the updated model held fixed. Because weight updates and harness changes are coupled, this alternating scheme manages their interaction explicitly. Using Qwen3.5-9B, VACE reports strong results such as 45.26% test accuracy on OfficeQA, evidencing gains from co-evolving scaffolds with weights.

entry.title: When Models Don't Manipulate Manifolds: The Geometry of a Comparison Task

author.name: Sai Sumedh R. Hindupur, Hadas Orgad, Thomas Fel, Demba Ba

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability paper precisely characterizes the geometry of computation in a number-comparison task, testing whether low-dimensional representation manifolds (like helices for numbers) are actually used by models during computation. It finds models do not necessarily manipulate these manifolds, challenging a common premise that representation geometry explains how computations are performed. This is a useful corrective for interpretability research methodology.

entry.title: VidHarness: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Cost-Efficient Long Video Understanding

author.name: Susan Liang, Jianmin Wu, Daxiang Dong

entry.summary: VidHarness automates the design of agent harness programs wrapped around frozen VLMs for cost-efficient hour-long video understanding, where processing every frame is prohibitively expensive. A harness proposer iteratively evolves harnesses via Monte Carlo tree search using execution feedback, avoiding local optima of greedy refinement. This replaces slow expert-driven build-and-test cycles for selective video observation.

entry.title: EPIC: Epipolar-Consistent 360{\deg} Immersive Stereo Video Generation

author.name: Debabrata Mandal, Dongdong Fu, Jonathon Miller, William Villareal, Xi Peng, Praneeth Chakravarthula

entry.summary: EPIC is a zero-shot generative pipeline extending existing video diffusion models to produce 4K stereoscopic 360-degree videos suitable for immersive headsets, enforcing epipolar consistency across views. It notes that temporal and stereo inconsistencies tolerable on flat displays become disruptive in headsets, and addresses the impracticality of manually authoring immersive content. The approach leverages epipolar geometry constraints to keep stereo pairs coherent.

entry.title: Matisse: Evidence-Space Reasoning for Active 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Xihang Yu, Kaichen Zhou, Lorenzo Shaikewitz, Cl\'ement Jambon, Xiao Zhan, Rajat Talak, Luca Carlone

entry.summary: Presents Matisse, a training-free framework unifying active view acquisition and keyframe selection for 3D reconstruction under limited computation. It derives Evidential Uncertainty from cross-attention evidence of a pretrained generative 3D model's latent tokens and uses an Evidential Information Gain to guide view selection, addressing reasoning about unseen structure.

entry.title: Beyond Local Linearity: Scale-Resolved Geometry of Learned Image Encoders

author.name: Jakub Szymkowiak, Wojtek Pa{\l}ubicki, Kamil Adamczewski

entry.summary: This work introduces a scale-resolved statistic comparing an encoder's measured feature displacement against its local linear prediction as perturbation magnitude grows, revealing a characteristic plateau-rise-peak-decay profile called the bump across diverse image encoders. The bump is absent at initialization, emerges early in training, does not form under random labels or noise inputs, and its shape tracks training distribution and robustness.

entry.title: Universal Cross-Prompt Adversarial Attacks on Promptable Concept Segmentation

author.name: Ziqi Zhou, Yifan Hu, Yufei Song, Haowen Jiang, Xianlong Wang, Shengshan Hu, Dezhong Yao, Leo Yu Zhang

entry.summary: AdvPCS is the first systematic adversarial attack on SAM3-style promptable concept segmentation, featuring min-max prompt optimization, global-local perception deception, and temporal transition deviation attacks to achieve universal cross-prompt transferability. It extends the adversarial robustness analysis of SAM and SAM2 to the newer concept-level segmentation paradigm.

entry.title: BIND: Binding 3D Robot Actions to 2D Image Features

author.name: Cameron Smith, Arsh Tangri, Vitor Guizilini, Yue Wang, Zubair Irshad, Sergey Zakharov

entry.summary: BIND is a new action representation for visuomotor policies that explicitly binds 3D robot actions to their corresponding 2D image features, replacing the typical MLP regression from a single global feature vector. This structured binding yields strong data efficiency gains and robustness to out-of-distribution object positions and camera viewpoints. The key insight is that policies should not have to rediscover the action-feature relationship from demonstrations alone.

entry.title: Memorize, Adapt, Ignore: Diagnosing Robot Learning Mechanisms under Training Data Variation

author.name: Ke Zhang, Danica J. Sutherland, Chao Liu

entry.summary: This paper investigates the mechanisms underlying domain randomization and demonstration curation for robust manipulation policies through case studies randomizing object size, color, type, lighting, and prompts across ManiSkill RL and VLA fine-tuning on LIBERO and RoboTwin. By examining both behavior and internal representations, it provides an empirical account of when policies memorize, adapt, or ignore training variation, moving beyond trial-and-error randomization tuning.

entry.title: Cue the Flow: Steering Flow-Matching Policies for Open-World Delivery Manipulation

author.name: Haoxuan Wang, Griffin Galimi, Junhua Huang, Selina Song, Wayne Wu, Yan Yan, Bolei Zhou

entry.summary: The paper uses a pretrained flow-matching vision-language-action model as the low-level control interface for open-world goods delivery, treating high-level grounding model outputs as spatial cues that steer the policy rather than replacing its control. The insight is that the pretrained VLA already provides strong manipulation priors, and the spatial cue supplies only the missing task grounding, improving robustness under noisy perception and contact-rich interactions.

entry.title: Discrete Forcing: Infusing Discrete Guidance into Continuous Denoising for Few-Step Action Experts

author.name: Jingbo Wang, Wenxuan Song, Wenhao Yu, Han Zhao, Xi Wang, Jiayi Chen, Donglin Wang, Yan Wang, Haoang Li

entry.summary: Discrete Forcing is a flow-matching framework for VLA action generation that first predicts discrete action tokens for coarse structure, then uses them to guide continuous action refinement, sharing a diffusion transformer backbone across specialized branches. This coarse-to-fine scheme achieves high-precision actions in few denoising steps, addressing the discrete-versus-continuous action representation tradeoff. Efficient few-step action generation matters for real-time robot control.

entry.title: ChunkTrust: Adapting Execution Horizons for Robot Policies with Action-Expert Evidence

author.name: Fanding Huang, Jingyan Jiang, Shifeng Bao, Mingkang Pu, Shiwei Li, Jing Xu, Shijia Xu, Guanbo Huang, Chenghao Gu, Yuzhi Huang, Chenxin Li, Faisal Nadeem Khan, Huan Yang, Yan Wang, Cheng Chi, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: ChunkTrust treats the action-chunk execution horizon of robot foundation policies as a latent variable inferred from action-expert evidence instead of a fixed hyperparameter. Its training-free horizon selector combines intra-chunk spectral stability with inter-chunk continuity, tracked via an online Beta posterior with kernel forgetting, and an optional learned adapter adds a context-conditioned prior. Adaptive horizons directly affect the reliability and reactivity of chunk-based policies like those in modern VLAs.

entry.title: SplineWAM: Adaptive Action Horizons for World Action Models via B-Spline Representations

author.name: Jun Guo, Xiaoshen Han, Qiwei Li, Nan Sun, Peiyan Li, Heyun Wang, Hang Lai, Weinan Zhang, Xinghang Li, Huaping Liu

entry.summary: SplineWAM addresses the fixed-length action chunk limitation of world action models by adaptively compressing action trajectories into fixed-size windows of cubic B-spline parameters with motion-adaptive knot times. One parameter budget then decodes into chunks of varying temporal resolution and duration, enabling longer free-space motion or more compute on contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches the no-CoT performance of GPT-6 Astra

author.name: Rauno Arike

entry.summary: Independent benchmarking on the Think Fast task suite shows GPT-6.1 Sol closes roughly 80% of the gap between GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra on mean no-chain-of-thought accuracy, likely because 6.1 Sol is a looped transformer like Astra. The post reports per-task results, wide confidence intervals on time-horizon estimates due to benchmark saturation, and discusses implications of the looped architecture.

entry.title: Chris Painter's testimony to the U.S. Senate on AI agent incidents

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: METR President Chris Painter's written testimony to the U.S. Senate Subcommittee on Disaster Management at a hearing titled 'Rogue AI: Securing the Homeland Against AI Agent Attacks', published in full on the day of the hearing (September 30, 2026). The testimony aims to give policymakers reliable, factual evidence about observed AI agent incidents and capabilities, grounded in METR's model evaluation and threat research. It represents a leading evaluation nonprofit directly shaping legislative understanding of agent risks.

entry.title: Multi-LLM Collaborative Alignment via Stackelberg Games

author.name: Christina Hahn, Shangbin Feng, Dean Light, Swastik Roy, Hila Gonen, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: Stackelberg Alignment is a game-theory-inspired leader-follower framework in which an EXP3 bandit leader adaptively allocates an instruction-sampling budget as a curriculum for a pool of collaboratively learning language models. This replaces uniform instruction sampling, which ignores that instruction usefulness changes as models improve.

entry.title: Can Computation from Earlier Problems Help LLMs Solve New Ones?

author.name: Jipei He, Wenhui Tan, Xiaoyi Yu, Enver Sangineto, Fiorenzo Parascandolo, Rita Cucchiara, Ruihua Song

entry.summary: This paper studies whether retained conversation history affects later-turn problem solving in LLMs, showing history can raise or lower accuracy even within the same domain. It introduces STAIR, which stores keys and values from earlier response generation in a fixed bank and redirects attention to reuse them, improving reasoning under retained history.

entry.title: A helps B while B hurts A: directed transfer in instruction-tuning mixture

author.name: Nima H. Siboni, Vahid Rostami

entry.summary: The authors show that transfer between instruction-tuning tasks is directed: task A can help task B while B hurts A, refuting the assumptions that transfer is never negative and that it is symmetric. They introduce a signed transfer map estimated from hundreds of fine-tuning runs on Qwen3 and Mistral models from 0.6B to 32B, enabling better source-task selection under a fixed budget.

entry.title: Life-Bench: A Benchmark and Knowledge Graph Framework for Multimodal Personalization Beyond Concept Recognition

author.name: Xia Hu, Honglei Zhuang, Brian Potetz, Alireza Fathi, Bo Hu, Babak Samari, Howard Zhou

entry.summary: Life-Bench is a fully synthetic, human-verified multimodal benchmark with over 11,800 QA pairs across 10 tasks testing personalization at three evidence scopes: concept identification, event understanding, and aggregated reasoning over personal photo histories. The authors also propose LifeGraph, a personal knowledge-graph solution. Notably, the author list includes several Google researchers (Zhuang, Potetz, Hu, Fathi, Zhou, Samari).

entry.title: Evaluating Persistent Calibration under Evolving Model Knowledge

author.name: Victor Wang, Thomas Hofweber, Mohit Bansal, Elias Stengel-Eskin

entry.summary: Introduces persistent calibration, the problem of whether confidence estimators continue to faithfully reflect a model's knowledge as the model continually adapts, without recurring supervision. The authors operationalize this by testing whether confidence estimators trained on earlier checkpoints of open models generalize to later checkpoints, probing whether confidence is an intrinsic, transferable property.

entry.title: Audio Token Attention Is Predictable Before the Language Model Runs

author.name: Kyoungjun Park, Yunzhe Li, Lili Qiu

entry.summary: The paper shows that the attention an audio token will receive across an audio language model is linearly predictable from its encoder output before the LM runs, enabling a label-free closed-form predictor (Triage) that cuts audio tokens with rho at least 0.69 on eleven of thirteen LALMs. This differs from image-token pruning, where tokens draw little early attention.

entry.title: Faithful Dual-constrained Erasure for Robust LLM Safety Alignment

author.name: Jiaqing Li, Shide Zhou, Zhibo Zhang, Yuxi Li, Tianlong Yu, Kailong Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the vulnerability of unlearned LLMs to retraining attacks, identifying shallow alignment as the root cause: models exploit dormant parameters as spurious suppressors forming a fragile inhibitory shell over intact malicious representations. It proposes a dual-constrained erasure method that genuinely removes target knowledge rather than merely suppressing it.

entry.title: Speculative Safety Honeypot: Toward Proactive Defense Against Multi-turn Agent Attacks

author.name: Zezhong Wang, Xueyang Tang, Rui Lian, Yang Lou, Heqing Huang

entry.summary: SSH is a proactive defense against multi-turn attacks on LLM agents, inspired by speculative decoding: small LLMs speculate future agent behaviors by building an action-level trajectory tree, then verify predicted risks in advance rather than relying only on retrospective context analysis. This targets deep malicious intents split across turns.

entry.title: GFD-OPD: Guidance-Folded On-Policy Distillation of Diffusion Models Across Scales

author.name: Zhenxing Zhang, Jiayan Teng, Wenxu Wu, Zhuoyi Yang, Jiazheng Xu, Wendi Zheng, Jie Tang, Dan Guo, Meng Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies large-to-small on-policy distillation for diffusion models, showing the standard recipe fails across scales and diagnosing why via a proposed Fixed-State KL metric that fairly measures student-teacher distribution gaps. The resulting guidance-folded OPD method supports both compressing large diffusion teachers into small students and merging experts.

entry.title: Revisiting On-policy Adversarial Black-Box Distillation: Calibrating Groupwise Reward Geometry for Effective Advantage Construction

author.name: Xiao Cui, Mo Zhu, Yulei Qin, Yuze Wu, Wengang Zhou, Houqiang Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies an objective mismatch in on-policy adversarial black-box distillation methods like GAD: GRPO computes group-relative advantages while the critic is trained to distinguish teacher from student outputs, causing collapsed reward scales and brittle optimization. The authors propose calibrating groupwise reward geometry to construct more reliable advantages for student policy optimization.

entry.title: MotionWeave: Learning Motion-Centered Future Dynamics for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Jingqiu Wang, Yan Wang

entry.summary: MotionWeave is a motion-centric future-dynamics framework for VLA action-chunk prediction, with an Action-Induced Motion Grounder that conditions on action and proprioceptive representations and a Horizon Residual Composer for timestep-specific supervision. It avoids predicting control-irrelevant appearance in full future images and links actions to local visual changes per timestep.

entry.title: Almost Human, Except When It Matters: VoxParity and the Decisions a Voice Should Change

author.name: Bhavik Mangla

entry.summary: VoxParity tests whether voice agents act on audio context, not just words: across 183 scenarios from 14 sectors, the transcript is held fixed while audio changes (a mayday under a radio check, a child's voice placing a bet), and systems are credited only if hearing the call shifts actions more than a words-only pipeline. It probes safety-critical decisions where prosody and background audio should matter.

entry.title: Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States

author.name: Haojin Wang, Dylan Zhang, Huaibo Chen, Suhao Yu, Yihang Sun, Zhanyang Jin, Jiaying Ye, Dianqi Li, Prasanna Sattigeri, Kamal Youcef-Toumi, Hao Peng

entry.summary: OLIVE is an online distillation method where the student generates prefixes and the teacher autoregressively continues them, with the student updated via cross-entropy on teacher tokens. Each design choice targets a known limitation of offline SFT, token-level on-policy distillation, and distribution-matching approaches. OLIVE achieves higher reasoning performance than on-policy distillation at comparable GPU-hour cost.

entry.title: MeshOctave generates meshes via cascading resolution transitions

author.name: Junkai Lin, Tianhao Zhao, Hang Long, Huipeng Guo, Jielei Zhang, Youjia Zhang, Jiale Xu, Wenbing Li, Rendong Liang, Jozef Hladk\'y, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner, Yuanming Hu, Wei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes MeshOctave, a next-scale mesh generation method that defines scale via dyadic spatial grid resolutions instead of progressive mesh simplification, enabling parallel intra-scale token prediction and coarse-to-fine refinement. This yields compact, artist-style meshes with explicit topology while avoiding prohibitive autoregressive per-token costs and linear scaling of generation steps with face count.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Consistency Distillation for Few-Step Video Generation

author.name: Lingyu Liu, Yaxiong Wang, Li Zhu, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: This work improves few-step video generation by making consistency distillation uncertainty-aware: teacher-guided consistency targets are weighted by local content difficulty, since temporally varying regions like flowing water produce unreliable endpoint predictions while static regions yield consistent ones. The method concentrates learning where supervision is trustworthy rather than where content is semantically complex.

entry.title: OccluDex: Hierarchical 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Learning for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation under Self-Occlusion

author.name: Ziheng Xu, Yueyuan Chen, Xinyuan He, Guoxing Liu, Yuanshuo Tan, Huiming Pan, Bin He, Shuo Jiang, Peter B. Shull

entry.summary: OccluDex is a hierarchical 3D visuo-tactile representation learning framework that fuses global geometric structure with local contact information to support dexterous manipulation when the egocentric-viewed hand occludes task-relevant surfaces. It uses multi-scale masked autoencoding to pretrain representations supporting robust closed-loop control and generalization to unseen object geometries.

entry.title: From Local Whole-Body VLA Behaviors to Scene-Scale Aerial Manipulation

author.name: Weixiang Guo, Rui Jin, Haotian Jin, Xinhang Xu, Ruiyang Liu, Haoran Zhao, Yi Wang, Weiqi Gai, Kun Cao, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified framework for training and executing VLA policies on articulated uncrewed aerial manipulators at scene scale, featuring a scene-reconfigurable pipeline that synthesizes kinodynamically feasible trajectories and synchronized multiview observations without physical demonstrations. Its MPAR mechanism aligns asynchronously returned action chunks with measured execution progress for correct continuous control. It tackles demonstration cost, latency-induced misalignment, and cross-site behavior composition in aerial manipulation.

entry.title: Improving OCR Faithfulness via Gated and Attenuated On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Baode Wang, Zuming Huang, Kexuan Ren, Jun Huang, Wei Chu

entry.summary: This paper addresses a real weakness of vision-language models in OCR: rewriting anomalous text in images into linguistically plausible but incorrect transcriptions. The authors show empirically that a fixed teacher's supervision becomes less useful as the student improves, and propose GAD-RL, which adaptively gates and attenuates teacher guidance during joint post-training based on the student's current task performance and local distributions.

entry.title: SimTrace: Grounded Multimodal User Trajectories Generation for Online User Modeling

author.name: Yunan Lu, Shuang Xie, Meghna Allamudi, Mingyu Zhao, Han Li, Lingyun Wang, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: SimTrace generates faithful, fine-grained synthetic multimodal clickstreams using a computer-use client agent to support virtual clients for A/B testing, recommender development, and interface evaluation. It targets the gap between public datasets that abstract away interaction detail and proprietary logs unavailable due to privacy or traffic constraints.

entry.title: When Scientific Contradictions Are Lost in Translation

author.name: Tal Zeevi, Trey W. Jensen, Maxwell Strome

entry.summary: The authors study how frontier models like GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 decide whether two scientific findings genuinely conflict, using a controlled XOR-constraint task translated into reports from different laboratories. Models must choose between constraint-consistent assignments and biologically plausible ones, revealing tension between logical and domain-expectation reasoning. The work probes a subtle failure mode relevant to AI-assisted scientific synthesis.

entry.title: When Reasoning Goes Astray: Attention Dynamics of Uncontrolled Reasoning

author.name: Yuanhe Zhang, Ziwei Wang, Jie Ren, Haoran Gao, Zhenhong Zhou, Fanyu Meng, Cong Wu, Li Sun, Sen Su

entry.summary: The paper operationalizes large reasoning model generation into four states and introduces RADAR, a method using attention dynamics to identify reasoning state in real time, distinguishing productive thinking from degenerate loops and redundant verification. Existing mitigations truncate outputs or react to surface repetition and cannot explain how benign reasoning degenerates. This has implications for inference cost control and service reliability.

entry.title: Learning What to Forget: Distributional Unlearning for LLM Representation Spaces

author.name: Pinaki Mohanty, Haoran Tang, Maggie Makar, Rajiv Khanna

entry.summary: The paper tackles distributional unlearning, where entire data domains like toxic language must be removed from a model rather than isolated records, and introduces Mamushi, a non-parametric framework ranking forget examples using probability measures over LLM representations. This removes parametric assumptions that are ill-suited to high-dimensional language model spaces.

entry.title: Beyond the Remembered World: Predictive 4D Belief for Persistent Navigation in Evolving Worlds

author.name: Mingjian Gao, Zhaocheng Li, Haoyang Huang, Wenqiao Zhang, Yingjie Niu, Hao Zhou, Chao Li, Juncheng Li, Siliang Tang, Yueting Zhuang

entry.summary: EvolvingNav introduces Evolving-World Navigation, where embodied agents must account for objects that move while unobserved, maintaining a time-indexed belief from 3D object histories and revising it under limited visibility. The structured persistence-relocation framework addresses a realistic gap where remembered locations become stale by arrival time.

entry.title: Referential Uncertainty in Human--AI Collaboration

author.name: Christian Poelitz, Finale Doshi-Velez, Si\^an Lindley

entry.summary: This study examines how AI workers identify and communicate uncertainty over which object a description refers to, in a collaborative puzzle task with a human helper. It finds separately elicited belief distributions are better calibrated (ECE 0.15) and more discriminative (AUROC 0.65) than raw action-token probabilities, which are severely overconfident.

entry.title: ArchitectureIQ: On the Measure of Training Intuition

author.name: Zirui Ren, Shaoyang Guo, Chencheng Tang, Jinxin Wang, Chengyu Xiong, Shanbin Yu, Peihang Li, Yidi Wu, Bangzhe Huang, Qingyu Qu, Leqian Yang, Ziming Liu

entry.summary: ArchitectureIQ is a benchmark asking test-takers to predict which of several training recipes yields the best test metric for a given synthetic dataset, measuring ML training intuition. It finds frontier LLMs achieve about 76% accuracy versus 66% for the best human researcher, yet remain far from perfect and can be sub-human on architecture-only questions (GPT-6 Astra at 38% versus 65% for the best human).

entry.title: Unlearnable, or Unmeasured? On the Reliability of Difficulty Labels in RLVR

author.name: Chandak Chakma, Syed Nazmus Sakib, Nafiul Haque, Shifat E. Arman

entry.summary: This paper re-examines the claim that some prompts in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) are inherently unlearnable. The authors show that supposedly unlearnable prompts do improve at about one third the rate of learnable ones, and that the difficulty labels used to define such sets are noisy and poorly reproducible due to limited response sampling. They propose a sampling-based framework for quantifying this measurement uncertainty.

entry.title: LogiC-Diff: Embedding Security Properties Into AI-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Ziyan An, John Stankovic, Meiyi Ma

entry.summary: LogiC-Diff embeds formal security properties, expressed in Signal Temporal Logic, directly into an AI-enabled cyber-physical system's prediction process via a logic-conditioned bi-stage diffusion framework, enforcing system-level constraints at inference rather than relying on external filters. This aims to prevent small adversarial perturbations from inducing unsafe control actions.

entry.title: TACIT: Optimization Models that Learn from Their Mistakes

author.name: Maxime Bouscary, Marco Molinaro, Sirui Li, Saurabh Amin, Ishai Menache, Konstantina Mellou

entry.summary: TACIT automatically repairs misspecified optimization models, whose miscalibrated objectives and missing constraints reflect experts' tacit knowledge, using historical data of past solutions and user overrides. It combines LLM reasoning and prior knowledge with statistical validation to avoid overfitting that plagues inverse optimization and constraint learning on sparse data.

entry.title: Re-ranking and Late Interaction Drive Retrieval Quality: A Controlled Comparison of RAG Strategies for Scientific Question Answering

author.name: Bhagyesh Rathi, Eshan Chawla, William B. Andreopoulos

entry.summary: This work provides a controlled comparison of six retrieval-augmented generation strategies for scientific question answering, ranging from classic dense retrieval to agentic tool-call pipelines, RRF fusion, and ColBERTv2 late interaction. The findings emphasize that re-ranking and late-interaction retrieval are the main drivers of retrieval quality on domain-specific corpora.

entry.title: Bandits with Multiple Optimal Arms: Minimax Regret and Non-Adaptivit

author.name: Kaixuan Ji, Qiwei Di, Qingyue Zhao, Heyang Zhao, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Analyzes multi-armed bandits where several arms are optimal, a common situation in practice when multiple answers are acceptable. The paper sharpens prior sub-sampling analyses to achieve an improved minimax regret of order sqrt(T) times (K-A)/sqrt(KA), proves a matching lower bound up to logs, and shows that knowing the number of optimal arms A does not help adaptively.

entry.title: Soft Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Rafi Ibn Sultan, Md. Sajid Alam Chowdhury, Saleh Zare Zade, Chengyin Li, Prashant Khanduri, Marco Brocanelli, Dongxiao Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes Soft Spatial Reasoning, a post-training framework letting LVLMs perform soft thinking for spatial tasks: at each intermediate reasoning step the model forms a continuous soft state by mixing token embeddings instead of committing to a single discrete token, avoiding premature discretization and error propagation. The same lead authors as the SpatialCORE paper, suggesting a broader research program on spatial reasoning in LVLMs.

entry.title: Future Video Generation Better Aligns with the Human Visual Cortex than Observed Video

author.name: Chang-Bae Bang, Hyungjin Chung, Byung-Hoon Kim

entry.summary: The authors hypothesize that internal representations of generative video models predicting future frames align better with human visual cortex fMRI responses than representations of observed video, reflecting the predictive nature of human visual processing. They compare video-generation model internals against brain recordings during video watching to test this.

entry.title: Trustworthy Runtime Error Healing in Real-World Repositories: A Benchmark and Guardrail

author.name: Gou Tan, Pengfei Chen, Zhensu Sun, Jieke Shi, Junkai Chen, Ting Zhang, Weifeng Sun, Junda He, Shuai Liang, Chuanfu Zhang, Lwin Khin Shar, David Lo

entry.summary: This paper moves LLM-based runtime error healing from small competition programs toward real-world repositories by introducing HealBench, a benchmark of 265 runtime errors from 18 real repositories with reference patched executions, and HealGuard, a guardrail for safely executing LLM-generated healing code in live processes. It addresses the previously unexamined safety concern of running generated code inside a crashed program's runtime state.

entry.title: Who Said What, and Will It Be Remembered? Evaluating Persistent Speaker Attribution Across Meetings

author.name: Shantanu Vispute, Aditya Mishra, Siddhartha Saxena

entry.summary: The authors introduce SI-cpWER, a metric that evaluates whether speaker identities remain stable across an entire corpus of meetings rather than being remapped per recording. They benchmark five commercial diarization-identification cascades, two academic baselines, and their end-to-end system ThyVoice on the full 129-meeting CHiME-8 NOTSOFAR evaluation set plus CHiME-6.

entry.title: Text-to-3D Policy: Fine-Grained Language-Behavior Alignment for Unseen Specification Generalization

author.name: Xinhao Yang, Wenhao Wu, Ning Lv, Yanshen Ding, Zhenhong Sun, Daoyi Dong, Chunlin Chen, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces T3DP, a Text-to-3D Policy framework that improves fine-grained alignment between language instructions and robot manipulation behaviors. It addresses unseen specification generalization, where language specifies behavioral variations such as target position or articulated state that were absent from training demonstrations.

entry.title: Community-Driven API and AI Writer Design for Openly Scaling Community Notes

author.name: Brad Miller, Jay Baxter, Jiansong Chao, Keith Coleman, Sophie Hilgard, Daniel Ortiz

entry.summary: This paper by the Community Notes team presents the design, operation, and impact of the AI Note Writer API on X, which since late 2025 has let AI propose notes while users, not the platform or AI, control visibility. It analyzes interactions between AI- and human-generated notes across topics, showing how explicit note requests shape the AI's post feeds.

entry.title: On the (In)effectiveness of AMR Augmentation for Large Language Models

author.name: Hoa Quynh Nhung Nguyen, Jacopo Staiano, Michael Sullivan

entry.summary: This reproduction study finds that previously reported downstream gains from Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) augmentation likely stem from specific experimental settings rather than genuine benefit. Using a unified hyperparameter-selection protocol, text-only baselines match or exceed AMR-augmented models, and a perplexity-based probe shows AMR adds little relational knowledge beyond what LLMs already encode. A valuable negative result for the semantic-parsing augmentation literature.

entry.title: Learning to Plan from Random Exploration

author.name: Deqian Kong, Guangyan Sun, Sheng Cheng, Sirui Xie, Bo Pang, Jianwen Xie, Tony Geng, Caiwen Ding, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that experience from random exploration can support long-range planning without policy-improvement training. The authors analyze random walks to characterize what temporal relations encode at different horizons (geodesic geometry at short horizons, regional connectivity at longer horizons), and learn these relations with a conditional energy-based model trained via noise-contrastive estimation on unlabeled observation pairs, which a planner then queries at multiple horizons.

entry.title: SparseEngine: Sparse-First Inference Engine

author.name: Jitai Hao, Quansheng Gu, Qiang Huang, Jun Yu

entry.summary: SparseEngine is a sparse-first LLM inference engine that lets sparse attention methods control their own KV-cache representations while sharing common serving infrastructure via a lifecycle contract. It supports 15 sparse-attention methods across four categories and introduces Chain Cache for cross-request state management, addressing integration friction that has limited sparse attention adoption.

entry.title: Robustifying Asynchronous SGD via Soft Throttling

author.name: Kaoru Otsuka, Maxime Meyer, Yuki Takezawa, Makoto Yamada, Anastasia Koloskova

entry.summary: The paper introduces Throttle, a Byzantine-robust generalization of asynchronous SGD that exponentially down-weights updates from faster clients by a factor q, unifying asynchronous SGD (q=1) and synchronous robust SGD (q to infinity) as special cases. The authors provide convergence-rate theory and show the mechanism also addresses stragglers empirically.

entry.title: Certification-Based Differentially Private Learning

author.name: Mihnea Ghitu, Matthew Wicker

entry.summary: This paper extends formal-methods-based tighter privacy analysis beyond private prediction in classification, generalizing abstract gradient training to continuous regression and introducing Abstract Gradient Sampling (AGS). AGS reduces learning to a reachability problem over parameter space, enabling reachability-based privacy certification for parameterized models.

entry.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression

author.name: Massimo Bini, Anders Christensen, Stephan Alaniz, Judah Goldfeder, Ole Winther, Yann LeCun, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: The paper introduces Learnable Subspace Projections (LSP), which learn end-to-end which low-rank subspaces to discard per layer, replacing local closed-form criteria that ignore cross-layer error propagation. This prevents error compounding at high compression ratios in transformer compression.

entry.title: Distribution Matching Distillation for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Paul Le Van Kiem, Dario Shariatian, Umut Simsekli, Alain Durmus

entry.summary: The paper develops distribution matching distillation to cut the number of network evaluations needed by continuous diffusion language models, exploiting the student's probabilistic token outputs. It proposes two methods under a unified reverse-KL formulation: Simplex-DMD with continuous relaxations and pathwise gradients, and Reinforce-DMD with categorical sampling and a learned density ratio. This addresses a key efficiency bottleneck for parallel token generation.

entry.title: Privacy in Personalized AI Is a System Property, Not Just a Model Property

author.name: Guillaume Salha-Galvan, Jiaying Xu

entry.summary: A position-style paper arguing that privacy in personalized AI (assistants, recommenders) must be evaluated at the system level rather than per model, since user information flows across components and over time. The authors identify four interconnected privacy-risk channels and propose four requirements for system-level privacy evaluation.

entry.title: RSIGame: Autonomous Agentic Game Development with Recursive Self-improvement

author.name: Wenyi Wu, Minghao Fu, Jieyu You, Kun Zhou, Siqi Liu, Aayush Salvi, Yiheng Lin, Ce Zhang, Xiaohan Lan, Jiahui Zhu, Yujie Zhong, Qi She, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: RSIGame is an autonomous agentic framework for game development organized into local explore-diagnose-improve loops and global refinement loops, designed to avoid overfitting to a small test set during iterative game improvement. It performs evidence-grounded revision with an evolving issue repository, targeting reliable improvement of LLM-generated games beyond a merely playable version.

entry.title: HAPMoE: Heterogeneity-Aware Automatic Parallelism Planning for Mixture-of-Experts Models Training

author.name: Mengyuan Fan, Peizhuang Cong, Zixiao Huang, Si Xu, Tong Qiao, Yanghao Li, Jing Yang, Tong Yang, Quanlu Zhang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: HAPMoE addresses automatic parallelization for training mixture-of-experts models on heterogeneous compute clusters, a combination existing approaches handle only separately. As MoE architectures dominate large-model training and accelerator diversity grows, joint treatment of model and cluster heterogeneity is increasingly important. The system derives efficient parallelism strategies automatically at low cost.

entry.title: STARS: From Spatiotemporal Dynamics to Social Representations in Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Nathan Tsoi, Michael J. Munje, Tejas Oberoi, Rishab Maheshwari, Pengen Zheng, Tanush Chauhan, Peter Stone, Joydeep Biswas

entry.summary: STARS is a systematic benchmark evaluating whether vision-language models can understand complex social navigation scenes, including spatiotemporal relations among agents and human intentions, which underpin safe and socially compliant robot navigation.
