entry.summary: DTMR jointly optimizes timing and control in a single optimization for transferring expressive human and animal motions to legged robots, adjusting timing at every control step so only motion segments needing temporal change are deformed. It uses GPU-parallelized sampling-based MPC, which is especially important for dynamic motions like jumps where timing and control are interdependent.

entry.title: Plan-Conditioned Imitation for Robust Object Retrieval under Self-Occlusion in Dense Clutter

author.name: Kowndinya Boyalakuntla, Ajinkya Pawar, Abdeslam Boularias, Jingjin Yu

entry.summary: TRACE is a plan-conditioned imitation framework for retrieving objects from dense clutter where the manipulator's own motion occludes targets. A privileged teacher generates a nominal rollout in a digital twin from a single unoccluded observation, and a recurrent student trained with behavior cloning and DAgger learns to correct deviations without repeated arm withdrawals to restore visibility.

entry.title: Social-WM: Safety-Aware Latent World Models for Robot Social Navigation

author.name: Zhihao Zheng, Mooi Choo Chuah

entry.summary: Social-WM is a latent world-model planning framework trained from egocentric RGB video that learns the discrepancy between nominal and realizable actions in social navigation, e.g., constraining forward motion near pedestrians. Through action-conditioned future prediction targeting actual executed actions, the model captures safety-relevant consequences directly for planning.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Harness on Multiple Tasks with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer

author.name: Qiankai Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for self-evolving agent harnesses in which the same frozen model on the same harness version alternates between solving tasks and proposing improvements to its own harness, rather than using a separate proposer or per-benchmark harnesses. This moves the line of work closer to recursive self-improvement and evaluates evolution across a diverse range of tasks rather than a single benchmark.

entry.title: Budget Boundary Effects in Test-Time Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Guilin Zhang, Ziqi Tan, Wulan Guo, Kai Zhao, Hongyun Yang, Mei Luo, Qi Ning, Feng Yang

entry.summary: This paper measures how token-budget boundary policies (strict stopping at a cap versus letting the current attempt finish) affect test-time mathematical reasoning, using paired offline replays of 19,200 traces over competition math problems. Findings include that advisory stopping mostly converts abstentions into correct answers and that cost comparisons differ depending on whether they are made along realized cost. It offers practical guidance for inference-time compute controllers.

entry.title: More Choices, Fewer Decisions: Ordinal-Scale Bias in JEV-like Direct-Decision Models

author.name: Tianxiang Gao, Jinzhe Li, Zhiyuan Li, Yi Chang, Yuan Wu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes ordinal-scale bias in direct-decision models, showing JEV 1.13 and open KEV models compress decisions onto a subset of the ordinal scale, e.g., assigning 38.8% of ANLI predictions and over half its errors to Neutral despite high accuracy. Across 36 ordinal datasets, final decisions use only 67-76% of effective gold support versus near-full usage on nominal tasks. This highlights a reliability failure beyond accuracy for models emitting structured scores.

entry.title: How Much Can Reliability Drift Under a Fixed Confidence Distribution?

author.name: Wenhao Liang, Lin Yue, Wei Emma Zhang, Mingyu Guo, Olaf Maennel, Weitong Chen

entry.summary: This theoretical paper characterizes worst-case movement of the reliability relation under covariate shifts that preserve the confidence score distribution, bounded by a chi-squared reweighting budget. It derives a fragility profile that equals the square root of the budget times within-level variance of correctness propensity on a computable interval, connecting to calibration-refinement decompositions.

entry.title: RealWorldShop: Benchmarking and Improving Conversational Shopping Agents in Real-World E-commerce

author.name: Xinwei Yang, Kelong Mao, Yudong Guo, Sulong Xu, Simiu Gu, Chen Huang, Wenqiang Lei

entry.summary: RealWorldShop is a benchmark for conversational shopping agents built on 3.28 million grounded products, structured shopping episodes, a profile-grounded user simulator, and role-play evaluation. It targets session-level decision processes like constraint revision and multi-goal coordination, and finds current systems locally plausible but weak at state tracking and constraint updating.

entry.title: Who Owns That? Evaluating Ownership Intuitions in Large Language Models

author.name: Xizhi Xiao, Yue Wu, Shan Xu, Jia Liu

entry.summary: Using the Competing Ownership Attribution Task of 42 scenarios, the study compares ownership judgments from 24 LLM configurations with 108 human participants. Models approximate human-human similarity but are more homogeneous than humans, and they divide ownership more evenly among claimants within individual answers.

entry.title: What Can Component-Replacement Evidence Establish? A Critical Scoping Review of Local Decisions in LLM Agents

author.name: Shuyang Zhang (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Jianshuo Chang (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)

entry.summary: This critical scoping review maps 348 studies and examines 90 comparison records to assess what component-replacement experiments in LLM agents can actually establish, analyzing replaced decisions, measurement comparability, controls, and alternative explanations. Of 222 studies reporting local decision metrics, only 142 also report task endpoints, exposing a gap between local metrics and task-level claims.

entry.title: Belief-Aware Multi-Agent Path Finding under Map Uncertainty

author.name: Viraj Parimi, Shao-Hung Chan, Han Zhang, Jingkai Chen, Brian Williams

entry.summary: This work extends multi-agent path finding (MAPF) to environments where obstacle traversability is uncertain and spatially correlated, so a single observation can inform beliefs about nearby unobserved locations. The approach uses these inferred beliefs to anticipate collisions that prior contingent-planning or replanning methods would miss. It matters for real-world robotics in dynamic environments like warehouses.

entry.title: Searching for BSM Experimental Signatures with Large Lagrangian Models

author.name: Ibrahim Elsharkawy, Victoria Knapp-Perez, Wahid Bhimji, Aishik Ghosh

entry.summary: The authors present hAIthem, a framework combining reinforcement learning exploration with literature-derived knowledge from large language models to search the vast theory space of physics beyond the Standard Model for overlooked experimental signatures, with dark matter as a motivating case. The goal is to identify testable observables that can guide the design of future experiments.

entry.title: After a Decade: Bringing Shadow Removal into the Real World with Agentic Training Data

author.name: Shilin Hu, Jingyi Xu, Dimitris Samaras, Hieu Le

entry.summary: The paper argues shadow removal has stalled because paired training data have barely changed in a decade, and proposes an offline agentic workflow that converts abundant shadow detection data (images plus masks without shadow-free targets) into paired supervision using physics-motivated generation, failure detection, retry, and candidate selection. This refreshes training data for a field that looks solved on benchmarks but remains brittle in the real world.

entry.title: Template-Search Domain Adaptation via Multi-Stage Feature Alignment for Cross-Modal Object Tracking

author.name: Fereshteh Aghaee Meibodi, Amir Mehdi Soufi Enayati, Shadi Alijani, Homayoun Najjaran

entry.summary: Introduces TSDA-Track, a framework for tracking objects when the initial template and later search frames come from different sensing modalities, a setting harder than standard multi-modal tracking since paired modalities are not simultaneously available. It uses multi-stage feature alignment, including adversarial alignment before the transformer's template-search interaction, to reduce the modality gap during training.

entry.title: StateTree: Enhancing Long-Term Dialogue Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Naen Xu, Wanqing Cui, Yibo Hu, Shixin Hong, Hengyu An, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma, Tianyu Du

entry.summary: Proposes StateTree, a data-driven RL method for long-term dialogue reasoning that constructs a challenging auxiliary task from scarce dialogues with verifiable ground truth. It augments multi-session dialogues with a tree-structured path-tracing task where key-value records embedded across sessions form a binary tree the model must traverse via retrieval, addressing scattered evidence and revised preferences under data scarcity.

entry.title: The Invisible Language Tax: Token Premiums of French and Regional Languages in 2026 LLM Tokenizers, and a French-Optimized Prototype

author.name: Thomas Serval

entry.summary: This study quantifies token premiums across seven 2026 model tokenizers (including OpenAI o200k, Llama 3, Qwen3, DeepSeek V3/V4, Gemma 3, Mistral Tekken, and Anthropic's generation-5 tokenizer), finding French needs 31-58% more tokens than English while regional languages of France pay 1.6-3.3x. The author also releases a French-optimized tokenizer prototype.

entry.title: Structure-aware Reinforcement Learning for Protein Directed Evolution

author.name: Zikun Nie, Suyuan Zhao, Yizhen Luo, Siqi Fan, Zaiqing Nie

entry.summary: StructEvo is a structure-aware reinforcement learning framework for protein directed evolution that uses a delta-structure fusion encoder to approximate mutant structure features via feature differences, sidestepping the scarcity of reliable mutant structures. It then navigates the vast mutation space with RL. Integrating spatial and co-evolutionary constraints into protein optimization addresses a clear limitation of sequence-only methods.

entry.title: EngramBench: A Capability-Grounded Benchmark for Skill-Evolution Harnesses

author.name: Zhixuan Tan, Pengjie Gu, Zhao Li, Yihan Hu, Xu He, Dong Li, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: EngramBench is a benchmark for evaluating skill evolution in autonomous agents, governed by the axiom of capability overlap without solution overlap to resolve the identifiability problem where genuine abstraction is confounded with rote copying from historical training data. It comprises 30 learning tasks and 13 unseen transfer tasks requiring sustained reasoning and cross-domain abstraction.

entry.title: Belief-Based Maximum Occupancy Principle and Active Inference

author.name: Manolis Mylonas, Rub\'en Moreno Bote

entry.summary: This paper connects an intrinsic motivation approach, the Maximum Occupancy Principle (MOP), with Active Inference, showing how agents can maximize occupancy over future state-action paths without explicit preferences or epistemic targets. It grounds reward-independent objectives in the principled belief-updating framework of Active Inference for partially observable environments.

entry.title: ECHO-G: Embodied Co-speech Humanoid mOtion Generation

author.name: Yizhao Li, Pusen Gao, Ming Wang, Shaojie Shen, Shuo Yang, Hao Xu

entry.summary: ECHO-G generates full-body co-speech motion for humanoid robots, jointly conditioned on speech audio and timed transcripts via a Speech-Grounded Diffusion Transformer trained with rectified flow matching in robot space. The work also contributes a BEAT2-derived audio-text-robot dataset and a benchmark covering co-speech quality, motion quality, and runtime efficiency.

entry.title: Algorithmic Recourse Under Competition

author.name: Shahin Jabbari

entry.summary: This paper challenges the fixed-decision-rule assumption in algorithmic recourse, showing that when individuals compete for limited resources, widespread recourse adoption can shift acceptance thresholds and invalidate original recommendations. It formalizes this failure mode and studies recourse in the presence of such strategic population effects.

entry.title: OPSRD: On-Policy Self-Role Distillation

author.name: Weijie Ren, Yanwen Zhang, Hao Li, Zhuolin Qi, Hengyi Zhang, Naibo Wang

entry.summary: OPSRD is an on-policy self-distillation method that uses a fixed expert role prompt as privileged teaching context without requiring reference solutions. A role-free student generates trajectories while a frozen copy of the same base model supplies role-conditioned token distributions on the student's exact prefixes, transferring next-token preferences even when the sampled answer is incorrect.

entry.title: GateSPINE: Gated Cross-View Fusion for Lumbar Spine MRI Report Generation

author.name: Hoang Nguyen Van, Cuong Vuong Tuan, Trang Mai Xuan, Bien Tran Van, Nam Tran Van, Thien Van Luong

entry.summary: GateSPINE is a vision-language framework for automated radiology report generation from multi-sequence lumbar spine MRI. It fuses sagittal T1 and T2 volumes with a training-free gated operator and encodes fused sagittal and axial volumes with parallel 3D encoders, aiming to preserve plane-specific findings that single-volume encoders dilute. This addresses a clinically important recall problem where missed abnormalities are most costly.

entry.title: Synthesis Without Training: An Inference-Only Pipeline for Tabular, Temporal, and Relational Synthetic Data

author.name: Zilong Zhao, Abdul Raheem, Jiayu Li, Sohei Arisaka, Darius Lim Hong Yi, Milad Abdollahzadeh, Uzair Javaid, Biplab Sikdar

entry.summary: GENSCRIPT replaces the fit-then-sample paradigm for synthetic data with an inference-only pipeline that computes a deterministic statistical profile of source data and generates synthetic data without training any generative model. This addresses the per-dataset training requirement, modality-specific model engineering, and opacity of learned generators across tables, time series, and relational databases.

entry.title: Same Loss, Different Gradients

author.name: Ningkang Peng, Xiaoqian Peng, Yifan He, Anjie Hu, Chao Tan, Peirong Ma, Yanhui Gu

entry.summary: This paper shows that in differentiable learning, the forward-pass objective and the backward-pass gradient can silently diverge when probabilistic objectives rely on finite special-function recurrences, custom backward rules, and numerical clipping. Using high-dimensional von Mises-Fisher learning as a case study, the authors demonstrate that real implementations can produce identical losses while supplying different gradients and following different optimization trajectories. This highlights a previously overlooked correctness gap between mathematical definitions and their numerical implementations in autodiff systems.

entry.title: CDMD: A Cross-Dataset Mixed-Type Diffusion Model for Tabular Data

author.name: Mohamed Amine Ketata, Maximilian Schambach, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: CDMD is a tabular diffusion model trained jointly across heterogeneous datasets with different schemas and mixed numerical/categorical features, using schema-restricted reverse-process parameterization for masked diffusion. This enables knowledge transfer across datasets and reduces the need for many specialized per-dataset models.

entry.title: A Tilted Bowl Is Not a Slippery Slope: Compressing Looped Models

author.name: Steven Kolawole, Pearse Jim, Opegbemi M. Busoye, Glory Bagai, Virginia Smith

entry.summary: Testing over 30 models from five families, the authors find that compression-induced collapse in looped (weight-tied recurrent) models is not accumulated rounding error: for loops that settle, a fixed error merely shifts the fixed point, like tilting a bowl. This picture predicts which models fail from a single label-free measurement.

entry.title: Semantic-Aware Joint Source-Channel Optimization for Encoder-Agnostic Digital Video Communication

author.name: Xiangben Zhu, Caili Guo, Yang Yang, Chuanhong Liu, Meiyi Zhu

entry.summary: The authors propose SAJSCO, a lightweight plug-in module for digital video communication that jointly optimizes source and channel coding parameters using inter-frame semantic importance and estimated channel state. Unlike most video semantic communication work, it avoids heavy learned codecs and can integrate with existing systems, targeting resource-constrained deployments.

entry.title: The Geometry of Randomized Smoothing on Feasible Sets

author.name: Syed Izhan Khilji, Alireza Furutanpey, Schahram Dustdar

entry.summary: The paper analyzes randomized smoothing when a feasibility or confidence filter retains only some proposals, showing that naively substituting the retention ratio into the standard smoothing formula can certify balls containing decision boundaries. It separates the problem into geometric conditions (e.g., convex retained sets preserving Gaussian comparisons) and certification conditions.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Prototype Routing for Rehearsal-Free Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: HongWei Zhao (Beihang University), Rui Liu (Beihang University), Yong Chen (Beijing University of Posts, Telecommunications)

entry.summary: HyPro is a rehearsal-free class-incremental learning framework that assigns a dedicated LoRA-Expert module per incremental task and routes via geodesic nearest-prototype matching on a Poincare ball. This addresses catastrophic forgetting from cumulative interference and suboptimal module-sample matching when fine-tuning pre-trained models.

entry.title: Validity-Preserving Hierarchical RL for Joint Routing and Switch Placement in EDA

author.name: Dorian Gailhard, Ugo Lecerf, Enzo Tartaglione, Donatello Conte, Jhony H. Giraldo

entry.summary: The paper introduces a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for joint routing and switch placement in chip design, progressively building solutions from a minimal routing graph through switch expansion, placement, and routing operations while preserving validity constraints. It replaces heavily engineered heuristics with learned structured search.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Source-Free Universal Domain Adaptation on Time Series Representations

author.name: Romain Mussard, Fannia Pacheco, Maxime Berar, Paul Honeine, Gilles Gasso

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first benchmark for Source-Free Universal Domain Adaptation (SF-UniDA) on time series, where adaptation must handle unknown label-set mismatches without access to source data. It also studies pretrained foundation models as feature extractors and identifies a critical sensitivity of unknown-sample rejection thresholds, proposing a plug-in auto-thresholding fix.

entry.title: Compression Footprints as Security Signals for Model-Poisoning Defense in Federated Learning

author.name: Sachi Shome, William Eiers

entry.summary: This work reframes lossy compression in federated learning from an error source to a security signal, defining a compression footprint of reconstruction, directional, sparsity, and payload statistics that can separate honest from attack-generated updates. The authors characterize sufficient conditions for separation and build the CRAFT defense on this idea. It offers a novel detection surface beyond conventional update-geometry defenses.

entry.title: Which Models Work Well Together? Measuring Heterogeneity for LLM Team Selection

author.name: Liangyu Teng, Hengsong Liu, Juncen Guo, Jingyu Zhang, Yang Liu, Jing Liu, Liang Song

entry.summary: This paper proposes a heterogeneity-driven framework for selecting complementary teams of LLMs. It uses offline profiling to compute two interpretable signals: decorrelation of error patterns (to reduce co-failures) and divergence in predictive behavior (to capture strategy diversity), formulating team selection as an optimization problem rather than relying on heuristics.

entry.title: Average-and Last-Iterate Lower Bounds for Optimistic Matrix Mirror-Prox in Quantum Zero-Sum Games

author.name: Yiheng Su, Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong

entry.summary: The paper proves an Omega(1/epsilon) lower bound on average-iterate convergence for optimistic matrix mirror-prox in quantum zero-sum games, matching the known upper bound and showing tightness. It also constructs explicit single-qubit games where optimistic gradient descent-ascent fails to achieve geometric last-iterate convergence from the maximally mixed state.

entry.title: Fiber-Resolved Microstructure Quantification from Multi-Shell Diffusion MRI using Detection Transformers

author.name: Sebastian Endt, Marcus Wirth, Johannes Reinhold Schlund, Marion Irene Menzel

entry.summary: The authors reframe diffusion MRI microstructure estimation as an object-detection-like task, using a DETR architecture to jointly predict mean diffusivity, fractional anisotropy, fiber direction, and signal fraction for a variable number of fiber compartments. This avoids the expensive Monte-Carlo inversion of an ill-posed inverse Laplace transform required by nonparametric approaches.

entry.title: Discrete Score Matching Enables Causal Discovery from Count Data

author.name: Euijong Song, Hyewon Park, Gunwoong Park

entry.summary: This paper extends score-matching-based causal discovery to count data, where derivatives are unavailable. The authors generalize the SCORE constant-curvature criterion by conditioning on node values, introducing a conditional curvature score for node ordering and an off-diagonal curvature score for parent recovery, enabling full DAG recovery using concrete scores for counts. This matters because count data are common in genomics and other sciences where causal discovery previously had weak support.

entry.title: SE-ADD: Self-Evolving Audio Deepfake Detection with Mistake-Driven Supervision

author.name: Rong Wan, Wei Xie, Jiaxi Li, Wenwu Wang, Lu Yin, Yiliao Song, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: SE-ADD is a self-evolving framework for audio deepfake detection that iteratively adapts an audio language model via LoRA using supervision derived from its own mistakes, in evolving spoofing environments where new attacks dominate while old ones persist. The approach leverages model errors to target supervision where it is most needed, addressing post-deployment robustness. It matters as audio deepfakes are a growing security threat.

entry.title: Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations

author.name: Simone Ricci, Niccol\`o Biondi, Federico Pernici

entry.summary: This paper tackles the problem of embedding-space incompatibility when upgrading deployed contrastive vision-language models, which normally forces recomputation of entire image galleries. Building on orthogonal post-hoc alignment, the authors propose spherical interpolation to reduce residual incompatibilities between independently trained representation spaces. This matters for practical large-scale retrieval systems where re-embedding billions of items is prohibitively expensive.

entry.title: Sieve and Sage: Efficient Distraction Filtering for Reliable RALM Abstention

author.name: Jongbin Won, Sung Geun An, Jay-yoon Lee

entry.summary: The paper decomposes retrieval-augmented LLM failures into unanswerable (evidence absent) and distracted (relevant evidence mixed with conflicting or adversarial content) states, proposing a lightweight Sieve module that screens retrieved documents for distractions before a second module handles abstention. This improves abstention reliability at lower computational cost than monolithic single-step approaches. Learning to abstain appropriately is central to trustworthy RAG systems.

entry.title: TRACE: Deployable Tree-Relational Structure Enhancement for Oncology LLMs

author.name: Jizheng Lai, Yingyun Li, Ying Qin, Haiyang Qian

entry.summary: TRACE organizes oncology concepts and relations into an updatable tree-relational structure refined offline, retrieved at inference time as compact prompt evidence for label-free classification and QA. It improves performance across ten oncology classification tasks and a MedQA CancerGov benchmark without supervised labels.

entry.title: HeurEvo: Agentic Evolution of Hybrid Solver-Augmented Heuristics for Time-Critical Mathematical Optimization

author.name: Feijie Wu, Hugo Barbalho, Konstantina Mellou, Marco Molinaro, Jing Gao, Ishai Menache, Xinzhi Zhang, Sirui Li

entry.summary: HeurEvo automates discovery of hybrid heuristic-solver algorithms for time-critical mathematical optimization through plan-code-component co-evolution, unlike prior agentic heuristic design that improves components in isolation. It jointly adapts computation allocation, solver leverage, and overall algorithmic structure under strict runtime constraints. The work comes from a credible industry-academic team including Microsoft-affiliated researchers.

entry.title: DraftTrace: A Multi-View Analytics Environment for AI-Integrated Writing

author.name: Divyansh Chandarana, Sandipan De, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: DraftTrace is a writing environment that captures three complementary signals: the final document, the writing process over time, and student interactions with an integrated AI assistant. It turns these into submission-level, longitudinal, and class-level analytics for instructors. The authors deployed it in a graduate NLP course with 81 students and compared genuine sessions against LLM-generated responses entered by automated tools and copy-typed responses, finding that product-only measures are insufficient to distinguish them.

entry.title: Benchmarking Automatic Speech Recognition Tools for Iberian Languages

author.name: Fernando L\'opez, Pablo G\'omez, David Solans, Paulo Villegas, Jordi Luque

entry.summary: The authors benchmark eleven ASR systems, ten open-weight and one commercial, across five Iberian languages including low-resource Basque, Catalan, and Galician, using an 85-hour dataset spanning read speech, broadcast, and audiobooks with WER and real-time-factor metrics. Results show no single dominant system and substantial degradation for low-resource languages.

entry.title: Follow the Entities: A Corpus Map for Agentic Search

author.name: Soyeong Jeong, Sujay Kumar Jauhar, Sung Ju Hwang, Andrew Joohun Nam

entry.summary: CorpusMap introduces a navigation layer for LLM search agents that maps entity relationships across documents, so agents need not rediscover inter-document relationships for every query over flat file collections. This improves evidence connection across multi-document tasks while reducing token consumption.

entry.title: Learning to Retrieve Missing Evidence for Long-Term Memory QA

author.name: Yi-Xuan Deng, Yi Zhang, Wei Liu, Chao Xue, Shuojin Yang

entry.summary: MERA separates globally searchable memory from a question-specific evidence state for long-term memory question answering, training a lightweight planner via RL to issue retrieval queries conditioned on already-found evidence. Verified evidence guides subsequent retrieval without restricting access to global memory, improving answer accuracy when evidence is scattered across distant conversation turns.

entry.title: Evaluating Bounded Autonomy in Regulated Agentic AI: A Diagnostic Harness with Constitutional Rewards, Escalation Labels, and Runtime Governance

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: Introduces RegLLM, a diagnostic harness measuring bounded autonomy in regulated agentic workflows via six trustworthiness signals including citation validity, escalation correctness, and unsafe-action rate, with a deterministic runtime supervisor that blocks ungrounded answers. The same domain constitution drives evaluation, training rewards, and serving guardrails, and should-escalate labels make act-versus-defer decisions a measurable training signal.

entry.title: Zero-shot Dependency Parsing with Unsupervised Cross-Lingual Bootstrapping

author.name: Lalita Lowphansirikul, Attapol Rutherford, Jian Gang Ngui, Sarana Nutanong, Peerat Limkonchotiwat

entry.summary: This paper proposes a cross-lingual unsupervised bootstrapping method that injects syntactic knowledge into pre-trained encoder-based language models to improve zero-shot dependency parsing. The approach yields significant parsing gains on low-resource languages, and parameter-free tree probing shows the bootstrapped models better recognize syntactic structure. It matters because dependency parsing is hard to transfer cross-lingually and low-resource languages lack annotated treebanks.

entry.title: From Neurons to Conversation: Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces

author.name: Moein Khajehnejad, Forough Habibollahi, Tommaso Boccato, Margarida Sousa, Michal Olak, Francesco Jamal Sheiban, Matteo Ferrante

entry.summary: This is a review/perspective on speech brain-computer interfaces, covering how intracortical and ECoG recording, deep sequence models, and language-model-assisted decoding have enabled high-performance attempted-speech decoding and naturalistic synthesis. It argues speech BCIs are adaptive clinical systems where neural representations, hardware, decoding, language priors, feedback, and user learning interact over time. The paper synthesizes a fast-moving interdisciplinary field and frames system-level challenges beyond neural-to-text decoding.

entry.title: CoEM: Empowering Long-Context Reasoning with Commit-on-Evidence Memory

author.name: Jingguang Li, Yebo Wu, Zuyi Guo, Kailang Ma, Xianjie Dai, Han Zheng, Benwang Chen, Li Li, Can Rong, Heye Huang

entry.summary: CoEM improves chunked long-context reasoning by delaying irreversible compression of evidence: under a fixed context-memory budget, potentially useful excerpts are held verbatim in a pending set until later context clarifies their relevance, at which point they are committed to compact memory facts. This mitigates the common failure where premature compression discards details needed downstream. The approach targets bounded-memory processing of very long inputs.

entry.title: Solving Without Stopping: On-Policy Distillation at Small Scale

author.name: Hongyang Li, Yiming Zhu, Xiao Li, Caesar Wu, Said Mammar, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: The authors distill Qwen3-8B into 4B, 1.7B, and 0.6B students in both thinking and non-thinking modes to analyze what on-policy distillation transfers. They find solving ability transfers at all sizes, but knowing when a problem is solved (stopping) does not transfer in thinking mode, identifying two distinct capability ceilings. This decomposition clarifies a key limitation of distillation for long-reasoning small models.

entry.title: KUPAS MASTER: Distilling the Tacit Expertise of Master Practitioners into Agent-Ready Experience Corpora

author.name: Changmian Wang, Yuchao Ma, Xuchao Lu, Chen Zhang, Ping Sun, Jiazheng Wang, Shan Wang, Xuanwen Chen, Yihe Sun, Ziyu Lu, Jianqiang Huang, Hongzhi Li, Ziqing Xia, Kaihua Tang, Xian-Sheng Hua, Qinghua Zheng

entry.summary: KUPAS MASTER is an experience-engineering platform that converts work records and practitioner interviews into structured, traceable experience corpora for LLM agents, using a nine-layer cognitive corpus construction and six case elements (context, cues, judgment, action, boundaries, outcomes). It aims to capture tacit professional knowledge that routine records omit, making it usable by agents. This matters for deploying agents in expert domains where know-how is implicit.

entry.title: Pruning for Efficiency, Paying in Fairness: Demographic Disparities in Pruned Speech-LLMs

author.name: Ganesh Pavan Kartikeya Bharadwaj Kolluri, Michael Kampouridis, Ravi Shekhar

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies how audio-encoder pruning in SLAM-ASR speech-LLMs affects different demographic groups using Fair-Speech and Common Voice, finding that the gap between best- and worst-performing groups increases several-fold even when aggregate WER looks acceptable. Disparities appear across all encoder scales, with only the largest model hiding them behind aggregate metrics, and LoRA adaptation improves WER for all groups but benefits groups unequally. This exposes fairness risks of compression for deployment.

entry.title: Learning Semantic Inpainting for Animatable Gaussian Head Avatars

author.name: Pilseo Park, Fizza Rubab, Yiying Tong

entry.summary: SInGA creates animatable 3D Gaussian head avatars from a single image by completing unobserved facial regions via semantic inpainting in UV space. The structured UV topology and facial symmetry cues enable reliable completion of identity-specific features without multi-view observations. This addresses a key limitation of existing avatar pipelines that require multi-view capture.

entry.title: HIGS: Hierarchical Implicit Grids for Joint Geometric and Semantic Scene Understanding

author.name: Hanwen Cao, Wenqiang Wu, Kuang-Ting Tu, Mathias Otnes, Jeffrey Delmerico, Rui Wang, Yulun Tian, Nikolay Atanasov

entry.summary: HIGS introduces a hierarchical neural field using multiresolution submaps for efficient, scalable implicit scene representation supporting both geometric and semantic features through a unified query and decoding mechanism. This addresses two gaps in neural implicit representations for robotics: the lack of semantic information for high-level spatial understanding and task planning, and computational efficiency challenges in back-end optimization as environments grow. It enables robots to build continuous, differentiable, semantically rich 3D maps.

entry.title: No Corners Cut: State-Grounded Transitions for Mid-Stream Prompt Switches in Video Generation

author.name: Zejing Rao, Ketong Ren, Xiaoqiang Liu, Yiping Meng, Guoxin Zhang, Fan Tang

entry.summary: Introduces SEGUE, a framework for streaming video generators that handles mid-stream prompt switches faithfully by making intermediate state transitions explicit. A training-free planner parses the current frame and prompts to write segue prompts with roles and durations before handing control back to the user's prompt, preventing premature goal realization or heuristic shortcuts.

entry.title: MRI Super-Resolution with RCDM/WaveMix and Task-Aware Segmentation

author.name: Kavitha Viswanathan, Harsh Choudhary, Amit Sethi

entry.summary: This paper proposes an unpaired, physics-guided training pipeline for a lightweight recurrent convolutional enhancer that super-resolves 1.5T brain MRI, using a stochastic degradation operator, adversarial texture synthesis, and cycle-consistency with an anti-identity penalty. Crucially, it validates enhancement not by image fidelity metrics but by whether it improves downstream tissue segmentation across U-Net, Swin-UNet, and wavelet token-mixing segmenters.

entry.title: Is Better Teacher Supervision Enough? Unlocking Student-side Learning in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Siyuan Liu, Kanghui Tian, Yue Duan, Yutao He, Shangdong Yang, Jian Zhang, Yinghuan Shi

entry.summary: This paper identifies limited student perception, not just weak teacher supervision, as a key bottleneck in multimodal on-policy distillation, showing that providing oracle visual facts still improves student performance even with strong teachers. The authors propose S-OPD, a framework with two objectives (including Teacher-calibrated Policy Contrast) that explicitly strengthens student perceptual learning alongside token-level teacher guidance. This shifts the field's focus from teacher-side to student-side improvements in knowledge distillation for multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: TexTailor: Texture-Preserving Video Virtual Try-On via Adaptive Garment Conditioning

author.name: Zijing Qin, Jun Zhou, Ruicheng Zhang, Jiaqi Hou, Zunnan Xu, Ronghui Li, Zhenyu Xie, Xiu Li

entry.summary: TexTailor is a high-fidelity video virtual try-on framework built on a pretrained video Diffusion Transformer, targeting high-resolution scenarios where prior methods struggle. It introduces adaptive garment conditioning to better exploit reference garment information and explicit positional modeling between garment and video representations for fine-grained correspondence.

entry.title: MC-PanDA++: Simpler, Stronger, and More Robust Domain-Adaptive Panoptic Segmentation

author.name: Ivan Martinovi\'c, Josip \v{S}ari\'c, Yuki M. Asano, Sini\v{s}a \v{S}egvi\'c

entry.summary: This paper extends MC-PanDA, an unsupervised domain adaptation method for panoptic segmentation that combines mask-transformer architectures with fine-grained confidence estimation to suppress unreliable teacher gradients and avoid confirmation bias. The improved version aims for a simpler, stronger, and more robust domain-adaptive pipeline that reduces annotation costs by transferring knowledge from synthetic to unlabeled real data.

entry.title: Gaussian Stippling: Efficient Sorting-Free 3D Gaussian Rendering through Hybrid Sampling and Spatiotemporal Reconstruction

author.name: Zijian Huang, Suiliang Mai, Chuankun Zheng, Yuan Meng, Yuchi Huo

entry.summary: This work introduces Gaussian stippling, a sorting-free rendering approach for 3D Gaussian Splatting that uses stochastic transparency with discrete visibility samples instead of depth sorting and ordered alpha blending. The framework adaptively combines primitive-based and fragment-based stippling to manage spatial and temporal noise at low sample counts, and operates directly on unmodified 3DGS assets. This improves rendering efficiency while preserving compatibility with existing assets.

entry.title: MAGiDiff: Sampling the Photospheric Vector Field from UV/EUV Filtergrams

author.name: Ruoyu Wang (NYU), David Fouhey (NYU)

entry.summary: MAGiDiff uses denoising diffusion models to estimate photospheric vector magnetograms from UV/EUV filtergrams from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, an intrinsically ill-posed problem since the mapping from intensity to magnetic field lacks polarization information. This offers an alternative to demanding full Stokes inversion and disambiguation pipelines for producing solar vector magnetic field data. The work matters for solar activity modeling and space weather forecasting.

entry.title: Fiatlux: A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Humanoid Ladder Climbing and Light-Bulb Replacement

author.name: Pavel Bushuyeu, Yujin Chen, Anton Nikolaev, Brian Shu, Igor Molybog

entry.summary: Fiatlux is a benchmark built on NVIDIA Isaac Lab requiring a Unitree G1 humanoid to position a step ladder, climb it, replace a light bulb, and dispose of the spent bulb in one long-horizon episode, decomposed into twelve difficulty-weighted subtasks. It uniquely combines vertical mobility with dexterous work on a fragile payload, filling a gap left by tabletop, flat-floor, and locomotion benchmarks.

entry.title: FAST-Sync: Fast Group Synchronization for any Matrix Lie Group

author.name: Shane Holmes, Yiran Luo, Firat Taxpulat, David M. Rosen, Frank Dellaert

entry.summary: FAST-Sync provides a fast linear approximation for group synchronization over any matrix Lie group, generalizing chordal initialization to estimate unknown group elements from noisy pairwise ratios. The method serves to initialize local manifold optimizers or certifiable global solvers for core state estimation problems in robotics and vision.

entry.title: HALO: Heterogeneous Allocation Via Localized Observations for the Vehicle Routing Problem

author.name: Andrew Meighan, Hyungsub Kim, Or Dantsker

entry.summary: HALO is a hybrid method for the multi-robot vehicle routing problem that splits allocation and routing, enabling onboard, real-time fleet control under realistic decentralized constraints like limited observation and communication ranges. It targets heterogeneous robotic fleets for delivery, warehouse, and military applications where prior centralized algorithms handling up to 1,000 tasks are infeasible to deploy.

entry.title: Video2SwimFish: An Automated Pipeline for Reconstructing Controllable Fish Models and Biological Locomotion from Real Fish Videos

author.name: Hangong Chen, Linfeng Cheng, Tahsin Zaman Jilan, Ian Fuller, Lee Caesar, Jiaye Wu, Yantian Zha

entry.summary: Video2SwimFish is an automated pipeline and benchmark that reconstructs metrically scaled, controllable deformable fish models from synchronized multi-view real-fish videos, using a VLM-selected canonical frame and a VLM actor-critic loop for morphology-adapted articulation. It extracts a Biological Locomotion Manifold from observed midline curvature as a low-dimensional action space and releases paired top/front-view datasets of multiple fish.

entry.title: Drape-Compatible Tool-Tip Localization for Hand-Held Laparoscopic Instruments via UWB Carrier-Phase Ranging and Trocar-Constrained Geometry

author.name: Jinseok Lee, Dongho Yee, Minsung Kim, Younghoon Noh, Seonho Shim, Juahn Oh, Yechan Seo, Jiyul Lee, Seong Jeong, Hyuk Choi, Hyoun-Joong Kong

entry.summary: This paper proposes localizing the tool tips of draped laparoscopic instruments using ultra-wideband carrier-phase ranging between antenna nodes on instrument handles and the endoscope, combined with an IMU and trocar-constrained geometry, since sterility drapes block all optical tracking. It addresses an underdetermined estimation problem by exploiting kinematic constraints from the trocar pivot point. The work matters for surgical robotics where instrument pose must be known without contaminating the sterile field.

entry.title: Tool-Policy Co-Design for Powder Weighing in Laboratory Automation

author.name: Nikola Radulov, Xin Yang, Kevin S. Luck, Gabriella Pizzuto

entry.summary: This paper presents a bi-level optimization framework that jointly optimizes the physical morphology of a powder-dispensing tool and its control policy for robot chemists performing autonomous powder weighing. The outer loop tunes tool parameters like depth, width, and rim spike topology via Bayesian optimization while the inner loop trains the control policy across a distribution of powder flowabilities.

entry.title: Fast and Scalable Multi-Agent Distribution Matching via Partitioned Optimal Transport

author.name: Kooktae Lee, Ruchika Singh

entry.summary: The paper develops a scalable optimal-transport framework for terminal distribution matching in multi-agent systems by partitioning agents and targets into spatially corresponding blocks and solving smaller local transport problems. Under a mass-balance condition, the restricted coupling remains feasible for the global problem and provides an upper bound on Wasserstein cost, with local assignments feeding finite-horizon agent control.

entry.title: A Unified Dual Method for Matching Problems

author.name: Guillaume Houry (HeKA | U1346), Ferdinand Genans (SU, LPSM), Jean Feydy (HeKA | U1346), Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Vialard (LIGM)

entry.summary: This paper unifies a broad class of matching problems (alignment of structured objects and distributions) under a common duality-based optimization framework. It shows that objectives expressible as differences of convex functions can be recast as implicit registration problems, and applies the resulting dual method to quadratic matching with extended analysis.

entry.title: Will AI Agents Pay to Avoid Killing Animals?

author.name: jonahmattwoodward

entry.summary: Summarizing the HarvestBench study from Compassion Aligned Machine Learning, this post evaluates whether LLM agents will pay a cost to avoid killing animals while pursuing an unrelated goal, using a tractor-harvesting game where swerving costs fuel. Hit rates vary enormously (0.4% to 98.8% with moral instructions) and do not track capability; without explicit moral instruction, all six reasoning models killed over 84% of animals, and moral improvements are fragile under prompt perturbations. It is a novel probe of embedded moral behavior and instruction robustness in agents.

entry.title: Reach Into The CHOIR: Free-List Elicitation Uncovers Distinct Model Voices in LLM Ensembles

author.name: Ben Wigler, Maria Tsfasman

entry.summary: CHOIR adapts free-list elicitation from cognitive anthropology to LLM ensembles, repeatedly eliciting ranked response lists and clustering them into concepts to measure salience across models and personas. It aims to distinguish genuine perspective diversity from false plurality, where models appear independent but return the same default answers.

entry.title: Component-Aware Feedback for Self-Evolving Programs

author.name: Ethan Lin, Jinming Nian, Yi Fang

entry.summary: This paper proposes component-aware feedback for LLM-guided evolutionary program search, logging which component edits caused which fitness changes in an attribution memory that later mutations read. This addresses the instability of forcing mutator LLMs to infer edit effects from cluttered histories, particularly for locally hosted models evolving multi-component systems. It could make program search faster and more stable.

entry.title: PathAnchor: Path-Structured Evidence for Scientific Agents

author.name: Qiuhui Chen, Jiafan Lu, Shuaimin Tang, Tao Dai, Suyuan Wang, Chenrui Ji, Zhenglei Zhou, Weimin Zhong

entry.summary: PathAnchor organizes scientific evidence as source-linked Material-Sensor-Signal-System trajectories that preserve role, direction, and supporting transitions, with a controller using read-only tools to trace paths and open exact evidence before producing claim-cited answers with explicit evidence boundaries. It targets failure modes where agents retrieve relevant passages but lose functional order or overstate conclusions. Evaluated on single- and cross-paper flexible QA tasks.

entry.title: OpenJev-RLCD: A Working RLCD Implementation

author.name: Zhimin Gao, Pichao Wang

entry.summary: The paper presents a working implementation of reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions (RLCD), scoring the answer distribution a model commits to after sampling a rationale with a strictly proper scoring rule. A variance identity shows RLVR is equivalent to the mixture objective without its diversity term, explaining why RLVR induces overconfidence. This offers a principled alternative to temperature scaling for calibrated decision models.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Adaptive Evaluation: Finding High-Impact Failures Under Limited Budgets

author.name: Priyanath Maji, Spandan Ghose Chowdhury

entry.summary: The authors formulate agent evaluation as a sequential budget allocation problem and propose a risk-aware contextual Thompson Sampling policy that combines scenario context and impact scores with observed failures. Tested by offline replay over roughly 70 scenarios, the method targets finding high-impact failures under limited evaluation budgets.

entry.title: RefCon: Iterative Refinement and Contrastive Memory Extraction for Context-Evolving Agent

author.name: Ubaidillah Ariq Prathama, Bo Liu, Yeo Boon Hong, Yu-Xuan Huang, Yangkai Ding, Tao Yu

entry.summary: RefCon extracts agent memories without gold labels by combining sequential self-refinement with parallel self-contrast, improving memory quality as test-time compute scales. On AppWorld and BFCL-V3 it delivers gains including 21.6% on ACE and 16.6% on ReMe over no-scaling baselines, with a diversity variant reaching 35.5% on ReasoningBank.

entry.title: ConflictGuide: AutoResearch Improves When Competing Behaviors Are Made Visible

author.name: Binqian Xu, Qiran Zou, Xiangbo Shu, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: The paper finds that LLM-based AutoResearch systems relying on scalar task-performance feedback cannot see how edits affect competing behaviors, which limits progress once gains plateau. Introducing explicit competing-behavior feedback in matched-budget experiments increases the share of proposals that improve both behaviors and sustains search progress beyond scalar-only plateaus.

entry.title: WorldAuditBench: Interactive 3D World Auditing with Multimodal Agents

author.name: Ziyan Jiang, Jingbo Yang, Jiabao Ji, Yujian Liu, Qiucheng Wu, Tommi Jaakkola, Yang Zhang, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: WorldAuditBench is a benchmark for auditing interactive 3D simulated environments for anomalies such as floating objects or traversable walls, using multimodal agents that combine navigation with visual reasoning. It disentangles the action and perception capabilities required, revealing how current VLMs and VLAs fall short. This supports reliability of 3D worlds used to study intelligent behavior.

entry.title: GestAdapt: Workspace-Conditioned Co-Speech Gesture Generation for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Bosong Ding, Xianglin Zhang, Miao Xin, Murat Kirtay, Giacomo Spigler

entry.summary: GestAdapt conditions co-speech gesture generation on a prescribed wrist workspace so humanoid robots adapt gestures to physical constraints, such as speaking next to a wall, rather than merely correcting unconstrained motions. It learns a shared motion representation across six co-speech corpora and supports retargeting to different robot embodiments.

entry.title: ReLaG: A Scalable Framework Generalizing Random Splits to Data with Latent Relations

author.name: Anthony Lavertu, Jacob Cote, Sophie Gobeil, Jacques Corbeil, Isabeau Premont-Schwarz, Pascal Germain

entry.summary: ReLaG is a modality-agnostic framework that models sample relatedness via a hierarchical latent-variable process and infers groups of related samples using proximity graphs and community detection to produce independent train-test splits. It matches existing relation-aware splitting methods on molecular and protein datasets while scaling substantially better, plus a label-free procedure for tuning splitting resolution.

entry.title: Exo2EgoHOI: Hand-Object-Interaction Aware Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation

author.name: Hongjia Zhai, Xiyu Zhang, Haoran Zhang, Zhichao Ye, Haomin Liu, Guofeng Zhang, Ian Reid, Xingxing Zuo

entry.summary: Exo2EgoHOI is a video generation framework that converts third-person manipulation videos into first-person views while preserving hand-object interactions, using a unified 4D HOI prior combining scene and object-centric anchoring. It targets scalable egocentric data generation for embodied intelligence, where existing methods lose fine-grained interaction fidelity under large viewpoint changes.

entry.title: Where the Evidence Lives: Auditing AI Companions' Self-Descriptions

author.name: Seiya Ikeda, Shin-nosuke Ishikawa

entry.summary: Argues that AI companion agents' self-descriptions (e.g., claims about memory, understanding, or relational change) are checkable by users only where the evidence is accessible to them, in behavior or in themselves, not in internal machinery. The authors demonstrate an audit procedure comparing an agent's self-descriptions against user judgments and implementation records, applied to Lita, a proactive companion deployed for a month with nine colleagues.

entry.title: FFASR: Benchmarking Far-Field Automatic Speech Recognition using High-Fidelity Simulated RIRs

author.name: Shivam Saini, Eric Bezzam, Georg G\"otz, Alessia Milo, Steinar Gu{\dh}j\'onsson, Konstantinos Gkanos, Finnur Pind, Daniel Gert Nielsen

entry.summary: FFASR provides a held-out corpus of 15,637 utterances and an open leaderboard spanning nine single-factor acoustic conditions, from near-field to moving-talker far-field scenarios, using hybrid wave and geometrical-acoustics room impulse responses from 14 furnished rooms. Newly recorded dry speech and withheld test waveforms resist training-data contamination.

entry.title: What Streaming Anomaly Detection Finds (and Misses) in Industrial Time Series

author.name: Magali Parrino, Antoine Ajenjo, Emmanuel Remy, Pierre Stephan, Paul Boniol

entry.summary: In collaboration with EDF, this paper compares streaming anomaly detection methods against online-deployed state-of-the-art TSAD models on a real nuclear power plant dataset, also evaluating automated anomaly detection in a streaming context. Results show higher consistency for online TSAD and strong robustness from ensembling strategies.

entry.title: Scale and Selection: What Makes Automatic Harness Evolution Work for Visual-Interface Robot Agents

author.name: Zhijie Wei, Ferris Tan, Jinghui Wang

entry.summary: The authors show that a coding agent's harness for controlling a browser-based 3D robot interface can itself be improved automatically by an optimizer coding agent, and identify two key factors: the number of rollouts per round (single rollouts are noisy binary signals that let lucky revisions get promoted) and the selection strategy governing which revisions are accepted.

entry.title: From Search to Signal: Online Post-Training in Automatic Heuristic Design

author.name: Yilun Yuan, Tianyu Zhou, Zhenzhou Tang

entry.summary: The paper examines LLM-based automatic heuristic design where evaluated candidate outcomes both drive search and serve as RLVR training signals, creating a search-coupled feedback loop. It analyzes how to convert candidate outcomes into useful model updates given that validity and performance do not uniquely determine them.

entry.title: Probabilistic Adversarial Training

author.name: Andi Zhang, Xingyu Zhao, Siddartha Khastgir

entry.summary: The paper frames adversarial examples as arising from overlap between a distance-based distribution and a victim-classifier-induced distribution, motivating a KL-based robustness objective. It proves a lower bound relating this KL divergence to probabilistic robustness and derives a tractable training method that pushes the distributions apart to increase robustness.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory Selection for Parallel Scaling of Search Agents

author.name: Qisheng Zhou, Zhen Xiong, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: TRACE reframes answer consolidation in parallel search as trajectory selection, using a lightweight learned selector that ranks completed rollouts by the search evidence behind their answers. It preserves query and evidence provenance, links rollouts through shared content or document identity, and propagates information across these relations using frozen text embeddings trained with answer-level supervision.

entry.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents

author.name: Haoyuan Deng, Jiebin Liu, Tengxiao Zhang, Langning Yan, Hongye Cao, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: DynaHarness couples slow semantic reasoning with fast physical governance via a shared execution contract for long-horizon robot manipulation, converting episode-level failure evidence into validated capability revisions. The fast brain grounds and monitors commands, refuses unresolved actions, substitutes capabilities, and requests help, enabling self-evolving robot agents. Addresses the timescale mismatch in hierarchical robot architectures.

entry.title: When a Flatness Proxy Is Not a Function: Robustness Certificates and Training Interventions

author.name: Vicente Opazo, Jose Calatayud-Mateu, Cristobal Rojas, Cristian Buc Calderon

entry.summary: The paper shows that a last-layer relative-flatness proxy used for robustness certificates and training interventions is not a well-defined function of the predictor: certificates can underestimate loss increases by over 210x, and gauge transformations like common-row softmax shifts can make the proxy unbounded while preserving predictions. The authors derive a globally valid, gauge-invariant feature-space repair and quantify how reference-class choices inflate the proxy.

entry.title: Amortized Data Borrowing with Exchangeability-Aware Neural Posterior Estimation

author.name: Chin-Hung Huang, JooChul Lee, Huan He

entry.summary: This work proposes amortized neural posterior estimation as a replacement for classical Bayesian dynamic borrowing in clinical drug development, where external or historical trial data can augment small concurrent studies. A single network is pretrained on simulated pairs spanning covariate shift, outcome drift, and non-exchangeability, avoiding hand-specified priors and expensive MCMC inference at deployment. The approach makes principled external-data borrowing faster and more generalizable.

entry.title: Learning Where to Steer: Noise-Space Geometry for Efficient Offline Multi-Objective Optimization with Generative Models

author.name: Yuan Lu, Esha Singh, Yi-An Ma, Yusu Wang

entry.summary: The paper targets offline multi-objective optimization with diffusion models, observing that instead of guiding every sampling step, objectives as functions of the initial noise are sensitive to only a few directions. The authors estimate these directions once per task using a Recursive Feature Machine from function values alone, then steer via a small cache that serves every trade-off without modifying the sampling process. On Off-MOO-Bench this yields efficient Pareto-front optimization.

entry.title: Prequential E-Values for Selected-GP Near-Optimality Certificates

author.name: Ami Tavory, Noa Cohen

entry.summary: The paper introduces an auditable stopping rule for expensive black-box optimization (e.g., hyperparameter tuning) using prequential e-values, certifying when the best evaluated value is within epsilon of the global optimum. It addresses the common but statistically invalid practice of tuning the GP confidence envelope on the same adaptive evaluations used for certification.

entry.title: Understanding Head Geometry and Dynamics in Federated Regression through a Natural Solution Selection Rule: An Unconstrained Feature Model Analysis

author.name: Chuang Ma, Tomoyuki Obuchi

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies head-selection ambiguity in federated regression with private backbones and a shared linear head, introducing a natural rule where each client returns the optimal head closest to the broadcast head. Using an unconstrained feature model, it shows a vanishing proximal penalty realizes this rule and derives a closed recursion converging to the Bures-Wasserstein barycenter.

entry.title: Can Domain Generalization be Guaranteed in Small-Sample Learning?

author.name: Hong Zheng

entry.summary: This work establishes the first theoretical guarantees for Structural Risk Minimization in domain generalization, deriving learning consistency and generalization bounds based on stability that become tight under a stability condition on hypotheses. It extends classical SRM theory beyond the i.i.d. assumption to the small-sample DG setting.

entry.title: Stable Transformers for Graph Generation

author.name: Luca Miglior, Alessio Gravina, Davide Bacciu

entry.summary: This work analyzes depth-related degradation in Graph Transformers used as denoisers for graph generation from a dynamical systems perspective, showing that repeated self-attention becomes dissipative, causing vanishing gradients and representation collapse. The authors construct a permutation-equivariant test setup and propose stabilization to keep deep GT denoisers effective for graph generation.

entry.title: Dimension-Free Rank Lifting from Random Hyperplane Arrangements

author.name: Luca Becchetti, Matteo Russo, Ruben Skorupinski

entry.summary: The authors prove that for positively homogeneous nonpolynomial activations, a random hidden layer with roughly (1/theta)*max(m, log(1/delta)) neurons suffices to lift a separated dataset of m points to full row rank, independent of input dimension. This exponentially improves prior dimensional guarantees for sign-type activations.

entry.title: Conformal Factuality Control for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Muhammad Aimal Rehman, Chi-Kuang Yeh

entry.summary: The paper tests whether split-conformal claim filtering, previously developed for single-hop RAG, remains effective for multi-hop RAG where retrieval and reasoning proceed through dependent stages. Evaluations on HotpotQA, Natural Questions, and TriviaQA with Llama 3.1 8B and GPT-4o-mini show increasingly stringent conformal targets consistently increase factual support. This extends statistical guarantees on generated-claim factuality to more realistic multi-stage settings.

entry.title: GazeFlow: From Human Gaze Behavior to Generative Egocentric Gaze Prediction

author.name: Sheng Zhao, Weikai Lin, Yuhao Zhu

entry.summary: GazeFlow models egocentric gaze as a joint distribution over temporal trajectories using conditional flow matching, conditioned on top-down task information and bottom-up visual saliency, with temporal dynamics alternating between fixations and saccades. A learned velocity field transports Gaussian noise samples into plausible gaze trajectories.

entry.title: PrecipJEPA: JEPA-Regularized Future-State Prediction with Motion-Source Rendering for Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Yufeng Zhu, Dan Niu, Qiliang Wu, Weiwei Huang, Yixiao Liang, Yongchao Feng, Chunlei Shi

entry.summary: PrecipJEPA couples a structured forecasting path, which builds future radar states from spatiotemporal tokens and dynamics summaries, with an auxiliary JEPA-regularized path that enriches encoder representations from observed radar history. It separates echo displacement from intensity change to improve long-horizon precipitation nowcasting while preserving localized high-intensity structures.

entry.title: Synthetic Data Characterization via Training Dynamics

author.name: Irene Lago, Ana Ezquerro, David Vilares

entry.summary: The paper characterizes LLM-generated data through sample-level learnability, deriving empirical distributions from encoder training dynamics and comparing them to human-written data across classification, labeling, and tree prediction tasks. It also examines how learnability-based data selection strategies affect machine versus organic data differently. This offers a new lens for evaluating synthetic data quality beyond surface statistics.

entry.title: Better Supervision Is Nearby: Neighborhood On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Xincheng Wei, Yifan Ding, Yoshua Li, Yuquan Lu, Ziheng Li, Yi Lu, Dongsheng Ma, Rongxiang Weng, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: The paper extends on-policy self-distillation for mathematical reasoning by using local perturbations of the privileged teacher's parameters, which reveal complementary reference-aligned corrections at student-visited states. Neighborhood OPSD builds a compact pool of frozen experts via greedy offline selection and combines their corrections into richer supervision. This improves distillation-based training of reasoning models.

entry.title: Estimation of the Label-Noise Transition Matrix with Performance Guarantees via Selective Classification

author.name: Xabier de Juan, Santiago Mazuelas, Yilun Zhu, Clayton Scott

entry.summary: The authors propose estimating the label-noise transition matrix via one-sided selective classification, bypassing fragile class-posterior estimation while providing finite-sample performance guarantees and leveraging flexible binary classifiers. They also introduce effective algorithms built on this methodology. This improves the theoretical foundation of learning from noisily labeled data, which is increasingly common at scale.

entry.title: When Successful Memories Mislead Embodied Agents:Memory Adaption For Task-Conditioned Execution

author.name: Quanquan Li, Hongbo Zhang, Yihe Chi, Liuyang Song, Jingyu Li, Yuxiang Huang, Hongzhen Zhang, Guitao Cao

entry.summary: The paper introduces MATE, a deterministic post-retrieval procedure that adapts retrieved experience trajectories for embodied agents, removing obsolete control context and extracting condition-action-effect transitions. It addresses the problem that previously successful trajectories may be unsuitable in new execution contexts.

entry.title: DeepRewind: Predicting and Repairing Premature Commitments in Deep Research Agents

author.name: Amirhossein Abaskohi, Amirhossein Dabiriaghdam, Lele Wang, Peter West, Giuseppe Carenini

entry.summary: DeepRewind is a control layer for deep research agents that maintains a typed epistemic graph of sources, evidence, claims, hypotheses, and commitments, predicting reversibility of intermediate conclusions before accepting them. It estimates recovery cost, hypothesis narrowing, and information loss to detect premature commitments that later reasoning would otherwise reinforce. This targets a real failure mode in long-horizon research agents.

entry.title: RAEGNet: Relation-Aware Evidence Graph Network for Harm-Aware Multimodal Fake News Detection

author.name: Wenbin Shen, Guoxuan Qin, Guangxu Yao, Baodong Wang, Yuanbo Rui, Zhongjie Ba, Zhichao Lian

entry.summary: RAEGNet pairs an event-level evidence retrieval framework with a relation-aware directed evidence graph that encodes news-evidence stance relations and evidence-evidence interactions, moving beyond entity-level retrieval that introduces event-irrelevant noise. It also models differences in harm across fake news instances rather than optimizing only overall accuracy.

entry.title: SemOPT: Fixing Semantic Errors in LLM-based Optimization Modeling via Reward-Guided Search

author.name: Zetong Zhou, Wentao Zhang, Jingyuan Wang, Yifan Yang, Zizhuo Wang, Shixi Hu

entry.summary: SemOPT targets semantic errors in LLM-generated optimization models — code that runs and returns an objective but violates problem intent, which is harder to detect than syntactic errors. It uses reward-guided search to identify and rectify these silent violations in natural-language-to-solver-code translation.

entry.title: Who Warmed the Archives? LLMs Overestimate Historical Warmth

author.name: Claudiu Creanga, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LLMs can extract the Pfister temperature index from five centuries of German archival text for climate reconstruction, and whether their errors are safe for cross-century comparison. Lexical baselines beat all fine-tuned transformers, and all six tested LLMs (including Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek v4 Flash, and Claude models) exhibit systematic era-linked bias, overestimating historical warmth.

entry.title: CompOrca: Corpus-Scale Compliance Labelling of Instruction-Tuning Data

author.name: Philipp E. Glass, Alina Miron

entry.summary: Presents CompOrca, a compliance labelling of the entire 4.2-million-example OpenOrca corpus, classifying every example as compliant or noncompliant via five independent passes of a large open-weight judge, released with vote counts and unanimity partitions. Findings include that single-pass flagging overcounts noncompliance (2.7-3.2 percent) relative to unanimous labels (1.28 percent).

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Routing for Reliable Reasoning on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices

author.name: Avyay Sadhu, Alvaro Velasquez, Lekai Chen

entry.summary: The authors present a neurosymbolic router that classifies incoming queries and dispatches them to the cheapest correct solver, routing structured arithmetic, algebra, and logic tasks to deterministic symbolic engines rather than forcing small probabilistic edge models to approximate them. This improves accuracy and energy efficiency for reasoning on resource-constrained devices while preserving private, offline inference. The observation that many reasoning-looking queries are structurally deterministic is the key insight.

entry.title: CHAIN: Calibrated LLM Forecasting via Causal-Temporal Hypergraph Inference

author.name: Wenjin Liu, Chenxi Wang, Yue Lu, Zhe Cui, Haoran Luo

entry.summary: CHAIN addresses systematic calibration bias in LLM probabilistic event forecasting by decomposing prediction over causal-temporal hypergraphs into three stages: evidence weighting, evidence aggregation, and source fusion, with stage-specific mechanisms to mitigate bias at its structural source rather than post hoc. Calibrated probabilistic outputs matter for trustworthy decision-making under uncertainty. The structural decomposition of the prediction process is the key methodological idea.

entry.title: Effective Dense Retrieval using Only In-Context Examples

author.name: Nour Jedidi, Abdul Basit Ali, Hang Li, Jimmy Lin

entry.summary: RICE is a training-free approach that turns decoder-only LLMs into dense retrievers by conditioning on a few in-context examples that provide shared context for query and document encoding, producing high-quality embeddings without retriever training. Results show substantially improved accuracy over prompt-based LLM embeddings. This simplifies building LLM-based dense retrieval systems.

entry.title: Aperture: Training-Free Multiscale Concept Bottlenecks for Remote Sensing

author.name: Rishabh Mondal, Nipun Batra, Utkarsh Mall

entry.summary: APERTURE brings training-free concept-bottleneck interpretability to remote sensing, where existing concept models are either too expensive to train or perform poorly without annotations. It uses multiscale concept bottlenecks with greedy quadtree routing to locate small concepts in image space, and replaces contrastive vision-language models with pretrained MLLMs to obtain reliable concept scores in concept space. Concept scores are blended at global and local levels for interpretable earth observation.

entry.title: Here the World in Stereo: Learning Dynamic Spatial Correspondence for Immersive Joint Video-Audio Generation

author.name: Hanmo Chen, Chengcheng Liu, Tianxiao Chen, Zheyu Zhang, Siming Zheng, Jinwei Chen, Xu Yang, Cheng Deng, Bo Li, Peng-tao Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces StereoBind, a framework for joint video-audio generation that produces stereo audio whose perceived sound location evolves consistently with the motion of the corresponding visual source. It defines Dynamic Spatial Correspondence and binds visual motion tracks to stereo sound generation via three complementary mechanisms, targeting AR/VR and interactive gaming.

entry.title: OP-CAD: On-Policy Clean-Audio Distillation for Robust Audio-Visual Reasoning

author.name: Xingming Shui, Dapeng Chen, Bowei Liu, Jingqi Tian, Minfu Li, Kun Yi, Jiapeng Hong, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: OP-CAD is a curriculum-based privileged self-distillation framework that improves omni-modal LLM robustness to environmental noise and competing speech in audio-visual question answering, prioritizing token positions affected by acoustic interference during on-policy distillation. Training uses clean-audio privileges so the student learns to resist acoustic interference while preserving useful audio evidence.

entry.title: EffGS: Efficient and High-Fidelity Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Changbai Li, Shuo Yang, Yichen Yang, Shuwei Shao, Huobin Tan

entry.summary: EffGS is a general acceleration framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting that combines frequency-aware guidance, localized density control, and adaptive primitive scale modulation to improve training and rendering efficiency. It maintains or improves reconstruction quality on both bounded and large-scale scenes where prior acceleration methods degrade.

entry.title: Diffusable Latents from Structure-Agnostic Distillation

author.name: Adrien Ramanana Rahary, Nicolas Dufour, Patrick P\'erez, David Picard

entry.summary: The paper shows that aligning a single pooled image-level descriptor to a teacher feature performs as well as or better than dense position-wise distillation for making autoencoder latents more diffusable, removing the constraint that latent layout mirror teacher layout. It compares first-order and relational objectives across latent shapes and modalities, including cross-modal distillation of a text encoder into an image autoencoder.

entry.title: NavHarness: Adaptive Goals for Agentic Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Haoxiang Shi, Zaijing Li, Muhe Ding, Xiang Deng, Yaowei Wang, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: NavHarness is an agentic VLN framework with specialized Goal, Verify, and Memory agents: adaptive local goals keep long-horizon execution aligned with the intended route, verification checks goal completion, and memory compression reduces inference overhead from growing interaction history.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of a Driving VLA to Class 8 Trucks

author.name: Satyajeet Das, Aaron Buxbaum, Niels Joubert, Gaurav S. Sukhatme

entry.summary: The authors adapt an off-the-shelf driving vision-language-action model, NVIDIA's Alpamayo 1.5, to Class 8 trucks by fine-tuning only its action-generation stack on a few hundred real-world construction and accident scenarios, followed by a steering stage introducing Flow Velocity Sampling. This adapt-then-steer strategy avoids training a truck VLA from scratch while handling geometry and dynamics differences.

entry.title: LBDU-VIO: Learned Bias Dynamics and Uncertainty for Visual-Inertial Odometry with Unreliable Vision

author.name: Qizhi Guo, Junning Lyu, Defu Lin, Shaoming He

entry.summary: LBDU-VIO is a learning-augmented multi-state constraint Kalman filter for visual-inertial odometry that replaces random-walk bias assumptions with a neural ODE modeling continuous-time bias dynamics and predicts motion-adaptive IMU measurement noise covariances. These learned components improve filter robustness for aerial robots when visual information is unreliable.

entry.title: Decode-Latency Feedback Prefill: A Model-Free Controller and Its Generalization Limits

author.name: Gaurav Agarwal, Ashish Garg, Isha Singhal

entry.summary: DLFP is a model-free controller for concurrent LLM inference that resizes prefill chunks based on observed decode-latency feedback, reducing interference where prefilling a new long prompt delays tokens for requests already decoding. Implemented in vLLM and evaluated with open-loop Poisson arrivals, exact token accounting, and NVIDIA telemetry, the paper also explicitly documents its generalization limits.

entry.title: Where Scientific Search Agents Fail: Decision-Checkpoint Auditing of Exposure and Inspection Attempts

author.name: Hongmin Li, Wanli Zhao

entry.summary: This work introduces decision checkpoints that record an agent's observations and tool actions during inference, enabling attribution of failure to never encountering a target paper, failing to inspect it, or inspecting without using it. Applied to 540 AutoResearchBench Deep questions, the audit reveals that keyword search improves accuracy over raw search but also increases incorrect answers after the target was exposed. It offers a finer-grained diagnostic lens than final-answer accuracy.

entry.title: GraphCert: Bootstrap Agentic Graph Reasoning with Certified Evidence Rubrics

author.name: Weiqi Jiang, Yuchen Ying, Rui Wang, Kaixuan Chen, Bingde Hu, Shunyu Liu, Yu Wang, Tongya Zheng

entry.summary: GraphCert bootstraps training data for agentic graph reasoning using a Bootstrapped Graph Quizzer that generates graph-grounded QA pairs with certified evidence rubrics, avoiding costly manual trajectory collection and the privacy risk of exposing sensitive graph data to proprietary LLMs. It addresses supervision scalability for graph agents. The certified evidence framing supports verifiable multi-step reasoning.

entry.title: Reserve-Aware Contrast Certificates for Conservative Bandits with Uncertain Baselines

author.name: Qinchuan Cheng

entry.summary: Reserve-C4B improves conservative bandits by bounding the baseline-relative contrast directly instead of separately bounding candidate and baseline rewards, which double-charges shared estimation error. It includes a reserve ledger separating evidence from permitted deficit, a prefix-refresh extension, and self-normalized confidence sets for simultaneous validity with linear rewards.

entry.title: DualCast: A Dual-Path Language Model for Bimodal Financial Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Wentao Zhao, Hongqiang Wu, Shanghang Liu, Zhaochen Zan, Yu Zhang, Biqing Huang

entry.summary: DualCast extends a frozen Qwen3-8B language model with a learned discrete financial vocabulary for forecasting across heterogeneous assets plus news. It represents return patches via summary and residual shape tokens and introduces adaptive frequency-equalizing residual vector quantization to improve codebook utilization, training only new embeddings and heads on the frozen backbone. This is an efficient approach to bimodal financial forecasting.

entry.title: Policy-Conditioned AI-Use Detection: An Evidentiary Framework for Academic Publishing

author.name: Jairo Diaz-Rodriguez, Mumin Jia

entry.summary: The authors argue that AI detection targeting whether a model wrote text is misaligned with what conferences and journals need to decide, and propose policy-conditioned AI-use detection, an evidentiary framework that treats the governing AI-use policy as an explicit input and reports calibrated hypotheses and uncertainty rather than verdicts. Benchmarks are built from reproducible workflows.

entry.title: Security-Enhanced Seed-Based Weight Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Qiuyu Ren, Sudipta Paria, Aritra Dasgupta, Swarup Bhunia

entry.summary: Seed-Q is a sensitivity-aware, seed-based weight compression framework for LLMs that uses LFSR-based pseudo-random weight generation with non-uniform bit allocation, giving more representation budget to sensitive weights without requiring side information. It targets storage, memory bandwidth, and energy costs while adding a security dimension to compression.

entry.title: Towards Universal Wasserstein Barycenters through Flow Matching

author.name: Eduardo Fernandes Montesuma

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Universal Barycenter Approximation over the Wasserstein simplex and proposes BaryFM, a flow-matching model that transports marginal measures into any weighted Wasserstein barycenter, allowing sampling from barycenters via an ODE after training. This generalizes fixed-weight barycenter computation to the whole weight simplex.

entry.title: Uncovering Uncontrolled Repetition through Residual Stream Dynamics

author.name: Yuanhe Zhang, Xinyao Zhou, Haoran Gao, Yuyao Zhang, Zhenhong Zhou, Fanyu Meng, Li Sun, Sen Su

entry.summary: Investigates how uncontrolled repetition, which can prolong LLM generation and enable resource consumption attacks, emerges in large vision-language models. The proposed Tokenwise Residual Comparison (TRC) method identifies and localizes repetition-related anomalies in residual stream dynamics during generation, extending prior feature-based analyses to earlier layers.

entry.title: CellMSA: Context Modeling for Single-Cell Representation Learning

author.name: Suyuan Zhao, Minghao Liu, Yizhen Luo, Zaiqing Nie

entry.summary: CellMSA argues that single-cell foundation models should exploit relational information across batches and cell types rather than encoding cells independently, using cross-cell consistency and variation to capture gene-gene dependencies tied to cell states. The proposed attention-based context modeling improves representation quality under sparsity and batch effects.

entry.title: HO-FL: Hybrid-Order Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Edge Devices

author.name: Qiyuan Chen, Xian Wu, Yanan Ma, Xianhao Chen

entry.summary: HO-FL hybridizes zeroth-order and first-order optimization in federated learning, training the bottom segment of a model with ZO and the top with FO so memory-constrained devices can pick their order boundary while training one global model. The convergence analysis reveals a new trade-off where favoring clients with larger FO segments improves update accuracy but underrepresents others. It tackles a practical fairness-efficiency tension in edge FL.

entry.title: HiWE: Hierarchical World Knowledge Model with Visual Keypoint Enhancement for Zero-Shot 3D Path Planning

author.name: Guoqing Ma, Mingqi Yuan, Chen Gao, Jiayu Chen, Shan Yu
