It addresses noisy signals, delayed feedback, and catastrophic divergence that limit existing L2O methods versus hand-crafted schedules like Warmup-Stable-Decay.

entry.title: Beyond Verbalized Confidence: Calibrating Reasoners with Differentiable Readouts

author.name: Chenxiao Fan, Chongming Gao, Gangyi Zhang, Leyang Shen, Yaxin Gong, Jiamin Wang, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Fuli Feng, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: CREDO addresses systematic overconfidence in RLVR-trained reasoning models by replacing sampled textual confidence with a deterministic, differentiable readout inside the RLVR loop. This removes variance and value collapse of sampled confidences and allows direct calibration losses rather than scalar rewards. Important for trustworthy deployment of reasoning LLMs.

entry.title: BA-DPO: Bias-Adjusted Direct Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment

author.name: Antonio Ferrara, Alberto Rumi, Francesco Bonchi

entry.summary: BA-DPO generalizes DPO by adding a bias parameter per annotator toward responses carrying a declared attribute, preventing systematic annotator biases (gender, ethnicity, length, formatting) from being absorbed and amplified during preference alignment. Existing methods handle only length bias or disagreement, not arbitrary attribute biases.

entry.title: DRIFT: Disentangled Responsive-Invariant Flow Transport for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Mustapha Bounoua, Giulio Franzese, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: DRIFT uses flow matching to predict cellular responses to perturbations while disentangling responsive components from invariant cell-to-cell variability, avoiding confounding effects of unpaired single-cell RNA sequencing data. Unlike prior disentangled approaches, it does not prescribe perturbation mechanisms, learning the response transport flexibly.

entry.title: TANGO: Watermarking Masked Diffusion Language Models in Token Pairs

author.name: Kasra Arabi, Nir Weinberger, Micah Goldblum, Niv Cohen

entry.summary: TANGO is a watermarking scheme for masked-diffusion language models that keys each new token to a nearby already-unmasked token, avoiding the failure modes of left-to-right watermarks and frequency-recoverable fixed green lists. The paired-key design resists attackers who compare token distributions to forge detector-passing text.

entry.title: Teacher-Student Gaps Are Not Enough: Outcome-Guided On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Autonomous Agents

author.name: Tong Zhang, Zhou Liu, Yihao Liu, Jiahua Bao, Xuchen Li, Honglin Lin, Tao Cheng, Zhihan Yu, Kai Tang, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Shows that in on-policy distillation for multi-turn agents, large teacher-student token-level gaps are not reliable indicators of where teacher supervision helps: the benefit depends on future environment interaction. Proposes outcome-guided OPD that allocates supervision based on eventual outcomes rather than instantaneous distributional gaps.

entry.title: Quasi Linear Kernel Attention with Infinite Capacity

author.name: Nicolaj Rux, Johannes Hertrich, Sebastian Neumayer

entry.summary: Introduces a capacity metric for kernel attention measuring the maximum sequence length over which the attention matrix can approximate the identity, showing softmax, Gauss, and Laplace kernels have infinite capacity while common quasi-linear kernels from finite-dimensional feature maps do not. Uses this lens to identify kernels retaining expressivity at quasi-linear cost.

entry.title: CLIMB: A Clinical Multimorbidity Benchmark for Diagnosing Co-occurring Conditions through Multiturn Conversations

author.name: Yusuf Kesmen, Aniruddha Mukherjee, Yena Chang, David Sasu, Trevor Brokowski, Alexandra V. Kulinkina, Kristina Keitel, Akhil Arora, Lars Henning Klein, Mary-Anne Hartley

entry.summary: CLIMB is a benchmark where a doctor LLM interviews a simulated patient to recover a ground-truth set of co-occurring clinical conditions, with cases synthesized from clinical decision algorithms and diagnostic datasets. Across six frontier and open models, none recovers the exact condition set in more than 10 percent of interactive cases, revealing major gaps in multi-turn clinical reasoning.

entry.title: Cartridges++: KV Cache Compression without Off-Context Derailment

author.name: Sonia Laguna, Joao Monteiro, Marco Cuturi, Pierre Ablin, Eleonora Gualdoni

entry.summary: This work extends Cartridges, a learned KV cache compression method for serving long documents, by identifying failure on off-context queries where compressed caches derail model behavior. Cartridges++ addresses this limitation, improving robustness of compressed KV representations beyond document-related on-context questions, which matters for practical LLM serving with strong context-length memory savings.

entry.title: Panoptic Scene Program Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Chika Maduabuchi

entry.summary: PSP-DiT is a diffusion-transformer text-to-image architecture that treats a panoptic scene program as a first-class latent variable, jointly denoising image and scene-program latents with grounding and cycle-consistency objectives. It targets persistent weaknesses of image generators in compositional prompts involving counting, attribute ownership, and spatial relations.

entry.title: JEPA Learns What the Mask Leaves Unrecoverable

author.name: Peng Xie, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: This paper gives a theoretical account of why joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) are sensitive to mask structure: masks are linear measurements, and in a wavelet basis atoms fully inside the hidden region lie in the null space, so easily recoverable targets admit shortcut solutions that the moving-average target encoder can make self-consistent. What prevents shortcuts is the coarse-scale content the mask leaves unrecoverable, given sufficient context near each target. This provides a principled explanation for the empirical block-mask-vs-scattered-mask puzzle in self-supervised learning.

entry.title: In-Flight KV Cache with Clean Anchors for Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion

author.name: Yikai Wang, Xiao Han, Mengmeng Xu, Juan Camilo Perez, Yiannis Douratsos, Sen He, Zijian Zhou, Fei Zhang, Zhaochong An, Juan-Manuel Perez-Rua, Chen Change Loy, Tao Xiang

entry.summary: FlashForward reuses the KV cache already computed during denoising forwards in few-step autoregressive video diffusion, avoiding the expensive cache-update-only model forwards that prior methods used to reconstruct clean caches for previously generated chunks. Stage-specific caches become available for the next chunk after one denoising stage, and per-stage GPU assignment enables further efficiency. This directly reduces the compute cost of long video generation, a resource-intensive frontier application.

entry.title: Groupwise Agentic Grading and Advantage Redistribution for Code Agent RL

author.name: Jinhao Dong, Liang Zhao, Zihao Yue, Wenhan Ma, Linghao Zhang, Lei Li, Shicheng Li, Yifan Song, Bowen Ye, Fuli Luo

entry.summary: GAGAR addresses a weakness in GRPO-based RL for code agents, where all test-passing trajectories receive identical advantages regardless of implementation quality. Built on dynamic sampling that retains mixed-outcome groups, it places trajectories in a shared workspace where an agent grades quality and redistributes advantages to favor clean, targeted implementations over those with unnecessary or out-of-scope changes. This adds a quality-aware credit signal beyond binary test rewards for code-agent training.

entry.title: Copper-Policy: Focus on the Representation for Robust Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zexin Feng, Yixu Feng, Lingyu Xiao, Shang Su, Kexin Zheng, Chang Xu, Mengkai Shi, Shuo Feng, Xintao Yan

entry.summary: Copper-Policy is a robot manipulation approach that learns a compact world representation jointly with the policy via temporal joint-embedding prediction of future observation embeddings conditioned on task intention, avoiding costly pixel- or latent-space future reconstruction used in World Action Models. The policy retains access to current-frame spatial detail for execution, aiming to capture co-training benefits at much lower cost.

entry.title: Multimodal LLMs Outperform Pathology Foundation Models in Cross-Domain Histological Similarity

author.name: Yishu Zhang, Yun Li, Daiwei Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that general-purpose multimodal LLMs consistently outperform specialized pathology foundation models on cross-domain histological similarity judgments, evaluated via the released MOSAIC benchmark across 17 models and 6 datasets. Specialized encoders often rank same-institution different-disease tiles as more similar than same-disease different-institution tiles, a clinically dangerous failure mode.

entry.title: The Statistical Benefits of Multiple Responses for Learning from Demonstrations

author.name: Chandramauli Chakraborty, Cong Ma

entry.summary: The paper analyzes pass@k learning from demonstrations when the demonstrator is not optimal, showing a qualitatively stronger benefit than the known logarithmic improvement under optimal demonstrators. In a finite reward-class model without reward feedback, moving from pass@1 to any pass@k with k at least 2 changes worst-case dependence on target accuracy from 1/epsilon-squared to 1/epsilon, uniformly over demonstrator quality. This gives theoretical justification for best-of-k evaluation and training practices.

entry.title: Positions Are Not Facts: The Mismatch Between KV Caches and Memory

author.name: Changhai Zhou, Yuhua Zhou, Shiyang Zhang, Jun Gao, Zhen Li, Hua Wu, Hanchao Yu, Haifeng Wang

entry.summary: This controlled study examines how language models should update KV-cached history when facts change, comparing masking, selective hiding, and delete-and-recompute strategies. It finds masking biases models toward new values yet often breaks complete answers, and that positional information in later cache states carries earlier-record content crucial for multi-hop questions (20-41 point accuracy drops when rebuilt).

entry.title: DCEmbed: Scalable Optimization over Neural Surrogates

author.name: Akshay Sreekumar, Nicolas Christianson, Priya L. Donti, Ellen Vitercik, Ram Rajagopal

entry.summary: DCEmbed is a heuristic for optimization problems with embedded neural network surrogates that exploits difference-of-convex representations to avoid the binary variables that mixed-integer encodings of ReLU networks introduce. This makes large-scale optimization with learned surrogates computationally tractable, which matters for domains like energy systems where exact surrogates are prohibitive. The author group spans optimization, energy systems, and learning theory.

entry.title: AD-E2E-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture For End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Haoran Zhu, Wancong Zhang, Yann LeCun, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates existing action-conditioned JEPA world models (LeWM, DINO-WM, JEPA-WM) for end-to-end autonomous driving using goal-conditioned zero-shot planning, finding they trade off planning adequacy against computational efficiency. It proposes AD-E2E-JEPA to address both shortcomings.

entry.title: Unbiased Top-$k$ Estimation for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Linjian Meng, Siyuan Gan, YuHan Li, Xiran Wang, Ziyang Ding, Ditang Gou, Yiming Wu, Zhen Zhao

entry.summary: This paper studies gradient estimation of the reverse KL divergence in on-policy distillation, where sampled-token gradients are cheap but weakly informative and full-vocabulary gradients are expensive. The authors propose an unbiased Top-k estimation method that provides stronger distributional supervision than sampled tokens while remaining computationally tractable. It targets the core efficiency-accuracy tradeoff in OPD post-training.

entry.title: BEHAVE: Functional Behavior Modeling Enables Self-Improving Agents for Hardware Design and Verification

author.name: Yuheng Wu, Berk Gokmen, Sujeeth Jinesh, Lauren McLane, Aarav Wattal, Qi Yang Huang, Zhaozhuo Xu, Thierry Tambe

entry.summary: BEHAVE is an agentic framework for joint hardware design and verification that introduces a Behavior IR expressing task functionality as executable behavior models without over-constraining timing. An agent iteratively develops RTL design alongside a behavior model used as the verification reference, with an evaluator checking both separately. This solves the problem that cycle-by-cycle output matching wrongly rejects functionally valid designs.

entry.title: ReCAT: Remember, Count, and Time: Structured Recurrent Memory for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Pankhuri Vanjani, Mostafa Hatab, Can Mizrakli, Vaisakh Shaj, Zhuoyue Li, Moritz Reuss, Rudolf Lioutikov

entry.summary: ReCAT is a language-conditioned robot manipulation policy with structured recurrent memory, using Mamba-2 layers plus causal attention to integrate observation streams and a flow-matching Transformer decoder that reads current and historical representations through separate cross-attention. It enables memory-dependent tasks like recalling visual cues, counting events, and estimating time. It achieves 95.3% average success on LIBERO and strong results on RMBench.

entry.title: Which the Eye Fears: Writing with Read-Blindness Explains Massive Activations in Transformers

author.name: Swagatam Mukhopadhyay, Vishal Vivek Saley, Vraj Parikh, Mausam

entry.summary: This paper provides an operator-level mechanistic explanation of massive activation features in transformers, showing that both attention and feed-forward blocks systematically ignore MA coordinates when reading but not when writing, creating a read-write asymmetry that blocks corrective feedback while permitting continued accumulation. This both explains the persistence of extreme activations and adjudicates prior hypotheses about FFN amplification. Understanding massive activations is relevant to model stability and interpretability.

entry.title: mu-bench: A Multilingual Utterance Transcription Benchmark

author.name: Andrea Li (UC Berkeley), Soham Ray (Sierra AI)

entry.summary: mu-bench provides 4,270 caller utterances from real AI banking-agent calls in five languages, focused on form-field inputs like names and confirmation codes, and proposes Utterance Error Rate, an LLM-judged semantic accuracy metric calibrated against human raters. It addresses the mismatch between word error rate and the semantic fidelity voice agents actually need.

entry.title: Locally Sound, Globally Insufficient: The Local-Global Gap in Multi-Hop Reasoning

author.name: Bohao Chu, Hendrik Damm, Qianli Wang, Hui Wang, Shuning Zhang, Christoph M. Friedrich, Norbert Fuhr

entry.summary: This work identifies the local-global gap (LGG), a failure regime where a reasoning trace is sound at every step yet globally insufficient to answer the question. Using a human-adjudicated diagnostic of 2,598 responses across three multi-hop QA benchmarks and three models, the authors find LGG occurs in every benchmark-model pair and accounts for nearly half of globally insufficient responses. This provides a new diagnostic lens for why step-wise verification fails to predict final answer correctness.

entry.title: TCMQA: A 38K-Question Traditional Chinese Medicine Benchmark with a Licensed-Practitioner Reference

author.name: Tzu-Heng Huang, Jet Lin, Eric Lin

entry.summary: TCMQA is an open benchmark of 38,279 Traditional Chinese Medicine questions from licensing examinations, paired with 15,151 reference responses from 101 licensed practitioners. Evaluating 29 instruction-tuned models across 9 families, the authors find accuracy spanning 59 points with no saturation, and that pretraining data coverage predicts TCM ability far better than scale. This highlights the limits of scale for domain-specific, non-Western medical knowledge.

entry.title: Closing the Cross-Dialect Gap: Query Plans as a Portable Interface in Text-to-SQL

author.name: Corentin Royer (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland), Robin Oester (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Yotam Perlitz (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Yannick Metz (ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland), Andrea Giovannini (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Mennatallah El-Assady (ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland)

entry.summary: Shows that text-to-SQL systems trained and evaluated on a single dialect (SQLite) suffer substantial cross-dialect accuracy drops on PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and others, across 13 models from 3B to frontier scale. The fix is to have the LLM emit a dialect-agnostic relational algebra query plan that a deterministic compiler renders into backend-specific SQL. This restores portability nearly uniformly at a small cost, addressing a real production gap.

entry.title: LLMs are not stochastic parrots: Evidence for meaning-mediated abstraction from conlang-like tasks

author.name: Julia Witte Zimmerman, Calla G. Beauregard, Tabia Tanzin Prama, Parisa Suchdev, Kathryn Cramer, Elisabeth Kollrack

entry.summary: Testing the strong stochastic parrot hypothesis, the authors give LLMs only natural-language descriptions of fictional languages combining statistically uncommon and unattested features, with no example outputs. Observing rule-following behavior on these conlang-like tasks, they argue the models must rely on meaning-mediated abstraction rather than superficial statistical pattern reuse.

entry.title: Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Yunhao Liang, Qinghao Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: The paper asks what fraction of agent trajectory evaluation an automatic judge can take over while certifying the auto-decided error rate stays below a budget. Showing that correlated trajectory clusters invalidate i.i.d.-based certificates (a naive one claiming 98 percent automation exceeds budget in 17.5 percent of resamples), the authors introduce a task-level bootstrap certificate valid across tested regimes.

entry.title: InfiMed2: A Generalist Medical Multimodal Foundation Model from Contextual Evidence and Stability-Aware Supervision

author.name: Guanghao Zhu, Zeyu Liu, Zhitian Hou, Pengkai Wang, Zhijie Sang, Shuo Cai, Yang Yu, Yuanyi Wang, Yanggan Gu, Congkai Xie, Jianmin Wu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: Presents InfiMed2, a family of 4B and 27B medical multimodal foundation models built on stage-aware data design, with a curated 55.68M-instance corpus spanning continued pretraining and post-training. It includes stability-aware supervision to produce informative, answer-consistent medical explanations beyond short-form VQA.

entry.title: A mechanistic study of language model introspection

author.name: Jiahong Zou, Xiangkun Sun, Lingkai Kong, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: Uses a controlled intervention task with fixed input text, injecting concept vectors into hidden states at one of ten positions, to study how LLMs detect and localize internal perturbations. Across three model families it identifies two small groups of attention heads with distinct roles: gate heads that gate reporting and router heads that localize changes.

entry.title: Almieyar: A Culturally Grounded Benchmark for Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition

author.name: Omid Ghahroodi, Anas Madkoor, Dima Faris Al Saudi, Fagr Tahir, Malak Annan, Talha shahid javad allah rakha, Omar Al-Busaidi, Zineb El Kahla, Iheb Zouari, Essa Ahmed Abou Jabal, Ahmed Ezzat, Hind AL-Merekhi, Aisha Hamad M A Al-Naimi, Hadi Wazni, Bushra Alnajjar, Omar Amin, Haya Al-Thani, Houssam Eddine-Othman Lachemat, Marwa Elwakedy, Sundus Abdulmalik Al Nahari, Elahe Zahiri, Osamah Sarraj, Raghad Mousa, Mckeen Assi, Ahd Al Jumah, Heyam Salman, Alhanouf Abdulraqib, Sara Benoumhani, Alia Hamwi, Ayaat Al-Yasseri, Rim Ibrahim Ghazal, Lamia Ben hiba, Mohamed Eltabakh, Fatima Al-Raisi, Yassine El Kheir, Mohammed Abdulrahman, Hamdy Mubarak, Ayah Hashem, Lefkir Meriem, Ehsaneddin Asgari

entry.summary: ALMIEYAR is a new ASR benchmark covering 17 Arabic dialects across six dialect families, built entirely from newly recorded speech using culturally grounded image-description scenarios curated by dialect-community coordinators, totaling 13.7 hours. The authors benchmark 12 state-of-the-art ASR systems zero-shot, finding GPT-4o-transcribe achieves the lowest overall error. This meaningfully addresses the neglect of living Arabic dialects in speech technology, which has centered on Modern Standard Arabic.

entry.title: TraceDance: An Automated System for Building Agent Behavior Benchmarks from Real-World Agent Deployment Traces

author.name: Dehai Min, Daoan Zhang, Yiming Zeng, Huayi Zhang, Ziyi Chen, Yan Zhang, Qinbo Bai, Mengyuan Chao, Jing Ning, Qiyue Hua, Huiyi Chen, Hanrong Zhang, Henry Peng Zou, Jie Yang, Wei Xu, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Presents TraceDance, a system that constructs targeted agent behavior benchmarks from real deployment traces for user-specified undesirable behaviors, using retrieval plus LLM confirmation and an anchor synthesis loop for specifications. Benchmarks evaluate an agent's next turn at recorded decision points with behavior-specific rubrics and no reference answer or environment.

entry.title: DuraS2ST: Chain-of-Thought and Reinforcement Learning for Duration-Aligned Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Yayue Deng, Dingdong Wang, Yuxuan Hu, Jinyu Li, Yanqing Liu, Yuanyuan Wang, Weidong Chen, Helen M. Meng, Shujie Liu, Xixin Wu

entry.summary: Introduces DuraS2ST, a framework where a single speech language model first generates an explicit chain-of-thought planning target wording and phonetic length, then synthesizes duration-consistent speech tokens for time-sensitive applications like video dubbing. It contributes DuraSet-440K, a duration-aligned CoT corpus for supervised initialization, plus RL training.

entry.title: BIABench: Evaluating AI agents on real-world bioimage analysis tasks

author.name: Zixuan Pan, Davide Panzeri, Lukas Johanns, Marilin Moor, Yu Zhou, Hedi Peterson, Yiyu Shi, Jianxu Chen

entry.summary: BIABench is a benchmark of 16 end-to-end bioimage analysis tasks reconstructed from published peer-reviewed studies, spanning eleven subtasks and modalities from histology to time-lapse volumes. Agents must choose and run analyses through code and specialized software since images are too large to read as context, with ground truth from published results.

entry.title: After the Fix: Transfer of Corrected Agent Experience

author.name: Yanfei Zhang, Xu Lin

entry.summary: This large-scale study (3,300 runs across two model families and eleven conditions) asks whether repairing a failed agent episode makes its experience more useful as memory for future tasks. Findings show corrected experience transfers substantial gains, but much of the apparent advantage of fuller correction comes from worse uncorrected baselines rather than better corrected memory.

entry.title: CoDimRecon: Agentic Reconstruction of Sim-Ready 3D Scenes with Deformable Curves, Surfaces, and Volumes

author.name: Shuzhao Xie, Lelin Wang, Guying Lin, Zhi Wang, Minchen Li

entry.summary: CoDimRecon is an agentic framework that reconstructs editable, simulation-ready 3D scenes containing rigid, articulated, and deformable objects from multi-view RGB observations. It combines scene-level geometric priors with object-level generated meshes, decomposes articulated objects into movable parts with explicit joints, and addresses dimensionality-dependent simulation-ready geometry for deformables. This fills a gap left by methods that assume rigid objects only, with applications in robotics, gaming, and immersive media.

entry.title: Real2Gym: Building Gyms from Videos, Bringing Skills to Robots

author.name: Kerui Ren, Yingxiang Xu, Kaiwen Song, Linning Xu, Bo Dai, Mulin Yu, Tao Lu

entry.summary: Real2Gym is an agentic Real2Sim2Real framework that converts human and robot demonstration videos into interactive simulation gyms, reconstructing editable scenes, validating actions via physics execution, and generating task-conditioned variations. Agents then learn executable manipulation code in simulation that transfers to physical robots.

entry.title: Adaptive Reward Routing: Dynamic Multi-Reward Optimization for Joint Audio-Video Diffusion via Forward-Process RL

author.name: Songlin Yang, Xiaotong Zhao, Jiacheng Zhang, Zhe Wang, Toyota Li, Eric Liu, Alan Zhao, Anyi Rao

entry.summary: The authors propose Adaptive Reward Routing, which dynamically adapts both where reward-driven updates act and how competing rewards are combined during forward-process RL training of joint audio-video diffusion models. This addresses the brittleness of fixed routing and reward weighting, targeting modality-specific quality, cross-modal alignment, and temporal synchronization.

entry.title: APM-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-session Persistent Memory for Egocentric Streaming Video Assistants

author.name: Jianguo Huang, Jinming Liu, Qiyao Wang, Liang Xu, Jianhang Li, Zhimian Wen, Mingda Li, Shule Lu, Zhicheng Wang, Yuhan Guo, Xin Jin, Wenjun Zeng

entry.summary: APM-Bench reformulates egocentric streaming video understanding as multi-session life trajectories, testing whether models can persist and use memory across interruptions. It contains 549 sessions, 104 trajectories, and 2,719 candidates with fine-grained annotations, spanning objective and open-ended questions, filling a gap left by benchmarks that only consider continuous clips.

entry.title: TomoTransformer: Towards a Foundation Model for CT Reconstruction

author.name: AmirEhsan Khorashadizadeh, Benjam\'in B\'ejar

entry.summary: TomoTransformer is a transformer architecture for sparse-view CT reconstruction that treats each local filtered projection as a token and predicts missing views via self-attention, operating in back-projection space to separate projections across spatial locations. This design aims to be robust to distribution shifts in projection counts, angles, and detector resolutions where conventional supervised models require retraining.

entry.title: SYNCR: Diagnosing and Learning Cross-Video Reasoning from Simulation

author.name: Sara Ghazanfari, Siddharth Garg, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Farshad Khorrami

entry.summary: SYNCR is a simulator-grounded benchmark built on Habitat, Kubric, and CLEVRER that generates 4,000 evaluation and 15,960 training questions across eight cross-video reasoning tasks, such as event alignment and identity matching, with answers derived from environment state. Evaluation of 22 multimodal LLMs reveals persistent weaknesses in reasoning across multiple videos.

entry.title: MUGEN: Interactive Panoramic World Exploration via Camera Control

author.name: Jiaming Tan, Zhen Li, Shuwei Shi, Minggui Teng, Siqi Yang, Yuwei Wu, Bo Zheng, Chuanhao Li, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MUGEN, a large-scale real-world panoramic video dataset with over 1,300 hours of at least 4K footage with camera trajectories, plus Wan360, a camera-controlled panoramic video generation model, to enable interactive 360-degree world exploration. This addresses the coupled data and model gaps limiting panoramic video generation.

entry.title: DMA$^2$: Pixel-space Distribution Matching with Adversarial and Anchor Losses

author.name: Xin Lin, Zhifei Zhang, Yuqian Zhou, Haitian Zheng, Shaoteng Liu, Lehan Yang, Zhe Lin, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: DMA2 revisits distribution matching distillation (DMD) for native pixel-space diffusion teachers, showing that low-noise RGB matching is dominated by local texture cues and motivating a fixed high-noise matching band. It also leverages clean-RGB outputs to admit external visual representations (DINO-Adv) for adversarial guidance without a heavy fake-score critic in the adversarial path. This advances few-step pixel-space image generation.

entry.title: PE-OPSD: Internalizing Prompt Enhancement into Flow-matching Models via On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Mingfeng Lin, Chengfei Cai, Lin Xu, Chengqian Ma, Yuxiang Wei, Liang Han

entry.summary: This paper proposes PE-OPSD, a training method that internalizes the benefit of prompt enhancement directly into text-to-image flow-matching models, treating enhanced prompts as privileged training information rather than an inference-time add-on. A raw-prompt student learns from an enhanced-prompt teacher via on-policy self-distillation along the student's own generation trajectory. This removes external prompt-rewriter latency while preserving instruction-following quality.

entry.title: V2X-WAM: A Cooperative World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Junwei You, Weizhe Tang, Can Wang, Yan Zhao, Jun Hua, Haotian Shi, Wei Zhang, Lin Wang, Bin Ran

entry.summary: V2X-WAM is a cooperative world-action model that couples vehicle-infrastructure scene understanding, action generation, and explicit future-world reasoning for end-to-end autonomous driving. Unlike prior cooperative driving methods that only enhance current-scene representation, it models the anticipated consequences of driving actions within the evolving traffic environment. This enables planners to anticipate interaction effects of their decisions.

entry.title: From Routing Signals to Selective Review: Visual regrounding in MoE VLMs

author.name: Hongzhu Guo, Mohsen Fayyaz, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This paper identifies target-absence grounding failures in VLMs, where models answer questions about objects that are absent from the image. It presents the first framework leveraging internal MoE routing decisions to detect such failures before generation, training linear detectors on target-token routing probabilities from Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct and Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, then selectively invoking visual regrounding for correction.

entry.title: SkillWeaver: Agentic Exploration over Neural Interaction Skills for Scalable Robot Data Generation

author.name: He Zhu, Lusen Zhao, Kwan Man Cheng, Su Li, Katerina Fragkiadaki

entry.summary: SkillWeaver is an agentic framework that autonomously generates robot training data by exploring over Neural Interaction Skills: reusable, parameterized, closed-loop policies exposed to a VLM reasoning agent. Given a task and simulated environment, the agent reasons about next actions, invokes and parameterizes skills, addressing the cost bottleneck of teleoperated demonstrations.

entry.title: Faster and Better? Benchmark Bugs and Design Limitations Distort the Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Acceleration

author.name: Qiwei Chen, Kaijun Zhou, Nuohui Shi, Zhiyang Li, Yuxuan Feng, Jinyu Gu

entry.summary: The paper finds that some training-free VLA acceleration methods appear to beat their own baseline policies on simulated manipulation benchmarks, which is implausible and points to evaluation flaws. The authors distinguish implementation bugs from design limitations in success criteria and simulation settings, showing that measured gains can stem from benchmark errors rather than better task execution.

entry.title: EgoAlign: Bridging the Human-Humanoid Gap for Long-Range Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Yiming Jiang, Chen Jin, Chongyang Xu, Yilun Chen, Aimin Hao, Yisheng He

entry.summary: EgoAlign is a data-construction framework that converts egocentric human demonstrations into action and state supervision usable by a continuous whole-body humanoid controller, without requiring physical robot demonstrations. It uses the target robot model in simulation to align upper-body interaction geometry and preserve locomotion references through controller-in-the-loop refinement. This addresses the persistent human-to-humanoid embodiment gap that limits the value of cheap human demonstration data.

entry.title: Understanding Private Evolution as Learning-Augmented Clustering

author.name: Audra McMillan, Kunal Talwar, Felix Zhou

entry.summary: Recasts the differentially Private Evolution (PE) synthetic data algorithm as generative model-augmented Wasserstein learning, explaining why it beats worst-case Wasserstein bounds. The analysis shows sample complexity can depend on intrinsic rather than ambient dimension when the generator captures the true distribution, and also identifies simple cases where standard PE variants fail to converge.

entry.title: How Does Changing the Elo of a Chess Transformer Affect its Computations?

author.name: David Litman

entry.summary: This post presents mechanistic interpretability analysis of Maia-3, a chess transformer conditioned on an Elo skill input, showing that increasing the skill dial from 700 to 2500 monotonically migrates computation into deeper attention layers. The effect is strongest for specific tactics like knight forks, with the mechanism appearing to involve recruitment of deeper attention heads while shallow heads keep constant contributions. The author argues this depth migration shows safety-relevant circuits can move between operating conditions, a caution for interpretability work on LLMs.

entry.title: An Exact Generate - Transform Decomposition of Small-LLM Team Scaling Across Orchestration Architectures

author.name: Blaz Bertalanic, Carolina Fortuna

entry.summary: Sweeping eight orchestration architectures across five 7-9B models and multiple benchmarks, this paper shows returns to multi-agent team scaling are sharply task-dependent: up to 17 points on arithmetic word problems versus at most 4 on ARC, GPQA, and MMLU. It provides a generate-transform decomposition explaining when team scaling helps and identifies Proposer-Critic as capturing arithmetic gains best.

entry.title: SAKI: Maximal-Coupling-Routed Teacher Supervision for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Miteto Wei, Xiaohan Wang, Zehao Chen, Jiajun Chai, Sichao Liu, Li Wang, Haoyuan Xu, Zhaoyu Hu, Wei Lin, Guojun Yin

entry.summary: SAKI improves on-policy distillation for weak students that visit teacher-misaligned states, combining a KL-constrained teacher-guided rollout with maximal coupling. Accepted tokens keep reverse-KL supervision while correction positions receive direct supervision on the teacher's top token, and the coupling makes the correction probability exactly the total-variation distance, unifying the trust region for rollout and supervision. The math is elegant and the routing is principled.

entry.title: Calibrate the Decisions That Change the Future: On-Policy Post-Training Quantization for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Wenxiao Fan, Jingling Fu, Lichen Ma, Yu He, Luohang Liu, Jinbao Xue, Ke Zhang, Junshi Huang, Kan Li

entry.summary: OnPTQ is an on-policy post-training quantization framework for multimodal LLMs that calibrates on trajectories visited by the quantized policy and evaluates competing tokens via short counterfactual rollouts. It combines current discrepancy with branch consequence into a Decision-Consequence risk, capturing autoregressive feedback that fixed-sequence calibration misses.

entry.title: Beyond Prompt Count: How Data Shapes Transfer in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jiaxuan Wang, Jiafei Lyu, Yuchen Cai, Siye Wu, Pengyuan Wang, Jiashun Liu, Xiang Cheng, Kai Yang, Yangkun Chen, Saiyong Yang, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: Systematically studies how prompt quantity, source, and selection shape transfer in on-policy distillation across RL- and SFT-continuation and cross-model settings, finding OPD is highly prompt-efficient (four DAPO prompts can match 3,840 DeepMath prompts) but prompt utility is relational to the teacher, with parameter and functional change analyses explaining differences.

entry.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Generate and Detect Multimodal Social Media Fake News?

author.name: Jiyao Yang, Yang Liu, Zhenyue Qin, Qingyu Chen, Xiuzhen Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent framework where story, image, and critic agents collaborate to fabricate realistic multimodal fake news countering true posts, generating over 9,000 paired posts across science, health, and entertainment. Benchmarking 16 open- and closed-source MLLMs for detection finds most models struggle, exposing a generation-detection gap for multimodal disinformation.

entry.title: ThinQuant: Scalable Rotation Learning for Weight and Activation Quantization of LLMs

author.name: Mehdi Makni, Ryan Lucas, Rahul Mazumder

entry.summary: ThinQuant tackles the scalability bottleneck of learned rotations for low-bit LLM quantization, improving on gradient-based SpinQuant and gradient-free DartQuant. It introduces two efficiency ideas: a data selection procedure exploiting geometric structure to reduce calibration data requirements, and an exact reduction of the optimization problem on the reduced set. This makes rotation learning feasible for the largest architectures.

entry.title: WitnessGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents on the Construction of Bug Witnesses

author.name: Haomin Qi, Xiangzhe Xu, Yiming Huang, Jingbo Shang, Chengpeng Wang

entry.summary: WitnessGym is an automated framework for benchmarking coding agents on bug validation, requiring agents to produce executable witnesses combining a concrete input and testing harness that expose faulty behavior. It avoids the reuse and manual-construction problems of historical bug benchmarks by injecting bugs into test-reached paths of real projects and retaining cases exposed by construction-time witnesses. The design supports extension to additional bug types and languages via specifications and adapters.

entry.title: Selecting The Most Informative Tokens in Natural Language Autoencoders

author.name: Federico Torrielli, Gianluca Barmina, Andrea Blasi N\'u\~nez, Amon Rapp, Luigi Di Caro, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: This study examines which token positions auditors should explain in natural language autoencoders that translate model activations into readable text, analyzing 4.7 million explanations on prompt injection and concealment. It finds that a ranker using only chat structure usually selects more relevant explanations than signals from model computation, without needing a forward pass. Explaining just 5% of positions retains nearly all detection success on three of four datasets.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled Selective LLM Answering by Pricing Label-Free Checks

author.name: Dongyub Jude Lee, Jungseob Lee, Chanjun Park, Hyeonseok Moon, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: PriceCheck builds decision rules from label-free checks such as re-solving a problem, assigning each a price based on agreement rates and cost, then composing these prices to predict coverage and cost of check schedules. A small labelled calibration set selects a schedule meeting a stated selective-risk target. On mathematics benchmarks it serves 76.1% of answers while holding held-out selective risk below target.

entry.title: When Should a Human Take Back Control? Optimal Delegation under Turbulent AI Risk

author.name: Haoze Yan, Julien Roze, Ved Upadhyay, Unal Tatar, Thibaut Mastrolia

entry.summary: The authors present a continuous-time framework for adaptive human oversight of AI systems, modeling clustered failure events (where one hallucination or harmful output triggers further errors) via self-exciting dynamics jointly with the delegation decision and supervisory suppression effort. This fills a gap in oversight formulations that ignore incident clustering, characterizing when humans should take back control.

entry.title: Benchmarking EEG Foundation Models at Scale: Lessons from 20,000 Evaluations

author.name: Zhige Chen, Shu Peng, Chengxuan Qin, Rui Liu, Rui Yang, Kay Chen Tan, Jibin Wu

entry.summary: EEG-Arena is an open-source benchmark evaluating 30 EEG foundation models and 25 supervised baselines on 57 downstream tasks across 23 datasets, with over 20,000 evaluations covering performance, pretraining benefits, model and data scaling, and robustness to channel configurations. It finds EEG FMs outperform supervised baselines on most tasks, especially in non-bipolar settings, and offers lessons on scaling. This is a substantial community resource for neural decoding research.

entry.title: Quantifying Behavioral Tails in Black-Box Language Models

author.name: Elsayed Eshra, Ali Al-Lawati, Dongwon Lee, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: RareTrap is a framework for estimating the probability of severe behaviors in black-box LLMs by constructing a geometry-aware mapping from a latent reference space to an induced prompt distribution. It enables sequential rare-event simulation concentrating evaluations on progressively more severe behaviors while preserving probability estimates.

entry.title: Brain-Conditioned Action Policies for Neural Motor Decoding

author.name: Luyao Jin, Running Zhao, Huan Zhao, Vincent C. K. Cheung, Wei-Hsin Liao

entry.summary: BrainVLA adapts a pretrained vision-language-action model (OpenVLA-OFT) to motor brain-computer interfaces, aligning neural activity with actions through language-mediated instructions and rendered visual observations. This mitigates the scarcity of paired neural-action data by leveraging VLA policies for neural motor decoding, enabling people with paralysis to control devices. The cross-domain transfer from robotics foundation models to BCIs is the key novelty.

entry.title: Don't Forget! Decomposing the Training Dynamics of Memorization in Language Models

author.name: Florian Eichin, Philipp Mondorf, Andrei Mircea, Yupei Du, Barbara Plank, Michael A. Hedderich

entry.summary: The paper decomposes loss trajectories of memorized sequences across training and parameters in the Pythia family, distinguishing recitation (duplicated sequences) from recollection (rare sequences). It finds both are characterized by sequence-level gradient alignment, with recitation suffering misalignment-driven forgetting that explains why duplication is needed. Relevant to privacy, unlearning, and data curation.

entry.title: Not All Rollouts Are Worth Learning: On Trajectory Valuation for Post-Training Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuesong Jia, Ziao Yang, Zhanhe Huang, Hongfu Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Dynamic Trajectory Valuation (DTV), a lightweight framework that estimates trajectory utility at the mini-batch level using only gradient information and filters detrimental trajectories during online RL training. Unlike influence-function methods from classification, DTV works without fixed validation sets and integrates into existing RL pipelines with minimal overhead.

entry.title: Weighting Schedules Govern What and When Score-Based Generative Models Learn from Multimodal Data

author.name: J\'er\'emie Klinger, Rapha\"el Urfin, Giulio Biroli, Marylou Gabri\'e

entry.summary: Analyzes how the time-weighting schedule in score-based diffusion training determines which features of multimodal distributions are learned, decomposing the integrated loss at fixed signal-to-noise ratio. Shows that signal-to-noise ratio sets the rate at which mode directions and relative weights are captured, tied to a narrow speciation time window during generation.

entry.title: Deep Epistemic Value Functions for Optimistic Exploration

author.name: Leander Diaz-Bone, Marco Bagatella, Jonas H\"ubotter, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: The paper conducts a systematic study of how epistemic uncertainty is represented, propagated, and optimized in deep value functions for exploration, identifying distinct failure modes along each axis. Findings motivate DEVOTE, a model-free RL algorithm that controls uncertainty generalization, stabilizes temporal propagation, and preserves optimism for principled exploration.

entry.title: Correcting the Dropout-LayerNorm Expectation Gap Improves Protein Structure Models

author.name: Isaac Ellmen, David Errington, Matthew I. J. Raybould, Charlotte M. Deane

entry.summary: The authors show that E[LayerNorm(dropout(x))] differs from LayerNorm(x), so the common Dropout-then-LayerNorm pattern in AlphaFold2-style protein structure predictors introduces a systematic evaluation-time bias. They derive a closed-form first-order correction (DLC) that empirically matches large Monte Carlo dropout ensembles across nine protein structure models.

entry.title: DepthBench: Measuring How Residual Connections Enable More Computational Depth

author.name: Keyu Wang, Yangyi Huang, Jiale Kang, David Gonz\'alez-Mart\'inez, Weiyang Liu, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: DepthBench is a controlled benchmark for studying whether architectural techniques that enhance normalization or residual connections (LayerNorm Scaling, mHC, AttnRes) translate increased architectural depth into effective computational depth, systematically varying width and depth to separate information-flow gains from confounding factors. It addresses an important open question as models scale: whether deeper layers actually add computation or merely improve information access. This informs architecture design decisions for frontier-scale training.

entry.title: Identical Runs, Different Results: Benchmarking AI Coding Agents on Open-Weight Models

author.name: Eduardo Ari\~no de la Rubia (Central European University), Szilard Pafka (Epoch)

entry.summary: Across 584 runs of six coding agents on six open-weight model endpoints, identical runs of one agent-model pairing varied more than pairings differed, making small-sample benchmark comparisons unreliable and requiring hundreds of runs to resolve observed differences. The study quantifies variance implications for teams evaluating agents on their own tasks.

entry.title: Predictive Semantic Safety: From Visual Physical Reasoning to Safety-Critical Control

author.name: Taekyung Kim, Salem Fradi, Yanning Dai, Mateusz Ostaszewski, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: PSS connects visual physical reasoning to backup-based safety filtering: a VLM predicts physical events and their timing or object displacements, an explicit motion model converts hypotheses into trajectories, and split conformal prediction calibrates position errors to derive predicted occupancy used to evaluate backup maneuvers. It targets hazards not apparent from current geometric surroundings.

entry.title: Natural State-Prediction Accuracy can Hide Weak Controlled Responsiveness in VLA Readouts

author.name: Hyungjoon Kim, Wonbin Son, Mi Young Lee, Jun Young Lee, Seungmin Rho

entry.summary: This paper introduces an evaluation framework for vision-language-action model readouts that separates prediction accuracy, target-state responsiveness, and context stability, using physically validated observations crossing target coordinates with robot contexts. It demonstrates that high natural-trajectory accuracy can coexist with weak controlled target-state responsiveness because contextual cues confound natural observations. This challenges standard evaluation practice for decoding physical states from VLA representations.

entry.title: Simulation-Based Quantum System Inference with Neural Posterior Estimation

author.name: Hang Zou, Anton Frisk Kockum, Martin Rahm, Simon Olsson

entry.summary: This paper introduces a likelihood-free framework for quantum system parameter inference that pairs polynomial-cost classical simulators (Pauli propagation, tensor networks) with normalizing flows to learn posteriors from simulation data. A single trained model maps any new measurement record to its posterior in one forward pass, sidestepping intractable likelihoods from exponentially large Hilbert spaces. It bridges simulation-based inference and quantum physics.

entry.title: Rethinking Causal Action Tokenization with Conditional Annealing in Flow Matching

author.name: Chenyu Zhang, Yuhang Cao, Daru Du, Yingxi Lu, Jing Shao, Ruoqu Chen, Jiajun Liu, Liu Cao, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao, Mengdi Xu

entry.summary: CATok reframes action tokenization for autoregressive vision-language-action models as a causally structured generative process rather than pure compression. It introduces conditional annealing that extracts action tokens by progressively annealing a flow-matching process, with each token conditioned on preceding tokens and encoding residual reconstruction signal at a noise level, yielding a coarse-to-fine causal token space aligned with autoregressive backbones.

entry.title: Improving Test-Time Scaling with Adaptive Looped Transformers

author.name: Yichen You, Tianyu Fu, Aosong Feng, Xingtai Lv, Xuefei Ning, Ning Ding, Yu Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies whether looped transformers improve test-time scaling by measuring the accuracy-compute slope (accuracy gain per doubling of decoding FLOPs), finding that looped models have steeper slopes but underperform non-looped baselines at matched compute because fixed-depth looping wastes iterations on tokens that do not benefit. An adaptive approach targets extra computation only where useful. This contributes to the active area of compute-adaptive inference.

entry.title: SALMONN-duo: Adaptive Dual-System Coordination for Full-Duplex Voice Agents

author.name: Wenyi Yu, Siyin Wang, Terumi Chiba, Xianzhao Chen, Xiaohai Tian, Jun Zhang, Lu Lu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: SALMONN-duo is a dual-system full-duplex voice agent pairing a fast, always-on speech LLM (system 1) with a powerful asynchronous deliberative LLM (system 2), inspired by dual-process cognition. System 1 learns when to answer directly versus delegate to system 2, reconciling real-time conversation latency with tool use and deliberative reasoning.

entry.title: Late Attention Layers Alone Can Copy Entity Tokens, but Not Without Attending to Their Context

author.name: Muyu He, Yuchen Liu, Ran Tao, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Using Qwen3-8B, the authors develop two novel techniques, genie-in-a-bottle (controlling which layers participate in a task) and attention lobotomy (cutting specific tokens' attention), to map which layers perform entity copying. They find late attention layers can copy entity tokens on their own but only when they can also attend to surrounding context tokens. This yields a sharper mechanistic picture of how LLMs bind prompt entities into outputs.

entry.title: Auditing Agent Actions through Query-Conditioned Attribution

author.name: Yifan Liu, Praveen Venkateswaran, Abdulhamid Adebayo, Dong Wang

entry.summary: Formulates query-conditioned agent action attribution as a new task: given a natural-language auditing query, recover the source and ordered intermediate evidence for a realized agent action, working even when access to the acting model is limited. This addresses gaps in existing attribution methods that lack question-specific traces or rely on costly perturbations.

entry.title: ColNanoVDR: Document-Free Query Distillation for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval via Optimal Transport

author.name: Zhuchenyang Liu, Ziyi Wang, Yao Zhang, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: ColNanoVDR extends document-free distillation to multi-vector visual document retrieval, training a small student query encoder against the teacher's existing index without encoding and caching terabytes of page tokens. Its OTW objective combines optimal transport with learned weights to avoid the costly standard MaxSim-matching recipe.

entry.title: Improved Distributional Diffusion Models

author.name: Tommaso Martorella, Alexandre Galashov, Felix Krause, Stefan Andreas Baumann, Valentin De Bortoli, Arthur Gretton, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: This paper scales Distributional Diffusion Models, which learn a distributional denoiser via scoring-rule objectives instead of mean prediction, by deferring particle expansion to late transformer layers and introducing time-dependent scoring-rule schedules. These changes address particle-count training overhead and the fixed scoring-rule trade-off.

entry.title: Med-RADIO: Reducing All Medical Domains Into One via Multi-Teacher Distillation

author.name: Chu Zhang, Haoyu Jiang, Hongyuan Zhang, Hongbin Liu, Dong Yi

entry.summary: Med-RADIO unifies medical imaging across heterogeneous modalities by distilling multiple specialist models into a single generalist, aiming to lift the cross-modality baseline that generalists establish toward the per-domain ceilings defined by specialists. It addresses the dual shortfall of medical generalists: limited data scale and insufficient domain-specific depth.

entry.title: On the spectral properties of generative denoiser Jacobians

author.name: Alexandros Graikos, Nebojsa Jojic, Dimitris Samaras

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the spectrum of the denoiser Jacobian as a lens for characterizing differences among diffusion and flow-matching models, finding that better generative performance correlates with larger Jacobian eigenvalues across pre-trained models. It then introduces a regularization scheme controlling the Jacobian spectrum during training. This connects generative quality to a measurable, manipulable property of the denoiser.

entry.title: Urgent Actions Go First: Urgency-Aware Denoising for Real-Time VLA Control

author.name: Zibo Wang, Haochen Han, Pengzhen Ren, Mingtong Dai, Fangming Liu

entry.summary: Urgency-Aware Denoising exploits the fact that diffusion and flow-matching VLA policies generate action chunks jointly but consume them sequentially: time-critical actions are released after fewer denoising steps while the rest is refined asynchronously. This inference-time framework reduces effective latency for real-time robotic control without retraining the policy.

entry.title: Is Human-Readable Text Necessary for Effective LLM Fine-Tuning?

author.name: Jinhao Zhang, Zeyu Liu, Zicheng Yan, Yunquan Zhang, Daning Cheng, Song Tang

entry.summary: This work introduces DASA, a method that optimizes continuous synthetic input embeddings guided by activation-gradient feedback from a frozen reference model, allowing fine-tuning without human-readable training text. The results suggest adaptation utility does not require discrete, interpretable training data.

entry.title: GeoWind2Plan: Mission-Time 3D Urban Wind Prediction for Energy-Efficient UAV Planning

author.name: Shaoxiang Qin, Yucheng Zhao, Fuyuan Lyu, Di Zhou, Jiachen Yao, Xue Liu, Anima Anandkumar, Liangzhu Leon Wang, Xiongye Xiao

entry.summary: GeoWind2Plan is a geometry-to-wind-to-planning framework that predicts 3D urban wind fields from building geometry and a background wind vector fast enough for mission-time UAV planning, unlike CFD simulations that take hours to days. The predicted wind enables energy-efficient flight paths in urban low-altitude airspace.

entry.title: Going Beyond State-Reaching: Learning Abstractions for Intrinsically Motivated Option Discovery

author.name: Akhil Bagaria, Anita De Mello Koch, George Konidaris

entry.summary: This RL paper addresses a limitation of option-discovery algorithms, which typically learn subgoals targeting entire states, causing options that apply only in narrow state-space regions and eventually overwhelming the agent. The proposed algorithm instead identifies small, relevant feature subsets per subgoal, producing abstract, transferable options that generalize broadly. It demonstrates rapid exploration in three sparse-reward, image-based domains.

entry.title: Multi-Channel Mitigation of Source-Trust Shortcuts in Fact-Checking RL Agents

author.name: Jianchang Su, Yiwei Yang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: TrustSwap is a counterfactual test that swaps, lowers, or removes source-trust labels while holding evidence text fixed, separately measuring effects on verdicts, confidence, and search decisions in retrieval-augmented fact-checkers. Across 50 comparisons, confidence and search respond correctly in 49, but a label change alone flips 4-23% of confident verdicts for Qwen3 models, revealing shortcut reliance. The paper proposes multi-channel mitigations for RL-trained agents.

entry.title: Emergent Specialization in Populations of Self-Supervised Collaborative Vision Experts Without a Shared Gate or Cross-Agent Gradients

author.name: Aram Davtyan, Pablo Acuaviva, Sebastian Stapf, Paolo Favaro

entry.summary: This work tests whether populations of independently trained neural networks can develop division of labor without a shared gating mechanism, using a predictive visual pretraining proxy with masked prediction of frozen DINOv3 features across six domains. Specialization is measured by whether the best agent for an input aligns with the input's latent domain.

entry.title: Harness Evolution as Learning: Approximation, Generalization, and Optimization Limits of Self-Improving Personal Agents

author.name: Zeyu Gan, Zixuan Gong, Yong Liu

entry.summary: This paper studies harness engineering for personal agents whose underlying model is fixed, investigating how the surrounding layer managing context, memory, tools, and execution should evolve to adapt to individual users. It frames harness evolution as a learning problem and analyzes approximation, generalization, and optimization limits across architecture, scale, and self-evolution algorithms.

entry.title: VLALight: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Pan Zhang, Siqi Lai, Kemu Dong, Hao Liu

entry.summary: VLALight is presented as the first vision-language-action model for end-to-end traffic signal control directly from multi-view roadside camera video, replacing hand-engineered traffic states with learned spatiotemporal reasoning and topology-aware coordination across intersections. The work also establishes a benchmark for this capability. It bridges the gap between visual perception and control decisions in urban mobility.

entry.title: CF-LoRA: Decoupled Factor Aggregation and Adaptation-Aware Client Clustering for Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mengjun Yi, Langxing Yang, Suhan Guo, Furao Shen, Jian Zhao

entry.summary: CF-LoRA addresses two mismatches in federated LoRA fine-tuning under heterogeneous client data: structural mismatch from independently averaging LoRA factors, and statistical mismatch from forcing one global adapter on divergent clients. It learns a shared A factor while keeping personalized B factors, then clusters clients by adaptation-pattern similarity. This improves both aggregation quality and personalization in privacy-preserving fine-tuning.

entry.title: When Should Agents Check External State? Budgeting Observations for Stored Intentions

author.name: Zhengkun Di, Bin Shi, Kai Sun, Yiming Xu, Bo Dong

entry.summary: BudgetPM formulates, for the first time, the allocation of a shared observation budget across an agent's stored prospective-memory intentions, deciding when web access, tool use, or paid calls are worth spending to check whether a stored condition holds. It offers a static logistic scorer variant and a sequential variant distilled from full-episode hindsight schedules, sharing a hard-budget executor. This brings cost-awareness to intention maintenance in agents.

entry.title: SkillCome: Group Contrast Skill Optimization with Dual Memory

author.name: Haolin Li, Feng Hong, Ang Li, Chilin Fu, Weichang Wu, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Xiaolu Zhang, Jiangchao Yao

entry.summary: SkillCome improves LLM skill evolution by replacing single-trajectory skill edits with group contrastive optimization over multiple trajectories, using dual memory to stabilize optimization direction against noisy local evidence. This makes it easier to localize failure-causing actions and identify actions worth incorporating into a skill. The work targets the growing area of experience-driven agent self-improvement.

entry.title: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Giulio Segalini, Zhi Wen Soi, J\'er\'emie Decouchant, Lydia Chen

entry.summary: Identifies an inertia failure mode in computer-use agents, where they repeat fruitless actions despite recognizing their ineffectiveness, and shows via activation analysis that inertia corresponds to an absorbing region in the model's activation space. The findings offer interpretability-based diagnostics for agent reliability and potential mechanisms for intervention.

entry.title: Transolver-$\sigma$: Joint Spectral-Physical Subspace Modeling for Neural PDE Solving

author.name: Haonan Shangguan, Hang Zhou, Haixu Wu, Yuezhou Ma, Jianmin Wang, Mingsheng Long

entry.summary: Presents Transolver-sigma, a neural PDE solver that models spectral transformations and physical-state interactions in dedicated latent subspaces and recomposes them, addressing the gap between one-step accuracy and reliable autoregressive rollout. Built by the Transolver lineage authors from Tsinghua's ML group.

entry.title: Authority Before Utility: Non-Compensatory Control for Persistent LLM Memory

author.name: Wesley Shu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a separation between utility and authority in persistent LLM memory: a memory can remain useful after being invalidated by updates or revocations, and fixed penalties on unnormalized utility scores cannot guarantee exclusion under score reparameterization. The authors show rank-normalized compensation is scale-invariant and stronger, and report on a quarantined primary evaluation due to an adapter confound, demonstrating unusual methodological transparency.

entry.title: EnterpriseBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Enterprise-Level Strategic Reasoning and Decision-Making

author.name: Min Yang, Yichen Pan, Jinghua Piao, Dandan Song, Yongshun Gong, Yong Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces EnterpriseBench, a benchmark that evaluates LLM agents on enterprise tasks ranging from static question answering to interactive, long-horizon strategic decision-making under uncertainty and incomplete information. It unifies existing enterprise and financial QA datasets into a capability- and difficulty-annotated foundational suite and adds dynamic decision-making tasks, addressing a gap left by benchmarks that only test static skills like extraction, calculation, and financial QA. The work matters because real enterprise workflows demand feedback-driven, multi-step reasoning that current evaluation practices largely ignore.

entry.title: ContextRender: From Execution Dependencies to Agent Context

author.name: Savini Kashmira, Jayanaka L. Dantanarayana, Lingjia Tang, Jason Mars

entry.summary: ContextRender manages agent context through a persistent graph of execution dependencies, introducing Tool-Flow Analysis to track how later operations reuse earlier tool results (an observed-reuse signal) combined with recency and semantic relevance to select context within a fixed budget. This exploits execution structure that prior context-management methods overlook.

entry.title: NeuronEye: Query-Guided Visual Concept Activation for Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Ruiyu Yan, Bowen Chen, Shaowen Wan, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: NeuronEye is a plug-in framework that decomposes vision-language model hidden states into a sparse, concept-level neuron vocabulary and selectively activates query-relevant visual concepts during inference. Inspired by sparse population coding and top-down modulation in biological vision, it aims to disentangle object identity, spatial layout, and attributes that are otherwise entangled in dense representations.

entry.title: Reconstructing Implicit Scientific Knowledge: Evaluating LLM Agents through End-to-End Reproduction of Astronomy

author.name: Yuehui Wang, Xinyu Qi, Guirong Xue, Cheng Wang, Yangbin Xie, Xiaoyu Tang, Cong Sun

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework evaluating LLM agents on end-to-end reproduction of fourteen astronomy studies, separating execution failure from methodological ambiguity that arises when papers leave data selection, calibration, priors, and assumptions implicit. It enables more meaningful assessment of whether reproduction failures reflect agent limitations or underspecified source material.

entry.title: Learn Now, Use Next, Trust Later: Prequential Test-Time Learning for LLM Agents

author.name: Tong Zhao, Reed Li, Yuyang Hu, Yutao Zhu, Haijin Liang, Haibo Shi, Yu Lu, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: StepLearn is a nonparametric test-time learning method for LLM agents that distills feedback at the granularity of individual transitions during ongoing interactions, reducing the delay of episode-level learning. It balances immediate reuse of newly learned rules against the risk of propagating unreliable or misattributed guidance. The approach enables agents to adapt during deployment without parameter updates.

entry.title: ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision

author.name: Zhiwei Zhang, Huayu Deng, Fei Zhao, Jiayan Fu, Bin Liang, Kam-Fai Wong, Mu Chuan

entry.summary: ROSS proposes reusing historical self-generated rollouts from reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation for LLM post-training, rather than discarding them as stale. The method keeps full trajectories as context but applies loss only to selected continuations that remain valuable to imitate, filtering out mistakes and redundant actions. Experiments across domain-specific RL settings show the value of this selective supervision approach.

entry.title: PHASE: A Physiology-Guided Hierarchical Foundation Model for Intracranial EEG

author.name: Yipeng Zhang, Chenda Duan, Yuanyi Ding, Tianyi Wang, Atsuro Daida, Masaki Izumi, Yuta Tanoue, Naoto Kuroda, Shaun A. Hussain, Nishant Sinha, Eishi Asano. Hiroki Nariai, Vwani Roychowdhury

entry.summary: PHASE is a physiology-guided foundation model for intracranial EEG that makes clinically measurable physiological characteristics explicit learning targets, combined with masked latent prediction, unlike prior iEEG models that learn only via input reconstruction. On the broad Omni-iEEG clinical benchmark, prior frozen foundation models underperformed task-specific models, while PHASE aims to close this gap across a wider range of clinically relevant tasks including seizure detection.

entry.title: Compress to Remember: Learning Compact Memory via On-Policy Distillation for Long Video Generation

author.name: Xiaoyu Wu, Weihang Guo, Yifei Wang, Xinze Feng, Lydia E. Kavraki, Zhiwei Steven Wu

entry.summary: The paper proposes PACC (Prediction-Aligned Context Compaction), which trains a learned compressor to aggregate past video frames into compact memory tokens using supervision from a frozen video generator. This addresses long-context degradation in long video generation without discarding whole frames as key-frame methods do. It is relevant to the growing area of efficient autoregressive video generation.

entry.title: Longer Records, Broader Invariance: The Hidden Scaling Problem in Longitudinal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Rameen Mahmood, Xuhai "Orson" Xu, Zachary Beattie, Jeffrey Kaye, Danny Yuxing Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a fundamental flaw in person-level contrastive learning on longitudinal data: as record span grows, treating same-person observations as positives creates broader invariance that suppresses recovery of genuine behavioral change. The authors separate record span from supervision span using in-home sensing data spanning up to 2.7 years. This has direct implications for health and behavioral sensing applications built on self-supervised learning.

entry.title: Reliable Parallel Decoding in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zhenghao He, Bohan Liu, Guangzhi Xiong, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: The authors study when it is safe to commit multiple masked tokens in parallel in masked diffusion language models, showing that confidence alone is a poor criterion because confident late-sequence predictions can lock in answers before supporting computations are established. They identify cross-layer prediction stability as a better signal for reliable parallel commitment.

entry.title: SERA: Scale-Equalized Rollout Allocation for Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zihao Chen, Fanxiang Xiong, Hongran Ren, Xuefeng Bai, Zhongxiang Dai, Kehai Chen, Zhiguo Zhang, Zhiyong Wang, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: SERA addresses gradient attenuation in Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (MaxRL), where under uniform rollout allocation low-success prompts suffer stronger success-dependent attenuation and contribute less to the aggregate gradient. The method redistributes a fixed rollout budget to approximately equalize the finite-rollout scaling factors, backed by theoretical analysis. This improves training of reasoning models under constrained rollout budgets.

entry.title: Simple Agentic Memory for Generalist Robot Policies

author.name: Yuyou Zhang, Yunbei Zhang, Miao Li, Janet Wang, Zijian Jin, Shilong Liu, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: SimpleARM is a training-free memory layer for frozen generalist robot policies that maintains compact typed interaction state online, using frozen perceptual tools to track history-dependent quantities like persistent identity and accumulated progress that individual frames do not represent. Structured access retrieves state only when a proposed subgoal depends on history, and current-view grounding resolves recalled entities before execution. It is evaluated on RoboMME, a memory-dependent manipulation benchmark.

entry.title: MyoCodec: A Streaming Neural Codec for Electromyography

author.name: Jihwan Lee, Kleanthis Avramidis, Junhyeok Lee, Tiantian Feng, Najim Dehak, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: This paper introduces MyoCodec, a streaming neural codec for electromyography (EMG) signals that combines causal Transformers with residual vector quantization to compress continuous biosignals into compact discrete tokens. It extends the neural audio codec paradigm to the biosignal domain, enabling low-bitrate streaming and token-based sequence modeling for tasks like gesture or speech decoding from muscle activity. This matters because it provides a foundational interface for applying modern generative sequence models to wearable health and human-machine interface applications.

entry.title: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It

author.name: Long Li, Qichao Zhao, Yue Yang, Fan Xu, Zhe Wang, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Chao Qu, Heng Tao Shen, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: The paper shows empirically that current embodied models cannot repair their own failures when allowed to retry, because they train only on successful demonstrations and receive inputs too narrow to reveal what went wrong. Spotter proposes a division of labor where the embodied model acts while a vision-language model reflects on failures and produces corrections. This transfers the reflection-driven gains seen in language models to robotics, a meaningful direction for robust manipulation.

entry.title: Safer Content or Firmer Refusals? A Hybrid Perturbation Defense for Alignment under Harmful Fine-tuning

author.name: Muhammad Zeeshan Akram, Mufid Kamel Marican, Anvesh Reddy Yenugu, Ali Zain Kaimkhani, Minghong Fang

entry.summary: VaccineBooster combines two alignment-stage defenses against harmful fine-tuning attacks: Vaccine's embedding-level perturbation for representation robustness and Booster's weight-level gradient attenuation against simulated harmful updates. The paper investigates whether these mechanisms are complementary and unifies them into a single alignment procedure. This is relevant to fine-tuning-as-a-service, where a small amount of poisoned data can silently degrade a model's alignment.

entry.title: Purlin: Separating Orchestration from the Datapath of Collectives

author.name: Osayamen Jonathan Aimuyo, Swapnil Gandhi, Christos Kozyrakis

entry.summary: Purlin is a scale-up GPU communication framework that decouples collective semantics, orchestration, and datapath, specifying collectives as layout naming plus copy/reduction operations with an SNAC (Stage, Notify, And Consume) protocol in between. This makes it cheaper to adopt new hardware mechanisms and customize communication for distributed inference workloads. As inference scaling makes collective communication a bottleneck, this systems contribution is timely.

entry.title: NowcastDiT: Diffusion Transformers are Effective Precipitation Nowcasters

author.name: Haoran Xu, Xingzhuo Guo, Yuchen Zhang, Jincheng Zhong, Jianmin Wang, Mingsheng Long

entry.summary: NowcastDiT shows that a standard Diffusion Transformer provides a simple, scalable foundation for precipitation nowcasting, with domain requirements handled within its natural design space. Two adaptations are introduced: a dynamics-aware noise prior for temporally coherent forecasts and end-to-end reinforcement-based fine-tuning. The paper argues against increasingly specialized architectures in favor of scaling a standard backbone.

entry.title: Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training

author.name: Hongyang Li, Xiao Li, Caesar Wu, Said Mammar, Gr\'egoire Danoy, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: This paper pushes back on the trend of removing critics from RL post-training of LLMs, showing that a pretrained critic can estimate the posterior probability of eventual success and improve long-horizon reasoning. The authors also show that critic-based RL instability is largely an optimization artifact controllable via low-variance policy updates. This offers a reward-free alternative for LLM post-training that reuses rather than discards the critic.

entry.title: Compiling Learning Problems into Adaptation Programs for Language Models

author.name: Rebecca Ramnauth, Brian Scassellati

entry.summary: The authors propose adaptation compilation, reframing model adaptation choices as a joint prediction and decision problem where a compiler predicts a counterfactual response surface over candidate update programs. The predicted geometry captures effects on acquisition, transfer, boundedness, and preservation before adaptation begins. This moves beyond fixed adaptation recipes toward learned selection of how and where to adapt.

entry.title: Evaluating and Benchmarking the System One Model Jev

author.name: Tobias Deu{\ss}er, Lorenz Sparrenberg, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks Jev, a commercial non-generative model from TypeSafe AI that returns choices, rubric positions, or calibrated probabilities for typed questions rather than generating text. The evaluation spans 37 datasets and roughly 346,000 requests across classification, routing, NLI, moderation, and rubric-scoring tasks with frozen templates. It provides rare independent scrutiny of a small-decision model class used inside information-access pipelines.

entry.title: Explore, Execute, Evolve: A Skill Acquisition and Reuse Loop for Embodied Agents

author.name: Sicheng Xie, Yitong Chen, Haidong Cao, Shunlin Lu, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: RoboSkill connects skill acquisition and reuse in a closed loop: a multimodal agent explores to gather task information, executes tasks while adapting to feedback, and evolves a skill library from execution records that then guides future exploration. The goal is to cut the high cost of zero-shot embodied reasoning by reusing learned skills for unseen tasks. It targets a key efficiency bottleneck for vision-language-action agents.

entry.title: Is manual software optimization a thing of the past?

author.name: Pavlin G. Poli\v{c}ar, Martin \v{S}pendl, Toma\v{z} Ho\v{c}evar

entry.summary: The authors task an LLM-based agent with autonomously optimizing mature, human-optimized scientific software implementations for t-SNE, single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and graphlet counting, comparing achieved speedups against human expert effort. The study empirically probes whether coding agents can now outperform or match manual optimization on real computational kernels. The results inform expectations for AI-driven software engineering in scientific computing.

entry.title: RLX: A Unified Multi-Backend Tensor Compiler and Distributed Runtime in Rust

author.name: Eugene Hauptmann, Nataliya Kosmyna

entry.summary: RLX unifies graph compilation and kernel execution in a single Rust codebase built on a three-level intermediate representation with a transparent dispatch contract that resolves operators to native, common-IR, or rewritten lowerings. The same IR targets fourteen runtime devices including CUDA, Metal, TPU, Hexagon, and WebGPU, plus specialty codegen paths. This addresses end-to-end opacity in production ML stacks where compilation and execution are split across languages and layers.

entry.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement

author.name: Zihang Rui, Renhao Wang, Haoxu Huang, Yang Gao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for robots to autonomously improve their policies beyond initial training by having foundation models compose learned behaviors into corrections for failures. The key insight is that recurring short behaviors (skills) can be extracted from agentic recovery attempts and converted into learnable policy corrections without human demonstrations.

entry.title: NanoForecast v0.5: Competitive Time Series Forecasting Through Training Pipeline Optimization

author.name: Gautam Kishore

entry.summary: NanoForecast v0.5 is a 6.5M-parameter time series forecaster that matches or beats models roughly 31x its size, including TimesFM and PatchTST, purely through training pipeline fixes such as corrected loss-scope handling and better augmentation. MASE improved 43.8% over v0.3 with no architecture change. The result is notable for showing how much headroom exists in training recipes rather than model scale.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Reveals Shared Causal Subspaces in Brain-to-Speech Decoders

author.name: Maryam Maghsoudi, Ayushi Mishra, Sanghamitra Dutta

entry.summary: Using activation patching on a brain-to-speech decoder across vocalized, mimed, and imagined speech conditions, the authors identify which internal neurons carry cross-modal information and show these causal subspaces are shared across speech forms. This mechanistic account clarifies how decoders internally represent different speech modalities, informing improved cross-modal transfer for covert speech decoding.

entry.title: CAFE: Counterfactual Prediction via Fast Posterior Estimation

author.name: Xinyan Han, Xiaoyu Lin, Hao Zou, Xingxuan Zhang, Bo Li, Peng Cui

entry.summary: This paper addresses the fact that individual counterfactual outcomes are not identifiable from observational data, even within fully observed additive noise models, because multiple causal graphs can match the same distribution while implying different counterfactuals. CAFE targets a Bayesian posterior predictive distribution that aggregates predictions across plausible structural causal models using fast posterior estimation. This matters because it moves counterfactual prediction beyond single-graph point estimates toward principled handling of structural uncertainty.

entry.title: A Comparative Analysis of Attention versus State-Space Models for In-Context Learning

author.name: Enes Arda, Semih Cayci, Atilla Eryilmaz

entry.summary: Develops belief geometry, a unified analytical framework comparing attention and state-space models on in-context learning via cumulative Bayes regret, abstracting three capabilities: evidence assembly, belief maintenance, and addressing. Three case studies isolate these capabilities to explain architectural differences.

entry.title: PolyStepOR: Learning to Decide Without Optimal Decisions

author.name: Viet The Nguyen, Gunther Gust, An Thai Le

entry.summary: This paper introduces PolyStepOR, a decision-focused learning method that trains predictors directly from realized decision costs instead of requiring expensive pre-computed optimal decisions.
