It handles piecewise-constant losses by perturbing predictor parameters and using optimal transport to identify lower-cost update directions, without needing derivatives. It performs strongly on classical optimization benchmarks and real-world problems without task-specific tuning.

entry.title: Timestep Weighting: A Hidden Key to Effective ELBO-Based Flow-Matching RL

author.name: Qinwei Ma, Jingzhe Shi, Simin Fan, Ling Li, Mengdi Wang, Alex Lamb

entry.summary: This paper studies timestep weighting in ELBO-based reinforcement learning for fine-tuning flow matching models with reward feedback, showing it provides a unified view of previously heuristic prediction losses. The authors demonstrate that effective weighting depends on the reward landscape and learning stage, with experiments spanning controlled image generation and robotics. This is relevant to the growing area of reward-based fine-tuning of generative diffusion/flow models.

entry.title: Theory of Scene: Breaking the Symmetry Trap in Multi-Agent LLM Coordination

author.name: Liangqi Yuan, Wenzhi Fang, Shiqiang Wang, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: The paper identifies a symmetry trap in homogeneous multi-agent LLM systems: agents acting concurrently without communication collide on split targets and diverge on shared targets, and Theory of Mind reasoning cannot fix this because identical agents form identical predictions. It proposes Theory of Scene, a training-free schema where each agent conditions on its public role and shared task context to break the symmetry.

entry.title: Constrained Flow Policy Updates: A Generalized Schr\"odinger Bridge View

author.name: Boyang Li, Matthew Kim, Sylvia Herbert

entry.summary: This paper addresses online safe reinforcement learning where policies must maximize reward while satisfying safety constraints, a setting where reward and safety objectives can create multimodal action distributions that trip up standard Gaussian primal-dual methods. Rather than estimating the score of an augmented-Lagrangian target policy as prior diffusion-actor work does, the authors differentiate the augmented objective directly through the generation path of a flow policy, avoiding score estimation entirely and framing the result through a generalized Schrodinger bridge perspective. This matters because it could make safe RL more stable and expressive in robotics and control settings with competing objectives.

entry.title: Flow-Matching-Based Protein Structure Tokenizer Made Efficient and Easy

author.name: Zhe Zhang, Yikai Zhang, Jiangtao Feng, Ya-Qin Zhang, Wei-Ying Ma, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: ProFiT is a lightweight flow-matching tokenizer for protein structures that learns semantically meaningful discrete representations with simple codebook-utilization strategies, without manual semantic alignment or heavily engineered objectives. It matches or exceeds substantially larger tokenizers in reconstruction quality and generalization across downstream tasks.

entry.title: Orthogonal Witness Control for Muon Optimization via Sigmoid Spectral Reshaping

author.name: Dat Phi Van, Ngo Vu Minh, Tuc Nguyen, Thin Nguyen, Ngoc-Thanh Dinh, Trung Le

entry.summary: This paper introduces Soren, a matrix-valued optimizer that modifies Muon-style Newton-Schulz orthogonalization by applying a bounded sigmoid transformation to singular values, preserving relative magnitude information across gradient modes while keeping the singular subspaces. The authors interpret Soren as a positive-definite preconditioned gradient method and provide convergence guarantees under relative smoothness and metric Polyak-Lojasiewicz conditions.

entry.title: The Selection Rule Decides the Winner: A Pre-Registered Audit of Open-Set Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Farhan Shahriyar Hossain, Taufikur Rahman Fuad, Md Abrar Jahin, Md Rizwan Parvez

entry.summary: This paper audits evaluation conventions in open-set graph anomaly detection, testing whether best-epoch-on-test-set scoring, copied baselines, and minority-class relabeling determine published method rankings. The authors re-run DEMO, NSReg, and a purpose-built detector OUTPOST under a unified protocol across eight graphs with ten seeds, comparing best-epoch versus last-epoch scoring rules.

entry.title: Source Anchoring for Physical Consistency in Flow Matching Models

author.name: Giulia Romoli, Filippo Ruffini, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: This paper proposes SAPC, a functional flow matching method that encodes physical constraints into the source noise distribution before generation, rather than correcting generated samples after the fact. Evaluated on five PDE-governed systems, it avoids the distribution shift that projection-based methods introduce, especially in high-noise regions.

entry.title: A Spectral Theory of Compositional Learning

author.name: Hugo Rydel

entry.summary: The paper develops a mathematical theory of how compositional reasoning emerges during learning, analyzing deep linear networks in structured synthetic environments and linking experience structure to compositional inference. The theory predicts when compositional inferences become identifiable and how new linking evidence can rapidly unlock them, qualitatively explaining human cognition phenomena like knowing premises yet failing at composition. It connects spectral analysis of learning dynamics to compositional generalization.

entry.title: dOPT: Differentiating Conic Optimization via Geometric Reduction

author.name: Fengyu Yang, Connor W. Magoon, Tyler Watts, Shahar Z. Kovalsky

entry.summary: Introduces a solver-agnostic framework for differentiating through conic optimization layers by reducing the full conic program to an equality-constrained quadratic program at the computed primal-dual solution, preserving first-order sensitivities. The method captures local conic geometry and remains well defined at singular configurations, requiring only a single symmetric linear solve.

entry.title: GradLev: Token-Parallel Test-Time Training Via Costate Prediction

author.name: Bo Liu, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: GradLev makes test-time training parallelizable by observing that online gradient descent admits exact parallel scans given layer inputs and activation gradients (costates). A causal auxiliary network predicts costates across all tokens in parallel, and associative scans compute adapted weights, with consistency guarantees recovering the exact sequential online gradient trajectory.

entry.title: Routing Without Embeddings: Fast And Interpretable Routing With Regular Expressions

author.name: Yifan Lu, Qiyue Zhang, Haotian Shan, Hanjie Chen, Jiarong Xing

entry.summary: REGEXROUTE replaces neural-embedding-based LLM routers with interpretable regular-expression features discovered via sparse autoencoders, motivated by the finding that scaling routing encoders from 0.5B to 72B parameters yields little accuracy gain. An LLM converts grouped SAE latent descriptions into regex extractors refined against latent activations, enabling fast and transparent routing.

entry.title: Unlocking Few-Step Diffusion for Faithful Previews

author.name: Jing Jia, Sifan Liu, Guanyang Wang

entry.summary: The authors show that frozen 3-4-step diffusion samplers can nearly reproduce full-step outputs by optimizing only the initial noise, indicating the bottleneck is the noise rather than reconstruction capacity. They learn corrections to initial noise and denoising updates with endpoint supervision, enabling cheap previews for candidate screening before committing to expensive full-step generation.

entry.title: PulseInfer: I/O-Centric Sparse KV Cache Offloading for Efficient Long-Context LLM Decoding

author.name: Qiuyang Zhang, Kai Zhou, Kai Lu, Haocheng Lu, Jian Zhou, Yuanpeng Su, Kun Bao, Jiguang Wan, Fei Wu

entry.summary: PulseInfer is a systems contribution for long-context LLM serving that shifts sparse KV cache offloading design to be I/O-centric, since existing systems bottleneck on fragmented CPU-GPU recall transfers over PCIe. It hides variable recall latency with interruptible layer-wise scheduling and adapts offloading decisions via an IO-Adaptive Offloading Admission policy. This expands effective memory capacity and batch sizes for long-context decode.

entry.title: Compute Time Scaling with Recursive Models for Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Zhengxi Zhang, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: This paper proposes Tiny Recursive Models for Combinatorial Optimization (TRM-CO), a neural method that scales both recursion depth and parallel sampling width, using a graph-aware tiny network with adaptive halting and a lightweight problem-specific decoder. The approach aims to balance compute scaling on hard instances against the need for small networks that avoid overfitting, outperforming prior heatmap-based general neural solvers.

entry.title: Quality Determines Direction, Length Shapes Magnitude: Length Control for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zijun Weng, Zhongan Bi, Xuanang Gao, Xiaohui Hu, Shuangyong Song, Yongxiang Li, Kaidong Yu, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: This paper addresses response-length growth in reinforcement learning for language models on open-ended tasks, where length is entangled with quality and rewards are dense and graded. It proposes an asymmetric principle in which quality determines the direction of reinforcement while length shaping only modulates magnitude, protecting quality-induced advantages from sign reversal. This matters for token-efficient RL fine-tuning of LLMs.

entry.title: Muon Sublates the Edge of Stability in LLM Pretraining

author.name: Yanzhe Chen, Qifang Zhao, Xiaoxiao Xu, Fanghui Liu

entry.summary: The paper shows that Muon, increasingly used for LLM pretraining, breaks the classical gradient-descent edge-of-stability coupling between loss neutrality, update reversal, and marginal stability. It derives a coherence-corrected loss-neutral boundary for stochastic no-momentum Muon and validates the decoupling in 130M Llama-like LLM runs. Advances optimization theory for modern pretraining optimizers.

entry.title: ORPG: Reconciling Multiple Reward Objectives through Objective-wise Policy Gradients

author.name: Shicheng Fang, Yiwen Zhao, Wenbo Tian, Jiahao Lu, Yining Zheng, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: ORPG constructs separate clipped policy objectives per reward and reconciles the gradients into a single update, using cosine-dependent interpolation for compatible gradients and priority-based projection for conflicts, with a characterization as the unique solution of a spherical directional compromise. It is evaluated on helpfulness-safety alignment among other multi-reward settings.

entry.title: GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Haodong Zhu, Yangyang Ren, Changbai Li, Sheng Xu, Linlin Yang, haiguang liu, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: GraphHCA realizes hindsight credit assignment in a model-free way for group-based RL, attributing credit through hindsight-to-behavior probability ratios without auxiliary models or extra passes, and provides closed-form computation for terminal-goal tasks. It targets sparse-reward, long-horizon LLM agent training where step-level credit is essential.

entry.title: CacheRepair: Learning to Repair Cross-Chunk Context in RAG for KV Cache Fusion

author.name: Genglin Wang, Wangsong Yin, Yeerzhati Abudunuer, Haoxuan Xu, Guoliang Xing, Zhenyu Yan

entry.summary: CacheRepair is a lightweight network that learns the difference between independently precomputed per-chunk KV caches and joint-cache representations, enabling fast multi-document RAG without expensive selective recomputation. It restores cross-chunk attention information to accelerate retrieval-augmented generation.

entry.title: Beyond Teacher Assignment: Domain-Normalized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xin Li, Hao Jiang, Xin Gao, Annan Wang, Yuchen Xie, Jinghao Guo, Xingwei Qu, Yichi Zhang, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: Finds that multi-teacher on-policy distillation with routing alone fails to beat single-best-specialist teachers on Qwen3.5 models at three sizes, because specialist feedback strength is unbalanced across domains. Proposes domain-normalized MOPD that modulates how strongly each specialist's feedback moves the shared student.

entry.title: An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning

author.name: Shangzhe Li, Yuxiao Yang, Tianrun Yu, Kaixiang Zhao, Xiaoyun Wang, Taylor W. Killian, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper connects on-policy distillation's reverse-KL objective to KL-regularized policy optimization, and introduces LSPD, which brings optimistic exploration and off-policy data reuse from value-based RL into distillation. The idealized formulation achieves a sharp O(log K) regret bound and improves rollout efficiency for LLM reasoning training.

entry.title: Output-aware Residual Stream Pruning for Large Language Models

author.name: Chayne Thrash, Kevin Chen, Soheil Kolouri

entry.summary: This paper introduces a sensitivity-aware residual stream pruning method for LLMs that uses a second-order approximation to output KL divergence, rather than the standard activation reconstruction error criterion. By accounting for direction-dependent sensitivity of downstream layers, it selects which hidden dimensions to prune in a way that better preserves model output quality while reducing inference cost.

entry.title: What Stops Recursive Self-Improvement in Robotics? Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery

author.name: Jiaming Wang (National University of Singapore)

entry.summary: This report describes an agentic system that autonomously diagnosed robot failures, wrote new skills or installed external models, and tested changes in simulation over 123 improvement rounds on household manipulation tasks. The agent successfully discovered capabilities, such as deploying an active-viewing model and search skill, but improvements did not compound: changes passed their tests yet the target task (putting condiments in a fridge) did not improve. It offers rare empirical evidence on why recursive self-improvement stalls in robotics.

entry.title: GT-VLA: Target-Conditioned Trace Guidance for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Ninghan Zhong, Jing-Chen Peng, Sriram Vishwanath

entry.summary: GT-VLA is a steerable vision-language-action framework in which an external generalist VLM provides semantic guidance converted into 2D traces that condition the VLA policy's action generation. This aims to combine VLM generalization with VLA control to improve generalization to unseen tasks, configurations, and long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Typed Decision Models: An Early Evidence Audit and Evaluation Checklist

author.name: Lijuan Tang, Yuemeng Zheng

entry.summary: A meta-review of 28 rapid-response papers evaluating TypeSafe's Jev, a commercial typed decision model released in mid-September 2026 that outputs probability distributions over caller-defined options instead of text. The audit finds that the typed readout has not demonstrated independent accuracy gains over label-probability baselines, with Jev's clearest benefits being latency and cost rather than accuracy on hard tasks.

entry.title: PULSE: Identifying Demonstration-Utility Features with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Chenduo Hao, Chuanbao Gao, Pinjun Zeng, Jingze Zhu, Chonghan Liu, Zidong Liu, Xu Yang

entry.summary: PULSE is a sparse-autoencoder-based framework that identifies model-internal features associated with in-context demonstration utility, rather than relying on external query-demonstration similarity. It samples candidate demonstration sets, measures their zero-shot-relative utility under the target model, and scores SAE features by how their activation differences align with utility differences, then uses these features for demonstration selection. This connects interpretability tooling (SAEs) to a practical inference-time problem.

entry.title: When Better Gets Worse: Improvement Fidelity for Self-Improving Agents in Adaptive Worlds

author.name: Ke Wang, Zijie Zhao, Zhiyi Yuan, Changlun Li

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Improvement Fidelity: whether proxy-verifier judgments of self-improving agent updates preserve the sign and ordering of true deployment-world improvements, showing that globally accurate verifiers can still mis-rank specific proposed updates. It introduces PIVO, a mechanism addressing update-level fidelity errors driven by operator shift and deployment response.

entry.title: One-Step Generative Modeling via Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Yirong Shen, Mengfei Xia, Junpeng Jing, Lu Gan, Cong Ling

entry.summary: For one-step generative drift models, the paper argues that balanced optimal transport's exact mini-batch mass matching makes the estimated transport field fragile to batch composition, and proposes treating generated and real samples asymmetrically via unbalanced OT, letting real-sample mass adapt while fully transporting generated samples. Improvements are reported across six benchmark families.

entry.title: Machine learning for the LHC physics program: a 2025-2026 stocktake

author.name: Jesse Thaler

entry.summary: A field review of machine learning for LHC physics covering May 2025 to May 2026, built on the HEPML Living Review corpus. Notably, an agentic AI pipeline surveyed 569 abstracts, read 103 papers in full, and synthesized six field-state claims, with independent verification, making it both a physics-ML review and a demonstration of AI-assisted literature analysis.

entry.title: Improving the Diversity of LLM Outputs without a Trade-off

author.name: Ryoma Sato

entry.summary: The paper introduces DAST, a method that increases diversity of LLM outputs by reassigning token IDs so semantically similar tokens are adjacent, then applying arithmetic or quasi-Monte Carlo sampling over that ordering. Diversity improves with essentially no change to the marginal output distribution and only microseconds of generation overhead, with a one-time reordering cost of a few hundred seconds per model. This offers a practical fix to the well-known diversity-quality trade-off in LLM sampling.

entry.title: Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Actor--Critic: Diffusion Policy Improvement with Finite-Sample Analysis

author.name: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Jincheng Ying

entry.summary: This paper proposes SFAC, an offline-to-online reinforcement learning method that performs KL-regularized policy improvement using conditional diffusion policies. It combines a minimax Bellman critic for advantage estimation with a Doob h-transform formulation, estimating the drift correction via paired self-normalized importance sampling, and provides finite-sample theoretical guarantees. This matters because diffusion policies can capture multimodal action distributions but prior advantage-weighted updates lacked a principled sampling procedure and formal analysis.

entry.title: Demonstration-Free Success-Probability Reward Learning for Generalist Robot Policies

author.name: Duo Wu, Haifeng Wang, Rongwei Lu, Jinghe Wang, Tianyi Xiong, Zhimin Wang, Chao Yu, Shuai Ma, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a demonstration-free reward learning paradigm for generalist robot policies in which dense rewards are learned directly from sparse terminal task outcomes and mixed-quality policy experience, avoiding the distribution mismatch of expert-trained reward models. The authors provide theory showing terminal outcomes imply reward information and empirically improve RL fine-tuning of generalist policies.

entry.title: EfficientAgent: What Makes KV Cache Offloading Work for Concurrent Agents?

author.name: Kunming Shao, Jierun Chen, Jiangnan Yu, Xiao-Hui Li, Chaofan Tao, Yanli Wang, Huanxin Lin, Kwang-Ting Cheng, Chi Ying Tsui, Haoli Bai

entry.summary: The paper explains why KV-cache offloading gives inconsistent speedups for concurrent LLM agents: cached state must survive until reuse while other agents' contexts evict it, so multi-agent concurrency determines whether host-tier offloading helps. It provides an analysis of when offloading works for agent workloads and presumably system designs based on it.

entry.title: Robot-GST: geometry-aware spatial-temporal robot policy representation and evaluation

author.name: Sichao Liu, Zekun Wang, Lixuan Tang, Yiming Li, Xiaohan Wang, Hanzhi Zhang, Daqiang Guo, Peng Zhou, Lihui Wang

entry.summary: Robot-GST addresses reliability of vision-language-model-based manipulation policies by introducing a geometry-aware spatio-temporal behavior representation plus a Gaussian-SAM robotic environment for real-to-sim policy verification. It provides explicit mechanisms for predicting task outcomes and evaluating whether generated actions will reach desired final states, reducing error accumulation in long-horizon manipulation. This is a meaningful contribution to safe deployment of learned manipulation policies.

entry.title: RewardExplainer: Learning Reward Model Explanations from Counterfactual Preference Feedback

author.name: Jingyi He, Nier Wu, Shuang Liu, Xin Wang, Mengnan Du, Xia Hu

entry.summary: RewardExplainer is a framework for interpreting reward models used in LLM post-training by obtaining feedback from the target RM via counterfactual rewriting and training a reusable explainer from that feedback. This closes the loop missing from prior interpretation methods that rely on predefined attributes and repeated per-pair interventions. Better RM interpretability directly supports alignment auditing of RLHF pipelines.

entry.title: The Statistical Cost of Causal Discovery with Feedback

author.name: Sunmin Oh, Seungsu Han, Gunwoong Park

entry.summary: The authors establish the first information-theoretic lower bounds on sample complexity for recovering the strongly connected component partition and inter-component edges in cyclic linear non-Gaussian causal models. The bounds separate the costs of SCC membership identification and external-parent selection.

entry.title: Look Before You Select: Rethinking Vocabulary Sparsification in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yongliang Miao, Shuang Liu, Yanguang Liu, Yandong Bai, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: SparseOPD tackles the memory cost of full-vocabulary teacher corrections in on-policy distillation by first computing the full-vocabulary correction signal, then deciding which token logits to backpropagate through before differentiation. This avoids the sampling noise of sampled-token approaches and the bias of TopK-restricted supervision. The work reframes vocabulary sparsification as a selection problem informed by the correction itself.

entry.title: CoHuB: A Simulation Benchmark for Multi-Humanoid Collaboration

author.name: Hyunjin Park, Jebeom Chae, Minwoo Park, Sunghyun Park, Hanjun Yoo, Seoyeon Choi, Soochul Yoo, Joohwan Seo, Sarmad Idrees, Jae-Sang Hyun, Jongmin Lee, Roberto Horowitz, Youngwoon Lee, Jongeun Choi

entry.summary: CoHuB is a simulation benchmark for multi-humanoid collaborative tasks under egocentric visual observations, featuring 10 tasks involving two or three humanoids and synchronized demonstrations collected via a multi-operator VR teleoperation pipeline. It fills a gap left by single-humanoid skill benchmarks. It enables evaluation of collaborative humanoid control, a prerequisite for robots assisting humans in shared environments.

entry.title: TempoKV: Timely Staging of LLM KV Caches for Memory-Semantic Flash

author.name: Jay H. Park, Hyungjun Kim, Dong Kim

entry.summary: TempoKV addresses LLM serving bottlenecks when reusable prefix KV caches outgrow GPU memory by staging them on a memory-semantic flash hierarchy. It separates early knowledge of cache reuse from resource commitment, recording hits as metadata-only claims and requesting fast-tier staging only when the estimated time until retrieval warrants it. This avoids both SSD latency exposure and premature capacity reservation.

entry.title: Sol-H3: Recursive Self-Improvement for MiniMax-H3 Inference Acceleration on Sol-Engine across Cloud and Edge

author.name: Yitong Li, Jincheng Yu, Junsong Chen, Haopeng Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu, Ping Luo, Song Han, Enze Xie

entry.summary: This paper presents a full-stack inference acceleration pipeline for MiniMax-H3, a 33-billion-parameter open-source video diffusion model, addressing the computational cost of multi-step iterative denoising. The approach combines algorithmic design with optimized operator implementations and is evaluated across heterogeneous hardware, from cloud GPUs (NVIDIA GB200) to memory-constrained edge devices (DGX-Spark). It matters because latency and memory limits are the main barriers to practical deployment of large video generation models.

entry.title: Beyond Energy: When Sustainability Dimensions Reshape LLM Serving Decisions

author.name: Tianyao Shi, Xipeng Shen, Yi Ding

entry.summary: PRISM is a unified framework for characterizing and optimizing LLM serving across energy, carbon, water, and biodiversity impacts, revealing that compute configuration determines energy use while deployment location and timing determine the other impacts. This decomposition clarifies when sustainability metrics lead to different optimization decisions than energy alone. It matters because AI sustainability analysis has largely treated these environmental dimensions in isolation.

entry.title: Omni-IO Skills: Harnessing Your Agent Omni-Native

author.name: Yanlin Li, Mingyang Hao, Shengqiong Wu, Hao Fei, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: Omni-IO Skills is a plug-and-play agent harness that extends existing agents to multimodal outputs (images, audio, video, documents, 3D, code) without retraining the foundation model. It uses hierarchical Skills, a standardized multimodal execution interface, dependency-aware orchestration, and a persistent Asset Registry to coordinate multi-asset workflows.

entry.title: Does CoT-Pass@k Really Check the CoT? A Multilingual Mathematical Audit

author.name: Tar{\i}k Tuna Ta\c{s}alt{\i}, Burcu H\"udaverdi, David Semedo

entry.summary: This paper audits CoT-Pass@k, a metric that adds an LLM-as-judge to Pass@k to verify reasoning chains, testing the unexamined assumption that the judge catches flawed reasoning. The audit runs under the metric's own protocol on five mathematical benchmarks in English, Turkish, and Portuguese, corrupting reasoning to measure judge sensitivity. It is the first such audit inside the metric and the first outside English.

entry.title: Knowing Is Not Choosing: What Explicit Verification Adds Beyond Generative Preference

author.name: Yilong Li, Chengpo Yan, Aayan Arish, Suman Banerjee

entry.summary: This work decomposes factual recall into candidate generation, ranking, and final selection, showing that pre-generation readouts predict recall but not whether a correct available answer gets chosen. Explicit verification with P(True) improves within-question ranking over mean log-likelihood with AUROC gains of 0.08-0.12 and lifts plurality accuracy by roughly 5 points in a Gemma cohort. It clarifies a real gap between a model knowing and using the right answer.

entry.title: Quizzing the Translation: A Prover-Grounded Evaluation Metric for NL$\rightarrow$FOL

author.name: Pu Suo, Ali Emami

entry.summary: Introduces SIV, an evaluation metric for natural-language-to-first-order-logic translation that generates positive and contrastive probes from the target formula and verifies candidate translations with a theorem prover. This fixes a serious flaw where BLEU, BERTScore, and Smatch++ score broken translations higher than less broken ones. It matters because translation quality is the bottleneck in the popular NL-to-prover reasoning pipeline.

entry.title: Unknown is not normal: separating language-model extraction from rule-based decision logic for clinical risk scores

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: This single-author study tests whether separating LLM three-state extraction (present, absent, unknown) from deterministic decision logic improves clinical risk score computation on incomplete notes. Across 1,200 synthetic emergency cases and six clinical calculators, the bounds-based policy that only asks decision-relevant questions is compared against missing-equals-normal schemas and end-to-end agents including one built on Claude Opus, an established model rather than a new release.

entry.title: RGDT-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning for Rule-Governed Decisions and Their Justifications

author.name: Jianpeng Zhao, Haihua Xu, Haoyang Zhang, Shuang Qian, Yixiang Tang, Xintao Wang, Kun Sun, Pei Wu, Shuhan Zhong, Pengyang Wang

entry.summary: RGDT-Bench targets rule-governed decision tasks where models apply external rules to case facts and justify decisions, as in policy, contract, and compliance settings. It provides 202.1K condition-level supervision slots across four task tracks and eight task-probe combinations, evaluating both decisions and their checkable justifications including rule exceptions.

entry.title: CARDAMOM: A Micro-Dialectal Arabic Speech Dataset for ASR

author.name: Bashar Talafha, Samar M. Magdy, Aisha Alansari, Alaa Alkhawaldeh, Abdurrahman Juma, Sharaf Makahleh, Nour Gamal, Omar Attia, Hanaa Kurdi, Najwa Rizk, Maysa Anaya, Hessah Altimyat, Layal Alhazmi, Shumukh Alotaibi, Hajar Alhadaris, Rayan Alomari, Rahaf Almalaq, Malak Alkhorasani, Sara alghamdi, Rahaf Alshamrani, Nsrin Ashraf, Ibrahim Jaradat, Nada Qardahji, Yasmin Zaraket, Elmoukhtar Brahim, Sidi Ebeidy, Oumoulmouminin Mahmoud, Yahjeb Bouha Khatraty, Meya Haroune, Mohammad Ghaddar, Mohamad Eldirany, Rashed Alamoush, Tala Chhaytle, Nuha Albadi, Yahya El Hadj, Hamzah Luqman, Fadi A. Zaraket, Mustafa Jarrar, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed

entry.summary: Introduces Cardamom, a community-curated dataset of roughly 40 hours of transcribed YouTube speech covering 21 Arabic micro-dialects across six countries, with labels for code-switching and perceived gender. It enables fine-grained evaluation and adaptation of ASR systems beyond coarse country-level dialect labels.

entry.title: When Confidence Rises Too Early: Detecting Shortcut Reasoning via Premature Answer Commitment

author.name: Zhaohan Zhang, Junjie Liu, Chengzhengxu Li, Chen Shen, Xiaoming Liu, Chao Shen, Jieping Ye, Ziquan Liu, Ioannis Patras

entry.summary: Presents ConfLens, which tracks how an LLM's confidence in its final answer evolves during chain-of-thought generation to detect shortcut reasoning that textual traces miss. Across three shortcut settings it finds a consistent pattern of premature confidence signaling unfaithful reasoning.

entry.title: Measuring Collapse and Correction in Homogeneous-Panel LLM Debate

author.name: Xin Li, Mengbing Liu, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: Introduces an auditable protocol that logs multi-agent LLM debates as transition ledgers distinguishing collapse (correct majorities degraded) from correction (wrong majorities rescued) across 6,925 MMLU-Pro debates. Replay experiments reveal tradeoffs in intervention strategies, showing final-accuracy metrics conflate opposing mechanisms.

entry.title: Who Is Left of Whom? Tracing Spatial Evidence and Role Binding in Relative-Position Reasoning

author.name: Yingjin Song, Denis Paperno, Albert Gatt

entry.summary: The paper dissects how models perform relative-position reasoning, separating object-location tracking from query-role binding using activation patching across three vision-language models and their language backbones. It reveals a staged progression from early-layer source representations through intermediate query-object representations to late-layer answer states, with causal validation via targeted interventions. This contributes a fine-grained causal account of a reasoning capability where high accuracy often masks inconsistencies.

entry.title: Choir: An Open Protocol for Distributed Multi-Agent Autoformalization

author.name: Yidi Qi, Melanie Weber

entry.summary: Choir is an open-source protocol for distributed autoformalization, decomposing formalization projects into tasks completed by independent contributors running their own agents and LLM subscriptions, coordinated via a GitHub repository with deterministic pre-merge checks. It supports Lean 4, Isabelle, and Rocq. This is a novel social-technical infrastructure contribution that could democratize large-scale formalization of mathematics.

entry.title: IGSD: Environment-Verified Hindsight Self-Distillation for Search Agents

author.name: Angqing Jiang, Gaoming Zhang, Chaoqun Zhang, Jianchun Song, Liyuan Kong, Kena Qi, Wei Lin, Defu Lian

entry.summary: Introduces IGSD, which gates hindsight self-distillation for search agents by verifying each proposed query's actual retrieval effect through environment feedback before distilling it. This addresses the flaw that hindsight-based teacher preferences may not help the student's actual search state.

entry.title: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing

author.name: Keliang Li, Heng Wang, Chen Hu, Daxin Jiang, Hong Chang, Shiguang Shan

entry.summary: Introduces P2A, an active probing framework for browser agents that renders on-demand symbolic DOM hypotheses back into pixels at decision time, letting the agent verify DOM-pixel alignment with lightweight probes before committing state-changing operations. This replaces static Set-of-Marks overlays and per-step dense alignment.

entry.title: PlaylistEval: Can Video-Language Judges Be Trusted at Day Scale and Beyond?

author.name: Shayekh Bin Islam, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: PlaylistEval is an agentic framework for building video-language judge benchmarks over 100-hour video collections without human annotation, generating question-answer pairs whose separability is controlled via causal degradation. It tests whether video-LM judges remain reliable when evidence is buried in day-long videos, which existing minutes-long benchmarks cannot assess.

entry.title: CoVLM-Bench: A Real-World Benchmark for Cooperative Driving Question Answering and Planning

author.name: Kang Yang, Shuai Liu, Hang Li, Yance Fang, Deying Li, Yongcai Wang

entry.summary: CoVLM-Bench is a real-world benchmark that jointly evaluates cooperative driving question answering and trajectory planning on vehicle-infrastructure scenes, moving beyond ego-centric evaluation of vision-language models in autonomous driving. It enables direct incorporation of infrastructure-side views into VLMs rather than reducing them to geometric representations. This fills a gap where QA and planning have not been jointly assessed on the same real cooperative scenes.

entry.title: LEGO-Anything: Coding Agents for 3D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Xirui Li, Peng Shi, Mingwen Dong, Sheng Zhang, Zhuoyan Xu, Dongkyu Lee, Shuaichen Chang, Yi Xiang, Lin Pan, Jiarong Jiang

entry.summary: LEGO-Anything is an Image-to-Code framework where a coding agent iteratively writes and executes Blender code, inspects scenes and renderings, and revises an explicit scene program, making reconstructions inspectable, editable, and queryable. It introduces LEGO-Bench, a simulator-grounded benchmark of 208 images from 104 indoor and outdoor scenes that separately scores artifact validity, visible-surface geometry, and rendered appearance. The program-based representation enables precise automatic evaluation and extensibility.

entry.title: You Cannot Recover What Was Never Measured: Quantifying the Information Ceiling of Ultra-Low-Field MRI Super-Resolution

author.name: Prathamesh Pradeep Khole, Shreya Handa, Utkarsh Gupta, Razvan Marinescu

entry.summary: This study quantifies how much subject-specific information real 64 mT ultra-low-field MRI scans actually contain relative to 3T scans, using paired same-subject data from three public datasets with a validated measurement protocol. It challenges evaluation practices in the field, where generative super-resolution models are judged with PSNR and SSIM on synthetically degraded pairs despite known hallucination. The findings establish an information ceiling that has direct implications for clinical deployment of low-field MRI enhancement.

entry.title: World2Motion: Turning Video World Models into 3D Human Motion Generators

author.name: Tu Fangyuan, Xiangyue Zhang, Yiyi Cai, Yichen Peng, Kunhang Li, Bo Zheng, Zhixiang Wang, Kaipeng Zhang, Erwin Wu, Haoran Xie, Haiyang Liu

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Cosmos 3 video world model into a single-stage generator of scene-aware 3D human motion and video from one image and a text prompt. It addresses the scarcity of paired video-motion data and temporal instability in generated motion, avoiding costly two-stage inference.

entry.title: Why Cross-Skeleton Retargeting Is Non-Identifiable: Structural Limits of Generative Motion Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Li, Wenyan Yang, Pekka Marttinen, Joni Pajarinen

entry.summary: The paper proves that cross-skeleton motion retargeting is structurally non-identifiable under standard generative objectives: training data cannot distinguish whether a model transferred the source clip or recovered a typical motion for the target action. It formalizes gauge non-identifiability in unpaired distribution matching across heterogeneous skeleton latent spaces.

entry.title: The Domain Is a Residue: Adapting Self-Supervised Features, Not Generators

author.name: Thomas Deixelberger, Markus Steinberger

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Representation Feature Adapter (RFA), a small 2.9M-parameter network that removes domain-specific appearance (fog, rain, snow, render style) from frozen DINO self-supervised feature maps rather than editing pixels with a generative translator. The key insight is that domain information exists as a small residue (13-14% of feature norm) on top of scene content in DINO features, so training only the adapter and discriminators while keeping the encoder and a feature-conditioned decoder frozen achieves competitive results against CycleGAN-Turbo on fog removal and night-to-day translation.

entry.title: MG-Thinker: Bi-Axial Self-Reflection for Multi-Image Reasoning Grounding

author.name: Heyu Huang, Chi Chen, Zonghao Guo, Yuhua Li, Maosong Sun, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: MG-Thinker is an RL post-training framework for multi-image reasoning grounding that introduces hierarchical coarse-to-fine self-reflection and handles heterogeneous task-sample difficulties, supported by a curated 25K dataset with task-adaptive Chain-of-Thought annotations. It targets pixel-precise localization when reasoning over real-world multi-image contexts.

entry.title: PoE-Fuse: Precision-Weighted Expert Fusion for Bi-Temporal Change Understanding

author.name: Haruki Watase, Shunya Nagashima, Takayuki Nishimura

entry.summary: PoE-Fuse is a parameter-efficient framework for bi-temporal satellite change understanding that composes frozen foundation experts for geometry, grounding, and language, fusing their resampled features as Gaussian observations of a latent scene state via a lightweight trained trunk. This avoids costly and unstable full fine-tuning or reinforcement learning for change detection, building localization, and damage assessment tasks.

entry.title: WINGS: Reference-Free Gaussian Splatting Inpainting with 3D-Native Generative Priors

author.name: No\'e Lallouet, Michael Fischer, Elie Michel

entry.summary: WINGS performs inpainting of 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes directly in 3D space, using a pre-trained 3D generative prior and a structure completion network rather than relying on multiple 2D diffusion inpainted views. This avoids multi-view inconsistency and long optimization times that plague 2D-reference-based approaches, an important step for practical 3D scene editing.

entry.title: LIFT: Layout-In-Future Video Generation under Large Viewpoint Change via On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Shengxiang Ji, Boyang Wang, Haiyang Xu, Bingnan Li, Yucheng Mao, Zeyuan Chen, Xiaojun Shan, Xiang Zhang, Gang Hua, Jianwen Xie, Zezhou Cheng, Zhuowen Tu

entry.summary: LIFT extends image-to-video generation with Layout-In-FuTure control, letting users specify both what should appear in future views and where, complementing camera-trajectory control. It targets large viewpoint changes where text prompts are too coarse, using on-policy self-distillation for training. This addresses a real gap in fine-grained controllable video generation.

entry.title: Distilling Privileged Control Barrier Functions into RGB-Only Safety Filters for Dynamic Visual Navigation

author.name: Seungyeon Yoo, Gawon Lee, Seungwoo Jung, Inkyu Jang, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes a teacher-student distillation framework transferring the safety behavior of a privileged control-barrier-function teacher to an RGB-only student safety filter for navigation in dynamic environments, mapping a short RGB history, robot velocity, and nominal action directly to a safe action. It avoids the real-time rendering or explicit reconstruction required by prior visual CBF methods and targets onboard deployment. This is a practical path to certifiable-feeling safety layers for learned navigation policies.

entry.title: Massively Parallel Reinforcement Learning with a Chaotic Reconfigurable Clockless Chip

author.name: Eric Oliveira-Gomes, Damien Rontani

entry.summary: The authors introduce a quasi-analog decision-making architecture based on asynchronous Boolean networks implemented on a clockless reconfigurable chip, where each logic element acts as an autonomous entropy source producing statistically independent chaotic streams. This provides many independent entropy sources needed to scale physical-system-based RL accelerators. Experimental results demonstrate massively parallel reinforcement learning with energy efficiency benefits.

entry.title: NeuroDyn-EEG: An Interpretable Pre-trained Model for EEG Based on Neural Dynamics

author.name: Yi Cui, Tong Zhao, Jiaxin Lei, Chuyi Yang, Yifan Cui, Ling Zhang, Yuxiang Yan, Bo Hong

entry.summary: NeuroDyn-EEG is a pretraining framework for EEG that couples an extended Jansen-Rit neural mass model, leadfield-based source projection, and simulation-based parameter inversion. Trained on synthetic parameter-EEG pairs, the compact ~2.43M-parameter model estimates 11 regional parameter families across 90 AAL brain regions from standard 19-channel scalp EEG. This brings anatomically indexed physiological interpretability to clinical EEG analysis.

entry.title: KPI: A Promptable Kernel for Physical Interaction on Humanoids

author.name: Yikai Wang, Honghao Zhu, Xiao Hu, Hao Zhang, Zelin Wang, Yip Fun Yeung, Ding Zhao, Lingfeng Sun

entry.summary: KPI introduces a promptable interaction kernel inserted between a trajectory source and an unmodified whole-body tracking policy on humanoids, allowing the trajectory source to dynamically specify contact behavior at runtime. This addresses the limitation that trajectories alone carry limited information about the interactions they should produce, avoiding per-task controller hand-tuning.

entry.title: T$^2$Mem: Learning Test-Time Memory for Robotics

author.name: Yize Liu, Huang Huang, Yining Hong, Zijian Du, Zhi Cao, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: T2Mem enables a pretrained vision-language-action policy to retain and use historical information via test-time training, encoding observation history into compact fast weights through online self-supervised updates without external reasoning models or memory annotations. This addresses manipulation tasks where needed information is absent from the current observation. It matters because memory-augmented VLA policies are essential for long-horizon, partially observable tasks.

entry.title: Anisotropic Representations Improve Planning in JEPA World Models

author.name: Mingu Kang, Yoori Oh, Sookyung Kim, Joonseok Lee

entry.summary: The paper shows that accurate prediction and noncollapsed representations do not guarantee a task-aligned latent planning cost in JEPA-style world models, since isotropic regularization can induce geometries that misrank feasible outcomes. AnisoWM with LambdaReg replaces the fixed isotropic Gaussian target with a learnable diagonal covariance, improving planning by aligning representation geometry with task cost.

entry.title: CrossBFM: Distilling a Shared Latent Behavior Space Across Humanoid Embodiments

author.name: Tan-Dzung Do, Tuan Dat Phuong, Nico Bohlinger, Cuc T. Trinh, Siwei Ju, Vien Anh Ngo, Jan Peters, Xinchao Wang, An T. Le

entry.summary: This paper introduces CrossBFM, a method that treats the latent behavior space of Behavior Foundation Models as the transferable asset across different humanoid robot embodiments. By exploiting retargeting-based frame-level cross-embodiment correspondence and a unified encoder architecture, it avoids the need to retrain Forward-Backward representations from scratch (hundreds of GPU-hours per robot) and produces a single shared latent space rather than unrelated embodiment-specific ones. This matters because it makes promptable robot skills (imitating motion, reaching poses, maximizing rewards) cheaper to deploy across heterogeneous hardware.

entry.title: Into the danger zone: stable extrapolation in high-dimensional function and operator learning

author.name: Ben Adcock, Simone Brugiapaglia, Xuemeng Wang

entry.summary: Studies when out-of-distribution extrapolation is provably stable in scientific machine learning, identifying classes of holomorphic functions and operators for which OOD error converges at algebraic rates. This gives far more optimistic guarantees than additive distribution-shift penalty analyses, matching empirically observed OOD performance.

entry.title: SPARK: A General Goodness-of-Fit Assessment via Residual Projection

author.name: Xingwei Liu, Yuhong Yang, Wangli Xu

entry.summary: SPARK is a general framework for goodness-of-fit testing that extends beyond parametric regression to black-box learners, supporting continuous and binary responses and low- and high-dimensional predictors. The method uses a debiasing strategy that projects residuals from an initial fit onto nearly orthogonal directions. This addresses a real gap since predictive success alone does not verify that a flexible model has captured systematic structure.

entry.title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining

author.name: André Rubbia

entry.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence article (by Alonso-Monsalve et al., with an accompanying piece by André Rubbia) demonstrating that self-supervised pretraining enables deep learning models to interpret complex neutrino detector events, improving classification, reconstruction, and data efficiency while transferring across different detector technologies. The work extends the foundation-model paradigm to heterogeneous scientific instruments.

entry.title: The Layer Mystery of VLA: An Information-Theoretical Analysis of VLA Latent Interface

author.name: Yuxiang Liu, Lizhi Yang, Fengze Xie, Aaron Ames, Yisong Yue

entry.summary: This paper studies which vision-language backbone layers should feed action heads in VLA policies, finding that 47 of 54 multi-layer fusion configurations underperform the best single-layer policy across LIBERO and CALVIN benchmarks. The optimal layer varies substantially across backbones and tasks, making layer selection consequential but fusion largely unhelpful.

entry.title: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval

author.name: Bin Kang, Jiarui Ouyang, Li Jiang, Bin Chen, Zhuotao Tian

entry.summary: PrecogUI shifts GUI agents from reactive execution to proactive decision-making using a Proactive Experience Pool of anomaly and success patterns and a Proactive Simulation Executor that forecasts the next symbolic UI layout given a candidate action. This enables early anomaly avoidance and reliability-ranked action selection in long-horizon dynamic scenarios.

entry.title: Solving Without Stopping: On-Policy Distillation at Small Scale

author.name: Hongyang Li, Yiming Zhu, Xiao Li, Caesar Wu, Said Mammar, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: Analyzes what on-policy distillation transfers at small scale, distilling Qwen3-8B into Qwen3 4B/1.7B/0.6B students in thinking and non-thinking modes. It finds distillation transfers problem-solving but not knowing-when-to-stop in thinking mode, and characterizes two ceilings on student performance across sizes and modes.

entry.title: Locating Answer-Correctness Signals in Frozen Large Language Models

author.name: Yuansen Liu, Yixuan Tang, Anthony Kum Hoe Tung

entry.summary: This work systematically searches over internal signal families in frozen LLMs (hidden states, token probabilities, residual-stream features, attention, and their fusions) to find where answer correctness is readable from a single forward pass. It addresses brittleness of single-signal probes under distribution shift and divergence between passage-faithfulness detectors and true correctness in RAG settings.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Improving Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Huaman Sun, Dingcheng Wang, Jason Hartline, Jessica Hullman

entry.summary: Proposes a decision-theoretic framework decomposing LLM decision loss into belief formation from evidence and action selection under a provided utility function. Using a synthetic benchmark with known ground truth, the authors characterize frontier and open models and test whether RL interventions targeting beliefs, decisions, or both improve these components and transfer across domains.

entry.title: UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training

author.name: Ashish Jain, Armaan Sandhu

entry.summary: Introduces UserProxyBench, an evaluation layer over the tau-bench family, and the User Fidelity Score to measure whether LLM user simulators actually follow their private user instructions, scored independently of agent success. Holding the agent fixed (at the existing GPT-5.5) and varying the user proxy across 375 enterprise tasks shifts mean task reward by 15.2 points, with a quarter of successes contaminated by simulator errors.

entry.title: Environment Steering: Using Data Flow Control to Improve Agent Utility and Safety

author.name: Charlie Summers, Prajwal Raghunath, Aaditya Pai, Mayur Kulkarni, Zhuo Zhang, Oliver Kennedy, Eugene Wu

entry.summary: Environment Steering proposes that the execution environment, not the model or a judge, should enforce agent safety during runtime and steer agents toward safe alternatives after violations. The implementation models agent and harness execution state as database tables, tracks record-level data flows, and checks them against declarative policies, delivering policy- and context-specific feedback on violations.

entry.title: PrivacySkills: How Privacy Guidance Shapes Source Selection in LLM Agents

author.name: Lucas Biechy, C\'edric Eichler, H\'eber H. Arcolezi, Nicolas Anciaux

entry.summary: PrivacySkills is a controlled framework evaluating how LLM agents choose among equivalent-value information acquisition pathways: public personal data, confidential sources, or asking the user. With 55 synthetic tasks across 11 personal-information categories and 169 skills, it varies privacy guidance delivery (system instructions, skill metadata labels, or both) and user availability. The work clarifies which presentation formats of privacy guidance actually change agent behavior.

entry.title: Representation by Design in Generation: Cross-View Class-Token Alignment in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Xiaoyu Wu, Yifei Wang, Chen Wei

entry.summary: Extending the SelfFlow framework with DINO/iBOT-inspired cross-view class-token alignment on dual independently noised views, this work trains diffusion transformers to learn substantially stronger semantic representations without sacrificing generation quality. It inverts the usual asymmetry where representations serve generation but generative representations are treated as by-products.

entry.title: AutoLoCo: Communication Efficient Distributed LLM Training via Adaptive Synchronization

author.name: Pengyu He, Yan Zhang, Ruien Li, Guangwen Yang

entry.summary: AutoLoCo targets the communication bottleneck in multi-datacenter LLM pre-training by adaptively varying the number of local optimizer steps between synchronizations, rather than fixing this interval for the whole run as prior local update methods do. An adaptive mechanism adjusts both the synchronization interval and the optimizer to the current training state. This reduces communication costs as accelerator counts scale up.

entry.title: Diffusion Policy Improvement with Proposal-Conditioned Refinement Flows

author.name: Junhyun Ha, Juho Lee, Byungwoo Park

entry.summary: PReFlow is a policy extraction method for offline RL that combines critic-based selection of behavior proposals with a conditional refinement flow, avoiding the expressiveness limits of Gaussian editors and the KL-regularization issues of diffusion policies. It formulates a KL-regularized objective whose optimum induces a Gibbs policy, jointly optimizing proposal selection and refinement. This improves the ability of offline RL policies to capture multimodal action distributions.

entry.title: Safe-by-Design Learning via Energy-based Neural Networks

author.name: Simone Betteti, Morteza Lahijanian, Luca Laurenti

entry.summary: The paper introduces a neural architecture based on energy-based modern Hopfield networks that guarantees state-space invariance by design, so every trajectory initialized in a safe set provably remains there, without expensive post-hoc verification. It retains enough expressiveness to model complex nonlinear dynamical systems. This matters for safety-critical control where formal guarantees and model expressiveness are usually in tension.

entry.title: V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents

author.name: Yang Zhang, Jiangyuan Zhao, Chenyou Fan, Jiayu Hu, Xiu Yuan, Chenjia Bai, Xiu Li

entry.summary: V-JEPA Policy builds a world-action model on the latent space of a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder, combining an instruction-conditioned future-latent predictor with a flow-matching action expert. It asks whether large-scale predictive pretraining can substitute for inheriting a full pretrained visual generative model, answering affirmatively with a simpler framework. This is a notable data point in the debate over generative versus predictive representations for robot control.

entry.title: Concealing LLM-Based Multi-Agent Topology via Phantom Structure Injection

author.name: Longzhu He, Zelang Wen, Xinfeng Li, Sen Su, XiaoFeng Wang

entry.summary: MIRAGE defends LLM-based multi-agent systems against black-box topology inference, which can leak proprietary architecture knowledge from observable reasoning traces. The framework preserves the genuine communication topology for internal agents while injecting phantom structure to mislead inference attacks. This addresses a newly recognized intellectual-property and attack-surface risk for MAS deployments.

entry.title: Does Local Video Understanding Transfer Across Encounters? The EgoGears Benchmark

author.name: Yuedong Tan, Lei Qi, Yu Liu, Di Wen, Ruiping Liu, Xiaoye Wang, Yufan Chen, Junwei Zheng, Chengzhi Wu, Chen Zhang, Zhihang Chen, Haiwen Sun, Zongwei Wu, Radu Timofte, Danda Pani Paudel, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: EgoGears is a single- and multi-video egocentric benchmark with 567 single-video and 1,487 multi-video questions from 126 human-collected outdoor recordings across 39 routes, with repeated traversals under varying speed and lighting. It is designed to disentangle whether failures in aggregate cross-video accuracy stem from local perception or from identity preservation, correspondence, and evidence composition. This diagnoses a gap in embodied AI evaluation.

entry.title: seq2cause: One Autoregressive Backbone, Four Causal Discovery Tasks in Event Sequences

author.name: Hugo Math

entry.summary: Seq2Cause is a unified autoregressive framework handling four structurally distinct causal discovery regimes in event sequences, organized along dependency type and causal scope axes, where prior methods each address only one regime and do not scale beyond a few hundred event types. It uses a single shared backbone with regime-specific identifiability handling. The unification matters for causal analysis in vehicles, healthcare, and genomics event streams.

entry.title: Graph Forward Distribution Matching for Molecular Inverse Design

author.name: Yihan Zhu, Yuhan Liu, Brett Savoie, Tengfei Luo, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: The paper introduces GraphFDM, a new online RL paradigm for graph diffusion models that performs optimization through the forward process, using valid generations to define a reward-tilted target distribution over graph size and molecular structure. This avoids the instability, validity collapse, and limited property gains seen when reverse diffusion is treated as a sequential policy in molecular inverse design.

entry.title: Shared Autoregressive Context Can Distort Relationships in Synthetic Data

author.name: Thomas S. Robinson

entry.summary: The paper shows that generating multiple synthetic survey respondents in a single LLM autoregressive completion distorts variable relationships: batching ten respondents per request inflates correlation error by 48-58% for Qwen3.8-27B and 114-127% for Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on European Social Survey profiles, with all else held fixed. The distortion mainly exaggerates relationship strength. This is a practical warning for LLM-based synthetic data generation.

entry.title: SketchSSM: Write to the Full State, Read from a Compact Sketch

author.name: Omin Kwon, JoongWon Shin, Minseo Kim, Kurt Keutzer, Sehoon Kim, Jae W. Lee

entry.summary: SketchSSM accelerates hybrid-attention language models by preserving full recurrent-state updates while approximating state reads with a low-rank, offline-fixed query basis, building on the observation that low-rank state-weighted query approximation accurately preserves read outputs. This targets the recurrent-state access bottleneck that limits decode batch sizes in linear-attention architectures.

entry.title: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers

author.name: Jia Liang, Xi Jin, Liangming Pan

entry.summary: The paper mechanistically compares Matched-Recurrence and Decoupled-Recurrence looped Transformers on polynomial iteration, finite-state composition, and knowledge-graph traversal, using attention analysis and causal interventions to reveal distinct learned mechanisms under final-answer supervision. It explains how and to what extent looped transformers generalize to longer reasoning chains than seen in training.

entry.title: Two Heads Are Better Than One: Aggregating Weaker LLMs for Better Forecasts

author.name: Cheng Peng, Ruixi Luo, Zhi Chen, Wei Tang

entry.summary: Using ForecastBench with 70 LLM forecasters and over 1,000 shared subquestions per comparison group, the paper shows that carefully weighted aggregates of individually weaker LLM forecasters can outperform the strongest single model on real-world forecasting. Aggregation weights are learned on separate training data across 1,121 weaker-model pairs.

entry.title: ALDER: Discovering the Laws of a World by Acting in It

author.name: Teng Cao, Yu Deng, Quentin Delfosse, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: ALDER is an active method for discovering symbolic world-model laws: it proposes parametric equations, fits coefficients numerically, verifies on held-out data, and actively designs new experiments to distinguish competing hypotheses and revise models. This overcomes limits of passive trajectory-based symbolic regression, which cannot separate equally valid hypotheses or escape a fixed hypothesis space. Relevant to interpretable world models and scientific discovery.

entry.title: Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning

author.name: Soutrik Sarangi, Yonatan Sverdlov, Adir Dayan, Haggai Maron, Nadav Dym

entry.summary: Establishes general identifiability and universality results showing when finite probe-based representations suffice for learning neural functionals, and demonstrates that intermediate hidden representations are more informative than final outputs alone. Motivated by the theory, the authors introduce HIDDENPROBE, an architecture for weight-space learning from network behavior probes.

entry.title: Emergence, Not Bandwidth: Physical Coupling and the Limits of Learned Multi-Agent Communication

author.name: Mihir Chauhan, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: The paper derives optimal-message and compression-cost results for rate-limited Dec-POMDPs, enabling a rigorous gap analysis between engineered and learned communication protocols. Experiments on three MuJoCo arenas with varying physical coupling show the learned-protocol gap is an optimization limitation rather than an information-theoretic one.

entry.title: Low-Confidence Remasking Traps Flexibility: Realizing Arbitrary-Order Potential for Diverse Rollouts in Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Moongyu Jeon, Dongjae Jeon, Bumjun Kim, Mingyu Kim, Albert No

entry.summary: This paper traces the diversity loss in masked diffusion LLMs not to arbitrary-order generation itself but to low-confidence remasking (LCR), a popular decoding rule that commits only the highest-probability token per step. The authors show LCR can exponentially suppress lower-probability tokens as more positions compete, observing the effect in LLaDA, and propose decoding changes to unlock diverse rollouts. This is directly relevant to using diffusion LLMs for sampling diversity in reasoning and generation.

entry.title: When Can Attention Heads Be Statically Defined?

author.name: Weixian Waylon Li, Yintao Tai, Marcio Fonseca, Shay B. Cohen

entry.summary: The paper identifies Selective Attention Freezing (SAF), which detects heads with low attention-pattern variance and replaces their weights with fitted post-softmax means halfway through training, representing fixed patterns with absolute-position and relative-distance preferences to reduce storage from quadratic to linear. Replacing 25 percent of attention heads yields about 1.056x faster training at matched token budgets using a fused kernel.

entry.title: When Sparse Reward Meets Dense Distillation: Training Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xinke Jiang, Tao Feng, Zhibang Yang, Zhixin Zhang, Weixuan Xu, Haoyu Zhang, Xu Chu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes hybrid post-training that combines sparse verifiable rewards with dense token-level teacher KL distillation, using neural tangent kernel analysis to explain how their interaction can destabilize joint optimization. The theory aims to guide more stable combined RL-distillation training. Relevant to current LLM post-training practice where such hybrids are increasingly used.

entry.title: Composable Decoding on the Probability Simplex: Theory and Implementation

author.name: Xiaotong Ji, Ahmed Khaled Khamis, Rasul Tutunov, Matthieu Zimmer, Haitham Bou-Ammar

entry.summary: The paper formulates LLM decoding as optimization over next-token distributions on the probability simplex, recovering familiar decoding methods via choices of regularizers and support constraints and enabling new decoders composed from distributional preferences without rewards, critics, or parameter updates. It ships as a library, CompoSimplex.

entry.title: Cross-Rollout Bellman Closure for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yangyang Ren, Haodong Zhu, Linlin Yang, Sheng Xu, Peichao Lai, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper addresses step-level credit assignment in group-based RL (GRPO) for long-horizon LLM agents by leveraging shared anchor states across rollouts, proposing a method that aggregates alternative continuations according to empirical frequencies and recursively propagates evidence across rollouts, avoiding the weaknesses of local averaging and shortest-path estimators.

entry.title: Inductive Feedback for Mixed-Policy Distillation

author.name: Amir Moeini, Huaijiang Zhu, Daniel Havir, Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes limitations of the standard on-policy distillation objective when using verbal feedback to condition teachers, showing that it can transfer unmotivated teacher preferences while leaving much feedback guidance unused. Proposes a mixed-policy distillation method that changes both the minimized divergence and the target distribution.

entry.title: SNIP++: Fine-Grained Symbolic-Numerical Alignment for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Benjamin L\'eger, Shubham Gupta, Samy Mammeri, Kazem Meidani, Cem Subakan, Christian Gagn\'e

entry.summary: The paper shows that existing multimodal symbolic-numerical embedding spaces are only globally aligned: local edits to an expression are not reflected in the representation of its behavior. SNIP++ introduces fine-grained alignment so that the contribution of expression parts is represented, addressing a central limitation for symbolic regression in scientific discovery.

entry.title: Instruct, Not Answer: Using Instruction Privileges in On-Policy Context Distillation

author.name: Hantao Yu, Sandy Han, Udaya Ghai, Ferhat Erata, Joe Lilien, Aman Goel, Ali Torkamani

entry.summary: The paper shows that in on-policy context distillation, general instructions targeting common student mistakes can outperform instance-specific gold answers or demonstrations as privileged information, especially out-of-distribution. This reframes how privileged information should be designed for distillation and self-improvement pipelines.

entry.title: Action Shaping: Policies Absorb What They Can Express

author.name: Yanjun Chen, Jinghan Wang, Xiaoyu Shen, Wenjie Li, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: This work develops a theory for action shaping, the reinforcement learning analog of reward shaping in which a trainable offset is added to actions during training and removed at deployment. It proves an expressivity-based principle: a policy can absorb exactly those offsets its output layer can reproduce, and such absorbed offsets can be removed without changing returns, with a minimal gated linear-head instantiation.

entry.title: CAPEX: Efficiently Distilling Foundation Model Behavior into Deployable Robot Policies through Experience-Adaptive Reasoning

author.name: Shivam Aarya, Zhang Xi-Jia, Chengyue Huang, Junhyun Kim, Huishu Xue, Hrishit Leen, Roman Yakunin, Animesh Garg, Zsolt Kira

entry.summary: Proposes CAPEX, a framework that uses general-purpose multimodal foundation models as autonomous demonstrators for robots, generating zero-shot manipulation trajectories and distilling them into deployable policies. Experience-adaptive reasoning makes expensive foundation-model calls only when needed, addressing the cost and latency of repeated invocation.

entry.title: An Active-Bottleneck Mechanism for Weak-to-Strong Generalization

author.name: Mohammad Zeinalpour, Amir Najafi

entry.summary: The paper gives a precise theory of weak-to-strong generalization in two-stage ridgeless linear regression: a student trained only on teacher pseudo-labels outperforms the teacher exactly when the number of pseudo-labels lies in an explicit intermediate range, with no early stopping or regularization and without assuming a more expressive student.

entry.title: Estimate, Don't Imitate: Reusing Differentiable State-Based Policies for Visuomotor Control

author.name: Denis Shcherba, Adrian Abel, Eckart Cobo-Briesewitz, Paul Mattes, Wojciech Samek, Marc Toussaint

entry.summary: This paper challenges teacher-student distillation for deploying simulation-trained manipulation policies, arguing the student needlessly relearns an action mapping already available in the privileged expert. Instead, the authors reuse the state-based expert and learn only a perceptual interface that reconstructs its missing state inputs, optimizing for downstream control error rather than state-estimate error. Results show this estimate-don't-imitate approach improves contact-rich visuomotor control.

entry.title: How to Tame a Multi-Headed Hydra? Adaptive Multi-Category Safety Steering for Large Language Models

author.name: Chenxi Wang, Ruiyang Huang, Li Huang, Yifan Wu

entry.summary: CAM-Steer is an activation steering framework for LLM safety that coordinates steering direction and strength when multiple harm categories co-occur in a single prompt, a gap in prior adaptive steering methods that handle categories independently. The approach modifies internal activations at inference without parameter updates. This directly addresses the realistic case where a harmful prompt spans several unsafe content types.

entry.title: On the Numerical Reliability of Differentiable Physics-Based Optimization for Robotic Material Manipulation

author.name: Xintong Yang, Minglun Wei, Yu-Kun Lai, Ze Ji

entry.summary: This paper studies the numerical reliability of gradients propagated through long, contact-rich differentiable physics simulations, using two Material Point Method benchmarks for elastoplastic and granular manipulation. It identifies GPU many-to-one sums with thread-scheduling-dependent ordering as a cause of altered long-horizon gradients, including a sign reversal on one parameter gradient. The findings warn that differentiable-physics optimizations may be built on unreliable gradients.

entry.title: Don't Throw Away the Tail: Action Upcycling for Policy Acceleration

author.name: Taesung Kwon, Jangho Park, Sunwoo Park, Youngmin Kim, Seonghyun Jin, Youngjun Jun, Kyumin Choi, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Action Upcycling is a training-free method for robot policy acceleration that reuses discarded action-chunk tails instead of dropping them at replanning, without accessing model internals or drawing extra samples. This mitigates the reactivity-versus-efficiency trade-off in choosing execution horizons for modern action-chunking policies. The observation that discarded actions carry usable information is simple but broadly applicable.

entry.title: Convex Optimization Is Free When Accuracy Is Expensive

author.name: Arthur Paing, Arthur Jacot

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes convex optimization when gradients are only available via approximations whose cost grows like delta to the minus gamma in accuracy delta. In the Harder-Than-Monte-Carlo regime (gamma greater than 2), it proves that minimizing a loss costs no more, up to a gamma-dependent factor, than a single gradient evaluation at the required accuracy. A randomized multilevel oracle adds variance as an independently priced dial.

entry.title: What Drives Dialectal Jailbreaks? An Ablation of Surface Form, Cultural Framing, and Strategy Banks

author.name: Qingyang Xu

entry.summary: This paper extends a classical-Chinese red-teaming framework to Shanghainese and Cantonese and runs a 36-cell ablation across surface forms, prompt-strategy variants, and two target models to determine what drives dialectal jailbreak success. The corrective finding is that dialectal surface form is neither necessary nor sufficient for high attack success, with non-optimized variants staying below 8% attack success rate. This refines understanding of why low-resource-register jailbreaks work, which matters for safety training design.

entry.title: Shared Worlds, Private Minds: Structured Memory for Long-Form Writing as World Creation

author.name: Qiuyu Tian, Xiaowen Gu, Hang Su, Jianghan Chao, Haojie Yin, Fan Guo, Xin Zhang, Jinjing Shen, Ewing Luo, Youyong Kong, Yingce Xia, Zequn Liu

entry.summary: NarraWorld is a structured memory system for long-form fiction writing that treats memory construction as world creation, deriving four connected views from an evidence-grounded graph: world facts, per-character beliefs, open developments, and hypothetical branches. Hierarchical aggregation consolidates events into scenes, plotlines, and plots to maintain long-range consistency.

entry.title: From Knowing to Abstaining: Bridging the Representation-Action Gap in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jialuo He, Huangxun Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces VAD-R, a benchmark for VLM abstention on unanswerable questions, built via a two-stage pipeline that removes shortcut cues and provides fine-grained rationale supervision instead of binary labels. It also enables measurement of spontaneous abstention without an explicit unanswerable option. The goal is to bridge the gap between VLMs knowing they cannot answer and actually abstaining.

entry.title: CertMark: Distortion-Free Multi-Bit Watermarking with Certified Decoding

author.name: Pawe{\l} Batorski, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: CertMark embeds multi-bit messages in LLM outputs via an exact Gumbel-max sampler seeded by the message, preserving the model's original distribution and thus eliminating the usual watermark-quality trade-off. It adds certified decoding with an abstention rule bounding the probability of incorrect message recovery, with both model-agnostic and model-aware decoders. This advances the theoretical rigor of LLM watermarking for provenance and detection.

entry.title: Understanding Confabulation and Rethinking Reconstruction in Activation Explanations

author.name: Gert Lek, Zixuan Xia, Pin-Yu Chen, Lydia Y. Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a standardized evaluation framework for natural-language autoencoder (NLA) explanations of model activations, separately measuring information recovery, contextual support for claims, and writing quality. It finds that under the standard point-reconstruction recipe, explanations become more behaviorally useful while increasingly confabulating unsupported details. The authors then move beyond single-activation reconstruction to reduce confabulation.

entry.title: MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-agent Systems

author.name: Qiyong Zhong, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Houcheng Jiang, Jiajie Su, Huwei Ji, Li Zhang, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: The paper extends on-policy distillation to multi-agent systems, providing token-level teacher supervision on trajectories sampled by interdependent role-playing agents, avoiding the credit ambiguity of team-level RL rewards and per-task reward redesign. It targets post-training small models for stable role competence and collaboration instead of costly API orchestration.

entry.title: Semantic Uncertainty Quantification Needs Factual Equivalence

author.name: Joseph Hoche, Quentin Guimard, Gianni Franchi

entry.summary: Formalizes semantic uncertainty quantification for LLMs into an answer-comparison operator and an aggregator, showing that off-the-shelf comparison operators (NLI models, sentence encoders) are the primary bottleneck because they poorly measure factual equivalence. Proposes a simple recipe that improves UQ substantially.

entry.title: Checking Leakage Witnesses versus Certifying Bounded Non-Leakage

author.name: Chao Feng, Burkhard Stiller

entry.summary: This paper gives a computational complexity characterization of certifying that a language model does not leak over a declared prompt domain under an executable leakage criterion: leak existence is NP-complete, deterministic certification coNP-complete, and exact stochastic certification coNP^PP-complete, with restricted model classes (e.g., finite probability tables, bounded attention windows) admitting polynomial-time certification. It provides theoretical grounding for what LLM privacy audits can and cannot guarantee. This is a rigorous, formal contribution connecting LLM privacy auditing to complexity theory.

entry.title: DynamicDx: Evaluating Evidence Acquisition in Video-Based Diagnosis

author.name: Jiahui Li, Yutong Guo, Nan Yang, Wenzhan Song, Jin Lu, Fei Dou

entry.summary: Presents DynamicDx, a benchmark evaluating each step of video-based neurological diagnosis across 71 consultations and 11 sign categories with authentic patient videos, confirmed diagnoses, and fixed evidence charts. Findings show video improves accuracy by 9.9-22.5 points but gains are driven by evidence acquisition strategies rather than recognition alone, since shuffling frames causes no reliable loss.

entry.title: ParaAgent: Reinforcing Parallel Acting in Open-World Tool Environments

author.name: Shengbin Yue, Hongru Wang, Siyuan Wang, Xiaoxin Chen, Wei Chen, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: Proposes ParaAgent (ParaAct), a structured parallel-action loop combining phase-level exploration-execution switching with action-level parallelism for open-world tool environments, learned via multi-agent cold-start demonstrations and reinforcement learning with multi-level advantage decoupling. The framing argues coordination across granularities matters more than whether to decouple exploration from execution.

entry.title: Reinforcing Agentic Creativity in Scientific Ideation with Night Science

author.name: Priyanka Kargupta, Silviu Cucerzan, Shweti Mahajan, Allen Herring, Jiawei Han, Ryen W. White, Sujay Kumar Jauhar

entry.summary: AI Night-Scientist is an agentic framework using reinforcement learning to teach LLMs when and how to depart from predictable reasoning for open-ended scientific ideation, modeling creativity along action, process, and outcome axes grounded in cognitive science. It targets the low-entropy bias that makes LLM ideation homogeneous, spanning structured day science and serendipitous night science.

entry.title: Boosting Metric Depth Completion via Training-Free Adaptive Response Geometry

author.name: Mia Zhang, Jizong Peng

entry.summary: The paper introduces adaptive response geometry for depth completion, making the choice among depth, log-depth, and disparity coordinates an image-level unknown rather than a fixed assumption, unifying them in a continuous response family with an explicit depth-dependent gain. It derives a response-gradient relation and estimates response parameters in metric space using hard-Dirichlet residual reconstruction. The method is training-free and improves metric alignment of foundation-model depth priors beyond rigid affine calibration.

entry.title: DARE to Mitigate Hallucination: Dual-path Auto-Regressive-aware Editing

author.name: Jae-Ho Lee, Jeong-Eun Lee, Gyeong-Moon Park

entry.summary: DARE is a training-free method for mitigating object hallucination in large vision-language models via representation editing that accounts for autoregressive decoding dynamics. The authors show that prior editing directions constructed from teacher-forcing contrasts do not fully reflect generation-time behavior, and propose dual-path auto-regressive-aware editing to bridge this gap. This improves the fidelity of generated descriptions to visual input without additional training.

entry.title: Spatial-OPSD: Self-Improving Spatial Reasoning via Label-Free Self-Distillation

author.name: Zhenyu Liu, Zhangquan Chen, Keyi Chen, Mingze Sun, Xiang An, Haodong Jing, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: Spatial-OPSD is a label-free self-improvement framework for VLM spatial reasoning where a privileged teacher uses automatically obtainable spatial priors (depth, 3D reconstruction, camera geometry) while the student sees only raw visual-language input. The student distills from teacher-guided trajectories without ground-truth answers.
