entry.summary: DEALS provides decentralized, expertise-aware load serving for multi-agent LLM systems, letting agents decompose tasks and self-organize while sharing resources without centralized controllers, dedicated routers, or expensive LLM-based agent selection. This reduces computational cost and coordination overhead compared to existing dynamic multi-agent approaches. It targets the growing infrastructure problem of serving heterogeneous LLM agent workloads.

entry.title: On the Two Faces of Adam in Separable Linear Classification

author.name: Chen Fan, Csaba Szepesv\'{a}ri

entry.summary: Gives a quantitative analysis of Adam with small fixed positive stability constant in separable linear classification, showing sufficient conditions under which an Adam-trained classifier nearly maximizes max-norm margin before updates become gradient-like, while reaching a target Euclidean margin only much later. This clarifies the transition between two previously known asymptotic regimes of Adam.

entry.title: Learning Perturbation Robust Policies for LLM Agents with Stable Optimization

author.name: Pengxin Wang, Yuanzhe LI, Yuxin Ren, Huanrui Yang, Jingdi Chen

entry.summary: The paper finds that RL-trained LLM agent policies are sensitive to perturbations such as hidden-state noise, pruning, and quantization, and proposes SPrPO (Stable Perturbation-Robust Policy Optimization), which applies adaptive sensitivity-aware perturbations during training. It includes theoretical conditions for stable monotonic improvement and evaluations on ALFWorld and WebShop.

entry.title: SlimWise: Decoupling Expert Pruning Across Prefill and Decode for Efficient MoE Serving

author.name: Gunho Park, Kyoungho Jeun, Juntaek Oh, Byeongjun Shin, Baeseong Park, Minsoo Rhu

entry.summary: SlimWise decouples MoE serving phases: prefill runs the full model while decode uses a pruned expert pool that directly reuses the prefill-generated KV cache without conversion. Across two MoE backbones and three pruning criteria, this training-free phase-tailored serving narrows accuracy gaps versus the full model while cutting expert-weight traffic, the main bottleneck in batched decoding.

entry.title: DreamingGoose: Staged Distillation from Autoregressive Transformers to Bidirectional Recurrent Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Julian Boesch, Andrew Wee, Alexander Stranzl

entry.summary: DreamingGoose converts Qwen3 teachers at 1.7B and 8B into attention-free, bidirectional, gated-delta-rule diffusion students via three-stage distillation, tracing which capabilities survive each conversion stage. It finds language modeling transfers only partially and in-distribution while in-context retrieval fails entirely, with converted students scoring 0.000 on a multi-query recall probe.

entry.title: GeoCFM: Positive-Only Conditional Flow Matching for Mineral Occurrence Sampling

author.name: Moshe Eliasof, Eldad Haber

entry.summary: GeoCFM frames critical-mineral targeting as learning a conditional spatial distribution over occurrence locations from multi-channel geo-images, using conditional flow matching with point-conditioned velocity prediction. This handles the positive-only supervision setting where unlabeled regions are unreliable negatives and similar geophysical signatures have distinct subsurface causes.

entry.title: QAMM: Adjoint MeanFlow Matching for Few-Step Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuehu Gong, Shutong Ding, Mokai Pan, Yimiao Zhou, Jiashu Hou, Ye Shi, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: QAMM converts critic-derived adjoint signals into supervision for MeanFlow average velocity, enabling flow policies to learn finite-interval transport directly and generate actions in few network evaluations without backpropagating through sampling trajectories. The authors derive the adjoint MeanFlow target and train it with an offline actor-critic, showing effective two-call policies on ten HumanoidMaze tasks. This addresses the slow iterative sampling of flow-based RL policies.

entry.title: Retracing Hodgkin and Huxley: State Recovery Does Not Certify Mechanism

author.name: Peiyu Zang, Jiayi Hao, Yongqiang Cai

entry.summary: This paper tests whether machine learning can recover the hidden mechanistic reasoning of the Hodgkin-Huxley neuron model by training structured latent models on simulated current-voltage data while withholding gate identities. It finds that good state recovery and prediction accuracy do not certify recovery of the underlying mechanism, with gate recovery depending on observation protocol and latent dimensionality. The cautionary result is relevant to AI for science claims about scientific discovery from data.

entry.title: FestDPO: Few-step Generator Alignment with Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Jaewoo Lee, Kyuil Sim, Hyeongyu Kang, Kanghoon Lee, Woocheol Shin, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: FestDPO extends direct preference optimization to few-step generative models, where likelihood evaluation required by DPO is intractable because the generators are implicit, by leveraging nonparametric likelihood estimation. This enables aligning efficient few-step generators with pairwise preferences without training a separate reward model.

entry.title: DivOPD: Spread Wide, Look Close for Asynchronous On-Policy Distillation of Multi-turn Agents

author.name: Hanyang Wang, Zeyuan Liu, Zhengyu Chen, Jingqing Ruan, Chaoxu Pang, Zhongda Su, Wulin Xie, Zhizhao Zeng, Ke Zeng, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: DivOPD addresses wasted experience in asynchronous multi-turn on-policy distillation by spreading a fixed turn budget across more rollouts and prioritizing turns with larger cumulative teacher-student disagreement, while excluding turns without usable teacher feedback. Only batch selection changes, keeping per-turn losses fixed. A practical improvement for training LLM agents via distillation.

entry.title: CTP-FL: Common-Trajectory Gradient Prediction for Federated Learning

author.name: Junkang Liu

entry.summary: CTP-FL proposes an alternative to independent local updates in federated learning: all clients evaluate the global objective along a shared, predicted trajectory rather than advancing separate local models. This makes aggregated updates interpretable as gradients of the global objective under heterogeneous data.

entry.title: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data

author.name: Simon Kl\"uttermann, Xueying Ding, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: Introduces PRODiGI, a pretrained data-to-program model that infers an explicit, executable generative program from samples in a single forward pass, supporting sampling, density and score evaluation, and inspection. Adds program-space fine-tuning that refines differentiable program parameters by matching generated to empirical samples.

entry.title: Do Temporal Link Predictors Need Learned Memory? A Smoothed-Count Baseline with a Handful of Parameters

author.name: Lisi Qarkaxhija, Ingo Scholtes

entry.summary: Shows that a simple statistical language-modeling baseline using pooled transition and co-occurrence counts with Kneser-Ney smoothing, popularity, recency, and a shared log-linear rule achieves the best MRR on 7 of 16 temporal link prediction datasets without learned node embeddings. Questions whether complex learned-memory models are necessary.

entry.title: Universal Approximation of Measure-to-Measure Operators by Pushforwards

author.name: Takashi Furuya, Nicholas H. Nelsen, Frank Cole

entry.summary: The paper studies when measure-dependent pushforward models, including measure-theoretic formulations of transformers, can approximate arbitrary continuous operators between probability measure spaces. It shows universal approximation fails for atomic inputs where operators split mass, and then characterizes positive approximation results under conditions on the operator.

entry.title: A Unified Uncertainty Representation for Graph Neural Networks via Doubly-Spectral Stochastic Expansion

author.name: Fred Xu, Thomas Markovich, Florence Regol, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: The authors model uncertain GNN node embeddings as random graph signals, combining graph Fourier filters for structural variation with orthogonal-polynomial chaos for stochastic variation in a doubly-spectral expansion. This single representation supports calibration, energy-based OOD detection, and robustness readouts, replacing the usual patchwork of separate models and objectives.

entry.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention

author.name: Shouren Wang, Chuang Ma, Mohsen Hariri, Debargha Ganguly, Wang Yang, Xiaoqing Tong, Qianying Liu, Xiaotian Han, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: The paper studies how to combine looped transformers with sparse mixture-of-experts, proposing Foil, which flattens experts (halving expert layers, doubling experts per layer and passes) and unties attention across passes. Holding expert parameters and per-token compute fixed, Foil gives each routing decision a larger expert pool and per-pass attention, improving parameter utilization of MoE models.

entry.title: Be Careful Who You Trust: Coordination Dynamics under Corrupted Communication in LLM Multi-Agent Games

author.name: Xuanyi Liu, Niall Dalton, Hairi Amin, Xiyuan Yin, Lydia Lim

entry.summary: This experimental study examines robustness of LLM multi-agent coordination in iterated N-player Stag Hunt games under controlled programmatic corruption of public communication. Across seven LLMs and varied corruption levels, honest agents maintain substantial pre-flip cooperative success even at high corruption (78% at 80% corruption in the focal setting), though public success falls mechanically. The findings inform safety and reliability of LLM agent swarms operating with unreliable channels.

entry.title: Amnesia by Design, Memory By Necessity: Persistent State for Document Intelligence

author.name: Souhail Bakkali, Ayoub Merimi

entry.summary: This survey formalizes the statelessness bottleneck in Document AI: systems process contracts and tables but retain no consolidated knowledge across sessions, a structural choice beyond what scaling, context extension, or retrieval augmentation fixes. It proposes persistent evidence-grounded document state as a unifying framework for memory in document intelligence.

entry.title: Before Answering: Evidence Sufficiency under Size-Matched Memory Construction

author.name: Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Md. Shifatul Ahsan Apurba, Mridul Banik, Md Masud Al Mahmud, Ibne Farabi Shihab

entry.summary: The paper exposes a label-leakage flaw in insufficient-evidence benchmarks where deleting passages leaks the answer through memory size (a paragraph-counting classifier achieves 0.979 AUROC on MuSiQue). The authors propose a provably shortcut-free size-matched construction and MemSafe, a cross-encoder plus set-transformer estimator for detecting when evidence is missing from agent memory.

entry.title: Gradients for Interventions and Activations for Detection: Targeted Feature Learning in Language Models

author.name: Jonathan Drechsel, Steffen Herbold

entry.summary: The paper studies targeted feature learning for predefined concepts in language models as an alternative to post-hoc dictionary search over sparse autoencoders, comparing activation values, activation gradients, and parameter gradients across two estimators for both concept detection and causal steering/editing effects. This yields guidance on which signal suits which interpretability question.

entry.title: TreeRef-BFN: Equivariance-Free De Novo Molecule Generation based on 2D Topology and Internal 3D Geometry

author.name: Ruiqing Sun, Sen Yang, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Yijie Wang, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: TreeRef-BFN proposes a tree-based molecular representation assigning topology and topology-dependent local 3D geometry to a variable-size tree, with ring-closure nodes and null nodes enabling size to emerge during generation. Built without equivariant architectures or autoregressive graph construction, it jointly models molecular size, topology, and geometry for de novo 3D molecule generation, supporting conditional tasks like fragment completion and scaffold decoration. This is relevant to AI-driven drug and materials discovery.

entry.title: Distributed Hydrological Modeling in the Feature Space

author.name: Mohamad Hakam Shams Eddin, Maria Luisa Taccari, Yikui Zhang, Shijie Jiang, Juergen Gall, Markus Reichstein

entry.summary: Introduces feature-space routing for river discharge and flood forecasting: a topology-aware state-space operator embedded directly in the forecasting dynamics, rather than routing predicted quantities through a separate physical model. This lets the model handle upstream-to-downstream flow through river networks across grid cells within the learned representation itself.

entry.title: CAME: Company-Aware Evidence-Memory Experts for Interpretable Quarter-Ahead Revenue Forecasting

author.name: Ya-Wen Wu, Meng-Fen Chiang, Kuang-Da Wang, Wen-Chih Peng

entry.summary: CAME is a residual-forecasting framework for quarter-ahead revenue prediction that refines a leakage-free statistical anchor using LLM-extracted semantic evidence from disclosures and memory of prior error patterns, with company-specific interpretability. On a rolling backtest of 336 company-quarters across 12 large technology firms it achieves the lowest reported error in its comparison. The work addresses combining stable numerical baselines with timely textual signals in financial forecasting.

entry.title: Tokens Change, Structure Endures: Spectral Watermarking for Generated Speech

author.name: Kanghwi Lee, Kyeongseok Jeong, Jeongmin Liu

entry.summary: Redwing is a training-free token-level watermark for AI-generated speech that survives retokenization by building a graph of observed token substitutions and watermarking in the Laplacian eigenbasis so tokens likely to substitute share values. This addresses the main weakness of token-level audio watermarking.

entry.title: HARMONIA: Interpretable Graph Learning through Mixtures of Neural Bases

author.name: Quan D. Bui, Nguyen Do, An Nguyen Dang, Huyen Nguyen, Nhu Duc Minh Nguyen, My T. Thai

entry.summary: HARMONIA is an interpretable-by-design graph learning framework that introduces a Mixture of Neural Bases, routing features to specialized basis experts to enable parameter sharing without sacrificing feature specialization. It addresses scalability and explicit source-to-target contribution decomposition limitations of prior interpretable graph additive models. The work targets applications where graph predictions must be explainable.

entry.title: RAGWarrant: Evidence-Preserving Governance for RAG Policy Promotion Under Quality, Cost, Latency, and Risk Constraints

author.name: Richard Krueger, Lucas Krause, Zach Pocquette

entry.summary: RAGWarrant is an open-source framework that treats RAG deployment decisions as constrained evidence-based decisions rather than leaderboard comparisons, applying predeclared quality and hard-risk gates, preserving negative outcomes, and emitting auditable PROMOTE/BLOCK/REJECT/INCONCLUSIVE decisions. It is evaluated across several standard RAG benchmarks plus synthetic reproduction.

entry.title: DF-CBM: Region-Aware Concept Bottleneck Models for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Georgios Tsoumplekas, Vazgken Vanian, Alexandros Doumanoglou, Panos K. Papadopoulos, Yannis Spyridis, Dimitrios Zarpalas, Vasileios Argyriou

entry.summary: DF-CBM is a concept bottleneck model for deepfake detection that provides interpretable explanations grounded in visual evidence. It builds a vocabulary of manipulation concepts from textual artifact annotations and links each concept to plausible facial and boundary regions, combining semantic description with localization. This addresses the gap between language-based explanations and localization-based explainability in forensics.

entry.title: SRHarness: A Harness for Agentic Symbolic Regression

author.name: Zihan Yu, Shixuan Zhou, Hao Huang, Jingtao Ding, Yong Li

entry.summary: SRHarness is a domain-specific runtime harness for LLM-driven agentic symbolic regression, providing composable scientific actions over raw, transformed, and candidate-derived quantities, persistent scientific state that retains evaluated hypotheses, and trajectory lifecycle management for long search runs. It targets the often-overlooked infrastructure layer that determines how well agentic scientific search systems perform. This matters because harness design is emerging as a key differentiator for AI-driven scientific discovery pipelines.

entry.title: QC-Stark: A Multi-Task Benchmark Revealing Capability Dissociations in LLMs Evaluated on Quantum Computing Tasks

author.name: Pranav Gupta

entry.summary: QC-Stark evaluates LLMs across 11 quantum computing tasks including circuit construction, debugging, compilation, error correction, and simulation, with 2,750 execution-verified evaluations showing that aggregate rankings mask substantial per-task variation. An IRT model validates measurement quality and prompt sensitivity analysis confirms robustness. It matters by exposing capability dissociations that single-number leaderboards hide in a specialized scientific domain.

entry.title: Quantization Thresholds Replicate, Failure Modes Do Not: A Three-Model Study of Agentic Tool Use in Polish from 8-bit to 2-bit

author.name: Jakub Prejzner

entry.summary: Using PolAgentBench, a deterministic 67-task Polish tool-use benchmark, the study measures three Polish-capable models at six GGUF precisions and finds a reproducible collapse between 3-bit and 2-bit quantization, while specific failure modes do not generalize across models. The headline drop is dramatic (e.g., 11B model falling from 0.716 to 0.045).

entry.title: Learning an Anchored Prompt Space for Continual Adaptation of Large Language Models

author.name: Rongguang Ye, Zhan Zhuang, Yichen Wu, Ming Tang, Kede Ma

entry.summary: LAPS addresses continual adaptation of LLMs by jointly adapting model parameters and task-specific soft prompts while preserving prior capabilities. It aligns historical prompts with the updated model via self-distillation and constructs an anchored prompt space whose vertices correspond to learned task relationships, enabling positive cross-task transfer. The method targets the twin problems of prompt staleness and unlearned task relationships.

entry.title: Dense Is Not Enough: Hierarchical Supervision Allocation for Long-Horizon On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuhao Sun, Binrui Wu, Zhuoer Xu, Ming Wen, Haoxiang Xu, Bin Chen, Yan Lin, Qianzijing Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates long-horizon on-policy distillation as hierarchical supervision allocation, arguing productive guidance lies at the intersection of future utility and current learnability, both of which evolve as the student learns. LENS-OPD is a coarse-to-fine framework allocating teacher supervision accordingly on student rollouts in agentic tasks. This improves on uniform token-level matching for transferring large-model capability to small agents.

entry.title: Coherence-Aware Distributional Evaluation of Open-Ended Text Generation

author.name: Jinnuo Liu, Junhao Zhu, Weifeng Jiang, Haoming Liu, Hongyi Wen

entry.summary: The authors identify global coherence as a blind spot in open-ended generation metrics and introduce CHORD, a distributional metric computed in the hidden-state space of a frozen LLM under a coherence-eliciting prompt. It compares generated and human-written corpora to detect locally fluent but globally incoherent text.

entry.title: Neural Language Models Learn the Contextual Distributions of Dependency Structures: a statistical learning theory to compositionality

author.name: Wang Bojun, Junjie Chen, Holly Jenkins, Elizabeth Wonnacott

entry.summary: Proposes that once a neural LM acquires a dependency structure, that structure becomes a new distributional unit whose contextual distributions the model tracks, supporting compositionality. Tests this with a synthetic grammar where structures have contextual distributions unrecoverable from component token statistics.

entry.title: SignFLIP: A Unified Model for Sign Language Translation and Generation via Stage-wise Alignment at Scale

author.name: Zhaoyi An, Sihan Tan, Youngbae Hwang, Kazuhiro Nakadai, Rei Kawakami

entry.summary: Proposes SignFLIP, a unified LLM-centered framework for bidirectional sign language translation and generation using a symmetric architecture and stage-wise training on large-scale data, where pre-alignment supports translation and the translation-adapted representation improves generation. It shows gains across multiple benchmarks over isolated-task approaches.

entry.title: NVAlign: Direct-Gradient Optimization for Non-Verbal Control in Continuous Autoregressive Flow Matching Text-to-Speech

author.name: Qiaolin Wang, Pedro Sandoval-Segura, Anunaya Joshi, Edvardas Jurkonis, Jake Downie

entry.summary: NVAlign is a direct-gradient post-training framework enabling precise control of inline non-verbal vocalization tags (laughs, sighs, etc.) in continuous autoregressive flow-matching TTS. It trains an NVV-aware ASR model to serve as a frozen reward model and uses a two-step gradient surrogate to backpropagate reward through the flow-matching decoder. This fills a clear methodological gap in controllable speech synthesis.

entry.title: Robust Hierarchical Structures for Agentic Document Analysis

author.name: Ruiying Ma, Yiming Lin, Aditya G. Parameswaran

entry.summary: Targets document analysis agents that treat PDFs and Word files as plain text, proposing a robust and compact variant of hierarchical section structure that is feasible to infer and comes with formal guarantees on how well it matches the true structure. Recovering only relevant sections improves efficiency and effectiveness for tool-using agents.

entry.title: Stealth Is a Relation, Not a Property: How Event Representations Create Blind Spots for Timing Attacks in Event-Based Perception

author.name: Shoaib Ahmed Dipu, Md. Shaown Miah, Kamrul Hasan, Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury

entry.summary: This paper characterizes observer-relative stealth in event-camera perception: retiming events within their accumulation window leaves accumulated integer tensors unchanged while altering responses of models that preserve finer timing. The authors construct Null, a gradient-guided timestamp-retiming attack exploiting this exact blind space, and propose a metric bounding the change visible to a given observer, demonstrating high attack success on DVS Gesture. The work reveals a fundamental representational vulnerability unique to event-based vision.

entry.title: UltraMatch: Transport Path Routing for Ultra-Fast and Memory-Efficient Image Matching

author.name: Jiajun Le, Yifan Lu, Zizhuo Li, Lei Cao, Junjun Jiang, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: UltraMatch is a semi-dense image matching framework that avoids the quadratic cost of dense token-level matching by using a lightweight Transport Path Router on coarse block representations to rank and retain only a small set of candidate matching paths. A sparse design then restricts token-level matching to selected paths without constructing the full matching matrix. It delivers large efficiency gains for a component critical to SLAM, 3D reconstruction, and image registration.

entry.title: GleanVID: Complementary Token Selection for Efficient Video Large Language Models

author.name: Shuo Yang, Changbai Li, Rui Tang, Xinyu Zhao, Linlin Yang, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: GleanVID is a training-free inference acceleration framework for VideoLLMs that treats visual token selection as progressive evidence accumulation, retaining tokens that are individually informative and collectively complementary across frames. This reduces redundancy compared to selection-independent scoring methods.

entry.title: Exemplar2VQA: A Scalable Exemplar-Driven Visual Question Answering Generation Framework via Multi-Agent Coding

author.name: Jiayu Ying, Qijian Tian, Ruijie Xu, Xinnan Zhu, Daoguo Dong, Jiachen Xu, Xin Tan

entry.summary: Exemplar2VQA synthesizes large-scale 3D spatial visual question answering data in simulated environments via multi-agent coding, where collaborative agents use a library of geometric utilities so that answers come from deterministic code execution rather than flawed LLM spatial reasoning. It targets the data bottleneck limiting spatial intelligence in MLLMs.

entry.title: ORMA: Optimization-based Monocular 4D Reconstruction of Articulated Animals

author.name: Xuyi Hu, Francesco Palandra, Shangzhe Wu, Daniel Cremers, Riccardo Marin, Silvia Zuffi

entry.summary: ORMA is a training-free framework for recovering articulated 4D animal representations from monocular video that decouples articulation from shape, avoiding the parametric model constraints and synthetic supervision that limit generalization of existing learning-based methods. It targets out-of-distribution species where shape models fail to fit observed morphology.

entry.title: VehicleArena: A Realistic Urban Environment for Multi-Agent Driving

author.name: Jie Yang, Jiajun Chen, Jiazheng Zhou, Mianqiu Huang, Yining Zheng, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: VehicleArena is a 3D urban-driving benchmark where independently operating LLM-controlled agents must fulfill evolving passenger requests in shared traffic, with each agent's decisions reshaping traffic flow, delays, risk, and other agents' observations. It provides 112 evaluation tasks studying emergent physical coupling rather than shared goals or prescribed protocols. It fills a gap in multi-agent embodied evaluation.

entry.title: World4Scorer: Outcome-Grounded World Modeling for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jieyuan Pei, Meiyi Lu, Sining Ang, Yubo Zhao, Zhangyi Hu, Mingwei Xu, Haokai Ding, Wei Li, Zihan You, Jianwei Zheng, Li Yu, Yifeng Pan, Ji Tao, Rongjunchen Zhang, Yan Wang

entry.summary: World4Scorer builds trajectory scorers for generate-and-select driving planners as trajectory-conditioned JEPA-style predictors, trained with simulator outcome labels so every candidate plan is scored against its predicted outcome rather than only the logged executed trajectory. This addresses the fundamental data limitation that driving logs record futures only for executed plans.

entry.title: LexiconVLA: Learning Reusable Atomic Action Codebooks for Unseen Tasks

author.name: Zeming Wei, Jianheng Ye, Xinshuai Song, Sirui Chen, Yang Liu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: LexiconVLA learns a retrievable lexicon of atomic actions using dual codebooks (global structure and fine-grained variation), grounded through joint trajectory reconstruction and visual outcome prediction, enabling cross-task reuse in vision-language-action models. A diagnostic study shows that task success does not imply consistent execution of atomic actions across contexts. Compositional reuse of learned interactions is a promising route to generalizing VLA policies to unseen tasks.

entry.title: Wrench-ACT: Enhancing Robot Policies for Contact Rich Behavior Using Direct Wrench Control

author.name: Johannes Hechtl, Yannik Blei, Simon Ball, Reihaneh Mirjalili, Michael Krawez, Seongjin Bien, Philipp Schmitt, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: Wrench-ACT proposes an imitation learning policy that predicts wrenches as its sole action output for a pure force controller, rather than poses or hybrid force control, targeting contact-rich manipulation. The study finds force-domain imitation depends critically on data collection, with force-feedback teleoperation capturing operators' deliberate force regulation and improving performance.

entry.title: MotorMind: Scaffolding General Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot Robot Manipulation

author.name: Bingxuan Li, Siqi Song, Yizhuo Wu, Jiarui Yao, Tong Zhang, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: MotorMind asks whether a general-purpose VLM can directly operate a robot like a human teleoperator, reasoning from observations, issuing actions, and adapting to execution feedback without specialized VLA training or external tool stacks. It scaffolds a general VLM for zero-shot manipulation, aiming to inherit the rapid capability gains of frontier VLMs. This is an interesting counterpoint to the dominant paradigm of training dedicated VLA models.

entry.title: Latent Inference-Time Guidance of Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Chlo\'e Hashimoto-Cullen, Amaury Durand, Laurent Bozzi, Benjamin Guedj, Yannig Goude, Sylvain Le Corff

entry.summary: This paper introduces latent inference-time guidance for time series foundation models, adaptively combining a pool of TSFM forecasts through a time-dependent latent space with independent components, with identifiability guarantees. Rather than selecting the best lookback or context, the method ensembles complementary forecasts in a principled way. This targets the sensitivity of TSFM performance to user-chosen settings.

entry.title: A stochastic subgradient method with optimal failure exponent

author.name: Bart P. G. van Parys

entry.summary: Designs a stochastic subgradient method minimizing the probability of exceeding a target suboptimality gap under only sub-Gaussian noise assumptions, proving a harmonic uniformly averaged schedule attains the optimal failure exponent via an optimized exponential supermartingale argument. Optimality is certified by a matching change-of-measure impossibility result under Gaussian noise.

entry.title: ChronoSRL: Temporal Geometry for Self-Supervised Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters

entry.summary: ChronoSRL shapes the critic's embedding space in reinforcement learning so that distances correspond to goal-reaching time, giving representations an explicit temporal geometry. Unreached goals and goals from other trajectories are pushed beyond a discount horizon, and the method accounts for the reliability of fast goal-reaching, not just a single fast trajectory. This addresses a known weakness of contrastive and survival RL critics that measure distance in purely spatial terms.

entry.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control

author.name: Zehao Jin, Junran Wang, Ruixuan Deng, Jiahao Chen, Jingyuan Zhang, Yuxuan Zhang, Xinjie Shen

entry.summary: PersonaDose enables controlling language model persona traits to a requested mean intensity via calibrated activation steering, adapting a shared description-conditioned controller without paired training data at target intensities. Across Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B, it raises core-trait expression substantially over contrastive activation addition while retaining coherence. This advances fine-grained, dose-calibrated behavioral control, which is relevant to both customization and safety monitoring.

entry.title: Bits Under ZK-LLM: Evaluating Zero-Knowledge-Friendly Quantization for Verifiable Private LLM Inference

author.name: Taeung Yoon, Yupeng Zhang, Xiaojing Liao

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how quantization choices affect the arithmetic structure, constraint complexity, and proving cost of zero-knowledge LLM inference, where providers prove claims about model behavior without revealing parameters. It fills a documented gap in understanding ZK-friendly quantization for private, verifiable LLM governance and auditing. The work matters as verifiable inference becomes relevant for AI auditing and regulatory assurance.

entry.title: FairDiff: Mitigating the Self-Reinforcing Matthew Effect in Diffusion Recommender Models

author.name: Song-Li Wu, Xianquan Wang, Zhaocheng Du, Weinan Gan, Jingyi Wang

entry.summary: This paper shows that diffusion recommender models uniquely amplify popularity bias: beyond loss domination by high-frequency items, DRMs suffer a structural prior mismatch where the forward terminal distribution of long-tailed data deviates from the Gaussian prior, so reverse sampling trajectories collide toward popular items. FairDiff mitigates this self-reinforcing Matthew effect, improving fairness of the recommendation distribution.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Agent Coordination for Hospital Patient Flow Optimization

author.name: Guoqing Zhang, Rafik Hadfi, Takayuki Ito

entry.summary: The paper combines queueing-theory structure (BCMP networks) with multi-agent reinforcement learning to coordinate patient flow across autonomous hospital departments, aiming to fix the brittleness of stationary analytical models and the centralization assumptions of standard RL. Departments act with localized observations and heterogeneous objectives under a physics-informed coordination framework. It is an applied contribution to healthcare operations.

entry.title: OptiCom : A Unified Framework for State-Conditioned Composition in LLM-Driven Optimization

author.name: Chenxing Wei, Sichen Liu, Lizhao Liu, Ningyuan Sun, Chen Bingzhou, Ying He, Bo Jiang, Fei Yu, Yao Shu

entry.summary: Analyzes how individual decisions drive outcomes in LLM-driven iterative optimization via an opportunity-loss decomposition of expected terminal improvement, then proposes OptiCom, a unified framework that composes diverse search mechanisms conditioned on the optimization state. This addresses the open problem of dynamically coordinating search strategies as candidate quality and budgets evolve.

entry.title: CRASM-Gate: Deterministic-First Constraint- and Role-Aware Semantic Mapping with Selective Model Assistance Across Heterogeneous Industrial Standards

author.name: Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Vahid Tavakkoli, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: This work tackles semantic mapping between industrial standards that encode the same concepts with incompatible hierarchies, roles, and constraints, where lexical or embedding similarity can yield inadmissible matches. CRASM uses deterministic constraint- and role-aware rules with ambiguity refusal, and CRASM-Gate adds a confidence gate that may invoke a candidate-constrained LLM while final authority stays with deterministic validation.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Hyperedges for EEG Seizure Detection and Prediction

author.name: Hyunju Kim, Sheo Yon Jhin, Noseong Park, Nabil Imam

entry.summary: HyBrain models EEG seizure detection and prediction using a small set of soft spatiotemporal hyperedges rather than per-time-step pairwise channel edges, with a per-channel Mamba backbone producing channel-second tokens pooled into shared group embeddings. This better captures the coordinated multi-channel propagation of seizures while cutting training cost versus dynamic graph neural networks.

entry.title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design

author.name: Mahish K. Guru, Mayank Nagar, Ayush vyas, Jan Bohlen, Roland Aydin, Noomane Ben Khalifa

entry.summary: Presents Co-PiLOT, a latent-space optimization framework for inverse design of physical systems that maps candidates through a generative encoder-decoder and searches with physics-informed black-box optimization. It is demonstrated on magnesium alloy microstructure and texture design using a vision transformer encoder paired with latent diffusion, diffusion transformer, and rectified-flow decoders.

entry.title: PrimeSeeker: Capability-Oriented Supervision for Deep Search Agents

author.name: Linzhi Peng, Hanting Chen, Heng Chang, Ke Cheng, Bowen Du, Weifeng Lv

entry.summary: PrimeSeeker argues that synthetic training questions for search agents scale difficulty via indirect proxies (larger evidence graphs, more hops, longer trajectories) rather than local retrieval capability. It introduces latent anchor reasoning - resolving an unnamed retrieval anchor from descriptions and transferring it into a subsequent information demand - as a primitive unit for capability-oriented question construction, and builds training data around it.

entry.title: PACT: Pairwise-Anchored Calibrated Tuning for Single-Token Typed Decisions

author.name: Yida Lin

entry.summary: PACT introduces a training objective for single-token typed-decision models whose data is organized as contrastive pairs with machine-checked certificates, adding four loss terms including a difference-in-differences margin invariant to shared logit offsets and a permutation-style term. This exploits structural information in training data that plain cross-entropy ignores, improving calibration on schema-constrained decisions.

entry.title: AerialDojo-200K: A Large-Scale Benchmark Suite for Open-World Aerial Object-Goal Search

author.name: Tongtong Feng, Xin Wang, Haoran Hou, Ren Wang, Weiran Wang, Shaokai Zhu, Ziqi Jia, Hao Wang, Yu-Wei Zhan, Zongyuan Wu, Jinghao Cui, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: AerialDojo-200K is a large-scale benchmark suite for open-world aerial object-goal search, where aerial agents must autonomously explore large unstructured 3D environments to reach targets specified by semantic descriptions or reference images. It addresses the fragmentation of prior small, environment-specific benchmarks with heterogeneous formats by unifying large-scale training and cross-benchmark evaluation. This aims to enable scalable and generalizable aerial agents.

entry.title: Representable but Unlearned: Encoding Rank and the Interaction-Prediction Floor

author.name: Zahra Khodagholi, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: The paper derives a label-free, model-free error floor for predictors by computing the attainable contrast space from an encoder's equivalence classes, applied to a siRNA interaction prediction task. On a 140-rectangle panel, a GNN's training-only feature mask collapses endpoint states and cuts interaction contrast rank, with the theoretical floor explaining most of the fitted model's error.

entry.title: PyroStack: A Multi-Band Spatio-Temporal Sub-Daily Dataset for Wildfires in the United States

author.name: Arya Kondur, Giosue Migliorini, Cameron Schmitt, Francesco Immorlano, Tairan Wang, Rebecca C. Scholten, Efi Foufoula-Georgiou, Gary Johnson, Chris Lautenberger, Valentin Waeselynck, J. Shane Romsos, Kasra Shamsaei, Alejandro Tejedor, Tianjia Liu, Yang Chen, Padhraic Smyth, James T. Randerson

entry.summary: PyroStack is a harmonized, event-based dataset integrating satellite-derived wildfire observations with meteorology, fuels, vegetation, and topography across the contiguous US and Alaska at sub-daily resolution. It supports both physical simulation and data-driven fire-spread modeling, addressing resolution and coverage gaps in existing datasets.

entry.title: Cross-attention encoding models reveal dynamic spatiotemporal routing across human higher visual cortex

author.name: Iishaan Inabathini, Margaret M. Henderson

entry.summary: The authors extend cross-attention encoding models from static images to naturalistic video, predicting fMRI voxel responses in higher visual cortex while respecting spatiotemporal structure. Their models reveal how the brain dynamically routes action and event information over time. This advances neural encoding research by going beyond simple linear mappings from video model tokens.

entry.title: BaLEEN: Biasing with Latent Encoded Entities for Context-Aware ASR

author.name: Chihiro Taguchi, Yotaro Kubo, Rujikorn Charakorn

entry.summary: BaLEEN is a plug-and-play contextual biasing framework for ASR that injects entity information into a frozen ASR encoder via hypernetwork-generated bias vectors, using a pretrained language model and Perceiver bottleneck to compress variable-length keyword context. It handles domain-specific entities and rare proper nouns without fine-tuning the ASR backbone. This matters for practical ASR deployments needing dynamic vocabulary adaptation.

entry.title: WeLike2Party! In-Context Motion Transfer for Multi-Human Image Animation

author.name: Sangeyl Lee, Seunghyun Shin, Seungho Park, Wooseok Jeon, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: WeLike2Party animates multiple interacting humans from a driving video without explicit pose or mesh extraction at inference, using direct in-context video conditioning. It introduces Reference Asymmetric RoPE Conditioning for appearance detail and Identity Binding Supervision to preserve identity-motion links under occlusion. This addresses a known weakness of skeleton/mesh-based human animation frameworks.

entry.title: FACT: Fidelity-Aware Construction of Articulated Twins

author.name: Kuixiang Shao, Chuansen Nie, Yinuo Bai, Jiayuan Gu, Jingyi Yu

entry.summary: FACT is an agentic framework that progressively constructs articulated digital twins with improved geometry, contact, and dynamic fidelity. The agent drives an evidence-diagnosis-revision loop on a shared editable representation, selecting measurements and model edits from quantitative feedback, while numerical tools execute and validate updates. It reconstructs editable articulated geometry from images and repairs collision proxies for interaction fidelity.

entry.title: EgoHumanoid-V2: Human-to-Humanoid Transfer of Coordinated Whole-Body Skills for Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Jin Chen, Yiming Jiang, Chongyang Xu, Modi Shi, Shijia Peng, Li Chen, Tianyu Li, Mu Xu, Yilun Chen, Steven Hoi, Hongyang Li

entry.summary: EgoHumanoid-V2 is presented as the first egocentric human-to-humanoid skill transfer framework for coordinated whole-body loco-manipulation, combining coarse-to-fine action alignment with kinematic reference correction and dynamics-aware refinement. Robot-arm rendering and training-time image augmentation reduce the visual embodiment gap. This advances scalable humanoid skill acquisition from human video demonstrations without teleoperation.

entry.title: Evaluating Bounded Autonomy in Regulated Agentic AI: A Diagnostic Harness with Constitutional Rewards, Escalation Labels, and Runtime Governance

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: RegLLM is a diagnostic harness for bounded autonomy in regulated agentic workflows, instrumenting six trustworthiness signals including citation validity, grounding, schema compliance, escalation correctness, constitutional alignment, and unsafe-action rate. A deterministic runtime supervisor blocks ungrounded answers and forces escalation, with one domain constitution shared by evaluation, training rewards, and serving guardrails. Results are demonstrated at smoke scale only.

entry.title: TReVS: Integrating Textual Relevance and Visual Saliency for Efficient Vision-Language Model Token Pruning

author.name: Jing Wang, Zhiping Wu, Dongdong Ren, Youfang Han, Wei Zhao, Wenbin Li

entry.summary: TReVS improves two-stage visual token pruning for VLMs by incorporating textual query guidance into the first, vision-only pruning stage, preventing premature removal of query-relevant tokens. Empirical analysis shows query-aware first-stage pruning better preserves task-relevant evidence and consistently improves downstream accuracy at reduced inference cost. It targets the substantial compute overhead of large visual token counts.

entry.title: GARDiff: Graph-Aligned Residual Diffusion for Probabilistic Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Rui Han, Min Yang, Xu Zhang, Xinghao Yang, Wei Liu, Yongshun Gong

entry.summary: GARDiff identifies a previously overlooked misalignment between dependency graphs derived from deterministic forecasts and the residual structures that stochastic diffusion actually needs to model. It proposes a graph-aligned residual diffusion framework to correct this edge-level mismatch in decoupled probabilistic forecasting. The contribution sharpens how structure is transferred between the deterministic and stochastic components of hybrid forecasters.

entry.title: doPlan: A Variable-Horizon Dataset for Multi-Stage Language-Conditioned Planning in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Parthib Roy, Yash Tandon, Marcus Blennemann, Giovanni Tapia Lopez, Angel Martinez-Sanchez, Mohan M. Trivedi, Ross Greer

entry.summary: doPlan is claimed to be the first publicly available human-annotated real-world dataset treating passenger natural language as persistent, multi-stage task context for autonomous driving, containing 5,154 instructions over 169.1 hours built on nuPlan. It fills a real gap since existing language-driving datasets focus on short, localized commands, enabling research on long-horizon language-conditioned planning.

entry.title: What Next-Event Accuracy Cannot See: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Emergency Department Trajectory Simulators

author.name: Zhen Xuen Brandon Low

entry.summary: The authors introduce EDSim-Bench, a closed-loop evaluation protocol for clinical trajectory simulators that measures error compounding when models condition on their own generated events, using 425,028 MIMIC-IV-ED stays with external replication. They evaluate termination, event composition, timing, conditional fidelity, and occupancy forecasting, revealing failure modes invisible to standard next-event accuracy.

entry.title: When Does Domain Adaptation Help on Physical Vibration Sensors? A Held-Out-Bearing Study of Neural-Operator and Convolutional Models

author.name: Kumbha Nagaswetha, Rabi Pathak

entry.summary: This paper revisits bearing fault diagnosis, a canonical domain adaptation benchmark, under a held-out-bearing protocol and finds that widely reported 99%+ accuracies collapse (to 0.36 on shaft-speed change versus a 0.97 ceiling) when the same physical bearing never appears in both train and test. It further analyzes what governs transfer, including computed order tracking for placing fault frequencies.

entry.title: Autonomous Research Project Management as an Agent Skill: A Case Study in Exact Spectral Spatial Regression

author.name: Alexander Chen (University of New South Wales), Jeffrey Meng (University of New South Wales), Bram Hoex (University of New South Wales, GreenDynamics), Tong Xie (University of New South Wales, GreenDynamics)

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate an end-to-end autonomous ML research run executed by DeepSeek V4 Flash (an existing model released in 2026) orchestrated via their agent skill suite on consumer CPU-only hardware. The agent ran an FFT-based kernel ridge regression study on NOAA SST data, using file-based epic/issue tracking across 74 sub-agent sessions with closed-loop recovery from failed hypotheses. It is a case study in making autonomous research tractable and auditable outside datacenter budgets.

entry.title: ROTE: Benchmarking Neural Memorization on Complexity-Controlled Symbolic Sequences

author.name: Xinye Chen, Stefan G\"uttel, Mohammad Mozaffari

entry.summary: ROTE is a benchmarking protocol evaluating symbolic memorization in neural sequence models using sequences with Lempel-Ziv-Welch controlled complexity, comparing gated recurrent, minimal recurrent, attention-based, and hybrid architectures under shared teacher-forced and closed-loop rollout evaluation. It isolates memorization versus rule extension capabilities under matched computational conditions. Relevant to understanding generalization versus memorization trade-offs across architectures.

entry.title: Integrating Language Models into Listened and Imagined Speech Decoding from MEG

author.name: Maryam Maghsoudi, Sai Samrat Kankanala, Shihab A. Shamma, Sriram Ganapathy

entry.summary: Using a paired listened-imagined MEG dataset, the authors integrate language model information at two stages: a contrastive neural decoder aligning MEG with acoustic and contextual language representations, and at inference via contextual cues. They quantify how much language models help neural decoding and show their contribution differs between perceived and imagined speech.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Selection of Online Algorithms with Simulator Ensembles

author.name: Yongyi Guo, Zifan Xu, Ziping Xu, Kelly W. Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies how to select online reinforcement learning algorithms whose performance depends on exploration-related design choices, given only limited offline data for fitting simulators. It proposes forming an ensemble of simulators via bootstrap resampling and choosing the algorithm with the best average ensemble performance, rather than relying on a single fitted simulator. This provides a practical, statistically grounded safeguard against unreliable simulator-based selection.

entry.title: Analog-Friendly Predictive Coding without Activation Derivatives

author.name: Francesco Innocenti

entry.summary: Introduces activation-matched Bregman predictive coding, replacing squared-error energies with Bregman divergences matched to the activation function, eliminating the need for activation derivatives during inference and learning. Combined with mirror descent, this yields local rules requiring only weighted sums, local errors, state integration, and activation evaluations, suitable for analog hardware.

entry.title: Recovery-Directed Symbolic Distillation of Neural Likelihoods

author.name: Kiant\'e Fernandez, Xinwei Li

entry.summary: Introduces a symbolic distillation pipeline that converts trained amortized neural likelihoods into explicit interpretable expressions, using a recovery-directed objective that optimizes for parameter-recovery accuracy rather than likelihood approximation. Candidate expressions are selected jointly on complexity, recovery performance, and distributional criteria.

entry.title: DimPO: Dimensionality Reduction for Attention using Preference Optimization

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Lanz, Yufei Cui, Prasanna Parthasarathi

entry.summary: DimPO reduces the dimension of query and key vectors in frozen language models using listwise preference optimization over key preferences plus a top-k cross-entropy head-fidelity term, arguing this preserves behavior better than KL matching of full attention distributions. It is trained offline per layer from a frozen model's attention and evaluated across LLaMA and Qwen families, particularly in long-context settings. This is an efficiency technique for long-context inference.

entry.title: Stabilizing the Dynamic Low-Rank Training

author.name: Zhonghan Xu, Ling Wang, Junhao Chen, Jianwei Zhao, Jinwei Yang

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why dynamic low-rank training (DLRT) fails to find trainable networks under aggressive compression, identifying a large curvature-coupling term in the gradient flow of the best rank-r approximation as the culprit. Guided by this analysis, the authors modify the method to stabilize training under high compression. Low-rank training matters for reducing memory, compute, and storage simultaneously during training and inference.

entry.title: Equivariant Neural Primal-Dual Assignment for Maximum Common Edge Subgraphs

author.name: Jiaqing Xie, Yanchao Li, Zhuo Yang, Yuxin Wang, Tianfan Fu, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: ENPDA learns a shared equivariant matching policy for maximum common edge subgraph problems, replacing per-pair trained networks and enabling generalization to new graph pairs without retraining. It achieves roughly three orders of magnitude faster query answering with amortized training cost after a few dozen queries. This is valuable for molecular similarity search and other graph-matching applications.

entry.title: Mind the Spike: Mechanisms and Brittleness of Visual Massive Activations in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jonas Ngnaw\'e, Yann Pequignot, Sabyasachi Sahoo, Christian Gagn\'e, Fr\'ed\'eric Precioso, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: This study examines massive activation spikes in large vision-language models, finding text spikes are content-independent and appear in early layers while visual spikes vary by model and image. The authors identify a trigger direction and location rule for spike formation from model weights and study brittleness under image perturbations.

entry.title: Counting on Thinking: Tracing Evidence Integration in Language Models

author.name: Jingming Xue, Robert C. Wilson, Huadong Xiong

entry.summary: The paper uses an evidence-integration task from psychology to probe why LLMs need extra computation for elementary counting, presenting letters one per conversational turn and asking which target letter appeared more often. The study examines whether tokens represent and update an optimal running count difference or deviate toward suboptimal strategies.

entry.title: Mycelium: A Generalizable Cross-Grid Multi-Task Model for Electrical Distribution Systems

author.name: Zhengyang Wei, Shourya Bose, Helgi Hilmarsson, Elena Carnio, Dhruv Suri

entry.summary: Mycelium builds a unified model for electrical distribution grid operations using a grid ontology that represents variable-sized networks as heterogeneous graphs preserving topology, asset types, and electrical relationships. It combines a physics-based simulation pipeline with procedural network generation, faults, and reconfigurations to train models that generalize to unseen networks.

entry.title: SMORE: Stability-Promoting Mesh-Agnostic Model Reduction for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Yangyuan Li, Weichao Li, Shaowu Pan

entry.summary: SMORE is a mesh-agnostic reduced-order modeling framework for time-dependent PDEs that trains latent dynamics with Lyapunov-guided stability regularization to promote stable long-horizon rollouts. It targets the common failure of learned surrogates producing unstable forecasts and exploding gradients during backpropagation, with theoretical stability guarantees.

entry.title: KoopCell: Koopman-Based Generative Model for Learning Single-Cell Dynamics from Distribution Snapshots

author.name: Wanfeng Lu, Yutong Zhang, Keyi Zhou, Chenxin Ge, Wei Lin, Qunxi Zhu

entry.summary: KoopCell learns population-level single-cell developmental dynamics from temporally sparse, unpaired distribution snapshots using Koopman-Mori-Zwanzig theory, jointly learning representations and linear latent dynamics with an explicit branching mechanism. It derives a closed-form least-squares estimator for the Koopman generator via the weak continuity equation with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Hamiltonian JEPA: Action-Conditioned World Models with an Inherited Control State

author.name: Tamim Zoabi, Ameen Ali, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: H-JEPA separates perception and control in action-conditioned JEPAs: a wide perceptual code regularized by a Bures-Wasserstein prior hosts a fixed orthonormal control slice that evolves under phase-conditioned dissipative port-Hamiltonian dynamics. This structures the planner's latent state by how actions move the system, improving planning from pixels.

entry.title: LLM4Trust: Exploring the Capabilities of Large Language Models for Trust Evaluation

author.name: Jie Wang, Yanbo Sun, Zheng Yan, Jiahe Lan, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: This work presents the first benchmark framework for using LLMs in cybersecurity trust evaluation, constructing diverse trust graphs modeling five basic trust properties. It leverages LLM zero- and few-shot reasoning to address limitations of learning-based trust evaluation such as ground-truth requirements and poor explainability.

entry.title: You Only Edit Once: Incentivizing In-Context Capability of LLMs via Local Demonstration Refinement

author.name: Jiarong Wen, Qi Wang, Yun Qu, Yixiu Mao, Heming Zou, Haoang Chi, Lizhou Cai, Yiqin Lv, Kaiyu Zhang, Yuhang Jiang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: This paper frames in-context demonstration selection as a constrained local search and introduces local demonstration editing (LDE), which uses a single structured edit to improve an initially retrieved demonstration set. This avoids the combinatorial cost and repeated LLM queries of existing selectors.

entry.title: Theory Guided and Interpretable Neural Operator Design for Partial Differential Equation Learning

author.name: Zeyuan Song, Zheyu Jiang

entry.summary: AFDONet is a neural PDE solver that for the first time incorporates adaptive Fourier decomposition theory into a VAE-based neural operator architecture for nonlinear PDEs on smooth manifolds. Its design is fully guided by an established mathematical framework, giving architectural explainability and grounding. The claim of turning neural operator design from an art to a science is notable for scientific machine learning.

entry.title: ChemOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task Chemical Reasoning

author.name: Yaoyao Xu, Xinjian Zhao, Xiaozhuang Song, Xuemin Chen, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: Presents a method for consolidating specialized chemical reasoning capabilities into a single LLM via multi-teacher on-policy distillation. It estimates task affinities from supervised fine-tuning gradients, uses a mixed-integer program to form partially overlapping specialist groups, and keeps a generalist teacher so specialist guidance supplements rather than replaces general supervision.

entry.title: Behavioral Monitoring of JEPA World Models with Jacobian Centroids

author.name: Thomas Walker, Randall Balestriero, Richard Baraniuk

entry.summary: Shows that centroids, computed as sub-component Jacobian row-sums via cheap Jacobian-vector products, characterize how JEPA world models organize their input-space geometry and can identify behavioral misalignment during model-based planning. The approach yields task-relevant saliency maps and complements activation-based monitoring signals for detecting planning failures.

entry.title: When Known Physics Helps Neural PDE Models: Residual Constraints Out-Regularize Generic Priors for Nonlinear Dynamics

author.name: Zahra Farazpay, Aniruddha Bora

entry.summary: This paper evaluates physics-informed priors for neural PDE surrogates under a common protocol against matched baselines, finding that known-equation residual constraints consistently beat generic regularizers for nonlinear PDEs (Burgers, KdV, Allen-Cahn) while offering little benefit for linear dynamics. It clarifies when physics-informed structure provides durable value beyond ordinary regularization.

entry.title: UOPD: Uncertainty-Aware Intervention for On-Policy Distillation of Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Pengcheng Xu, Weizhi Du, Jing Zhang, Hengrui Cai

entry.summary: UOPD improves on-policy distillation of multi-turn LLM agents by using low teacher confidence on student actions to identify high-uncertainty decision steps where teacher intervention is most valuable. Experiments in ALFWorld show that a single correction at a low-confidence step can improve subsequent behavior and task success.

entry.title: KVCMAS: Efficient KV cache Correction for Shared Context in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Hyesung Jeon, Hyeongju Ha, Seoyoung Lee, Beomseok Kang, Jae-Joon Kim

entry.summary: KVCMAS addresses redundant prefill in prompt-specialized multi-agent systems where agent-specific prefixes alter KV caches for the same shared context. It provides efficient cache correction that works for first-seen shared contexts without memory-intensive online correction states, reducing computation and memory overhead relative to recomputation and prior delta-correction methods.

entry.title: Rotated Manifold Optimization for Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Yuhui Ding, Javier Zazo, James Hensman

entry.summary: This paper proposes a LoRA optimizer that explicitly incorporates the gauge symmetry of low-rank factorization by extending recent full-parameter matrix optimizers to the fixed-rank manifold via normalization under a rotated basis. The optimizer converges faster to lower held-out loss with better or comparable downstream performance on supervised fine-tuning and RL tasks.

entry.title: MASCIT: A Mask-Aware State Space Classifier for Naturally Irregular Time Series

author.name: Yoo-Min Jung, Hyeon-Gi Kim, Jonghun Park

entry.summary: MASCIT is a mask-aware state space model classifier for irregular time series that feeds observation masks to the encoder and excludes invalid steps from gated temporal aggregation. Across 34 irregular time series datasets it achieved the strongest aggregate performance and the lowest point rank across six irregularity indicators, with ablations favoring partial selectivity.

entry.title: Verifying Neural Networks with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hai Duong, Thanh Le, ThanhVu Nguyen

entry.summary: RSB is a reinforcement learning framework that learns branching heuristics for neural network verifiers, training an actor-critic architecture to maximize cumulative future efficiency within branch-and-bound verification, rather than using greedy static scoring functions. It leverages growing verification data to improve performance over time. This targets more scalable formal verification of DNNs for safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: Shaping Persistent Representations from Independent Interactions

author.name: Ji Dai, Quan Fang, Junyu Gao, Rongfeng Guo, Haoyan Rong, YipingHuang, Yongxi Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces SPRII, a world-model training principle that uses relations between interactions (e.g., trajectories of the same system sharing persistent properties) as weak supervision for learning persistent context, without requiring numerical property labels. Two composable components encourage consistent organization of reusable context while retaining the native predictive objective.

entry.title: Uniform Race: Parameter-Free Approximate Rejection Sampling

author.name: Seiyun Shin, Juhyeong Pang, Kwang-Sung Jun

entry.summary: The paper proposes Uniform Race (UR), a parameter-free approximate sampling algorithm that attains the best rejection-sampling guarantee without requiring the acceptance threshold M as input, using importance-weight-based racing. This resolves a limitation of prior finite-budget bounds whose optimal threshold depends on unknown distribution properties.

entry.title: Separating personal from population gains when calibrating EEG foundation models for new users

author.name: Xilin Tao, Kani Chen

entry.summary: This study evaluates personal adapter calibration of three frozen EEG foundation models across 235 subjects, carefully separating genuine per-user adaptation gains from gains attributable to a stronger population model. Personal adapters consistently improve over both population models and exchanged adapters, with effect sizes depending on data amount. Important methodological rigor for personalized brain-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Fast Learning Rate Transfer in Shallow Linear Networks at Growing Training Horizons

author.name: Mana Sakai, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: The paper proves conditions for fast hyperparameter transfer across model width in shallow linear networks when training horizon grows with width, establishing learning-rate transfer whenever the horizon satisfies a sub-sqrt-width scaling and characterizing transfer rates and failure regimes. It builds on a 2026 framework formalizing when hyperparameter transfer is effective.

entry.title: Explaining Hyperbolic Neural Networks via Geometry-Aware Relevance Propagation

author.name: Ping Xiong, Shanglin Li, Yi Ding, Thomas Schnake, Shinichi Nakajima

entry.summary: The paper develops layer-wise relevance propagation rules for hyperbolic neural networks, introducing Geometric Representation Invariance and zero-curvature consistency as desiderata. The proposed LRP-radial-all rule conserves relevance, is invariant to equivalent radial factorizations, and handles geometric scaling correctly.

entry.title: Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Pretraining for Relational Deep Learning

author.name: Yixin Peng, Er Jin, Diego Collarana, Stefan Decker

entry.summary: This work disentangles two temporal signals in relational databases-as-graphs: shifting record age relative to the prediction cutoff and fixed inter-record intervals. It combines multi-scale and rotary time encodings for temporal pretraining, showing explicit encoding of both signals improves downstream relational deep learning tasks.

entry.title: NeuronDiscover: Agent-in-Twin for Mechanistic Discovery in Neuronal Microenvironments with World Action Models

author.name: Haowei Xu, Wanyi Fu, Hongbin Han, Zhaoheng Xie

entry.summary: Formalizes twin confounding in neuroscience, where a real mechanistic change and an error in a computational twin leave identical signatures in sparse observations, and designs interventions that separate them. NeuronDiscover uses an agent operating inside a digital twin with a mechanism-grounded World Action Model to propose experiments and maintain a scoped MIOY graph.

entry.title: Improving Generative Model Self-Training with Geometrically Modified Outputs

author.name: Patrick Batsell, Thomas Walker, Richard Baraniuk

entry.summary: The paper proposes Geometrically Modified Outputs, which reweight the singular values of generator outputs to explicitly strengthen the negative-guidance signal used in self-training, combating model collapse from training on synthetic data. This is motivated by growing scarcity of high-quality human training data.

entry.title: Control-Geometry Straightening for Sampling-Based Latent Planning

author.name: Ziang Fu, Ning Ning

entry.summary: This work proposes Control-Geometry Straightening (CGS), an auxiliary loss that shapes latent world model representations to make sampling-based planning easier by matching action cosine similarities to latent difference similarities. The method applies across world-model architectures and connects theoretically, under linear dynamics, to temporal straightening, improving planning efficiency from raw pixel-action pairs.

entry.title: SANTA++: Sampling Attention through Representative Keys

author.name: Kyle Lee, Christian Z. Pratt, Ruoyu Fang, Heekyung Lee, Avinash Lohitsa, Ryan Modafe, Kerem Y. Camsari

entry.summary: SANTA++ is a training-free stochastic attention method that accelerates long-context inference by organizing cached keys into teams and scoring one representative key per team, then computing exact attention within sampled teams with inverse-probability reweighting. This importance sampling correction yields unbiased estimates of full attention while trading memory reads against a controllable sampling budget.

entry.title: Calibration-Free Surface Normals Estimation in Vision-Based Tactile Sensing using Universal Photometric Stereo

author.name: Zdravko Dugonjic, Stefanie Speidel, Roberto Calandra

entry.summary: This paper proposes a calibration-free procedure for estimating contact surface normals in vision-based tactile sensors by leveraging universal photometric stereo networks, eliminating the need to physically press calibrated probes against each sensor elastomer. Experiments on three sensors with different optical systems validate the approach. Removing per-sensor calibration is a meaningful step toward scalable tactile sensing for robotics.

entry.title: Optimal transport meets speech: a tutorial review

author.name: Xugang Lu, Yu Tsao

entry.summary: A tutorial review of Optimal Transport (OT) methods for speech research, covering discrepancy measures between distributions with non-overlapping supports and their applications to generative modeling, domain adaptation, and transfer learning. It argues OT is underexplored in speech despite its success in vision and NLP, and maps OT techniques to speech-specific challenges like temporal dynamics and multimodal representations.

entry.title: DegreeSpar: Structured Degree Sparsity for Efficient Secure Transformer Inference

author.name: Yifei Cai, Zhuoran Li, Xiaozuo Shen, Hongyi Wu, Chunsheng Xin

entry.summary: DegreeSpar formulates secure transformer compression as structured sparsification over nonlinear polynomial degrees, unifying approximation, token-pruning, and model-pruning that otherwise accumulate errors under aggressive compression. It addresses major cryptographic bottlenecks (Softmax, GeLU) in privacy-preserving transformer inference.

entry.title: Convergent Plug-and-Play Image Restoration with Annealed Noise Levels

author.name: Samuel Hurault

entry.summary: The paper establishes convergence guarantees for a broad family of plug-and-play image restoration algorithms with annealed denoiser noise levels, covering deterministic methods (RED-GD, PnP-PGD) and stochastic ones (SNORE, equivariant RED, a PnP-Flow variant). For each, it identifies an explicit nonconvex objective at the terminal denoising level and proves asymptotic stationarity.

entry.title: Plan-to-Synthesis: Cross-City Human Mobility Generation via Semantic Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Zhoufu Wang, Baoshen Guo, Zhiqing Hong, Junyi Li, Kailai Sun, Heye Huang, Alok Prakash, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao

entry.summary: SeMoFlow generates realistic cross-city POI visitation trajectories by encoding heterogeneous POIs into a shared semantic space and using latent flow matching, avoiding per-city diffusion training and the high cost of LLM-based generators for long-horizon mobility synthesis. It targets applications in transportation planning and urban modeling.

entry.title: Decision-Sufficient State Representations: Measuring and Reducing Write-Time Regret

author.name: Bingyu Shen, Boyang Li

entry.summary: Studies LLM agents that carry a short written state instead of full history, decomposing reader loss into an unavoidable budget loss and write-time regret from the writer's choices, by comparing against a hindsight-optimal state of the same size. The paper quantifies this regret in TextWorld cooking games and explores whether training can reduce it.

entry.title: Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation

author.name: Shuo Chang, Yueqi Wang, Zihuan Diao, Ali Montazer, Jiangguo Zhang, Joyneel Misra, Dapeng Hong, Tomer Margolin, Sourabh Bansod, Ningren Han

entry.summary: Proposes a Factorized Latent Value model for short-form video recommendation that treats behavioral signals as imperfect measurements of latent user preference, addressing confounders such as watch time scaling with video duration. The approach aims to stop recommender objectives from amplifying measurement artifacts rather than improving user value.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient 3D Segmentation of Liver and Liver tumors: Depthwise factorization Scales Better Than Dense Convolution with Spatial Dimensionality

author.name: Adham M. Alkhadrawi, Mohammed A. B. Mahmoud

entry.summary: The authors observe that depthwise separable convolutions scale from 2D to 3D with only about 5 percent parameter growth versus 200 percent for dense convolutions, and exploit this to build a 3D U-Net with roughly 537 thousand parameters, 24 times fewer than a dense equivalent. The model performs competitive liver and liver-tumor segmentation on the MSD Task03 benchmark. This demonstrates that efficient factorized architectures can challenge dense 3D convnets in volumetric medical imaging under tight parameter budgets.

entry.title: Beyond Calibration: Do a Typed-Decision Model's Probabilities Obey the Probability Axioms?

author.name: Keyi Li, Yihao He, Quanyi Li

entry.summary: The paper tests probabilistic coherence — whether probabilities assigned to logically related questions fit together — in typed-decision models, using a label-free battery of linked questions on ChaosNLI and PubMedQA items with three mutually exclusive labels. Across negation pairs and related queries, the tested model's probabilities violate basic probability axioms even when accuracy and calibration look acceptable. This argues that acting systems need coherence guarantees beyond calibration metrics.

entry.title: Neural Scaling Laws of Transformer Operator Network

author.name: Haoran Yan, Zhongjie Shi, Yuanzhe Xi, Peng Chen, Wenjing Liao

entry.summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework for approximation and generalization error scaling of transformer-based operator learning for physical systems, building on a local-to-global approximation principle aligned with softmax attention. It derives universal approximation results and scaling laws connecting data and model size to prediction error.

entry.title: Audit-First VAPO: Risk-Certified Selective Updates under Imperfect Verification

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Rui Chen, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: Audit-First VAPO separates directional admission from magnitude control in policy updates under imperfect verifiers: an observation-only accept-appeal-abstain policy with a finite verification budget is frozen before clean labels arrive, and finite-sample bounds certify harmful risk, coverage, and verifier-call rates. After admission, a bounded trust-clip-KL actuator controls update magnitude.

entry.title: Constrained Edit Fields for Training-Free Flow Editing

author.name: Jingxuan Kang, Yinsong Wang, Che Liu, Chen Qin

entry.summary: CEF improves training-free image editing with rectified-flow models by assigning each spatial location a continuous edit responsibility estimated from the source image, constraining trajectory updates to relevant regions. For edits whose target is absent, it first synthesizes the relevant content to estimate responsibility.

entry.title: Annealed Sinkhorn with Momentum: Certified Unregularized Optimal Transport in Linear Memory

author.name: Samuel J. K. Chin, Maximilian Schiffer

entry.summary: The paper characterizes Bregman Douglas-Rachford splitting for unregularized discrete OT, showing it coincides with warm-started IPOT with one inner Sinkhorn iteration and is equivalent to annealed Sinkhorn with an implicit inverse-linear temperature schedule plus log-scaling momentum. This yields an anytime primal-dual certificate with memory reduced from quadratic to linear.

entry.title: EEG-Fusion: Failure-Informed Source-Free Expert Routing for Robust Motor Imagery EEG Decoding

author.name: Abdul Basit, Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: EEG-Fusion frames source-free motor-imagery EEG decoding as label-free reliability estimation over heterogeneous experts, routing each target subject to a neural, covariance-based, or physiological-feature expert. The framework addresses the problem of decoders becoming overconfident near-one-class predictors under subject shift, using Euclidean alignment and normalization-only test-time adaptation. This improves robustness of brain-computer interfaces deployed without target-user labels.

entry.title: Stashbird: Efficient Speaker-Indexed Memory for Conversational Agents

author.name: Chidera Biringa, Lucas Yannul, Xiaowen Wang, Marco Ayala, Nicholas Yi, Alex Moyse, Nishant Manchanda, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: Stashbird is an agent memory system linking source episodes to derived memory state through explicit provenance, organized into episodic records, semantic relations, community summaries, and persisted graph state with lifecycle operations including episode-level deletion. It reports large efficiency gains, such as 76.4x fewer ingestion prompt tokens than Graphiti on LoCoMo.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Cardiac Model Personalisation from Ultrafast Ultrasound

author.name: Camilla Ferrario (CHU Bordeaux), Maelys Venet (CHU Bordeaux), Olivier Villemain (CHU Bordeaux), Maxime Sermesant (EPIONE)

entry.summary: This work formulates cardiac model personalization from ultrafast ultrasound shear wave elastography as a statistical inference problem using simulation-based inference. With a subject-adapted 0D cardiovascular model and neural posterior estimation, it estimates posterior distributions over mechanical parameters like active stiffness scale, acknowledging the ill-posedness of the inverse problem. This brings principled uncertainty quantification to clinical cardiovascular modeling.

entry.title: Multi-Task Learning of Conditional Mean Operators: applications to dynamical systems and uncertainty quantification

author.name: Sami Chemlal, Thibaut Germain, R\'emi Flamary, Vladimir R. Kostic, Karim Lounici

entry.summary: The paper proposes jointly estimating conditional mean operators, linear operators between function spaces that provide access to broad classes of conditional statistics, by assuming related CMOs share finite-dimensional input and output spaces specialized per task. This exploits shared structure across related conditional distributions rather than estimating each operator independently. Applications include uncertainty quantification and dynamical systems analysis, with an author team including Flamary and Kostic.

entry.title: Copy the Same, Distill the Difference: Initializing Linear Vision Transformers

author.name: Huaiyuan Qin, Muli Yang, Gabriel James Goenawan, Shiqi Huang, Min Kass Chong, Wahyu Wiratama, Peng Hu, Chen Gong, Wu Liu, Xi Peng, Chun Jian Ho, Hongyuan Zhu

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether linear ViTs, which replace softmax attention with linear-complexity operators, can be initialized from pre-trained softmax ViT weights, finding that contrary to prior attention-transfer work, softmax-to-linear transfer requires a copy-then-distill strategy rather than direct attention reuse. This enables efficient conversion of foundation ViTs to linear variants without full retraining. It matters for efficient deployment of vision transformers.

entry.title: Language Distances are Practical for Equitable Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: York Hay Ng, Razan Ahsan Rifandi, Aditya Khan, En-Shiun Annie Lee

entry.summary: The paper presents the first equity-focused evaluation of source-language ranking paradigms based on language distances, studying resource-level and task inequality across ten cross-lingual tasks and two multilingual models. It assesses how reliably distance-based rankers pick good transfer sources, especially for low-resource targets.

entry.title: PC-SubMax: Efficient Prompt Compression via Regularized Submodular Maximization

author.name: Ziyi Zhang, Shuang Cui, Haotian Zhang, Xiaoyu Wang

entry.summary: PC-SubMax formulates selective prompt compression as regularized monotone submodular maximization, capturing inter-sentence redundancy that fixed token- or sentence-level importance scores miss. The approach is model-agnostic and avoids the heavy overhead of autoregressive LLM scoring. It targets long-context cost and latency reduction and mitigation of the lost-in-the-middle effect.

entry.title: ARSM: Auto-Regressive State Machine for Agentic Reasoning Compression

author.name: Xiafeng Man, Siyuan Ye, Xiaosong Ma

entry.summary: ARSM is a lightweight, training-free framework for in-situ compression of agent reasoning context, framed as an auto-regressive state machine. It targets the memory bottleneck of long-horizon LLM agents, avoiding task-specific optimization and external auxiliary models used by prior compression methods while preserving structured relationships that prevent information dilution and attention collapse.

entry.title: The Text Beside the Image: Detection, Utility and Leakage for Trustworthy Multimodal Medical Data and Beyond

author.name: Andreas Maier, Monica Hinrichs-Mayer, Franziska Weber, Niklas Lackner, Matthias May, Bernhard Kainz, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: This study measures identifier detection, downstream utility, and residual identity leakage in medical report text released alongside images, testing pseudonymization policies across 15 detectors, three release conditions, and four corpora in four languages. A 13-detector union achieves very high sensitivity on medical reports with quantified trade-offs against specificity. It provides an unusually comprehensive empirical basis for privacy policy in multimodal medical data releases.

entry.title: MIC: Explaining Image-Claim Inconsistencies in AI-Generated Multimodal Misinformation
