author.name: Ruihong Zeng, Jonathan Tonglet, Preslav Nakov, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: MIC is a fact-checking framework that goes beyond detecting AI-generation artifacts by checking whether an AI-generated image's content is consistent with its accompanying claim and explaining inconsistencies using world knowledge. It combines supervised fine-tuning for task adaptation with Group Relative Preference Optimization-style refinement. This targets a fast-growing misinformation vector in a way aligned with human fact-checking practice.

entry.title: Jev Matches 7B Language Models for Speech-Neuroprosthesis Rescoring

author.name: Gabriele Cin\`a

entry.summary: Reframes rescoring in speech neuroprostheses (brain-to-text decoders) as a single typed decision, served by a hosted calibrated-decision model called Jev, removing the need for the GPU-scale 7B rescoring LM. On 978 held-out sentences from an ALS participant, Jev reduces word error from the decoder's 8.1% to 7.5%. This matters for making assistive speech technology cheaper and deployable.

entry.title: AgentHop: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Agentic Multi-Hop Scientific Question Answering

author.name: Chanhee Park, Jeongho Yoon, Sungbin Han, Hyeonseok Moon, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: AgentHop is a diagnostic benchmark of 1,011 multiple-choice scientific questions paired with a controlled seven-tool sandbox under fixed token, turn, and tool-call constraints. Unlike leaderboard-style benchmarks, it dissects a single accuracy score along four axes of agent operation to pinpoint specific failure modes.

entry.title: Fair Fact-Checking: Closing the Cross-Lingual Gap in LLM Factual Judgement with RoSh

author.name: Muhammad Ahmad, Fatemeh Seyedin, Adrian Weller, Dongwon Lee, Mahmoudreza Babaei

entry.summary: Evaluates eight LLMs on 1,500 factual claims in eight languages and finds English judged reliably better than all others, with the gap widest on small models. Proposes RoSh, a method that leverages the model's existing knowledge rather than retraining or unconstrained representation mapping to close the gap.

entry.title: Echoes of Deeds: Moral History Can Shape and Steer LLM Behavioral Choices

author.name: Lucio La Cava, Andrea Tagarelli

entry.summary: Introduces MoralLedger, a framework testing whether an actor's unrelated prior moral conduct influences LLM decisions about that actor, examining both behavioral responses and latent representations. It finds analogs of human moral-history effects in LLMs, suggesting contextual moral framing can steer model behavior.

entry.title: TRACE: Single-Pass Decoding-Trace Risk Localization for Generation Calibration

author.name: Yuebin Xu, Xuemei Peng, Junlan Chen, Zhiyi Chen, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE, a single-pass confidence estimator that records token-level surprisal and entropy during decoding and applies local risk operators to preserve localized uncertainty signals, rather than compressing everything into one global score. This targets answer-level calibration where errors concentrate in specific tokens like numbers or entities.

entry.title: IndustryLLM: Failure-Driven LLM Training for Industrial Procurement

author.name: Liang Ding (Project Lead), Zhiang Xu, Yuyang Sheng, Bin Chen, Songlin Bai, Run Zhu, Dingjun Wu, Hui Xu, Yandi Wang, Fulin Shi, Leilei Gan, Linlin Yu, Qihuang Zhong, Keqin Peng, Yalong Li, Chengfu Huo

entry.summary: IndustryLLM is an open-weight industrial language model built from a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B base, trained with a failure-driven recipe spanning continued pre-training on a ~100B-token curated corpus (national standards, de-identified industrial transaction records, technical archives) followed by supervised fine-tuning. It targets industrial procurement, where informal buyer jargon must be reconciled with engineering standards under safety tolerances. The open-weight release and domain recipe make it a useful reference for vertical LLM adaptation.

entry.title: Acoustic Progress Propagation for Long-Horizon Speculative Decoding in ASR

author.name: Yuanyuan Jia, Qianqian Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a progress-aware speculative drafter for autoregressive ASR that recurrently propagates an acoustic progress state across draft steps and feeds it back into audio cross-attention, trained over variable draft horizons. It achieves lossless speedups of 1.657x and 1.227x with Qwen3-ASR models and improves over AnchorDraft by up to 34.3%.

entry.title: Raven: The Harness of Harnesses for Composable Agentic Intelligence

author.name: EverMind AI

entry.summary: Introduces Raven, an open-source multi-agent ecosystem that automatically constructs and evolves modular harnesses for specific models and domains, and orchestrates them across domains for long-horizon cross-domain workflows. It targets the problem that harness complexity outgrows manual design and single-harness designs are domain-locked.

entry.title: ControlScope: Workflow Revision and Reliability in LLM Agents

author.name: Jingjie Ning, Xueqi Li, Yibo Kong, Dongting Li

entry.summary: ControlScope studies how much of a running agent workflow should be revised on failure, comparing continuing generated code, editing the next tool call, and full workflow replacement from the same execution state. Evaluations across filesystem tasks, ALFWorld, and AppWorld show tradeoffs between repair scopes under one-time and repeated reviews.

entry.title: RA-CFGCache: From Branch-Level Criteria to Guided-Risk Control under Classifier-Free Guidance

author.name: Yiming Liu, Ben Wan, Tongxuan Liu, Ao Wang, Yuqi Xiong, Fan Zhang, Hui Chen, Guiguang Ding

entry.summary: RA-CFGCache improves training-free caching for diffusion models under classifier-free guidance by addressing two identified misalignments: branch-guided mismatch, where guided error depends on magnitude and alignment of conditional/unconditional branch errors, and local-final mismatch, where downstream impact of local cache errors varies by timestep. The method reformulates branch-level reuse criteria as guided-risk control for more accurate cache decisions. This reduces the cost of CFG-based diffusion inference with better quality preservation.

entry.title: Representation Dynamics Reveal Semantic Saliency and Similarity for Visual Token Pruning in MLLMs

author.name: Weixuan Li, Zikun Zhou, Xinyi Zhuang, Xinyan Guo, Rui Tian, Chuyao Zhang, Lin Gao

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how visual token representations evolve across encoder depth in multimodal LLMs and derives pruning criteria from those dynamics. It finds token update magnitudes correlate with foreground saliency only in two depth intervals separated by sink-dominated layers, and characterizes semantic similarity patterns. The result enables more efficient MLLM inference by pruning redundant visual tokens with better-grounded importance estimates.

entry.title: OmniRoute: Mapping Temporal Semantic Evidence to Audio-Visual Token Budgets for Efficient Omnimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yuchen Deng, Zidang Cai, Feidiao Yang, Yufei Wang, Jie Wang, Hai-Tao Zheng, Yuxing Han

entry.summary: OmniRoute is a training-free two-stage compression framework for omnimodal LLMs that allocates per-chunk audio-visual token budgets based on temporal semantic relevance, then performs budget-constrained semantic compression. It targets the high prefill costs of long interleaved audio-visual token sequences.

entry.title: AESOP: Asymmetric Human-Camera Generation with Translation-Intensity Control

author.name: Jingzhong Lin, Zhanke Wang, Heng Li, Wenxiang Liu, Zhao Zhang, Kecheng Tang, Dongdong Xiang, Changbo Wang, Di Kang, Chunchao Guo, Linchao Bao, Gaoqi He

entry.summary: AESOP is a unified framework for joint human-motion and camera-trajectory generation built on an asymmetric design: an independent human pathway plus a shared human-conditioned camera generator. It also tackles underspecified translation intensity by constructing trajectory representations with explicit intensity control.

entry.title: Decompose Radicals, Then Reward: Fine-Grained Inspection for Accurate Chinese Text Rendering

author.name: Yazhen Xie, Xingsong Ye, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: This work improves Chinese text rendering in text-to-image models by replacing coarse OCR-based RL rewards with fine-grained rewards based on Ideographic Description Sequences, decomposing characters into radical components and spatial operators judged by an expert IDS recognizer. This gives structurally informative feedback rather than treating characters as atomic units.

entry.title: Tracing the Evidence: Faithful Token Attribution Through Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Bowen Yuan, Danny Wang, Ruihong Qiu, Zijian Wang, Zi Huang

entry.summary: This paper develops faithful token attribution for large vision-language models, assigning scores that rank image and prompt tokens by how much the model relies on them, validated by likelihood-drop under token removal. It addresses two challenges: joint image-text attribution underrepresenting visual evidence, and handling of complex multimodal source interactions.

entry.title: Minkowski Attractor Networks: Closed-Form Hyperbolic Flows for Visual Representations

author.name: Zhongping Ji

entry.summary: This work introduces Minkowski Attractor Networks, an operator-splitting framework that embeds visual representations in hyperbolic space using closed-form flows, avoiding the Riemannian optimization, gyrovector calculus, and numerical instabilities of prior hyperbolic networks. The goal is better embedding of multi-scale, tree-like visual hierarchies that Euclidean spaces represent poorly.

entry.title: Fisher-IRG: Fisher-Induced Local Invariant Representation Geometry across Language and Vision Models

author.name: Abdullah All Tanvir, Xin Zhong

entry.summary: Fisher-IRG defines a local metric on learned representations based on predictive sensitivity, constructing semantic-preserving and semantic-changing neighborhoods, aggregating local Fisher information, and recovering invariant directions via a contrastive generalized eigenvalue problem. It shows comparable Euclidean displacement can carry very different predictive significance across language and vision models. This offers a principled geometry for analyzing what representations actually encode.

entry.title: Track-and-Complete: Learning Humanoid Skills from a Single Failed Human Video

author.name: Sarmad Idrees, Jongeun Choi

entry.summary: TRACC leverages failed human demonstration videos for humanoid skill learning, imitating the usable motion prefix before the failure and then using an inferred task-outcome reward to complete the task. This avoids the customary requirement of a successful demonstration and reduces data collection cost. The approach treats failures as containing useful trajectory priors rather than purely negative examples.

entry.title: SAKI: Skill Assembly and Kinematic Imitation from Human Videos for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Yijie Lu, James Zhao, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: SAKI is a framework that acquires manipulation skills from human videos and composes them for long-horizon mobile manipulation, connecting skill acquisition, cross-demonstration assembly, and closed-loop whole-body execution. It maintains reusable object-centric skills that preserve task-critical interactions while adapting transfer paths across changing scenes and robot configurations.

entry.title: HACo: Learning Haptic Active Compliance for Force-Aware Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Naisheng Ye, Yinzhe Zhou, Junkai Zhao, Yuhang Lu, Checheng Yu, Zhenjie Yang, Pengwei Wang, Hongyang Li

entry.summary: HACo learns dexterous manipulation policies that regulate contact forces from haptic feedback, using compliance-regulated teleoperation to generate action supervision that preserves operator intent while bounding interaction loads. It incorporates fingertip tactile and joint-torque signals that most existing manipulation policies ignore. This addresses a key limitation of vision-only or position-controlled dexterity for contact-rich tasks.

entry.title: CoRe-VLA: Preserving Cross-View Coordination in VLAs under Camera Shifts

author.name: Tianhang Pan, Xuanhao Wang, Yiwen Pang, Bo Zhou, Jun Yang, Min-Ling Zhang, Shimin Di

entry.summary: This paper identifies cross-view coordination breakdown as a key reason vision-language-action policies fail when external cameras shift, without requiring paired multi-view fine-tuning data. CoRe-VLA preserves coordination across viewpoints, improving robustness of VLAs to camera placement changes at lower cost than prior adaptation approaches.

entry.title: RoboHarn-Evo: Evolving Hierarchical Physical Knowledge for Self-Improving Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Shifeng Bao, Fanding Huang, Yihan Lin, Youhe Feng, Guanlin Li, Chen Zhao, Yang Li, Jiawei He, Cheng Chi, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: RoboHarn-Evo is a dual-loop framework that evolves Hierarchical Physical Knowledge from repeated interaction without updating the base VLM, coupling Task Knowledge (which subtask and when complete) with Action Knowledge (object-relative geometric strategies and their effects). The agent retrieves knowledge at the corresponding decision level and grounds it in the current scene during execution.

entry.title: Action Chunking Proximal Policy Optimization with Feedback Correction

author.name: Sanghyun Hahn, Jonghyun Choi

entry.summary: ACPPO extends PPO with a chunked actor while retaining a standard state-value critic, avoiding hard-to-learn chunked Q-functions, and ACPPO-Corr adds a stepwise feedback corrector that adjusts planned chunks during execution. This restores within-chunk reactivity for contact-rich tasks while keeping the temporal abstraction benefits of action chunking. It directly addresses two known failure modes of chunk-based RL in high-dimensional robotic control.

entry.title: A Finslerian Approach for Embedding Directed Data

author.name: Gwendal Debaussart-Joniec (CB, ENS Paris Saclay), Th\'eau Blanchard (HeKA | U1346, GE Healthcare), Argyris Kalogeratos (CB, ENS Paris Saclay)

entry.summary: This paper models directed data (citations, cell lineages, traffic flows) as samples from a Finsler manifold whose distance depends on direction of travel, preserving asymmetry that spectral embedding methods destroy by symmetrization. Via moment expansion of the kernel operator, the symmetric and antisymmetric parts separate geometry from direction, with convergence guarantees as bandwidth vanishes. This offers a principled geometric home for directionality-aware embeddings.

entry.title: Optimal detection of general moment changes: Simultaneous mean and covariance change detection and beyond

author.name: Xiaokai Luo, Chenghao Xu, Haotian Xu, Carlos Misael Madrid Padilla, Daren Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a tensor-based framework for multiple change-point detection in multivariate time series that unifies changes in moments of all orders up to a fixed p, covering mean, covariance, and higher-order moments. The procedure handles temporal dependence and high dimensions, with optimality guarantees.

entry.title: Physical Muon: Orthogonalization as an Equilibrium Computation

author.name: Yuren Hao

entry.summary: Adapts the Muon optimizer for physical and analog in-memory computing by computing its Newton-Schulz orthogonalization as the equilibrium of a continuous-time flow, approximated with random probes using only matrix-vector products, reciprocal reads, and local rank-1 writes. Experiments test whether this physically implementable replacement preserves Muon's training performance.

entry.title: Mutual Information Constrained Chernoff Bottleneck

author.name: Dier Tang, Guangyue Han

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Chernoff information variant of the information bottleneck: maximizing the error exponent of downstream binary decisions subject to a rate constraint I(U;X) <= R, rather than maximizing I(U;Y). The authors characterize the optimal value C(R), showing it increases strictly up to a merging point and then stays at the uncompressed exponent. This refines information bottleneck theory to directly target decision error.

entry.title: Support-Set Target Leakage in Relational Foundation Models during In-Context Learning: Impact, Detection, and Mitigation

author.name: Roshan Reddy Upendra, Alexandre Dorais, Joe Meyer, Andrew Pouret, Anastasios Lambrianos Stappas, Dinesh Katupputhur Ramprasath, Tom Palczewski, Minghua Li

entry.summary: This paper formalizes support-set target leakage in relational in-context learning, where labeled support examples contain target-derived features unavailable for the query. The authors construct 14 synthetic leaker types across varied noise levels, modalities, and relational distances, and evaluate a frozen relational foundation model to characterize impact, detection, and mitigation. It identifies a distinct and previously underexamined leakage failure mode for a new model class.

entry.title: ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents

author.name: Haohao Qu, Yongcheng Jing, Chun Hin Chan, Shanru Lin, Wenqi Fan, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Proposes ReMem, a recommendation agent framework combining OCR-based multimodal perception of item pages via screenshots with time-evolving dynamic memory to handle noisy item pages and long-horizon user histories. Targets the shift toward active, user-side generative recommendation agents.

entry.title: ReLMem: Learning Recurrent Memory for Longitudinal EHR Modeling

author.name: Zijie Meng, Xiwei Dai, Yingying Zhang, Jian Wu, Xian Wu, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: ReLMem learns visit-wise recurrent compression of expanding patient histories into a compact memory for LLM-based electronic health record modeling, managing the tradeoff between integrating new visits and preserving critical historical evidence under a fixed budget. This reduces the growing computational and memory costs of processing full longitudinal records. It targets practical clinical prediction over long patient timelines.

entry.title: Graph Memory: Spectral Associative Memory via Dirichlet Energy

author.name: Zhaoyang Shi

entry.summary: Extends dense associative memories to graph data with a spectral dense associative memory that stores and retrieves Laplacians via a log-sum-exp energy induced by Dirichlet energy. The paper proves exponential storage capacity and exponentially decaying retrieval error, with retrieval outputs remaining valid graph Laplacians.

entry.title: Not Every Term Adds New Structure: Sobolev Novelty for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Boxiao Wang, Kai Li, Yuheng Jing, Tianyi Liu, Chen Li, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sobolev Novelty, a term-level measure of structural independence in symbolic regression that builds empirical Sobolev signatures (function values plus exact derivatives) to determine whether an individual term contributes new structure or is redundant. This moves beyond expression-level objectives like fitting error to guide combinatorial search at a finer granularity. It targets the core scalability challenge of symbolic regression.

entry.title: The Extender: A Log-Structured Transformer

author.name: Jakob Eriksson (UIC)

entry.summary: The Extender is a new Transformer variant that adds a concatenation channel alongside the residual stream: each layer emits a small extension appended to a growing vector x, and attention key-value projections take only x as input. This restructures information flow so the persistent attention memory is reduced, with implications for memory-efficient architectures. It is a novel architecture-level proposal from a single author.

entry.title: When Less Compute Is More: Adaptive Early Exit Improves Pretrained Outlier Detection

author.name: Tianyang Zhou, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: This is the first study of depth-adaptive early exit for pretrained tabular foundation models in outlier detection, finding that exiting at the optimal intermediate layer improves detection by 4.7-7.3% on average across three foundation models. The authors identify context pollution - outliers among in-context samples - as the key mechanism driving the gains.

entry.title: Balancing Early Performance Sacrifices with Long-Term Gains: Scaling Learning-Rate Warmup Duration Across Training Horizons

author.name: Kristi Topollai, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: Using a quadratic model with modes of differing sensitivity to peak learning rate, the paper derives a compact scaling law for learning-rate warmup duration as a function of training horizon, explaining when fixed versus growing warmup is appropriate. Higher peak rates shift the balance toward longer warmup by protecting directions near the stability edge.

entry.title: Apparent Compression, Real Stability: The Intrinsic Dimension of Learning a Quantum Wavefunction

author.name: Lu Wei, Yufeng Wang, Chenfeng Cao, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: The authors measure the intrinsic dimension of training for variational Monte Carlo — learning a neural network representation of a quantum many-body ground state — by training only a small latent vector mapped through a frozen random map to network weights. The setting is demanding (self-generated noisy samples) yet uniquely well-posed since exact answers permit scoring every run.

entry.title: Domain Generalization under Sampling Pattern Shifts in Irregular Time Series

author.name: Changhun Kim, Joohyung Lee, Kwanhyung Lee, Donghwee Yoon, Grigorios Chrysos, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces HAR-C, the first controlled benchmark for sampling-pattern shifts in irregularly sampled multivariate time series, showing that such shifts alone degrade performance and induce sampling-specific shortcuts. It proposes PRISM, a domain generalization framework that learns complementary feature-centric representations robust to sampling changes.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Rollouts as a Stabilization Mechanism for Long-Horizon Environmental Forecasting

author.name: Marina Vicens-Miquel, Amy McGovern, Aaron J. Hill, Efi Foufoula-Georgiou, Samuel S. P. Shen

entry.summary: Investigates diffusion-based rollouts for recursive forecasting on low-dimensional water-level series and high-dimensional precipitation fields, finding that diffusion suppresses recursive error growth most where deterministic rollouts are least stable. Crucially, it also shows stabilization does not guarantee fidelity: forecasts can lose event-level detail as rollouts lose access to external predictive information.

entry.title: SleuthBench: Benchmarking Statistical LLM Evaluation Using Tabular Hidden Signals

author.name: Jingyun Jia, Antoine Remond-Tiedrez, Aaron Alvarez, Joshua Shunk, Rich Caruana, Ben Lengerich

entry.summary: SleuthBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM statistical-discovery agents by injecting controlled data-quality problems and feature effects into public tabular datasets, so ground-truth answers are computed automatically and memorization of original tables is insufficient. It defines 17 question templates across two families, modeled on phenomena from real data analyses.

entry.title: Learning What to Recall: Adaptive Multi-Cue Episodic Memory for World Models

author.name: Beomsu Kim, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Bac Nguyen, Amir Bar, Jong Chul Ye, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: The paper proposes Future-Aware Recall (FAR), a framework that learns episodic recall for world models using future-aware predictive supervision and adaptive multi-cue scoring, addressing which past memories are useful for current prediction and which retrieval cues to trust. This replaces unreliable fixed criteria based on recency, pose overlap, or visual similarity.

entry.title: Reference-Tail Trust:Certified Probability Floors for Learned Updates Inside a Deployed Network

author.name: Abdolvahab Khalili Sadaghiani, Jose Nunez-Yanez

entry.summary: RTT is a framework that admits learned graph-based updates inside a frozen deployed GNN while certifying per-node probability floors on served predictions, charging each update for its worst-case cross-entropy increase through remaining layers and enforcing a call-level divergence budget. This brings formal safety guarantees to incremental GNN updates. Notable for safe deployment of evolving models.

entry.title: QAM: Quadratic-Accurate Checkpoint Merging via Sequential Consistency

author.name: Shihao Wang, Rui Kong, Xinran Chen, Hui Wu, Qipeng Qian, Jinman Zhao, Jiashu Zhao, Yuchen Li, Jimmy Huang, Dawei Yin

entry.summary: This paper studies how saved training checkpoints can reconstruct the endpoint of a reference training trajectory, deriving moment conditions that characterize convex merges accurate to second order. It also proves an information-theoretic lower bound showing no fixed-length gradient history can achieve better than cubic endpoint error for strongly convex losses.

entry.title: From Experience to Expertise: Adoption-Aware Memory Learning for Data-Scarce NPU Kernel Synthesis

author.name: Longxiao Fan, Tao Zhang, Han Yan, Jiajun Li, Mingcong Song, Guoping Long, Hongjie Si, Weiwei Sun

entry.summary: The paper improves LLM coding-agent memory learning for NPU kernel synthesis by fixing uniform credit assignment so adopted experiences receive rewards while unused ones do not, addressing bias in retrieval rankings for data-scarce domain-specific architectures. This targets the transfer gap between CUDA-centric LLM knowledge and NPU execution models without costly post-training.

entry.title: Fewer Tokens, More Self-Teaching: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Extreme Visual Token Reduction

author.name: Junxian Li, Ruixuan Yang, Tianao Zhang, Tiange Xu, Weisheng Dong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: LT-OPD accelerates multimodal LLMs via extreme visual token reduction using on-policy self-distillation, where a heavily compressed student is supervised on states induced by its own generations with its full-token counterpart as teacher. This targets the rapid performance degradation that plagues token-pruned MLLMs at very low budgets.

entry.title: When Privacy Moves ML-Mediated Decisions On Device: Information and Incentive Misalignment in Auctions

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: The paper studies what happens when ML-mediated auction budget pacing moves onto privacy-preserving on-device clients: shared budget constraints then rely on stale, non-globally-current information, causing systematic overspending that conventional pacing cannot handle. In an auction-faithful simulation with 36 campaigns and 50 devices, proportional pacing overspends by 17.77 percent after one tick of staleness and by orders of magnitude more under higher budget pressure. The work surfaces an information-structure failure created by privacy-driven decentralization of ad decisioning.

entry.title: OSCC: Certified Observation-Safe Coupling Optimization for Gradient-Noise Control in Imperfect-Information Learning

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Rui Chen, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: The paper introduces observation-safe counterfactual coupling (OSCC), a framework defining admissible couplings in imperfect-information environments that avoid exposing hidden state or misaligning chance events, while optimizing return-covariance objectives through policy-gradient geometry. It turns common-random-number constructions into a certified general learning primitive for multi-action policy optimization.

entry.title: ThinkNet: Compact Architecture Selection and Validation-Gated Ensembles for Subject-Independent MI-EEG Decoding

author.name: Abdul Basit, Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: ThinkNet is a validation-controlled framework for subject-independent motor-imagery EEG decoding that combines train-only normalization, validation-guided evolutionary architecture search, and validation-gated ensemble inference to avoid overstating held-out-subject performance. Evaluated on BCI Competition IV-2a with nine LOSO folds, multiple seeds, and seven fine-tuning variants, it targets compact decoders for compute-constrained assistive BCIs. The work emphasizes methodological hygiene in a field prone to leakage.

entry.title: Language Discrimination Improves Linguistic Learning in Multilingual Speech Models

author.name: Maureen de Seyssel, Jie Chi, Zakaria Aldeneh

entry.summary: In a controlled English/French HuBERT setting, the authors show that strengthening language discrimination during pretraining, via an auxiliary language classifier or per-language k-means targets, reduces or closes the multilingual-versus-monolingual gap on phonetic and higher-level measures while preserving cross-language sharing. This offers a simple lever for better multilingual speech pretraining under fixed data budgets. The finding nuances the view that multilinguality inherently trades off against per-language quality.

entry.title: CUE-Mem: Benchmarking Long-Term User Memory via Implicit Cues in Multimodal Conversations

author.name: Yulin Hu, Yanyan Zhao, Zimo Long, Xing Fu, Mengtong Ji, Weixiang Zhao, Yutai Hou, Qianchao Wang, Dandan Tu

entry.summary: CUE-Mem is a text-image-audio benchmark with 2,674 questions evaluating long-term user memory from implicit multimodal cues, such as recurring background objects or ambient sounds, across four tasks including Entity Recall, Long Pattern, Personalized Recommendation, and Answer Refusal. Existing benchmarks mostly cover text-only or explicit evidence, leaving implicit cues underexplored. It fills a genuine evaluation gap for multimodal personal agents.

entry.title: From Script to Drama: An Agentic Framework for Controllable Multi-Speaker Dialogue TTS

author.name: Kangxiang Xia, Xinfa Zhu, HangRui Hu, Kexin Huang, Wenjie Tian, Ziyue Jiang, Bingshen Mu, Jingbin Hu, Ting He, Lei Xie, Jin Xu

entry.summary: Proposes a controllable multi-speaker dialogue TTS framework built around critique-driven iterative refinement, with a ControlEdit-TTS backbone unifying instruction-following synthesis and natural-language attribute editing so expressive errors can be fixed without full regeneration. Hierarchical utterance- and scene-level critique plus routing handles long-form dialogue coherence and speaker consistency.

entry.title: VesselBench-800K: A Large-scale Perception Benchmark for Multimodal Vessel Detection, Counting, and Density Estimation

author.name: Danfeng Hong, Chenyu Li, Jocelyn Chanussot

entry.summary: VesselBench-800K is the largest-to-date global benchmark for vessel perception in multimodal remote sensing images, covering detection, counting, and density estimation across challenging maritime conditions like clouds, rain, and day-night variation that defeat single-modality optical imaging. Large multimodal benchmarks of this kind enable and standardize progress in maritime monitoring applications. Authorship includes Jocelyn Chanussot, a prominent remote-sensing researcher.

entry.title: TaRL: Learning General and Physical Rewards from Tactile Demonstrations

author.name: Po-Yi Wu, Dao-Jan Chang, Shang-Ya Hsiao, Hong-Ming Chen, Yu-Cheng Su, Tsung-Wei Ke

entry.summary: TaRL learns reward functions from tactile demonstrations, regressing task-completion progress from sequences of tactile deformation maps including both successful and failed attempts. This extends visual reward learning to capture rewards beyond visual goals, which is critical for contact-rich manipulation where force and grasp stability matter. It addresses the sparse-versus-dense reward dilemma in RL for manipulation.

entry.title: Remember What You Did: Action-History Memory with Dual-Expert Denoising for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Yaxin Zhao, Dianye Huang, Chenwei Wang, Chenguang Yang, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: This work adds explicit action-history memory to VLA policies to combat perceptual aliasing, where similar observations at different task stages cause action ambiguity. It separates a trainable history-conditioned steering module from a frozen base VLA via dual-expert denoising, avoiding costly joint fine-tuning.

entry.title: Cascaded consensus splitting for multi-branch contingency games

author.name: Bastien Lechardoy, Pau de las Heras Molins, Thibault Lahire, Laurent Pautet, David Filliat, David Fridovich-Keil, Georgios Bakirtzis

entry.summary: The paper extends contingency games for multi-agent trajectory planning to multi-branch architectures where different agents' intent uncertainties resolve at different branching times. A cascaded consensus splitting scheme addresses the computational blowup of solving all scenario-dependent best responses jointly, allowing trajectories to adapt as intentions are progressively revealed.

entry.title: Iterative Exact Discrete Guidance for Energy-Based Sampling

author.name: Yuwen Qian, Yidong Ouyang, Zhengyan Wan, Hongyuan Zha

entry.summary: Introduces IEDG, a trajectory-wise guidance framework for sampling from unnormalized discrete targets via a global Boltzmann tilt along an annealing trajectory. Each stage learns a stage-local posterior correction, and at the population optimum exact stage posteriors recover the correct reverse dynamics, avoiding one-step approximation bias.

entry.title: GeoOutageBench: Benchmarking Ambiguity-aware, Ontology-grounded Geospatiotemporal KGQA for Multimodal Power Outage and Resilience Analysis

author.name: Ethan D. Frakes, Amy Kvien, Rishabh Kundu, Redad Mehdi, Van D. Tran, Vibha S. Mandayam, Kristopher O. Davis, Erika I. Barcelos, Roger H. French, Yinghui Wu, Mengjie Li

entry.summary: GeoOutageBench is a benchmark for LLM-based question answering over spatiotemporal knowledge graphs integrating visual, textual, and structured data from power outage records, remote sensing, weather, and domain ontologies. It offers a difficulty-stratified query taxonomy and configurable evaluation dimensions for outage and resilience analysis.

entry.title: AdaST: Adaptive Coupling for Spatial-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Zhenyu Lei, Chenghao Liu, Yushun Dong, Qi R. Wang, Jundong Li

entry.summary: AdaST addresses spatial-temporal forecasting by dynamically modulating spatial and temporal modeling according to the data's inherent coupling structure, which varies from temporal-dominated to strongly coupled regimes. The method targets three challenges: unknown coupling structure, heterogeneous coupling dynamics, and suboptimal spatial modeling.

entry.title: FigAct: Turning Scientific Figures into Active Canvases for Explanation

author.name: Shishi Xiao, Zichao Wang, Alexa Siu, David H. Laidlaw, Jennifer Healey

entry.summary: FigAct transforms static scientific figures into question-conditioned visual presentations, where a multimodal LLM generates short narrations grounded in the figure's existing graphical elements and applies visual actions to guide the viewer's attention. It introduces a hierarchical search strategy for efficient element localization. This matters because it shifts figure explanation from pure text translation to action-based, attention-directed visual communication.

entry.title: HyperZip: Efficient Data Compression through Personalized Diffusion LLMs with Hypernetworks

author.name: Thai Nguyen, Khang Tran, NhatHai Phan

entry.summary: HyperZip uses diffusion-based LLMs with multi-token prediction to accelerate lossless LLM-based data compression, mitigating a trade-off where higher decoding throughput degrades compression rate. A hypernetwork generates data-specific model updates from context representations, adapting the dLLM without costly fine-tuning. This is a novel application of the emerging diffusion-LLM paradigm to a classical problem with practical efficiency implications.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Reasoning: Agentic Mechanism Prediction from Cell Painting Profiles

author.name: Jiayuan Chen, Botao Yu, Tianyu Liu, Thai-Hoang Pham, Meng Wu, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: This work reformulates mechanism-of-action prediction from Cell Painting morphological profiles as calibrated evidence reasoning, treating retrieved neighboring perturbations as uncertain observations to be evaluated rather than direct answers. An agentic framework weighs noisy, batch-effect-corrupted, and convergent phenotypic evidence before predicting. This improves robustness in a widely used phenotype-based drug discovery workflow.

entry.title: DualTrack: Synchronized speech-gesture generation via symmetric coupling of pretrained priors

author.name: Yuanzhuo Hu, Zehan Liu, Xiaoyi Qin, Ming Li

entry.summary: DualTrack jointly synthesizes speech and gesture by coupling pretrained speech and motion priors on a shared 12.5 Hz timeline, using causal adapters and current-state fusion before separate sixteen-codebook packet generation. Evaluation covers 43 BEAT2 recordings in four languages with held-out speakers, showing lower word error rate and full-motion Fréchet Gesture Distance versus baselines on shared English/Spanish inputs.

entry.title: Aperture: Merge-Consistent Rotary States for Compressed Tokens

author.name: Yuhao Du, Shunian Chen

entry.summary: Aperture addresses how positional information should survive token merging under rotary position embeddings by storing Fourier moments of a token's weighted support at the model's rotary frequencies. It proves these moments are minimally sufficient in dimension for expected rotary interactions and characterizes when merged-token centers determine interval widths.

entry.title: Automated Screw Planning for Reduced Pelvic Fractures Based on Statistical Shape Models and Deep Learning

author.name: Yang Gao, Sutuke Yibulayimu, Yanzhen Liu, Zian Zhao, Yudi Sang

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully automated pipeline for preoperative iliosacral screw planning in pelvic fracture patients, using statistical shape models and deep learning to replace labor-intensive manual trajectory measurement. Accurate corridor planning directly affects surgical safety in this minimally invasive procedure.

entry.title: From Learner Behavior to Reusable Skills for Effective and Efficient Learner Simulation

author.name: Zijian Chen, Zheng Zhang, Miao Jia, Xingchen Hu, Weibo Gao, Linan Yue

entry.summary: Proposes Learner2Skill, which externalizes LLM-acquired learner simulation capability into a persistent, reusable Simulation Skill that captures a learner's state and response patterns without repeatedly reprocessing growing interaction histories. This reduces context and inference costs and makes simulation capability transferable across different LLMs, relevant for education and user modeling.

entry.title: AssayRouter: Historical Utility Priors for Frozen Molecular Predictor Routing

author.name: Dong Xu, Zhangfan Yang, Jiantao Wu, Shipeng Zhang, Zexuan Zhu, Jiangqiang Li, Jun Zhang, Junkai Ji

entry.summary: Addresses the practical lab problem of selecting which frozen molecular predictors to include for a new assay with few labels, treating completed assays as pseudo-targets and scoring candidates by their post-fit utility (held-out discovery loss reduction). A shared regressor predicts this utility without source identity, enabling one frozen ranking per new assay.

entry.title: Teaching LLMs to Generate Challenging MILP Instances via Solver Feedback

author.name: Jitin Singla, Parikshit Pareek, Pratik Jawanpuria, Parag Singla

entry.summary: Trains LLMs via RL to generate feasible yet computationally challenging mixed-integer linear programming instances, using a reward derived from solver stage costs (branch-and-bound effort) to score both solvability and hardness. This improves on prior LLM generators lacking hardness measures and non-LLM generators with high test-time cost.

entry.title: Governing the Edge: Automating Commercial Property and Casualty Insurance Underwriting via a Hybrid Local-Cloud Multi-Agent Framework

author.name: Vivek Kumar Singh, Gautam Bhowmick

entry.summary: The authors present a 13-node LangGraph multi-agent system for commercial P&C insurance underwriting, designed around a data-residency constraint: agents handling sensitive submissions run locally on Gemma 2, while only anonymized scores reach a cloud Claude Sonnet tier. The system targets the 30-40% of underwriter time lost to administrative work, with a human-escalation interrupt node and tool-invocation logging.

entry.title: Generative Interactions: Weaving Multiparty Human Motion with Bilevel Latent Dynamics

author.name: Ojas Shirekar, Yash Surange, Agustinas Ju\v{c}as, Chirag Raman

entry.summary: BRAID is a hierarchical sequential latent-variable model for generative multi-person social motion, formulating interaction generation as meta-transfer learning where shared interaction priors are learned across datasets and adapted to arbitrary contexts. It makes group-level and individual-level dynamics explicit, improving transfer across groups, tasks, and partial observation.

entry.title: Can a Cacheable Decision Model Follow Rules?

author.name: Dushyant Rajput (AltSlate Labs LLP), Nirdesh Chauhan (AltSlate Labs LLP), Siddharth Kosaraju (AltSlate Labs LLP)

entry.summary: Studies Certo, a small non-generative decision model built on Qwen3-4B that scores candidate actions and returns probabilities. The paper shows that converting a joint scorer into an independently encodable, cacheable form loses most rule sensitivity (recall@1 drops from 1.00 to 0.24), and shortlist-plus-rerank rescues fail, quantifying the tradeoff between caching efficiency and rule-following.

entry.title: You Cannot Pick a Provider From the Price List: Market-Aware Routing for Open-Weight LLM Inference

author.name: Liang He, Jingbo Wen, Yixiong Chen, Yue Yang, Qizhen Lan, Kangning Cui, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: Shows that for open-weight LLMs, choosing a provider is a second decision axis beyond choosing a model: the same model varies sharply in quality, latency, availability, and price across providers. The paper measures live endpoints across multiple models, providers, tasks, and three waves, and builds a market-aware router, finding that higher price predicts speed but not quality.

entry.title: Position: Let's Strengthen Verifiability If We Can't Enforce Reproducibility

author.name: Samet Hicsonmez, Nermin Samet, Renaud Marlet

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that because empirical results in machine learning are increasingly hard to reproduce and code is often unavailable, the community should prioritize verifiability of claimed results instead. The authors quantify the reproducibility problem and make concrete proposals for improving result checkability.

entry.title: Evaluating Name-Only Directory Routing for One-Shot Code Search

author.name: Manoj Bajaj

entry.summary: This evaluation tests whether an LLM can locate annotated code files using only directory and file names, as an alternative to lexical search for coding agents. Across 82 audited issues in 11 repositories, name-only routing recovered 0.465 of gold files within eight candidates versus 0.352 for FTS5, and combining both reached 0.491. The results show structured navigation cues can outperform fixed lexical queries under tight context budgets.

entry.title: Understanding Decision-Making Mechanisms in Neural Routing Solvers

author.name: Fatemeh Askari, Mazdak Teymourian, Mohammad Izadi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

entry.summary: This paper probes the internal decision mechanisms of three neural combinatorial optimization models for routing (AM, POMO, LEHD) using behavioral analysis, representation probing, and causal interventions. It finds AM and POMO follow a persistent geometric pattern during solution construction while LEHD maintains linearly accessible information about multiple future actions. These insights clarify how different encoder-decoder configurations shape model behavior.

entry.title: Encoder-Sharing Hierarchical Federated Multi-Task Learning for VANETs

author.name: M. Saeid HaghighiFard, Sinem Coleri

entry.summary: The paper proposes EN-HMTFL, a federated learning framework for vehicular ad hoc networks in which vehicles perform heterogeneous but related perception tasks. A globally shared encoder is exchanged and aggregated hierarchically while task-specific decoders remain local, enabling transferable representations without a single common task assumption.

entry.title: How Much Prompt Is Enough? A Blackbox Minimization of Few-Shots in LLMs

author.name: Ali Alfageeh, Rahul Gopinath, Amin Alipour

entry.summary: The paper presents a blackbox framework for reducing few-shot prompts to their necessary minimal subset, probing which prompt components are causally necessary versus redundant. A case study on a few-shot learning system demonstrates practical insights, motivated by reliability concerns where subtle prompt variations silently shift outputs in critical software systems.

entry.title: DraftTrace: A Multi-View Analytics Environment for AI-Integrated Writing

author.name: Divyansh Chandarana, Sandipan De, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: DraftTrace is a writing environment that captures the final document, the writing process over time, and student interactions with an integrated AI assistant, organizing these into submission, longitudinal, and class-level analytics for instructors. Deployed with 81 students in a graduate NLP course, it distinguishes human-AI-assisted sessions from LLM-generated and copy-typed responses. It addresses the problem that final artifacts alone no longer reveal how student writing was produced.

entry.title: Frontier Autolab: Organizational Memory, Adversarial Dissent and Temporal Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Firms Across Fifty Years of Technological Change

author.name: Bravish Ghosh

entry.summary: Frontier Autolab is a long-horizon testbed where a simulated sixteen-role LLM firm with a dedicated Red Team re-founds itself across nine technology eras from 1990 to 2040, with a historian-judge scoring decisions against history and a persistent organizational Playbook. It probes how multi-agent organizations behave when the technological ground shifts beneath them over decades. This is a creative exploration of organizational memory and adversarial dissent in agent systems, though more a simulation artifact than a validated benchmark.

entry.title: Embedded Bi-Temporal Building Damage Assessment for On-Board Data Reduction

author.name: Thomas Goudemant, Benjamin Francesconi, Marjorie Bellizzi, Adrien Dorise

entry.summary: This paper presents a bi-temporal building damage assessment pipeline using a siamese YOLOX-derived detector designed for satellite on-board processing. Pre-disaster reference images are compressed up to 64x into a latent space and uplinked, so the downlink carries only actionable damage-relevant information after comparing with fresh post-disaster imagery. This mitigates uplink/downlink capacity and ground-latency constraints in disaster response.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Narrowing: Robust and Efficient LLM Watermarking with Hamming Neighborhoods

author.name: Zewen Sun, Tongyang Zhao, Liyao Xiang, Mingxuan Ma, Lingzhe Wang, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies semantic narrowing as a failure mode of sentence-level LLM watermarking, where watermark-specific semantic preferences conflict with the model's natural generation preferences. HammingMark uses semantic hashes of preceding sentences with Hamming neighborhoods to relax watermark constraints, improving robustness against removal attacks while preserving semantic freedom. This matters for deployable, low-distortion LLM provenance.

entry.title: TAEC: Trajectory-Aware Evidence Coordination for Multi-Step Visual RAG

author.name: Yalun Wu, Bingzhou Wang, Boyang Wang, Peiying Wang, Shaojie He, Yunhan Wang, Shaozu Yuan, Jiawei Wang

entry.summary: TAEC addresses trajectory-level evidence utilization degradation in multi-step visual RAG, where redundant and stale observations crowd out context needed for new evidence and fine-grained reading. The framework coordinates evidence across the reasoning trajectory, managing what is retained, refreshed, or discarded as the intermediate state evolves. This improves multi-step visual question answering efficiency and accuracy.

entry.title: Complexity-Aware Evaluation of LLM Comprehension

author.name: Ali Mohammadi Esfahani, Nafiseh Kahani, Samuel A. Ajila

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework for evaluating LLM code comprehension conditioned on structural complexity metrics like cyclomatic complexity, nesting depth, and Halstead volume. Testing DeepSeek-Coder-V2 and Llama on input-output prediction and semantic comprehension tasks over Python functions, it shows aggregate benchmark accuracy hides reliability degradation on complex code. This matters for realistic assessment of coding assistants.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Semantic Grounding for Trustworthy LLM-Based Robot Planning

author.name: {\L}ukasz Sobczak, Nur Kele\c{s}o\u{g}lu, S{\l}awomir Piotr Nowak

entry.summary: The paper formulates semantic grounding reliability for LLM-based robot planners as a multi-dimensional risk estimation problem, explicitly modeling ambiguity, hallucination, and semantic-conflict risks before planning. Based on estimated risks, the system decides whether to execute an instruction, request clarification, or reject it. This adds a safety layer beyond the usual focus on plan-generation quality.

entry.title: ProCTI: Prototype-Refined Global Conditioning for Diffusion-Based Time Series Imputation

author.name: Fariza Rashid, Duc Van Le, Rahat Masood, Gustavo Batista, Aruna Seneviratne, Suranga Seneviratne

entry.summary: ProCTI improves diffusion-based time series imputation by adding retrieved global dataset-level priors, learned via prototypes, to the usual local window-based conditioning during reverse diffusion. The motivation is that local context alone fails when observations are sparse, noisy, or unrepresentative. This is a sensible architectural contribution to a growing line of generative imputation work.

entry.title: Pixel-Level Transformers in Remote Sensing: A Canopy Height Case Study

author.name: Sven Ligensa, Jan Pauls, Karsten Schr\"odter, Ibrahim Fayad, Fabian Gieseke

entry.summary: This study shows that pixel-level attention schemes outpatch-size-large-patch transformers for dense regression on satellite imagery, using canopy height prediction from medium-resolution data as the case study for forest monitoring. Because pixel-level attention is resource-intensive, the authors conduct an extended efficiency analysis to make the approach practical. The findings generalize to dense prediction tasks beyond remote sensing.

entry.title: Jaxolotl: A Unified High-Performance Benchmark Suite for LTL-Based Multi-Task RL

author.name: Mathias Jackermeier, Jacques Cloete, Alessandro Abate

entry.summary: Jaxolotl provides a modular, end-to-end JAX implementation of six representative algorithms and four environments for multi-task reinforcement learning with linear temporal logic instructions, aiming to standardize comparison and enable large-scale, statistically reliable experiments. This addresses a real reproducibility problem in LTL-RL where differing implementations and protocols make methods hard to compare.

entry.title: EEGAgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Short- and Long-Horizon EEG Analysis

author.name: Huyu Wu, Weining Weng, Yuchen Liu, Yiqiang Chen, Yang Gu

entry.summary: EEGAgentBench is a unified benchmark evaluating LLM agents on EEG analysis across short-segment classification and long-horizon interpretation tasks requiring iterative evidence accumulation, multi-step reasoning, and tool use. It addresses the fragmentation of prior EEG agentic evaluations with consistent protocols covering reasoning, tool-use, and workflow construction.

entry.title: Information Design Against Gaming and Learning Adversaries

author.name: Madhava Gaikwad

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how a classifier deployer should choose abstention queries when facing either a gaming adversary who knows the classifier or a learning adversary who probes it, showing that boundary-localizing abstention is optimal against the former but catastrophically bad against the latter via a binary search attack. It proves the two natural defenses are Blackwell-incomparable and explores hybrid policies.

entry.title: TemporalGraphLLM: Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Large Language Models for Dynamic Text-Attributed Graphs

author.name: Moran Beladev, Or Eitan, Gilad Katz, Lior Rokach

entry.summary: TemporalGraphLLM is a framework that integrates arbitrary temporal graph neural networks with LLMs to jointly model evolving graph structure and rich textual attributes in dynamic text-attributed graphs. It bridges the gap between TGNNs that lack contextual text reasoning and LLMs that struggle with temporal graph structure. Applications include social networks, citation graphs, and knowledge graphs.

entry.title: Handwritten Digit Leakage from Smartphone Motion Sensors Across Unseen Users and Phone Models

author.name: Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Erkka Rantahalvari, Matteo Pedone, Matti Matilainen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Le Nguyen, Simo Hosio, Olli Silv\'en, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: This privacy study shows that handwritten digits typed on smartphones can be reconstructed from motion sensor readings, evaluating handcrafted features, MiniRocket, and a compact sensor patch transformer on 19,628 HuMIdb recordings from 481 participants. A transformer achieves about 58% accuracy and 83% top-3 accuracy on unseen users and phone models, demonstrating that even low-motion recordings leak touchscreen input.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Channel Importance in Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yong-Hoon Choi, Kwang-Hyun Park, Youngjin Cho

entry.summary: The paper disentangles different notions of cross-channel importance in multivariate forecasting—statistical relatedness, predictive usefulness, and actual model usage—showing they do not coincide and that dependency structures shift across prediction horizons. Horizon-adaptive source selection improves a controlled Ridge predictor in most tested conditions, but the same logic yields marginal gains on iTransformer, revealing limits of imposed channel selection in modern architectures. This offers a valuable diagnostic lens on multivariate forecasting models.

entry.title: Certification Frontiers for Gaussian LoRA: Independent Priors, Posterior Risk, and Prediction-Preserving Balancing

author.name: Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Ibne Farabi Shihab

entry.summary: This work characterizes when post-hoc Bayesian Gaussian LoRA fine-tuning can yield informative PAC-Bayes generalization certificates, separating the effects of prior choice, stochastic predictor modification, and complexity counting. It derives an exact isotropic KL envelope that induces width thresholds and identifies zero-KL floor targets for certification.

entry.title: Active Feature Acquisition With Incomplete Training Data

author.name: Reza Rezvan, Valter Sch\"utz, Han Wu, Linus Aronsson, Morteza Haghir Chehreghani

entry.summary: Studies active feature acquisition (AFA) when training data itself is incomplete, showing that under MCAR missingness one-step acquisition values remain unchanged while multi-step values can decrease. The paper analyzes theoretical properties and develops methods for this practical but previously overlooked setting.

entry.title: DiffPTS: Rethinking Diffusion ELBO for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Weiwei Ye, Dongyuan Li, Hangchen Liu, Haotong Jiang, Yoshihide Sekimoto, Renhe Jiang

entry.summary: Rethinks the ELBO under a Location-Scale Noise Model for diffusion-based probabilistic time series forecasting, showing it naturally induces a Gaussian negative log-likelihood objective for pretrained mean and variance estimators rather than treating them as separate regression tasks. This unifies estimator training within the variational framework.

entry.title: Rondo: Unsupervised Discovery of Recurring Temporal Structure

author.name: Yingtian Shi, Ankith Chandra, Thomas Pl\"otz

entry.summary: Rondo performs unsupervised, online discovery of hierarchical recurring structure in time series, capturing both short repeating units and complex sequences composed of them. Unlike prior approaches that treat different temporal scales independently and assume complete data, Rondo evolves as new observations arrive. This reduces costly annotation for interpreting temporal data.

entry.title: What Does a ProcGen Generalization Gap Measure? Action Rules, Convergence, and the Missing Random Floor

author.name: Abhisek Keshari

entry.summary: This single-author methodological paper argues that RL generalization gaps on ProcGen are meaningless without a reference random-policy floor measured under the same harness. It shows that switching between sampled and greedy test-time actions moves held-out return in both directions, and greedy evaluation can push performance below the random floor in some environments. The findings call for standardized reporting practices in procedural generalization benchmarks.

entry.title: Extremely Fast and Compact Binary Graph Representations via Randomized Operator Sketching

author.name: Srajan Agarwal, Megha P, Bikas C Das, Zakaria Laskar, Saptarshi Bej

entry.summary: The authors propose an ultra-fast, algebraic graph hashing method that produces compact binary node representations directly from graph structure using randomized column sampling inspired by the Nyström method. It avoids node features, gradient training, and the trade-off between topological fidelity and speed in prior binary hashing approaches. This matters for scaling graph learning to large graphs with limited memory and compute.

entry.title: Structuring Relations Among Learning Paradigms via Protocol--Objective--Resource Reductions

author.name: Junwei Su, Changjie Wang, Dongyang Chang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a protocol-objective-resource (POR) framework that formally specifies machine learning paradigms (supervised, transfer, continual, meta-learning) via environment classes, observation protocols, admissible learners, performance functionals, and resource accounting, with reduction relations between them. This allows determining whether paradigms are genuinely distinct, special cases, or part of a hierarchy. It is a conceptual/theoretical contribution to unifying ML's fragmented landscape.

entry.title: Retimed Bellman Flows: Escaping the Impossible Triangle of Velocity Bootstrapping

author.name: Boyang Xu, Shengzhe Chen, Hao Yan

entry.summary: This paper introduces Retimed Bellman Flows (ReBF) for flow-based critics in RL, which queries a teacher critic at a dynamically shifted earlier flow time combined with fresh decoupled noise to construct provably unbiased velocity targets. The method resolves a structural dilemma in velocity bootstrapping for return distribution learning.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Edge Classification on Dynamic Text-Attributed Graphs

author.name: Tyler Bonnet, Marek Rei

entry.summary: The paper establishes a leave-one-domain-out transfer protocol for edge classification on dynamic text-attributed graphs and shows state-of-the-art self-supervised dynamic graph methods transfer poorly, even underperforming a structurally unaware Bag of Events baseline. This exposes overfitting to domain-specific patterns in current approaches.

entry.title: Optimal Nonparametric Dynamic Pricing with Censored Demand and Adversarial Inventory

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang, Yingfei Wang, Haipeng Luo

entry.summary: This theory paper studies online dynamic pricing with censored demand and adversarially revealed inventory, extending prior sqrt(T) regret results beyond restrictive linear-demand assumptions to a nonparametric setting requiring only that expected sales are nonincreasing in price. It achieves optimal regret under substantially weaker structural conditions.

entry.title: \L{}ukasiewicz Neural Networks Extended: Residual Architectures and Crystallization Strategies for Interpretable Rule Extraction

author.name: Carlos Leandro

entry.summary: This work extends Lukasiewicz neural networks, whose integer weights and truncated-identity activations exactly implement many-valued logic connectives, enabling trained networks to be read out as logical formulas rather than black boxes. The paper tackles two barriers that previously limited the approach to shallow networks and small datasets: probabilistic success of crystallization (forcing weights to integers) under Levenberg-Marquardt training, and the breakdown of theoretical guarantees in deeper architectures, via new residual architectures and crystallization strategies. This is significant for neuro-symbolic AI and interpretable-by-construction models.

entry.title: What Must a World Model Distinguish for Planning?

author.name: Rongzhe Wei, Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, Peizhi Niu, Yifan Li, Pan Li

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a hierarchy of mechanism, response, and decision sufficiency to characterize what distinctions a world model must preserve for planning, showing that coarse decisions can discard much prediction-relevant information while fine decisions may need nearly full resolution. It also analyzes how adaptive candidate search changes what information is necessary.

entry.title: Simulation-Free Learning of GP-SDEs from Irregular Observations

author.name: Zhidi Lin, Yuhao Liu, Ying Li, Edwin Fong, Petar Djuri\'c

entry.summary: GP-SDE Matching is a simulation-free variational framework for Bayesian learning of Gaussian process stochastic differential equation drifts and continuous-time state smoothing from noisy, irregular observations. It analytically marginalizes the sparse GP posterior into a tractable drift-matching objective and introduces an irregular-time-aware variational state posterior.

entry.title: When Does Backpropagating Through Policy Memory Matter? Physical Credit, Optimizer Updates, and Observability

author.name: Xingjian Li, Yi Han, Jianhua Z. Huang

entry.summary: This work examines when backpropagation through stored memory (e.g., Transformer-XL KV caches or truncated BPTT) matters for memory-based policies, holding forward computation fixed and varying only derivative edges. In vessel-trajectory and quadrotor-tracking models, detaching the KV cache effects depend strongly on whether gradients flow through earlier physical states.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimality of Posterior Sampling for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Taewon Goo, Kihyuk Hong

entry.summary: The paper resolves an open theoretical question by proving that vanilla posterior sampling for reinforcement learning (PSRL) achieves minimax-optimal leading-order Bayesian regret in finite-horizon tabular MDPs under arbitrary, possibly correlated, priors. The proof uses a common empirical transition reference to isolate value mismatch plus a Bellman-based variance argument.

entry.title: BITS: Rethinking Fair and Comprehensive Evaluation for Irregular Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Kangjia Yan, Linfeng Wang, Tianen Shen, Xiangfei Qiu, Ruitong Zhang, Hao Miao, Jilin Hu, Chenjuan Guo, Bin Yang, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: BITS is a standardized, reproducible, and extensible benchmark for irregular time series forecasting, covering eleven datasets across nine domains and characterizing them by missing rate, missing pattern, and other irregularity attributes. It addresses inconsistent protocols and error-only metrics that hamper fair method comparison in the field.

entry.title: StarBOA: Real-Time Mamba State-Space Unrolling for Sparse Radar Micro-Doppler in ISAC Networks

author.name: Mustafa Bora \c{C}elik, Ceren \c{C}elik, Orhan Gazi

entry.summary: The paper addresses radar sensing in Integrated Sensing and Communications networks where chirp subsampling leaves up to 90% of data missing. It replaces an attention-based baseline, which fails under high sparsity due to a limited buffer, with a causal Mamba state-space model that maintains persistent state and integrates over 100x more temporal history at no extra per-step cost. StarBOA outperforms the published baseline results across all sparsity levels with increasing SSIM gains.

entry.title: Compressing Value Predictions for Learning-Augmented Metrical Task Systems

author.name: Sizhe Li, Yecheng Li, Kun He

entry.summary: The paper shows that learning-augmented algorithms for metrical task systems can operate with dual-value predictions compressed to a small set of landmark states, reconstructing the rest via Lipschitz extension. It provides additive excess cost bounds involving landmark covering radius and prediction error.

entry.title: FuseAlign: Forced Alignment in the Wild

author.name: Mithilesh Vaidya, Stephen Bailey, Sumukh Badam, Matthew Bendel, Xingzhe He

entry.summary: This paper shows existing forced alignment evaluations understate real difficulty by using short, clean speech and perfect transcripts, and introduces improved metrics, a scoring protocol for error-prone ASR output, and AlignBench spanning diverse conditions. It targets practical uses including media editing, subtitling, and speech-data curation.

entry.title: Scalable Attribution and Control of Model Behavior During Training

author.name: Sleem Abdelghafar

entry.summary: The paper introduces Batch-Space Ghost (BS-Ghost), an algorithm for attributing individual example contributions to model behavior changes during training, using mutual information to disambiguate examples whose batch effects interfere. Behavioral Gradient Uniqueness gives the information measure a geometric interpretation, enabling per-example attribution fast enough to act before the next update. This is relevant to data-centric training control and could influence data selection and debugging.

entry.title: StatD2GAN: When Calibration Masks Generator Quality in Held-Out Evaluation of Synthetic Weather Sequences

author.name: Mustafa Ozaytac, Ozge Karadag Atas

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard evaluation of synthetic weather generators — pooled distributional metrics after marginal calibration — can invalidate architectural conclusions, since calibration drives Kolmogorov-Smirnov metrics regardless of generator quality. It rebuilds evaluation around a strict held-out protocol with a 168-hour embargo, testing across 25 matched location-seed pairs in five climates with corrected statistical tests. A rigorous methodological corrective for generative weather modeling.

entry.title: Where Activation Sparsity and KV-Cache Sparsity Cross in LLM Decoding

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Seungyoon Lee, Seongtae Hong, Sugyeong Eo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Provides an analytical study of when activation sparsity versus KV-cache sparsity delivers greater LLM decoding speedup, deriving a byte crossover context length at which the two savings are equal, plus ideal speedup bounds for each branch and their composition from model dimensions and keep ratios. Empirical timing from 2K to 128K tokens on two GPUs with real text validates the analysis.

entry.title: ICMAPE: In-Context Multiagent Pure Exploration

author.name: Xinyi Hu, Alessio Russo, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: Presents a Bayesian framework for decentralized multi-agent pure exploration (active sequential hypothesis testing), converting the fixed-confidence identification objective into an inference-confidence reward usable with standard RL machinery. This fills a gap between single-agent, well-specified ASHT theory and practical multi-agent settings.

entry.title: T-SNN: Temporal Simplicial Neural Network for EEG Decoding

author.name: Nikita Malik, Shubhajit Roy, Mohit Kataria, Isuru Herath, Suraj Yadav, In\'es Garc\'ia-Redondo, Dhananjay Bhaskar

entry.summary: T-SNN represents EEG recordings as sequences of evolving simplicial complexes, combining simplicial convolutions with recurrent updates to capture dynamic higher-order interactions among brain regions. It outperforms convolutional, recurrent, graph-based, and Transformer baselines on the seven-class SEED-VII emotion recognition task.

entry.title: Vision--Language Signals in Constrained RL: Safety Gains Without Anticipation

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: VLM-Safe-RL integrates frozen CLIP signals into PPO-Lagrangian for safe reinforcement learning in driving, using reward shaping and an augmented multiplier update. Notably, the paper analyzes whether VLM scores actually anticipate collisions and finds safety gains arise without genuine hazard anticipation, a useful negative/clarifying result.

entry.title: MaskCoFT: Masked Co-Adaptive Fine-Tuning for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference

author.name: Junfeng Wu, Zehao Fan, Hadjer Benmeziane, Kaoutar El Maghraoui, Liu Liu, Yinan Wang

entry.summary: MaskCoFT co-adapts routers and experts in MoE language models with a learnable binary mask restricting Top-K routing to a subset of experts, so experts adjust to tokens the reshaped routing sends them. This improves expert offloading efficiency beyond router-only fine-tuning, reducing how many experts each token must fetch during decode.

entry.title: Beyond Correctness: Evaluating Semantic Knowledge in Cross-Table Transfer

author.name: Seokyong Sheem, Hochang Lee, Suyeong Lee, Daekyum Kim

entry.summary: This paper examines how semantic knowledge is used to bridge heterogeneous schemas in tabular learning and questions whether common ablation-based evaluation methods actually measure predictive benefit. The authors show that semantic ablations can yield misleading conclusions, since altering semantic content can produce large performance differences even when the model gains little genuine predictive advantage from that knowledge. They propose separating these effects through controlled experiments on real and synthetic data.

entry.title: What Does a Stream Model Buy You in Flow Matching?

author.name: Jian Xu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper analyzes stream-level flow matching, which replaces the linear interpolant of conditional flow matching with a Gaussian-process stream, and shows the design space collapses to exactly what standard CFM already parametrizes under its construction. It provides a reduction result clarifying that stream models offer no expressivity gain in the Gaussian regime.

entry.title: Direct Self-Evolving Optimization: Evolving LLMs without Challenger Training

author.name: Yuyang Deng, Yu Wang, Jiayun Wang

entry.summary: DEO replaces explicit challenger training in self-evolving LLM pipelines with solver-guided task sampling, interpreting the KL-regularized challenger objective as an exponential tilt of a fixed base task distribution. A frozen LLM generates and mutates tasks, the solver scores them, and an approximate Metropolis rule refines the training pool so only the solver is trained.

entry.title: MegaGraph: Towards Efficient Training of Large-Scale Graph Transformers with Automated Hybrid Parallelism

author.name: Tong Qiao, Ao Zhou, Yingjie Qi, Chunming Hu, Jianlei Yang

entry.summary: MegaGraph is the first automated hybrid parallelism framework for training graph transformers at scale, addressing GT-specific bottlenecks such as per-layer memory overhead from attention and topology-aware bias matrices plus workload imbalance from heavy graph embedding layers. It provides a dedicated parallelism solution beyond what standard GNN or Transformer techniques offer.

entry.title: Harmonizing Spectral Evolution in Conditional Flow Matching for TTS

author.name: Isha Pandey Varad Deshpande Abhijat Bharadwaj Ganesh Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: This paper identifies incoherent frequency evolution during inference in conditional flow matching TTS models and proposes a training-free fix using the Discrete Wavelet Transform to dynamically modulate mel-spectrogram sub-bands during ODE integration. The method penalizes aggressive low-frequency growth while boosting lagging high-frequency detail, validated across multiple architectures including Matcha-TTS.

entry.title: FlexLoop: Depth-Elastic Looped Policies for Adaptive Test-Time Computation in Deep RL

author.name: Xun Wang, Ruishuo Chen, Yu Chen, Zhuoran Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: FlexLoop addresses the surprising finding that pretrained looped RL policies specialize to their trained recurrent depth, so decisions are only reliable near full depth, blocking adaptive test-time computation. The paper proposes depth-elastic looped policies that produce reliable decisions across recurrent depths, enabling variable computation at deployment. This connects test-time compute adaptation to deep RL policy architectures.

entry.title: Scalable GNN-based Knowledge Graph Representation Learning with Efficient Message Passing

author.name: Huu Tan Mai, Cuong Xuan Chu, Heiko Paulheim, Daria Stepanova

entry.summary: This paper extends Relational Sparse Matrix Multiplication (RSPMM) to losslessly reduce the space complexity of message passing in GNNs on knowledge graphs, addressing scalability bottlenecks that subgraph-sampling approaches handle only in task- and model-specific ways. The work targets link prediction and entity classification on large KGs with guaranteed lossless reductions. This makes GNN-based KG learning more deployable at industrial scale.

entry.title: HALO: Enhancing Time Series Generation via Hyperspherical Latents and Masked AutoregRessive Modeling

author.name: Chunyi Hou, Xiangfei Qiu, Hanyin Cheng, Yutong Li, Bin Yang

entry.summary: HALO improves time series generation by moving from the common two-stage discrete-latent plus next-token-prediction paradigm to generative modeling in a continuous hyperspherical latent space with masked autoregressive modeling. This avoids information loss from discretization and error accumulation from strict autoregression. Time series generation matters for simulation, augmentation, and privacy-preserving data sharing.

entry.title: Universal Dynamic Portfolios

author.name: Yu-Jie Zhang, Yu-Xiang Wang, Peng Zhao, Kevin Jamieson

entry.summary: This work generalizes Cover's Universal Portfolio to compete with arbitrary dynamic comparator sequences, formulating a dynamic regret minimization problem for log loss. It proves the exp-concavity advantage disappears in the dynamic setting, with an unavoidable linear-loss-type sqrt(T*P_T) dependence on path length, and develops methods accordingly.

entry.title: Instance-Adaptive Prompts as Context for Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Zehao Xiao, Shifeng Xie, Lei Zan, Jianfeng Zhang, Lujia Pan, Ievgen Redko, Malik Tiomoko, Keli Zhang

entry.summary: PaCTS compresses long historical context into a small set of instance-adaptive latent prompt tokens for frozen time-series foundation models, combining global statistics with segment-level temporal information. This reduces inference cost relative to feeding long histories while retaining predictive information. Relevant to efficient deployment of TSFMs.

entry.title: Structured Neural SDEs for Functional Calibration

author.name: Francesco Piatti, Andrea Iannucci, Thomas Cass

entry.summary: SLiSDE is a family of neural stochastic differential equations built from structured linear stochastic layers, enabling parallel-in-time simulation and expressivity via gated stacking. It adds a Girsanov tilt as learned importance sampling for functional calibration tasks where rare paths dominate the loss. Useful for simulation in quantitative finance and path-functional training.

entry.title: XMatch: Enhancing Covariate-Aware Time Series Forecasting through Tree-Structured Exogenous Matching

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Hanyin Cheng, Xiangfei Qiu, Yang Shu, Bin Yang, Chenjuan Guo

entry.summary: XMatch improves covariate-aware forecasting by matching future exogenous variable patterns to historical ones and transferring the associated endogenous response patterns, using a tree-structured mechanism to handle large numbers of exogenous variables. This complements direct influence modeling. A useful advance for real-world multivariate forecasting.

entry.title: Cyclostationary Phase Conditioning for Medical Time Series Diffusion

author.name: Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Michele Copetti, Jorge da Silva Goncalves, Sonia Laguna, Thomas Hofmann, Julia E. Vogt

entry.summary: The paper introduces inductive biases for diffusion-based restoration of physiological signals such as cardiac and brain recordings, encoding cyclostationarity via a shift-covariant wavelet representation and dense per-sample phase conditioning. It also provides a training-free cyclostationarity index that predicts when phase conditioning helps.

entry.title: SymbolicArena: A Unified Infrastructure for Benchmark Distillation and Dynamic Evaluation in Symbolic Regression

author.name: Ziwen Zhang, Xiju Wu, Yuheng Jing, Runxiang Wang, Boxiao Wang, Yifan Zang, Yifan Zhang, Yang Wang, Kai Li, Yifan Zhang, Huilin Xu, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: SymbolicArena standardizes 664 heterogeneous symbolic regression tasks with executable ground truth and distills them into Core50, a validated 50-task benchmark that preserves task diversity and algorithm discriminability. It offers dynamic evaluation infrastructure addressing the cost-versus-validity tradeoff in SR benchmarking.

entry.title: ConRAG: Lightweight inference of multi-hop relations

author.name: Kilian B\"anziger, Sonia Laguna, Markus Kreft, Robert Jakob, Kevin O'Sullivan, Lasse B. Strand, Julia E. Vogt

entry.summary: ConRAG formalizes multi-hop relation inference between two known endpoint entities, recovering bridge entities and evidence-grounded reasoning chains across a document corpus with generated explanations. It targets a gap left by standard multi-hop RAG systems, which seek unknown answers rather than explaining connections between known entities.

entry.title: Tetra: Serving Leech-Lattice Quantized LLMs at 2.7 Bits per Parameter

author.name: Pier-Jean Malandrino

entry.summary: Tetra introduces a new codebook for leech-lattice quantization that decodes 24-weight blocks with six table loads via a trellis of the Golay code, reducing GPU memory reads from 4.8 to about 2.1 bits per weight, plus mixed 4-bit storage and embedding tables for full models. It demonstrates serving quantized LLMs such as Qwen3-4B at roughly 2.7 bits per parameter.

entry.title: Arbitrary-Accuracy Neural Approximation with Optimal Neuron Count and Near-Optimal Bit Complexity

author.name: Zilan Cheng, Li-Lian Wang, Zhongjian Wang

entry.summary: This theory paper constructs explicit activation functions for which a network with only d+1 hidden neurons achieves arbitrary-accuracy uniform approximation of Holder-continuous multivariate functions, proving d+1 is the exact minimum among standard feedforward networks. They also provide simpler constructions with floor and exponential activations and analyze associated encoding/bit complexity.

entry.title: MeqMuon: Matrix-Equilibrating Muon for LLM Pretraining

author.name: Chang-Wei Shi, Xu Wang, Wu-Jun Li

entry.summary: MeqMuon improves the Muon optimizer for LLM pretraining by balancing both row and column magnitudes of update matrices with normalization automatically tailored to different imbalance patterns, going beyond recent row-wise normalization. It also eliminates a manual parameter, aiming for better pretraining efficiency and accuracy at scale.

entry.title: Exterior complex scaling enables physics-informed neural networks for quantum scattering

author.name: Jin Lei
