entry.summary: The paper shows that exterior complex scaling transforms oscillatory, non-decaying scattering boundary conditions into exponentially decaying waves, making nuclear scattering problems solvable with physics-informed neural networks for the first time. A driven-equation formulation confines the source term to the real axis, avoiding analytic continuation of nuclear potentials. Validation on nucleon-nucleus scattering demonstrates the approach.

entry.title: Data Processing for Offline Evaluation in Recommender Systems: a Survey

author.name: Alberto Carlo Maria Mancino, Angela Di Fazio, Danilo Danese, Matteo Attimonelli, Daniele Malitesta, Antonio Ferrara, Claudio Pomo, Tommaso Di Noia

entry.summary: This survey systematically characterizes data processing practices preceding offline evaluation in recommender systems, covering the pipeline from dataset selection through interaction processing. It argues these under-scrutinized decisions materially affect comparability and reproducibility of experimental results. The work offers a cross-domain reference for more rigorous recommendation research methodology.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for Acoustic Pedestrian Detection

author.name: Yonghyun Kim, Chaeyeon Han, Sancho Gatungay, Subhrajit Guhathakurta, Alexander Lerch

entry.summary: The paper introduces Trust-Filtered Distillation (TFD), which selectively suppresses teacher supervision for pedestrian samples in video-to-audio knowledge distillation, interpreted as conditional label smoothing. A rigorous evaluation across ten distillation configurations with cross-session validation shows most methods give only modest gains under severe class imbalance and modality gap.

entry.title: Identifiability Limits of Gravitational Wave Phase Deviations: Multiclass Classification with a Multihead Neural Network

author.name: Lavinia Heisenberg, Shayan Hemmatyar

entry.summary: A multihead neural network classifies gravitational-wave phase deviations of general relativity against six parametrized post-Einsteinian families and regresses coupling magnitude, using waveform-mismatch sensitivity responses under realistic LIGO noise for hundreds of sources. The work probes the identifiability limits of deviations across Gaussian, measured, and real detector strain conditions.

entry.title: High-Probability Guarantees for SGD under $\beta$-Heavy-Tailed Gradient Noise

author.name: Qijun Tong, Masahiro Ikeda, Ryota Kawasumi

entry.summary: The paper provides high-probability convergence guarantees for SGD under heavy-tailed gradient noise, using Orlicz space theory and Young functions to unify noise tail models beyond sub-Gaussian and sub-Weibull assumptions. The framework accommodates distributions such as lognormal noise, which better matches empirical reports from deep learning.

entry.title: Federated Subspace Guided Vision-Language-Action Policy Distillation for Non-IID Multi-Robot Manipulation

author.name: Biprodip Pal, Kaushik Roy, Yanming Zhu, Brendan Tidd, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: FedDRMan enables multiple robots to jointly learn manipulation policies via federated learning despite non-IID tasks, using a frozen server teacher for local behavior cloning plus low-rank subspace and action-distribution distillation to prevent destructive aggregation. It targets heterogeneous robot fleets without centralized demonstration access.

entry.title: Agnostic Smoothed Online Regression with Adversarial Responses

author.name: Xuanyu Chen, Yue Yu

entry.summary: The paper studies smoothed online prediction with bounded adversarial responses, a framework interpolating between i.i.d. sampling and adversarial covariate selection via a smoothness parameter. It proposes Hedge-Cover, an information-theoretic algorithm achieving sublinear regret O(sqrt(Pdim(F) * C_cov * T)) for function classes with bounded pseudo-dimension, using Hedge over a carefully constructed expert family. It advances the theoretical foundations of online learning under partially adversarial conditions.

entry.title: Learning What to Evaluate: Correlation-Aware Decoupling for Multiobjective Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Ashwin Renganathan, Peter Bachman

entry.summary: The paper proposes exploiting correlations between objectives and constraints in multiobjective Bayesian optimization to decouple evaluations, allowing only a subset of objectives/constraints to be evaluated per round rather than all. This reduces expensive evaluation costs in GP-surrogate-based optimization.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Symbolic Discovery for Financial Fundamental Analysis

author.name: Kelvin J. L. Koa, Filip Orestav, Shengqiong Wu, Michael J. Wooldridge, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MUFASA, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that applies symbolic regression to financial fundamental analysis, using specialized agents that represent distinct valuation perspectives to disentangle equation discovery. It addresses why finance differs from scientific symbolic regression: multiple valid perspectives, non-stationary markets, and noisy performance signals.

entry.title: Readout is not Recovery: Dissociating Coordinate Emission from Visual-Corruption Repair in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Drandreb Earl Juanico

entry.summary: Studying Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct on COCO grounding, the paper dissociates coordinate-token readout from recovery of localization after visual corruption, finding coordinate rankings are inert through layer 24, load-bearing around layers 32-35 with a peak at layer 34, while corruption-repair signals behave differently across layers.

entry.title: CT-OPD: Counterfactual Trace On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Vision-Language Models

author.name: Long Qian, Bingke Zhu, Jiaqi Wei, Yu Li, Yingying Chen, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a post-training method for diffusion vision-language models that combines counterfactual traces with on-policy distillation, aligning token-level supervision with the model's own masking/reveal decisions instead of prescribed masks. This addresses the coarse, response-level-only feedback of outcome-based RL when rewards tie.

entry.title: Sharp Critical Minimax Laws and No-Learning Thresholds in Continuous-Time Adaptive Control

author.name: Chen Jia

entry.summary: The paper derives sharp minimax regret laws for episodic continuous-time adaptive control with unknown control gain, proving a critical asymptotic law for the minimax improvement over zero control near a no-learning threshold, with matching upper and lower bounds. It also characterizes normalized minimax regret over episodes for local parameter regimes. This is rigorous theoretical work quantifying exactly when and how much adaptive control can learn in hard regimes.

entry.title: Offline Policy Evaluation via Mixed Bellman Residuals and Adaptive Critic Representations

author.name: Amitakshar Biswas, Yuhan Li, Ruoqing Zhu

entry.summary: For offline policy evaluation, the paper proposes optimizing a convex combination of one-step and two-step Bellman residuals to trade off approximation bias against the variance of multi-step importance weighting. It adopts a minimax formulation with a data-dependent adaptive critic representation rather than a fixed function class. This improves the reliability of evaluating target policies from behavior-policy data.

entry.title: Let CSP Be Your ANCHOR: Adaptive Crystal Search over Frozen Structure Priors

author.name: Emma Lei Hovmand, Jonas Elsborg, Melih Kandemir, Arghya Bhowmik

entry.summary: ANCHOR decouples where to search from how to generate in de novo crystal discovery: a frozen crystal structure prediction model acts as a physical prior while a GRPO-trained composition policy explores with multi-objective rewards. It also introduces continuous adaptive novelty (CAN), a graded novelty score against known structures and a growing discovery history.

entry.title: Protected Cores Are Not Enough: Certifying AI-Proposed Revisions of Temporal Specifications

author.name: Ruggero Lanotte

entry.summary: The paper introduces an intersymbolic architecture where an untrusted AI proposer suggests revisions to temporal runtime-monitoring specifications while a symbolic governor controls activation, using origin-version semantics to track each obligation's outcome. This addresses the safety problem that directly letting AI rewrite formal specifications can weaken protected requirements or overfit transient behavior.

entry.title: Multi-Marginal Inverse Optimal Transport for Contrastive Learning Via Explicit Anchor-Positive-Negative Coupling

author.name: Ngoc-Hai Nguyen, Thuan Nguyen, Prakash Ishwar, Shuchin Aeron

entry.summary: Neg-MMIOT-CL extends inverse optimal transport representation learning to a multi-marginal formulation that explicitly couples anchors, positives, and negatives, addressing dimensional collapse caused by ignoring negative pairs. It makes inverse-OT representation learning genuinely contrastive.

entry.title: Neuron-Level Architecture Growth: A Controlled Evaluation for EEG Time-Series Decoding

author.name: Adam Mounir, Stella Douka, Arnault H. Caillet, Bruno Aristimunha, Sylvain Chevallier

entry.summary: This paper provides the first controlled evaluation of neuron-growing methods for convolutional EEG decoders, growing three backbones across 12 motor-imagery datasets under three protocols and comparing each to its fixed reference width. Results are mixed: growing ShallowFBCSPNet gains 2.9 points with roughly half the parameters, SCCNet changes marginally, and Deep4Net shows decreased accuracy with adaptation complications. The study offers honest, per-subject evidence about where growing helps.

entry.title: Kafila: Serving Large Language Models on a Trusted Set of Heterogeneous Commodity Machines

author.name: Murtaza Rangwala, Richard O. Sinnott, Rajkumar Buyya

entry.summary: Kafila is a system for serving large language models across a trusted, bounded set of heterogeneous consumer machines, pooling capacity from devices behind NATs via a ring protocol with carefully planned work partitioning. It addresses the gap between open swarms and groups that can only admit trusted members.

entry.title: MoSPR: Histology-to-Gene Expression Prediction with Morpho-Spatial Macrostates and Low-Rank Molecular Programs

author.name: Dongmyung Shin, Geongyu Lee, Yesung Cho, Park Jong Bae

entry.summary: MoSPR is a linear framework for predicting gene expression from histopathology whole-slide images. It clusters frozen patch embeddings into morphology microstates, groups them into spatially informed macrostates based on adjacency patterns, and linearly maps slide-level morphology features onto a low-rank molecular basis. This offers an interpretable, computationally lightweight alternative to heavy end-to-end deep models for the challenging histology-to-transcriptomics task.

entry.title: Probabilistic Geodesic Flow Matching on Location-Scale Families

author.name: Zeyuan Yu, Zhi Chang, Shiwei Lan

entry.summary: This paper generalizes flow matching beyond optimal-transport-derived Gaussian probability paths to the broader class of location-scale families, handling data with inhomogeneous structures such as heavy tails or sharp contrast. It develops probabilistic geodesic paths on these families to improve the expressiveness of the induced ODE-based generative process. The work addresses a known suboptimality of Gaussian OT paths in flow matching.

entry.title: ResonAct: Streaming Metrics for Runtime Diagnosis and Self-Healing in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Tarun Chintada, Neelamadhav Gantayat, Ishaan Romil, Renuka Sindhgatta, Soujanya Soni, Sameep Mehta

entry.summary: ResonAct is a runtime self-healing framework for multi-agent systems that continuously monitors streaming operational metrics to diagnose and remediate failures during execution rather than after completion. It addresses failure modes including tool degradation, context propagation errors, coordination breakdowns, and repetitive agent loops in enterprise workflows. The framework ingests execution traces and agent interactions to enable mid-execution recovery.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction and Conditional Coverage for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Sungwoo Park, Sunghee Park, Won Chang

entry.summary: This paper introduces C-USIM, a lightweight conformal prediction method for tabular foundation models that handles multimodal predictive distributions via highest predictive density split conformal prediction without additional training or inference. It provides finite-sample marginal validity, bounds conditional-marginal coverage gaps, and analyzes coverage heterogeneity, with experiments on TabPFN-class models. It addresses unreliable prediction regions even when point predictions are accurate.

entry.title: Perceptual Quality Loss or Loss of Perceptual Quality?

author.name: Danilo de Oliveira, Tal Peer, Maur\'icio do V. M. da Costa, Timo Gerkmann

entry.summary: This paper examines whether adding perceptual metric terms (PESQ) to speech enhancement loss functions actually improves listening experience. Through objective and subjective experiments, the authors find that PESQ-optimized models gain little beyond PESQ scores and can even perform worse on mismatched conditions. It is a cautionary study on metric-driven training in audio processing.

entry.title: Building Transformation Layers for Riemannian Neural Networks

author.name: Ziheng Chen

entry.summary: This work presents a general framework for constructing fully connected and convolutional layers over computationally tractable Riemannian spaces, unifying previous manifold-specific layers as special cases. The framework is instantiated on ten representative manifolds including three hyperbolic models and five geometries of SPD matrices. It offers a systematic generalization of Euclidean neural network layers to non-Euclidean geometries.

entry.title: Learning Conditional Expectation Operators via Functional Newton Updates

author.name: Thiago Ramos, Alek Fr\"ohlich, Daniel Perazzo, Massimiliano Pontil

entry.summary: This paper presents the Functional Spectral-Newton Method (FSNM) for learning the leading singular structure of conditional expectation operators without fixing a basis or RKHS, using alternating functional Newton updates approximated via vector-valued regression trees in a boosting scheme. The authors provide population-level convergence guarantees including an O(1/T) rate and global optimality of nondegenerate local minima. It is a theoretical contribution relevant to kernel-free operator learning.

entry.title: Parser, Chunking, and Embedding Interactions in Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Indian Government Regulatory Documents

author.name: Shubham Kumar Singh

entry.summary: The paper runs a controlled factorial study of 3 parsers, 3 chunking strategies, and 5 dense embedding models plus BM25 across four structurally distinct Indian government regulatory documents, using 800 question instances with automatically validated evidence strings and linear modeling of component interactions. It addresses the common practice of assembling RAG pipelines from independently chosen components without joint evaluation. The findings inform practical RAG system design, particularly for regulatory/legal text.

entry.title: A model of rational interlocutors: Unification of comprehension and production

author.name: Hanlin Wu, Zhenguang G. Cai

entry.summary: The paper proposes the Rational Interlocutor model, a computational account unifying speaker modeling in comprehension and audience design in production as a single rational computation. A partner model is characterized by parameters for identity, fidelity, and knowledge, formalizing how communicators adapt to whom they talk with.

entry.title: Streamlined Reflective Evolution for Task-Adaptive Self-Refinement Pipelines

author.name: Xiaofan Zhou, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces Workflow-Designing Agents (WDA), a framework that evolves both the instructions and the sequential structure of self-refinement pipelines without updating model weights. It identifies a failure mode where repeated revisions accumulate redundant instructions in a single prompt and proposes SPLIT, which redistributes instructions across specialized stages. Selection is guided by three-example reflection, local screening, and Pareto-based calibration scores.

entry.title: Hesitation-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jianguo Huang, Lipeng Wan, Yanchen Deng, Bo An

entry.summary: The paper identifies that trace-based on-policy distillation for diffusion LLMs supervises only committed token positions, discarding so-called hesitation proposals that make up 24% of pairs but carry 66% of teacher-student divergence. The authors propose leveraging these uncommitted proposals to improve distillation efficiency on an SDAR-4B student. It offers a targeted improvement to an emerging model class.

entry.title: Rethinking Token Reweighting for SFT: Suppress, Reverse, and Extrapolate Learned Features

author.name: Cunchun Li, Haonan He, Yifan Gao, Minglei Li, Jingqi Ye, Qingyu Yang, Peng Ye

entry.summary: Through a unified policy-loss view, the authors show existing token-reweighting methods for SFT assign nonnegative coefficients and thus cannot reverse harmful learned features, only suppress or amplify updates. They argue reversal and extrapolation require a stable reference frame anchored in pretrained features, proposing an approach beyond standard reweighting. This offers both a critique and constructive direction for safer fine-tuning.

entry.title: Tsubame: Tree Replay for Diffusion-Based Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yepeng Weng, Qiao Hu, Takehisa Yairi

entry.summary: Observes that context-aware dynamic draft trees under stochastic speculative decoding can fall behind sampled chains because their nodes are populated with deterministic high-score tokens. Tsubame fixes the tree topology via construction and then repopulates its nodes by sampling, combining structural advantages with the acceptance gains of stochastic verification. It matters for accelerating diffusion-based language model inference.

entry.title: When Do Agents Help? Embedding, LLM and Agentic Alignment of Classical Texts and Their Translations

author.name: M\'at\'e Metzger

entry.summary: Compares seven text-alignment systems (embedding pipelines, direct LLM calls, an autonomous agent, and an audited agent) on 452 classical texts in Pali, Sanskrit, Mishnaic Hebrew and Tibetan with 9,833 human-aligned units. Generative workflows recover 93-94% of reference correspondences versus at most 77% for embeddings, though the agent's edge over direct LLM calls is only about 0.5 points. The study answers when agentic workflows actually add value over simpler approaches.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Cue-Grounded Topic Segmentation of Spoken Documents

author.name: Suhwan Choi, Myeongho Jeon, Myungjoo Kang

entry.summary: CGS is a training-free framework for topic segmentation of spoken documents that first anchors boundaries on phrases explicitly signaling topic onset, then falls back to semantic segmentation when cues are insufficient. This adapts granularity across documents, addressing over- and under-segmentation failures of LLM-based segmenters.

entry.title: ReMCTS: Reflection-Enhanced Monte Carlo Tree Search for Code Generation

author.name: Huifei Wang, Xinying Huang, Yiheng Sun, Yifan Yuan

entry.summary: Presents ReMCTS, an execution-grounded, memory-augmented MCTS-style search framework for code generation that organizes candidates as tree states, keeps branch-local debugging context, and retrieves cross-branch failure experience. It improves over direct generation on HumanEval and MBPP-Sanitized in most model-dataset pairs under held-out evaluation.

entry.title: TQTS-Bench: A Multi-Syntax Benchmark for Text-to-Query over Time-Series Databases

author.name: Fei Lyu, Zhiyi Peng, Jiaming Liu, Yixuan Yang, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, Jiapeng Zhang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: Introduces TQTS-Bench, a benchmark of 6,125 QA pairs for text-to-query over time-series databases, spanning 97 TSDBs, 23 query syntaxes, 22 domains, and time-specific query intents. It fills a gap left by text-to-SQL benchmarks that ignore TSDB-specific syntaxes and intents.

entry.title: From Weak Task Specifications to Scientific Extraction Agents: Optimizing Task Construction

author.name: Zixiao Dong, Wei Yang, Zihao Liu, Chenshu Li, Longzhang Liu, Tao Tan, Hong Xie

entry.summary: Addresses the upstream problem of building task configurations (schemas, extraction instructions, rubrics) for scientific extraction agents from only a short goal and unannotated documents. The framework keeps schema construction and instructions editable during optimization rather than treating them as fixed preprocessing.

entry.title: SCBO: Semantically Coherent Batching and Ordering for LLM-Based Social Surveys

author.name: Yuanzi Li, Lingjie Wang, Zihang Tian, Lei Wang, Xu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SCBO, a training-free framework that batches and orders multiple survey questions into single prompts for LLM-based respondent simulation, allowing shared reference responses and sequential conditioning on earlier answers. This reduces redundant context encoding and improves simulation efficiency for social science applications.

entry.title: Tracing the Evolution of Oracle Bone Characters Across Three Millennia

author.name: Tianhao Fu, Xinxin Xu, Spike Wang, Cunyi Kang, Jian Cao, Xixin Cao

entry.summary: The paper proposes MSEF, a manifold-based framework modeling the evolution of Chinese characters across five script periods (Oracle Bone, Bronze, Seal, Clerical, Regular) as continual evolution of a manifold space. Unlike single-period comparison approaches, this handles substantial structural and semantic changes between eras, addressing the fact that only about 1,600 of roughly 4,500 Oracle Bone characters have been deciphered. This demonstrates computational methods contributing to digital humanities and epigraphy.

entry.title: Improving Medical Calculation of LLMs with Embedded Coding

author.name: Tianshi Ming, Yingying Zhang, Xian Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces MedCode, a framework training LLMs to generate embedded executable code for medical calculations (dosing, organ-function scores, prognostic indices), delegating arithmetic to a deterministic interpreter to avoid numerical errors. Given a clinical context, the model identifies the calculator, extracts inputs, and produces a script whose execution returns the value. This targets a safety-critical LLM failure mode with a straightforward, well-motivated mitigation.

entry.title: EngramRAG: Dynamic Usage-Weighted Topology and Synaptic Consolidation for Multi-Hop Agentic Memory

author.name: Bhavyateja Potineni, Lohit Giri, Anu Jain, Vadim Kutsyy, Rajasekhar Pentakota

entry.summary: EngramRAG is an adaptive agent memory architecture grounded in complementary learning systems theory, coupling a fast waking-state reflex with an asynchronous dreaming-state consolidation cycle. It introduces usage-modulated Personalized PageRank with Hebbian plasticity to address associative blindness, temporal decay of core invariants, and static graph topology in multi-session agents. The neuroscience-inspired design is ambitious and targets known memory failures of autonomous LLM agents.

entry.title: CLAIRE: A Schema-Grounded Hybrid Workflow for Healthcare Administrative Form Completion

author.name: Garapati Keerthana, Manik Gupta

entry.summary: Describes CLAIRE, a hybrid agentic workflow for healthcare form completion that separates field discovery, mapping, validation, correction, escalation, and audit tracing. It is evaluated at large scale across synthetic schemas with 24,000 benchmark episodes and comparisons against multiple baselines.

entry.title: Self-Adapting Group of Experts for Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Mohammad Atif Quamar, Nurbek Tastan, Karthik Nandakumar, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: SAGE is a training-free multi-agent framework that uses answer agreement, prefix consistency, and reciprocal peer review to identify which agent's reasoning strategy best suits a problem and transfer that strategy to other agents via prompt adaptation. This contrasts with frameworks that only modify context while leaving prompts fixed.

entry.title: FD-AA: A Lightweight Focal-Diffuse And Attenuation-Aware Head for Incidental Abdominal Abnormality Detection in Chest CT

author.name: Haoyan Ding, Kritika Iyer, Halid Yerebakan, Zhenyu Bu, Chushu Shen, Peiyu Duan, Xinyuan Zheng, Sepehr Farhand, Xueqi Guo, Chaowei Wu, Yoshihisa Shinagawa, Gerardo Hermosillo Valadez

entry.summary: FD-AA is a lightweight organ-aware classification head for frozen 3D CT encoders that detects incidental abdominal abnormalities visible in routine chest CT. It combines an attenuation-aware module preserving sparse focal evidence with masked generalized-mean pooling for diffuse anomaly patterns across seven abdominal organs. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on CT-RATE and external validation on RAD-ChestCT, improving macro AUC and AP over baselines.

entry.title: Foresight at the Event Boundary: Evaluating Physical Prediction in Video World Models

author.name: Estela Monserrat Arriaga Santana (National Autonomous University of Mexico), Julian Rosas Scull (National Autonomous University of Mexico), Eh\'ecatl Sacamch'en N\'u\~nez Rico (National Autonomous University of Mexico), Hugo Jair Escalante (University of Texas at El Paso)

entry.summary: This work proposes an event-anchored evaluation protocol testing whether video world models can anticipate physical consequences, using 62 controlled real-world free-fall recordings with ground-truth trajectories and fine-grained release/impact annotations. It argues that prior evaluation metrics measure anticipation only indirectly. This matters because physical grounding is a core claim for video world models and rigorous direct testing has been lacking.

entry.title: You Only Reprogram Once: Rethinking Prolonged Training for Visual Reprogramming

author.name: Zizhao Li, Mohammed Yaqoob Ansari, Xinyu Su, Jiayang Ao, Joseph West, Kourosh Khoshelham

entry.summary: YORO shows that strong downstream predictions can be obtained from a frozen pretrained model's full response space without any prompt optimization, constructing the predictor in a single forward-only pass via a covariance-aware Bayesian Discriminant Mapping. This eliminates the hundreds of epochs of training typical in visual reprogramming. It matters as a major efficiency win for parameter-efficient adaptation.

entry.title: Does the VGGT Family Need All Its Layers?

author.name: Fengyi Zhang, Holger Caesar, Xiangyu Sun, Zheng Zhang, Zi Huang, Yadan Luo

entry.summary: The paper performs a large-scale layer-redundancy analysis of feed-forward 3D geometry models (VGGT, pi3, VGGT-Omega), evaluating 3,018 pruned configurations across seven metrics and four datasets. It finds removable layers cluster in an early and a late redundancy region, contradicting the commonly reported middle-to-late redundancy in the literature. This can enable cheaper deployment of feed-forward 3D foundation models and improves understanding of their internals.

entry.title: Seg3DParts: Segmentation-Grounded Controllable Part-Level 3D Generation

author.name: Jiantao Lin, Meixi Chen, Yingjie Xu, Chenbo Fu, Leyi Wu, Hao Chen, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen

entry.summary: Seg3DParts generates controllable part-level 3D assets from a single image by treating segmentation as an explicit grounding signal that anchors each generated component to an image region, ensuring coherent multi-part assembly. This addresses occlusion, ambiguous boundaries, and implicit part-identity inference in prior work. Part-level 3D assets are valuable for editing, reassembly, and interaction in 3D content creation.

entry.title: Back2Struct: Making Structured Images Editable Again

author.name: Pengyu Yan, Yixin Wu, Yunjie Tian, David Doermann

entry.summary: Back2Struct recovers editable object-level SVG/XML vector code from images of diagrams, charts, and flowcharts, enabling researchers and designers to edit rendered graphics without manual reconstruction. It predicts structured code that explicitly encodes text, shapes, and layout.

entry.title: InsightMap: Structured Spatial Modeling for Embodied Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Hongpei Zheng, Hujun Yin

entry.summary: InsightMap uses top-down maps as both explicit spatial memory and action-conditioned prediction targets for language-guided navigation, jointly training navigation action prediction and post-action map generation in a shared multimodal backbone. An aligned RGB-D pipeline supports navigation, VQA, situated reasoning, and 3D grounding under a common interface.

entry.title: Collision-Aware and Observation-Aligned Object-Centric Scene Reconstruction from Point Cloud

author.name: Yuxuan Xie, Xuan Yu, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes COOL, a framework for object-centric scene reconstruction that conditions a generation model on instance and background point clouds to complete partial observations while preserving metric alignment and avoiding collisions. It introduces an explicit collision loss with joint optimization and resampling to reduce collisions during generation.

entry.title: PCaPaint: Prostate Cancer Inpainting by Mitigating Shortcut Learning

author.name: Levente Lippenszky, Hongxu Yang, Marcell D\"om\"ot\"or, Krisztian Koos, L\'aszl\'o Rusk\'o

entry.summary: PCaPaint is a latent-diffusion-based tumor inpainting method for multi-sequence prostate cancer MRI that explicitly mitigates shortcut learning, where models simply reproduce masked lesion regions instead of synthesizing realistic tumor texture. A modified conditioning strategy prevents the condition image from leaking the target output.

entry.title: Visual Anomaly Synthesis for Model Selection in Data Scarcity

author.name: Daniel Pr\"oll, Thomas Kraxner, Tobias Schaefer, Sebastian Hegenbart

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework that synthesizes severity-graded defects on real non-defective industrial images using a literature-derived defect taxonomy distilled into prescriptive prompts and an image generation model, enabling model selection and validation when no defect references exist for an asset. Color-matching and blending improve structural coherence.

entry.title: Targeted Visual Counterfactual Explanations for Contrastive Vision-Language Model

author.name: Van Bach Nguyen, J\"org Schl\"otterer, Christin Seifer

entry.summary: MACE generates targeted visual counterfactual explanations for CLIP zero-shot classification, constructing an editable region from source or source-target attribution differences and expanding the mask only as needed to reach a specified target class, using latent diffusion inpainting guided by frozen CLIP. Unlike saliency methods, it shows how to change an input to obtain a target prediction.

entry.title: The Camera Inside the Editor: Reading the Implicit Camera of Image Editors with Painted Calibration Patterns

author.name: Sebastian R\"uckerl

entry.summary: This solo-authored paper shows that instruction-based image editors reveal their implicit assumed camera by painting projectively consistent structures, measurable via classical vanishing-point geometry on painted checkerboard patterns without training. On 120 rendered cameras, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 paints tile edges accurate to 0.26 degrees and matches ground-truth pitch to 0.8 degrees and focal length to 6 percent.

entry.title: EndoPrior-GS: Dynamic Endoscopic Reconstruction with a Joint Texture Prior

author.name: Jiaqi Huang, Shidong Wang, Tong Xin, Kabita Adhikari

entry.summary: EndoPrior-GS extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to deformable endoscopic scenes by deriving a joint texture prior from tool-filtered tissue masks, non-specular photometric filtering, and anatomical salience to guide primitive initialization and density control. It targets spurious geometry and illumination variation in robotic surgery reconstruction.

entry.title: CLeaR: A Unified Framework for Resolving the Leakage-Degradation Dilemma in Style Transfer

author.name: Teng Zhou, Yunhao Chen

entry.summary: CLeaR addresses content leakage in image style transfer, where objects or semantics from the style reference bleed into the output, and frames a leakage-degradation dilemma across feature separation, grounding, and diffusion generation. It proposes a training-free framework that suppresses leakage without sacrificing style fidelity. The work matters for practical controllable generation with diffusion models.

entry.title: Making Cross-Continental Federated Learning Repeatable with FLIP: a Multi-Application Study

author.name: Rafael Garcia-Dias, Alexandre Triay Bagur, Chayanin Tangwiriyasakul, Virginia Fernandez, Parhom Esmaeili, Piyalitt Ittichaiwong, Yang Li, Lawrence Adams, Wason Buncharoen, Martin Chapman, Benjamaporn Chayanond, Sadthavud Chunrod, Tanawat Fongsri, Kass Gibson, Supat Plungprasertkul, Supawit Tangpanithandee, Kanyakorn Veerakanjana, Vicky Goh, Michela Antonelli, Joe Zhang, Kongkiat Kespechara, Sebastien Ourselin, M. Jorge Cardoso

entry.summary: FLIP is an open-source federated learning interoperability platform that makes healthcare FL training and evaluation repeatable through composable services: per-site cohort queries, on-demand DICOM retrieval from PACS, project approval workflows, and reusable FL job types. It was demonstrated with federated fine-tuning and evaluation on synthetic chest X-ray cohorts across nodes in the UK and Thailand. It addresses the governance overhead that stalls healthcare FL at proof-of-concept.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Classifier Systems as Universal Approximators

author.name: Hiroki Shiraishi, Hisao Ishibuchi, Masaya Nakata

entry.summary: This paper addresses the exponential scalability bottleneck of rule-based machine learning (Learning Classifier Systems) by reorganizing rules dimension-wise using the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem. The proposed KACS decomposes target functions into superpositions of one-dimensional functions, providing universal approximation with far better scaling in input dimension than traditional rule-partitioning approaches.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation of Manipulation Policies Under Actuator Degradation

author.name: Som Sagar, Ransalu Senanayake

entry.summary: The paper introduces TeAR, a policy-agnostic method that converts frozen manipulation policies into telemetry-conditioned policies that adapt to actuator degradation such as motor heating, current saturation, and voltage sag. It repurposes onboard telemetry already collected for logging or safety checks as a signal for action rectification at test time.

entry.title: EquivDP3: A SIM(3)-Invariant Point-Cloud Encoder for Data-Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Abu Hanif Muhammad Syarubany, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: EquivDP3 extends SIM(3)-equivariant point-cloud encoders from wheeled manipulators to the 43-joint Unitree G1 humanoid, combining a diffusion planner with equivariant vector neuron features for whole-body loco-manipulation. The two-stage design targets generalization across object poses and lighting from few demonstrations. It matters because data efficiency for humanoid manipulation is a core obstacle to real-world deployment.

entry.title: Foundation-Model-Guided Topology-Aware Semantic Risk Fields for Manipulation

author.name: Giung Lee, Weihang Guo, Lydia E. Kavraki

entry.summary: This paper constructs dense 3D semantic risk fields for manipulation by combining foundation-model priors (directional risk weights and spatial decay per object pair) with voxelized geometry using topology-aware shielding and geodesic decay, computed with a GPU-parallel backend. The resulting field acts as a modular cost for downstream motion planning, extending manipulation safety beyond pure collision avoidance. This bridges semantic commonsense reasoning and classical planning in a computationally practical way.

entry.title: Beyond Token Importance: Preserving Spatial Scaffolds for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference

author.name: Jiayu Chen, Shuyong Gao, Jingkai Jia, Xiaosheng Bu, Jiyuan Fu, Lingyi Hong, Kaixun Jiang, Yipan Xu, Wenqiang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper shows that visual token pruning for VLA models based on semantic relevance neglects spatial coverage: a simple uniform Stride baseline can beat semantic pruning at certain ratios, yet collapses when the token budget shrinks slightly. The authors characterize pruning quality via a spatial coverage radius (largest induced blind spot) and correlate it with performance. This provides a better principle for efficient VLA inference, where real-time speed matters.

entry.title: Recovering the View: Benchmarking Physical Active Vision for Occlusion Recovery in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Kaijun Luo, Yudi Huang, Qijun Zhong, Xinshuai Song, Yang Liu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: The paper introduces BAVO-Bench, a bimanual active-vision benchmark with controlled Clean, Stage Occlusion, and Random-time Occlusion conditions, plus A-FAR, a policy for joint viewpoint and manipulation control. It enables systematic study of how manipulation policies recover from occlusion by actively moving cameras during execution.

entry.title: Surgical Master Console Using General-Purpose Robot Arms and a Separable Articulated Distal Interface: Porcine In-Vivo Evaluation

author.name: Minsung Kim, Seonho Shim, Dongho Yee, Younghoon Noh, Juahn Oh, Yechan Seo, Jinseok Lee, Jiyul Lee, Seong Jeong, Hyuk Choi, Youngbin Kong, Hyoun-Joong Kong

entry.summary: The authors build a low-cost laparoscopic surgical master console from general-purpose robot arms with a custom separable distal adapter providing wrist articulation, continuous grasp sensing, and clutch-based workspace management, at roughly $5,500 total. The system is validated in porcine in-vivo evaluation, characterizing scaling, gravity compensation, and sustained hand-guided use.

entry.title: Geometry-Preserving Human-to-Robot Upper-Body Motion Retargeting from Monocular Video

author.name: Xiaoyu Yang, Sen Han, Da Li, Nan Wu

entry.summary: The paper presents a geometry-preserving retargeting framework that transfers upper-body and hand motion from monocular RGB video to robots, jointly constraining body estimates, video-level observations, and hand evidence within a differentiable Momentum Human Rig state. It addresses scale mismatches, kinematic differences, and preservation of fine distal (hand) motion across embodiments.

entry.title: Comparing Utility of Inertial, Occupancy, Semantic, and Intent Information in Human Motion Prediction During Daily Tasks

author.name: Max Burns, Maisha Khanum, Monroe Kennedy III, Steven H. Collins

entry.summary: This study uses a human motion diffusion model to quantify which information sources (body motion, scene, eye gaze, semantics, intent) most improve indoor human motion prediction, using a new dataset collected with Meta Aria glasses across ten campus buildings. They report a 42 percent improvement over a constant velocity baseline and show gaze and scene data significantly reduce error. The work is valuable for robot planners that need reliable human motion forecasts in shared indoor spaces.

entry.title: Post-Anomaly Detection Inference for Deep SVDD

author.name: Cao Le Cong Thanh, Dang Quang Vinh, Vo Nguyen Le Duy

entry.summary: PADI equips a trained and frozen Deep SVDD anomaly detector with statistically valid inference via the selective inference framework, providing p-values for flagged anomalies rather than relying on raw anomaly scores alone. This addresses the lack of false-positive control that limits deep anomaly detection in safety-critical and high-stakes applications. The framework works post hoc on existing detectors, which eases adoption.

entry.title: Copula Active Subspaces I: A Score-Covariance Method for Reduced-Order Non-Gaussian Density Estimation

author.name: Joshua Chen, Peter Jan van Leeuwen

entry.summary: Introduces Copula Active Subspaces, a rank-reduction method for non-Gaussian noise densities in Bayesian inference that isolates dependence in the copula and keeps only leading eigenvectors of the copula score covariance. This makes density and gradient evaluations pointwise cheap for gradient-based samplers without inner solves.

entry.title: GNA: Granular Neighbor Assembly for Retrieval-Augmented Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Vincent Uhse

entry.summary: GNA is a retrieval-augmentation layer for time-series forecasting backbones that addresses the limitation of fixed-length lookback windows in multivariate forecasting. It assembles retrieved neighbors at two granularities — whole past windows for cross-variate coherence and per-variate neighbors for individually best-matching continuations — with a learned gate balancing the two per forecast step and variate. This offers a mechanism to sidestep the diminishing returns of simply lengthening context windows.

entry.title: When Is Coarse Supervision Worth It? Cost-Aware Learning under Unknown Aggregation

author.name: Jianyu Xu, Smriti Jha, Aarti Singh, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: Studies two-resolution learning where fine labels reveal a full vector response but cheap coarse labels reveal a scalar aggregate with unknown weights. The paper characterizes the information geometry of this trade-off, derives a closed-form break-even condition for when coarse supervision pays off, and proposes an estimate-and-track policy for the optimal resolution mix.

entry.title: Search Dimension in Unlabeled Projection Pursuit: A Scaling Law for Subspace Restriction

author.name: Rares Dimitrie Grozavescu, Mark Girolami

entry.summary: The paper shows that projection pursuit searches over high-dimensional spaces with large Gaussian complements can return signal-free directions that empirically minimize the objective, and that sample splitting exposes rather than fixes this failure. The authors derive scaling laws for how restricting the search to a known forward operator's column space or an estimated principal subspace repairs the problem. This quantifies when dimensionality reduction is necessary for unsupervised structure searches.

entry.title: An Alternative to Fully-Aligned Swarms

author.name: Jackson Mowatt Gok

entry.summary: Responding to Noam Brown's comments that OpenAI continues to pursue multi-agent swarms fully aligned with each other, the author argues this is dangerous and proposes agents that cooperate by default but side with the human when a peer acts against them. A small experiment shows a multi-agent-trained model that falsified results for a teammate 41.5 percent of the time was fixed by light fine-tuning on one deception type, generalizing to an untrained deception type without harming teamwork. This is an empirical counterpoint to a frontier lab design choice.

entry.title: “China needs more AI safety.” More of what, exactly?

author.name: Yulu Pi

entry.summary: The author, drawing on recent conversations in China, disambiguates what more AI safety in China could mean: state regulation (where China already has a comprehensive algorithm registration regime), in-company safety work, research, or expert channels. They note a very recent CAC official remark identifying extreme loss-of-control as an emerging risk, and ask whether recognition will translate into concrete requirements. This is the first in a planned series.

entry.title: AI Companies Are Not (Necessarily) Liable for Unintended AI Cyberattacks

author.name: sarahconstantin

entry.summary: A legal analysis examining whether AI companies face civil or criminal liability under US law when their agents commit unintended cyberattacks (such as the recent OpenAI agent incidents involving Hugging Face and government systems). The author argues that because CFAA provisions require intentional or knowing conduct, careless deployment may not satisfy the mental-state elements. The research was done with Claude and the author invites expert correction.

entry.title: Better Nearest Neighbor Graph Indices via (Efficient) LLM-Guided Pruning

author.name: Fangzhou Wu, Haike Xu, Sandeep Silwal

entry.summary: The paper addresses a geometry-semantic mismatch in graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search: indices are built on embedding geometry but evaluated on semantic relevance. It proposes pruning nearest neighbor graph indices at construction time using LLM guidance, rather than relying solely on query-time LLM reranking. This is a novel integration of LLM signals into the structural layer of retrieval infrastructure.

entry.title: Rethinking Reasoning Paths as Phase-Structured Trajectories

author.name: Zhenghao He, Guangzhi Xiong, Sanchit Sinha, Bohan Liu, Wenqian Ye, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper critiques standard probing protocols that assign final-answer correctness labels to all intermediate states along LLM reasoning paths, arguing this conflates question-level variation with path quality. It proposes viewing reasoning paths as phase-structured trajectories within fixed questions and instantiates this as PAIR, a phase-aligned analysis method. This provides a sharper lens on reasoning dynamics with implications for interpretability and process-based supervision.

entry.title: FineSID: Scalable and Efficient Semantic Identifier Learning for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Song-Li Wu, Weinan Gan, Zhaocheng Du, Xianquan Wang, Jingyi Wang

entry.summary: FineSID targets the sparse-gradient bottleneck in semantic identifier (SID) learning for generative recommendation, where Top-1 hard assignment in vector quantization concentrates gradients on frequently used codewords and causes SID collisions. The method relaxes hard assignment to improve gradient propagation, improving codebook coverage without heuristic collision resolution that disrupts end-to-end semantic alignment. It scales to large item sets efficiently.

entry.title: Beyond Sub-Gaussian Detector Scores: Robust Weighted Profile-Loss Change Point Detection for Human-LLM Text Segmentation

author.name: Wan Tian, Zhongyi Li, Yawen Li, Rui Zhang, Yijie Peng, Fuzhen Zhuang

entry.summary: RWCP is a robust method for locating human-LLM authorship transitions in mixed documents, combining capped reliability weights, Huber profile gains, and narrowest-over-threshold search over detector scores. It expresses the population gap between true and displaced splits as a merge cost, with guarantees under curvature, spacing, and dependence conditions.

entry.title: V-Engram: Trigger-Indexed External Memory for Modular Text-to-Image Personalization

author.name: Haoran He, Runyuan Cai, Yiming Wang, Lin Yu, Xiaodong Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces V-Engram, a trigger-indexed external memory for Stable Diffusion 3.5 personalization where each concept gets an explicit trigger retrieving concept-specific memory that enters frozen text-encoder and MMDiT states as gated residuals. This avoids costly persistent weight updates and interference when composing multiple personalized concepts.

entry.title: KUPAS MASTER: Distilling the Tacit Expertise of Master Practitioners into Agent-Ready Experience Corpora

author.name: Changmian Wang, Yuchao Ma, Xuchao Lu, Chen Zhang, Ping Sun, Jiazheng Wang, Shan Wang, Xuanwen Chen, Yihe Sun, Ziyu Lu, Jianqiang Huang, Hongzhi Li, Ziqing Xia, Kaihua Tang, Xian-Sheng Hua, Qinghua Zheng

entry.summary: KUPAS MASTER is an experience-engineering platform that converts heterogeneous work records and practitioner interviews into traceable, agent-usable experience corpora, using six case elements (context, cues, judgment, action, boundaries, outcomes) and a nine-layer cognitive corpus construction to capture tacit professional knowledge that routine records omit.

entry.title: The Detectability Gap: Hidden Heterogeneity in Hallucination Detection Across Language Models

author.name: Pranav Darshan, Pranav A, Sravan Karthick T, Minal Moharir, Ivan P. Yamshchikov

entry.summary: Studying sampling-based consistency for hallucination detection across four LLMs and three QA datasets, the paper identifies high-agreement (Ghost) and low-agreement (Flickering) hallucination regimes with a 0.35-0.46 AUC detectability gap. Notably, the authors candidly treat the raw gap cautiously because the defining statistics are strongly coupled, and instead analyze lexical and semantic response diversity after freezing regime assignments.

entry.title: Factorized Scheduling Principle: Learning Interpretable and Transferable Policies via Structured Additive Functions

author.name: Hong Je-Gal, Hyun-Suk Lee

entry.summary: The FSP framework learns interpretable and transferable scheduling rules by representing system states as condition distributions and decomposing a global scheduling principle into additive univariate and pairwise components with identifiability constraints. It combines a policy-based objective with a temporal-difference signal while preserving a simple priority-based structure at deployment. This targets scheduling problems reducible to priority scoring over candidates.

entry.title: UniAfford: Token-Routed Multitask Learning for Generalizable 2D-3D Affordance Perception

author.name: Yuhao Liu, Yiming Zhong, Hanqing Wang, Shaocheng Yan, Yuhang Zhang, Wenzhou Lyu, Ziyang Ding, Wei Zhang, Xue Zhao, Jin Pan, Yuexin Ma, Xinge Zhu

entry.summary: UniAfford unifies 2D and 3D affordance grounding, which have historically evolved as separate problems with different supervision and evaluation protocols. Its Token Router for Tasks routes MLLM contextual hidden states to task-specific branches without requiring special language markers, letting dense prediction losses shape shared representations. This improves transferable object-affordance semantics across visual and geometric spaces.

entry.title: Credit-Guided Policy Improvement for Test-time Adaptive Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yang Li, Sijia Zhang, Yihan Li, Aming WU, Zihao Zhang, Ziju Han, Yahong Han

entry.summary: The paper tackles test-time adaptation for vision-language navigation by identifying which executed actions genuinely support instruction-guided progress toward the goal, then using credit-guided signals for reliable policy updates. Existing uncertainty or trajectory-level feedback signals do not directly indicate goal-directed progress, and plausible corrections can yield unreliable updates. The method improves online adaptation to unseen environments.

entry.title: "Where Can I Trust You?": Boundary-Aware Evaluation of Surrogate Fidelity

author.name: Jackson Eshbaugh

entry.summary: This single-author paper shows that surrogate model fidelity to a teacher is systematically lower near the teacher's decision boundary, using two methods to identify near-boundary examples across multiple datasets and surrogate classes. Conditioning agreement on confidence-defined regions improves prediction of teacher-surrogate agreement when evaluation-set composition changes, arguing that boundary-aware fidelity metrics carry information beyond a single global score. This has direct implications for how distilled or surrogate models are evaluated and trusted.

entry.title: When the Merge Coefficient Stops Mattering: Proximity Regularized Merging for Continual LoRA Adaptation

author.name: Yixuan Liu, Yuhao Sun, Sen Song, Jin Li

entry.summary: Introduces Proximity Regularized Merging (PRM), a minimal modification to sequential LoRA merging for rehearsal-free continual learning that adds a proximal penalty during task-vector training without changing the merge rule. The regularization improves metrics across multiple write-in rules, backbones, and class-incremental settings, with mechanistic analysis via norm controls.

entry.title: HoTS: Homophily-Aware Temperature Scaling for Graph Neural Network Calibration

author.name: Inwoo Tae, Yoontae Hwang, Yongjae Lee

entry.summary: Shows that global or logit-only temperature scaling is insufficient for GNN calibration because nodes with identical logits but different local homophily need different temperatures, and proposes homophily-aware node-level temperature scaling. Analysis under a contextual stochastic block model with a linear GCN derives the principled structural form.

entry.title: CAESAR: Clustering via Autonomous Embedding-Space Agglomerative Reorganization

author.name: Ilan Bacry, R\'emi Devaux, Antoine Jardin

entry.summary: CAESAR retrains a reorganization network on pretrained vision/language embeddings, pulling mutual nearest neighbors together and pushing non-neighbors apart, producing spaces much better suited to graph-based clustering methods like FINCH. Notably, it discovers the number of clusters K automatically rather than requiring it as input. This addresses a realistic limitation of clustering on foundation-model embeddings in unsupervised settings.

entry.title: SIFT: Enhancing Time Series Foundation Models via Semantic Invariance and Structural Fidelity Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yi Tang, Tengxue Zhang, Yang Shu, Chenjuan Guo, Chenchen Sun, Yisheng An

entry.summary: SIFT is a fine-tuning method for time series foundation models that combats overfitting and the mean-prediction trap using semantic-invariant adversarial augmentation based on semantic spectrum decomposition, alongside structural fidelity preservation. It addresses the challenge that naive fine-tuning degrades TSFM zero-shot capabilities. This contributes to reliable adaptation of foundation models in the time series domain.

entry.title: Robust Bayesian Optimization with Q-Exponential Surrogates

author.name: Richard Cornelius Suwandi, Zhidi Lin, Feng Yin, Abdelhak M. Zoubir

entry.summary: q-ED-BO replaces Gaussian process surrogates in Bayesian optimization with a q-exponential distribution surrogate that retains closed-form posterior updates and adds a tunable tail parameter, recovering the GP at q=2 and heavier tails otherwise. It yields closed-form q-UCB and q-EI acquisition functions with sublinear regret, robust to outliers and heavy-tailed noise. This is a clean theoretical and practical extension of standard BO.

entry.title: Staying on the Attractor: Supervising Neural Surrogates of 3D Turbulence Where They Leave It

author.name: Yilong Dai, Shaswata Mitra, Raj Patel, Yiming Sun, Shengyu Chen, Jiaqi Gong, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi, Xiaowei Jia, Runlong Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes off-attractor supervision (OAS) for neural surrogates of 3D turbulent flows, teaching the model true Navier-Stokes evolution from off-attractor states where errors would otherwise amplify into blow-up or statistical drift. This targets long-term stability of chaotic flow surrogates.

entry.title: Efficient Dynamic Algorithms for Graph Neural Networks with Non-Linear Propagation

author.name: Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Silvio Lattanzi, Danny Mittal

entry.summary: The paper develops residual-based dynamic algorithms that efficiently maintain node representations for non-linear GNN propagation under edge insertions and deletions, extending beyond prior work restricted to linear Personalized PageRank propagation. The propagation is parameter-free with only a trained classifier applied afterward.

entry.title: Clipped or Unclipped? Finite-Sample Trade-offs for Averaged SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Alexandra Suvorikova, Egor Gladin, Darina Dvinskikh, Artem Agafonov, Mohammad Alkousa, Yuriy Dorn, Vladislav Matyukhin, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: The paper derives finite-sample comparisons of clipped versus unclipped Polyak-Ruppert averaged SGD under finite conditional p-th moments, showing that for p>2 the Gaussian term dominates so clipping need not improve the leading bound. It balances clipping bias and concentration to obtain a heavy-tail correction with logarithmic rather than polynomial dependence on the inverse failure probability.

entry.title: Downstream-Aware Context Selection for Online In-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ruihan A. Li, Shangtong Zhang, Rohan Chandra

entry.summary: The authors propose a bounded-history context-management framework for in-context RL that predicts the task-dependent downstream effect of removing historical interactions to guide history selection and set a decision-dependent context budget. This reduces token costs from conditioning on ever-growing interaction histories without parameter updates.

entry.title: Feedback-Robust AI for Patient Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Mohammed Sameer Syed

entry.summary: The paper introduces ClosedLoopBench, a benchmark of 29 signed physiological relations evaluated on 3,442 VitalDB surgical cases with negative-control action streams, testing whether causal estimators can distinguish true patient physiology from clinician policy feedback in intensive care data. Results show many estimators declare spurious relations significant even after calibration.

entry.title: SchemaMem: Schema-Indexed Recurrent Memory for Delayed State Retrieval

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: SchemaMem is an attention-based recurrent memory architecture combining chunk-local attention with a persistent schema-indexed phase state, where learned schema embeddings mediate reads and writes and chunk-boundary commits aggregate bounded phase increments. It aims to bound memory while preserving information for delayed retrieval, with the same parameters supporting full-history access.

entry.title: Predicting Block-Coordinate Performance via Cross-Curvature

author.name: Shengkun Zhu, Jinshan Zeng, Zhiqiang Kou, Yongxin Tong, Yang Liu

entry.summary: The authors develop a unified theory comparing Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, and partially sequential block-gradient updates, expressing one-step loss differences via cross-block curvature with O(eta^3) remainder and signed K-step comparisons. This predicts when simultaneous versus sequential updates are preferable based on objective geometry and iteration count, relevant to training, federated learning, and LoRA.

entry.title: Hierarchical Response Preservation for Continual Adaptation of Zero-Shot Graph-Text Models

author.name: Haopeng Zhang, Yuhan Wang, Yubing Su, Yingxin Chen, Xiao Wang, Ruijie Wang, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: HiRP tackles continual learning for pretrained graph-text models, balancing learning of new classes against retention of zero-shot transfer and historical knowledge via a hierarchical response structure. It addresses the problem that new classes can overturn historical predictions while strict preservation stalls new-class learning.

entry.title: Task-Aware Discretization of Differentiable Logic Gate Networks

author.name: Thore Gerlach

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard local discretization of differentiable logic gate networks (argmax or confidence-based) can be task-suboptimal even for globally optimal relaxed solutions, and derives bounds relating task-aware gate selection to tractable interventions. It then studies first-order downstream task information for progressive discretization. This improves the quality of highly efficient Boolean networks produced by gradient-based training.

entry.title: Do World Models Learn Global Understanding?

author.name: Alexander Detkov, Matt Thomson

entry.summary: The paper formalizes understanding as learning constraints and propagating their consequences, constructing learning tasks on monoid worlds where observed transitions plus an unseen constraint determine held-out transitions. This provides a controlled probe of whether models can lift local information into global understanding, addressing brittleness in LLMs.

entry.title: WorldGraph: Graph-Native World Modeling

author.name: Zezhong Ding, Yipeng Li, Xike Xie

entry.summary: This paper formulates graph world modeling, where the evolving graph itself constitutes the world dynamics rather than merely organizing internal states. It builds GWM-Z, a benchmark covering observed graph evolution, latent graph states, and heterogeneous transition prediction, establishing a new problem framing for relational environments.

entry.title: CasEm: A Cascade Architecture for Long-Horizon Neural Emulation

author.name: Zhaoyi Li, Jingtao Ding, Shihua Li

entry.summary: CasEm augments autoregressive neural emulators with an independently evolving model of physically specified aggregates whose forecasts correct full-state predictions without feedback, reducing rollout drift and divergence. It derives a finite-horizon error bound identifying three factors for effective guidance and demonstrates reductions across four ODE/PDE benchmarks.

entry.title: When Less Data Favors Smaller Teachers: Rethinking Teacher Capacity and Data Selection for Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Minjae Park, Taesun Yeom, Jaeho Lee

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why smaller teacher models can outperform larger ones in knowledge distillation when the data budget is limited, decomposing teacher supervision into relational ordering (class ranking) and score geometry (probability magnitudes and margins). It shows both factors drive the small-teacher advantage and derives actionable criteria for teacher selection and sample selection under data pruning. This offers practical guidance for cost-effective distillation pipelines.

entry.title: Gaussian Neural Networks

author.name: Peter Kuhn, Victoria Heusinger-He{\ss}

entry.summary: Gaussian neural networks (GaNNs) introduce a novel regularization mechanism by placing priors over activation space rather than weight space: activities from earlier layers are treated as Gaussian noise-corrupted signals, with an unsupervised loss predicting the noise properties. The penalty on surprising activations is claimed to outperform standard networks. A conceptually fresh take on regularization.

entry.title: THEIA: A Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Vision-Language Analysis of Layout

author.name: Giuseppe Chiari, Michele Piccoli, Federico Viola, Davide Zoni

entry.summary: THEIA provides a dataset of thousands of analog IC layout images paired with question-answer conversations, plus a benchmark using a fine-tuned vision-language model to analyze GDSII layout data. It enables multimodal AI research in electronic design automation.

entry.title: ProtoSeam: Lifting Classifier Training with Latent Gaussian Mixture Models

author.name: Robert Lampel, Timon Klein, Sebastian Sager

entry.summary: ProtoSeam splits a classifier at a semantic interface, inserting learnable class prototypes during training with a quadratic consensus penalty and no cross-interface gradients; prototypes are discarded at inference so the architecture is unchanged. Lifted training improves test accuracy across CIFAR-10/100 and TinyImageNet with ResNet and ViT backbones.

entry.title: Latency and accuracy tradeoffs in Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Zhanglu Yan, Zixuan Zhu, Kaiwen Tang, Yuyang Cai, Qianhui Liu, Weng-Fai Wong

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that SNNs are inherently slower than quantized networks, showing timestep-level computation overlap across layers can reduce latency below comparable bit-serial QNNs. It then analyzes the accuracy cost of spiking on incomplete inputs, formalizing the latency-accuracy tradeoff.

entry.title: An analysis of Mirror-Descent Soft Actor-Critic

author.name: Denis Zorba, Michal Valko

entry.summary: This paper proves finite-time convergence guarantees for Soft Actor-Critic when the target policy comes from policy mirror descent rather than the classical Gibbs target, deriving conditions on Q-function curvature for strong convexity and smoothness. It establishes an O(N^(-1/5)) best-iterate convergence rate up to actor and critic approximation errors.

entry.title: Learning the Robustness Mechanism with Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Yiyang Shen, Qihang Lin, Weiran Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning distributionally robust optimization's robustness parameters from held-out data via bilevel minimax optimization, with instances for settings with and without group labels. It provides sample complexity guarantees matching exhaustive grid search while being more computationally efficient, and evaluates under simultaneous intra- and inter-group distribution shift.

entry.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution

author.name: Chaoqian Ouyang, Ling Yue, Libin Zheng, Hanghui Guo, Shengxiang Xu, YiShu Wang, Ran Li, Jian Yin, Shaowu Pan, Shimin Di

entry.summary: TokenCast predicts token consumption of LLM agent tasks, which can vary by over an order of magnitude across runs, by learning a composable per-segment cost representation capturing its own consumption and induced context growth. Composing adjacent segments yields cumulative estimates that revise online as the run unfolds, addressing a practical cost-prediction gap for agent deployment.

entry.title: A Unified Optimism-Agnostic Framework for Linear Bandits over Spherical Action Sets

author.name: Arda G\"u\c{c}l\"u, Subhonmesh Bose, John R. Birge

entry.summary: The paper develops a unified framework for linear bandits covering both UCB and Thompson sampling over spherical action sets, showing that if the minimum eigenvalue of the design matrix grows on the order of sqrt(t), favorable estimation conditions hold. It provides optimism-agnostic regret guarantees connecting exploration quality to performance.

entry.title: Active Data Acquisition with Side Information via Discrete Diffusion Priors

author.name: An Vuong, Thinh Nguyen

entry.summary: This work frames active data acquisition as maximizing mutual information between an image and its partial observation under a budget, using a mask policy conditioned on side information. A frozen discrete denoising diffusion model (D3PM) supplies the posterior, enabling acquisition decisions relevant to broad task sets rather than a single downstream model.

entry.title: Neural ODEs Meet Concurrent Learning: Stable Online Learning with Lyapunov Guarantees

author.name: Omkar Sudhir Patil

entry.summary: This paper proves that the adjoint gradient of Neural ODEs decomposes into a positive semi-definite trajectory operator on parameter error plus a bounded perturbation, enabling Lyapunov-based stability certificates for online Neural ODE training over sliding windows. The certificate extends to concurrent learning on stored data under computable gain and horizon conditions.

entry.title: LocalProp: Neuro-Localized Memory-Efficient Backpropagation

author.name: Diana-Nicoleta Grigore, Iuliana Georgescu, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: LocalProp proposes a training procedure with localized weight updates following a pre-training (I-JEPA-based) then fine-tuning paradigm, with an intermediate pruning step that helps route learning signals from higher to lower blocks. It motivates the approach by biological plausibility and memory efficiency, avoiding backpropagation through the entire model. This contributes to the growing research area on alternatives to end-to-end backpropagation.

entry.title: Affine Geometry of Gaussian ReLU Networks via Conditional Kac-Rice Formulas

author.name: Recep \"Ozkan, Christian Hirsch

entry.summary: The paper derives exact finite-width conditional Kac-Rice formulas for the expected number of activation switches along input intervals in randomly initialized ReLU networks, showing convergence to deterministic limits at proportional width, and characterizes how supervised training reorganizes the network's piecewise-affine geometry.

entry.title: Domain-Adapted Diffusion Models for Conditional Independence Testing

author.name: Yanfeng Yang, Junda Zhao, Yijie Gao, Jiaqi Yang, Xinyu Shi, Ziqi Chen, Shunyu Zhao, Shuai Li, Wei Huang, Eshant English, Kenji Fukumizu

entry.summary: This work reformulates conditional generative modeling for conditional independence testing as a domain adaptation problem, leveraging auxiliary source-domain data to improve target-domain estimation and proposing DA-Diff, a multi-source diffusion approach. This addresses the accumulation of estimation errors in existing Type I error bounds for generative CI tests.

entry.title: Reliable Replay through Spatial Coherence in Online Continual Learning

author.name: Haixiang Sun, Jiefu Zhang, Yinghao He, Yang Xu, Vaneet Aggarwal, Bharat Bhargava, Andrew L. Liu

entry.summary: SPHERE improves experience replay in continual learning by aggregating signed prospective loss changes through a representation kernel, suppressing incoherent loss spikes and allocating memory via entropy-regularized transport toward supported high-risk regions. It generalizes loss-priority replay across broad learning settings.

entry.title: Controlling Speaking Rate in Autoregressive TTS via Activation Steering

author.name: Francesco Verdini, Antonis Asonitis, Aref Farhadipour, Marzieh Razavi, Pierre-Edouard Honnet, Vijeta Avijeet, Juan Pablo Zuluaga Gomez

entry.summary: The paper shows speaking rate in autoregressive TTS can be controlled at inference without retraining by clamping one decoder block's activation along a discovered speed axis, learned from synthetically time-stretched and compressed speech. The steering preserves speaker identity, generalizes across architectures, and maintains naturalness in human evaluations.

entry.title: Adapting neural operators for mechanics decisions under changing operating conditions

author.name: Prashant K. Jha, Koffi Enakoutsa, Ian Galloway, Henry Anderson

entry.summary: This work studies adapting neural operators for nonlinear mechanics calculations when operating conditions drift beyond the training range, using hard-magnetic soft-material systems simulated with high-fidelity finite-element models as testbeds. An empirical error estimator decides which surrogate predictions can be trusted for command selection, and selected FE evaluations are reused to adapt the operator online. This is a practical recipe for safe surrogate-assisted decision making in engineering.

entry.title: SeLMRoute: Probabilistic Semantic Evidence for Large Language Model Routing

author.name: Vasilis Perifanis, Nikolaos Pavlidis, Symeon Symeonidis

entry.summary: SeLMRoute is an LLM routing framework that separates extraction of candidate-independent semantic evidence (interpretable questions about a query's reasoning needs and knowledge requirements) from learning of candidate model performance and deployment objectives. Unlike routers that learn directly from embeddings or preference data, it produces interpretable probabilistic judgments about what each query requires. This grounds routing decisions in stated query characteristics rather than opaque representations.

entry.title: Recommendation Ranking Off-Policy Evaluation under Ranking-Dependent Examination via Examination-Relevance Decomposition

author.name: Riki Okamura, Toshiharu Sugawara

entry.summary: The authors propose two off-policy evaluation estimators for recommender rankings that decompose clicks into examination and relevance, correcting bias when logged clicks cannot distinguish unexamined items from examined non-clicks. LE-IIPS corrects IIPS bias using examination probability ratios, and ED-DR extends this to a doubly robust framework with stated unbiasedness conditions. This addresses a fundamental ambiguity in logged recommendation data.

entry.title: From internal representations to model improvement through prediction errors

author.name: Yushi Nakaya, Kenichi Higuchi, Shuichi Ishida

entry.summary: The paper proposes selecting images for labeling and retraining using the target model's own internal features linked to prediction errors and their expected performance impact, rather than features from separately trained models or VLM scene descriptions. Because the target model's representations evolve with retraining, they naturally reflect what it has learned. This enables label-efficient active learning without labels for selection.

entry.title: Learned Preconditioning for a Primal-Dual Interior-Point Method

author.name: Abhinav Madabhushi, Jialin Liu, Minxin Zhang

entry.summary: pdLIP integrates learned preconditioning with an all-shifted primal-dual projected-search interior-point method for smooth nonlinear programs, using a coordinate-wise recurrent network to predict a positive diagonal preconditioner. The work tackles the difficulty that logarithmic barrier singularities make IPMs sensitive to perturbation, complicating learning. It contributes to the learning-to-optimize line of research with potential speedups for constrained optimization.

entry.title: Focusing Condition: Inference-Time Self-Contrastive Steering Elicits Better Conditional Text Embeddings in LLMs

author.name: Zifeng Cheng, Lingyun Qian, Zhiwei Jiang, Cong Wang, Yafeng Yin, Fei Shen, Ao Zhou, Qing Gu

entry.summary: This paper proposes Self-Contrastive Steering (SCS), an inference-time, plug-and-play method that constructs unconditional general text embeddings and uses them to refine conditional embeddings extracted from LLMs. By subtracting general content, the conditional embeddings become more focused on the target condition without additional data or fine-tuning. This improves the quality of prompt-conditioned representations.

entry.title: NLPG: Natural-Language Policy Gradients for Self-Evolving Language Agents

author.name: Xu Liu, WenZhang Wei, Jun Cao, Dehua Peng, Huan Chen, Zhipeng Gui, Huayi Wu

entry.summary: NLPG is an external policy-memory method that improves a fixed LLM agent without changing parameters or program structure by diagnosing execution traces, propagating feedback backward through the module graph, and converting recurring failures into reusable natural-language policy updates. It targets compound agent programs where failures stem from local procedural decisions. This addresses a practical gap between prompt optimization and RL for agents.

entry.title: The Effects of Incremental Instruction Delivery on Language-Model Creative Writing

author.name: Anshuman Singh, Abrar Eyasir, Haseeb Yaqoob, John Manavalan

entry.summary: Studiea whether progressive, multi-turn delivery of creative-writing requirements harms outputs beyond what explicit requirement checks capture, using 160 human-authored tasks across six genres and six open-weight model families to form 960 matched pairs. Progressive delivery is found to reduce something measured (the abstract cuts off, but explicit constraint satisfaction is implied to drop). It extends multi-turn instruction-degradation findings into the creative domain where quality is not objectively verifiable.

entry.title: From Normative Frameworks to Alignment Data: Constructing and Evaluating SFT and Preference Data

author.name: Husrev Taha Sencar, Rezart Beka, Danish Naeem, Seda Ozalkan, Majd Hawasly, Ji Lucas, Ala AlFuqaha, Mohamed Abdallah, Recep Senturk

entry.summary: Presents an expert-driven, year-long methodology for translating an abstract normative framework, grounded in Islamic ethical and jurisprudential traditions, into SFT and preference data: roughly 2.8K SFT examples and 5.4K preference pairs in Arabic and English. It demonstrates a generalizable path from abstract principles to alignment training data.

entry.title: QuanReview: Offline, Auditable Reconciliation of Human and LLM Span Annotations

author.name: Matteo Musacchio, Juan Cruz Giner Pulero, Isabel Casta\~neda, Naomi Couriel, Yelena Mejova, Mariano G. Beir\'o, Kyriaki Kalimeri

entry.summary: QuanReview is an open-source system for auditing and reconciling structured span annotations from human and LLM annotators, aligning annotation streams at character level, resolving unambiguous cases via logged policies, and routing conflicts to a browser-based adjudication interface with configurable redundancy and agreement computation. It addresses the growing trust problem as LLMs enter annotation pipelines. This is practical data-quality infrastructure for AI-assisted dataset creation.

entry.title: MetaBench-Harness: Unlocking End-to-End Optimization of Benchmark Harnesses

author.name: Xuanjun Chen, Hua-Hsuan Chen, Wei-Chung Lu, Yinghao Ma, Jyh-Shing Roger Jang, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Proposes MetaBench-Harness, a dual-loop search framework where an inner loop generates new benchmarks via a harness and an outer meta-harness iteratively refines the harness implementations themselves using historical evolution trajectories. This moves beyond hard-coded perturbation rules for creating harder benchmarks as static suites saturate.

entry.title: Less Supervision, Better Generalization: Weakly Supervised Fake Region Localization in Diffusion-Edited Images

author.name: Junhee Lee, Donghyeon Jeon, Taeoh Kim, Beomyoung Kim, MyeongAh Cho

entry.summary: ReGFLoW is the first weakly supervised framework for localizing AI-edited regions in diffusion-edited images, using reconstruction guidance instead of pixel-level supervision from controlled editing pipelines. It argues that pixel supervision introduces misleading signals because artifacts extend beyond annotated regions while out-of-mask pixels are treated as authentic. Better generalization across generators matters for interpretable image forensics.

entry.title: DispFlow-GS: Displacement Flow Supervision with Motion Disentangling for Monocular Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Thai Duy Nguyen, Haitian Zhang, Addison Lin Wang

entry.summary: DispFlow-GS identifies a domain gap between rendered Gaussian flow and optical flow that limits motion supervision in deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting, and proposes a displacement-flow framework that splats per-Gaussian 3D displacements with motion disentangling. This improves dynamic scene reconstruction, which matters for temporally consistent robotic perception. The diagnosis of the supervision-paradigm limitation is a useful conceptual contribution.

entry.title: NRF-GS: Neural Residual Fields for Expressive and Compact Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Pratik Singh Bisht, Andreas Kolb

entry.summary: NRF-GS replaces per-splat low-order spherical harmonics in 3D Gaussian Splatting with a shared global neural residual field that predicts view-dependent appearance residuals, with each Gaussian keeping compact appearance features and a Lambertian base color. This improves view-dependent reflectance expressiveness while reducing splat count.

entry.title: Technical note on: Zero-Training Feature-Space Alignment via Information Geometry

author.name: Behraj Khan, Tahir Qasim Syed, Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari

entry.summary: ZFGA is a closed-form, zero-training test-time method for robustness under covariate shift: it estimates the Fisher information matrix of the predictive distribution over feature embeddings and applies a linear transformation aligning test-feature geometry with a clean reference geometry. It requires no iterative optimization or parameter updates, unlike typical test-time adaptation.

entry.title: PAIQ: Patch-Aligned Semantic Injection via Residual Rotation

author.name: Pinze Ren, Yuwei Zhang, Hao Chen, Linghao Meng, Chang Li, Qiankun Li
