entry.title: USAI-Quant: A Quantitative Reasoning Benchmark for Vision-Language Models in Built Environments

author.name: Dongdong Wang, Qingqi Song, Yuzhou Chen, Deepak Balakrishnan, Ravi Shankar Srinivasan, Shenhao Wang

entry.summary: Presents the first benchmark for quantitative evaluation of VLM reasoning on built-environment metrics from remote sensing imagery, curated from the 335 largest U.S. cities. It targets the gap where existing VQA benchmarks are largely qualitative, and finds that state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with quantitative reasoning on such imagery.

entry.title: SynCo: Learning Cross-Modal Synergy by Contrasting Interaction Residuals

author.name: Yavuz Yarici, Ghassan AlRegib

entry.summary: SynCo is a multimodal contrastive learning method that targets synergy undertraining: building on Partial Information Decomposition, it observes that standard contrastive objectives capture mostly redundant information, and it adds dedicated supervision on interaction residuals to learn synergistic information available only from joint observation of modalities. This improves the transferability of multimodal representations beyond redundancy-only objectives.

entry.title: MorphAtt: A Neuromorphic Accelerator for Efficient Multi-Head Attention Processing in Spiking Vision Transformers

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Amirhesam Jafari Rad, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MorphAtt is a digital neuromorphic accelerator that speeds up multi-head self-attention in spiking vision transformers using cascaded hardware modules: a spiking QKV generator, a low-complexity spiking attention engine, and reparameterization convolution. The design targets energy-efficient edge inference where SViT parameter counts and attention costs are bottlenecks. It contributes hardware-software co-design for low-power vision transformers.

entry.title: What Survives the Codec Shift: Pooled No-Vocals Residuals for Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Jiajun Xu, Menglu Li, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: This work investigates which acoustic representations remain discriminative for speech deepfake detection as synthesis shifts from vocoders to neural codecs, comparing 12 representations under a shared linear classifier. It finds complementary behavior between hierarchical XLS-R features and pooled no-vocals residual statistics, and combines them into a dual-view detector called MN-P that generalizes to unseen codecs.

entry.title: Sharp training-conditional coverage for conformal prediction under covariate shift

author.name: Mehrdad Pournaderi

entry.summary: This paper derives explicit training-conditional coverage bounds for weighted split conformal prediction under covariate shift using a single concentration inequality, showing the correct scale is a variance proxy based on chi-squared divergence rather than the supremum of the likelihood ratio. It also provides matching two-point lower bounds, establishing sharpness of the analysis.

entry.title: LieDiscover: Adaptive Symbolic Library Construction for Explicit Open-form Symmetry Discovery

author.name: Xinxin Li, Jianming Ma, Xingyu Cui, Da Li, Juan Zhang, Junping Yin

entry.summary: LieDiscover formulates data-driven Lie symmetry discovery as joint optimization over the function library and generator coefficients, using an encoder-decoder architecture to dynamically generate symbolic expressions. This overcomes the limitation of predefined libraries in existing explicit methods, which struggle with high-order polynomial or transcendental symmetries.

entry.title: TopoMamba: A Load-Support Relation-Guided Multi-Directional State-Space Model for Topology Optimization

author.name: Bin Lou, Yuxuan Cheng, Huaizhi Zong, Junhui Zhang, Bing Xu

entry.summary: TopoMamba applies a state-space (Mamba-style) model to topology optimization, using load-support relations to guide multi-directional scanning and spatially adaptive fusion for predicting material distributions. It improves out-of-distribution generalization over existing deep methods while lowering computational cost.

entry.title: Weighted Spline-Expanded Networks with Distributional Balancing for Continuous Treatment Effects

author.name: Shucheng Liu, Chan Park, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: WSENet is an end-to-end neural framework for estimating causal effects of continuous treatments, combining distance-based covariate balancing weights, structured treatment embeddings with spline expansion, and bias-corrected outcome estimation. It targets confounding, misspecification, and high-dimensional covariates in observational studies.

entry.title: Laya as a Typed Probabilistic Assessor: An Independent Reproduction and a Preregistered Study of Calibration and Selective Escalation

author.name: Gowthamkumar Nandakishore

entry.summary: An independent, preregistered reproduction of the Laya 421M-parameter typed assessor finds the shipped checkpoint is uniformly under-confident, contradicting the model card's over-confidence framing, and shows a single fitted temperature (T=0.469) cuts held-out ECE from 0.204 to 0.037, outperforming the shipped per-option-count table. The direction of miscalibration determines which way a confidence-gated escalation cascade fails.

entry.title: Two-Sample Testing for Inhomogeneous Random Graphs in Non-Integral $L_r$ Norms

author.name: Soham Dan

entry.summary: This paper resolves a gap in the optimal sample complexity of two-sample testing for inhomogeneous Erdos-Renyi graphs under non-integral Lr norms with r greater than 2, where prior upper and lower bounds did not match. The proposed test runs two existing statistics of orders 2 and ceiling-of-r on the same data, rejecting if either rejects, with thresholds unified via Hoelder interpolation. This closes a conjectured-tight lower bound with a matching upper bound.

entry.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Information: Revealed versus Hidden Lotteries in School Choice

author.name: Parinaz Naghizadeh, Jingyan Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies whether revealing lottery numbers in school choice matching helps or hurts, challenging prior theoretical claims that revelation strictly improves matches under deferred acceptance. It relaxes the unrealistic assumption that all students share identical preference rankings and analyzes the resulting tradeoffs.

entry.title: Functional Autoencoders for Amplitude-Phase Representation Learning

author.name: Peida Wu, Xinyang Xiong, Pengcheng Zeng

entry.summary: AP-FAE is an unsupervised framework for functional data that factorizes the latent space into separate amplitude and phase embeddings, with a smooth functional decoder reconstructing channel-specific amplitude functions in canonical alignment. It targets the problem that temporal misalignment (phase variation) becomes entangled with shape in standard functional autoencoders.

entry.title: AgentWare: Automating the Lifecycle of Agentic Applications across the Edge-to-Cloud Continuum

author.name: Michalis Kasioulis, Moysis Symeonides, George Pallis, Marios D. Dikaiakos

entry.summary: AgentWare is an AgenticOps framework that automates provisioning, deployment, observability, and evaluation of LLM-based agentic applications across heterogeneous edge-to-cloud infrastructures. It provides an end-to-end lifecycle pipeline that prepares heterogeneous execution environments and transforms user-defined agent implementations, addressing the fragmentation of existing tools that cover only development, observability, or benchmarking separately. It targets hardware heterogeneity and limited observability in distributed agent deployments.

entry.title: From Soft Targets to Reward Signals: How Assignment and Reward Objectives Interact

author.name: Jiangtao Lin, Bangyang Wei, Siyi Liu, Yihang Ding, Yuhan Dong

entry.summary: The paper introduces assignment geometry to study how fixed preference strength assignments to response pairs translate into learned rewards across five reward objectives. Using mean-matched smoothing and within-stratum reassignment, it shows intact correspondence retains the largest clean preference margins within an accuracy-equivalence budget, while attenuation orderings vary with the objective. This informs principled design of soft preference targets in reward learning.

entry.title: CoSE-E: A Benchmark for Code-switched Speech Evaluation in Enterprise Settings

author.name: Shama Gupta, Hoang H Nguyen, Chelsea Huang, Lindsay Devon Brin, Fanny Riols

entry.summary: CoSE-E provides a synthetic code-switched ASR benchmark and multidimensional evaluation framework targeting enterprise voice agents, evaluating frontier ASR systems across 5 language pairs and diagnosing how code-switching transcription errors propagate to downstream task failures. This shifts evaluation beyond edit-distance metrics to operational impact. It fills a gap in realistic multilingual speech evaluation for deployed agents.

entry.title: KinyaMed: Seeds, Not Rows -- What a Corpus Requirement Written in the Wrong Unit Fails to Constrain

author.name: Marius Bayizere

entry.summary: Building a Kinyarwanda patient-triage classifier, the author found that a specification asking for one million examples could be satisfied in 130 seconds of generation while failing four to six of nine quality gates, because the requirement counted rows rather than distinct authored seed phrases. The paper reports the failure and the per-language instruments that detect it instead of the classifier itself.

entry.title: DualGuard: Dual-Mode Quality Control for Logic-Preserving Data Augmentation

author.name: Shenghao Li, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: DualGuard is a dual-mode quality-control framework for LLM-generated logical reasoning data: one mode makes per-instance retain/filter/repair decisions using the current batch, while the other accumulates feedback to improve future generation. It targets the gap between generating large volumes of augmented data and guaranteeing semantic, label, and logical reliability.

entry.title: Explaining Textual Entailment with Lexical Entailments: Using LLMs to Supply Lexical Relations for Formal Proofs

author.name: Jorryt de Jong, Stefan Moraca, Ettore Cesari, Lasha Abzianidze

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LLMs can identify the structured lexical entailment knowledge (e.g., hypernymy-type relations) needed to solve natural language inference problems, and whether that knowledge improves proof search in a logic-based NLI system. This connects LLM latent lexical knowledge with formally transparent, logic-grounded reasoning systems. The goal is to combine LLM knowledge elicitation with rigorous, explainable inference.

entry.title: Where Do Test-Time Scaling and Training Fall Short in Individual Stance Prediction?

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Xuan Liu, HaoYang Shangm Haojian Jin

entry.summary: The paper evaluates test-time scaling and post-training methods (SFT, RL) for predicting an individual's stance from their discussion history and identifies four failure modes including incorrect consensus, selection failure, and response overfitting. It shows that techniques improving coding and math reasoning do not straightforwardly transfer to this social-prediction task. This is a useful caution about the generalization of scaling strategies to human-centered prediction.

entry.title: Context Spanning: A Communication Framework for Full-Duplex Speech Models and External LLM Backends

author.name: Seonghyeon Go, Yongwoo Kim, Hyeonjin Cha, Jaeho Shin

entry.summary: Context Spanning is a framework for injecting raw-text information between a full-duplex speech model and an external LLM backend in real time, avoiding the information loss caused by processing retrieved content in compressed latent spaces. It enables full-duplex spoken dialogue agents to access real-time information and tools. This addresses a concrete architectural gap as voice agents move toward production.

entry.title: One Model Is Not a Crowd: Multi-LLM and Aspect-Conditioned Diverse Comment Generation

author.name: Nafis Irtiza Tripto, Delvin Ce Zhang, Mahjabin Nahar, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM-generated comment threads can capture the diversity of human online discourse, motivated by concerns about homogenized AI content and model collapse. The authors combine multiple LLMs with aspect-conditioned generation to better approximate crowd plurality. This is relevant as AI agents increasingly populate online spaces.

entry.title: Yor\`{u}b\'{a} in Unicode: An Overview of a Problem

author.name: K\'ol\'a T\'ub\`os\'un

entry.summary: Documents how the lack of precomposed diacritic characters in Unicode forces Yoruba and other African languages to rely on combining character sequences that behave inconsistently across platforms, corrupt under font substitution, and fail in search. The paper traces the structural cause to Unicode's NFC normalization stability policy. It is an important infrastructure-level account of digital inequity for low-resource languages.

entry.title: SlopBench: How Well Can We Rank Language Models by Slop? A Multi-Domain Benchmark of Repetitive AI Writing

author.name: Dhruv Roongta, Harsha Gaddipati, Anh Tuan Huynh

entry.summary: SlopBench is a benchmark for measuring repetitive, formulaic AI writing (so-called slop) across four domains: emails, social posts, essays, and workplace chat. The authors evaluate eighteen models on 112 hand-written tasks with nearly 20,000 sampled outputs, scoring checkable surface behaviors such as length adherence, opener repetition, paragraph rhythm, and lexical conformity to pre-ChatGPT human corpora. Under a fixed weighting, Kimi K2.6 scores best and Mistral Large worst, though the ranking stability varies across 500 random reweightings, probing how reliably such rankings hold.

entry.title: Understanding Clinical Cognitive Dialogues Using Large Language Models

author.name: Vishalakshi Arumugam, Dan Schumacher, Veronica Rammouz, Enrique Gonzalez Guerrero, Jeremy Davis, Anthony Rios

entry.summary: The authors release a de-identified corpus of 33 cognitive assessment conversations with 8,250 utterances annotated for speaker roles and 56 dialogue acts, and benchmark LLMs on fine-grained dialogue-act classification and next-patient-utterance generation. They also test transfer from out-of-domain instruction data and explanation-augmented training into this clinical setting.

entry.title: Adapt Semantics, Not Structure: Few-Instance Schema Calibration for Scientific PDF Extraction

author.name: Zixiao Dong, Wei Yang, Zihao Liu, Chenshu Li, Longzhang Liu, Tao Tan, Hong Xie

entry.summary: Frames few-instance schema calibration for scientific PDF extraction: adapting field-level semantics of an existing schema from a few gold annotations while preserving its structural contract. The CPSE framework jointly calibrates prompts and field descriptions, separating identity discovery from record completion.

entry.title: When Words Speak Louder than Images: Towards Understanding Language Bias in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yizhou Fang, Siyue Chen, Zimo Qi, Zhiyu Xue, Xi Chen, Guangliang Liu

entry.summary: Presents a diagnostic framework that decomposes VLM inference into four stages to trace how language bias propagates and overrides visual evidence, using word completion tasks. It also examines how model factors influence bias, addressing conflicting findings in prior work on black-box VLM behavior.

entry.title: From Hand-Crafted to LLM-Based Variation Operators in Metaheuristics: A Tutorial

author.name: Camilo Chac\'on Sartori, Guillem Rodr\'iguez-Corominas, Christian Blum

entry.summary: This tutorial provides a framework for using LLMs as variation operators inside metaheuristic search loops, with two descriptors: prompt-conditioning information type (Numeric, Symbolic, Linguistic) and artifact persistence (Transient, Amortized, Transfer). It offers a build template, method survey, and evidence synthesis for classifying, building, and selecting these operators. It matters as a systematization of a rapidly growing LLM-plus-search intersection.

entry.title: CueKFS: Agentic Cue-Driven Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Weitai Kang, Hanieh Deilamsalehy, Yumo Xu, Dewang Sultania, Serdar Cellat, Yan Yan

entry.summary: CueKFS is a training-free agentic method for question-conditioned keyframe selection in long-video question answering, motivated by the failure of similarity ranking when questions combine subjects or moments not shown in a single frame. It avoids static question decomposition issues by using cues to refine frame selection. This improves an important efficiency bottleneck for long-video understanding with multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: Improving Audiovisual Speech Recognition through Synthetic Visual Data Augmentation

author.name: Pol Buitrago, Pol G\`alvez, Javier Hernando

entry.summary: This paper uses an audio-driven talking-head pipeline to generate lip-synchronized synthetic visual data from audio-only corpora, addressing the scarcity of labeled audiovisual speech data. Evaluated on Spanish and Catalan, augmenting real audiovisual data with synthetic samples yields relative word error rate reductions. The approach could ease a key data bottleneck for AVSR, particularly for lower-resource languages.

entry.title: 5W1H+Which: Context-Valid Semantic Indexing with Progressive Ontology Binding

author.name: Yaxiao Liu (PwC China AI Center), Pengbo Liu (PwC China AI Center), Yiwen Liu (PwC China AI Center), Yihua Guan (PwC China AI Center), Jiaxing Song (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: This paper proposes 5W1H+Which, a semantic indexing design separating content extraction from ontology binding: 5W1H questions organize source-grounded content units while Which points to versioned ontology elements with mapping relations, scope, and validation status. The aim is indexes that support both open-ended retrieval and checkable rule-based reasoning across changing business schemas.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Functional Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Efficient Medical Image Enhancement and Segmentation

author.name: Mohammad Sadegh Sirjani

entry.summary: FunKANLite is a two-stage hardware-aware compression of Functional Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for point-of-care medical imaging, combining architectural reduction and distillation. The compressed model achieves 5.6x fewer parameters and 3.7x fewer GFLOPs while maintaining accuracy on MRI Gibbs artifact removal and anatomical segmentation. This enables deployment of KAN-based models on edge medical devices.

entry.title: AffectReveal: Event-Grounded Emotion Recognition Beyond Visual Appearances

author.name: Yihao Qian, Runhao Zeng, Sicheng Zhao, Feng Liang, Hongmin Cai, Mingkui Tan

entry.summary: The paper defines Event-Grounded Emotion Recognition (EGER), where recognizing emotion requires recovering the affect-determining event beyond the visible frame, and releases EGER-Bench with over 10,000 videos and images across 11 emotions. A human study shows event context lifts human accuracy from roughly 34 percent to 72 percent, demonstrating visual evidence alone is often insufficient. This reframes emotion recognition as a causal, context-recovery problem.

entry.title: MeteoVerse: Unified Weather-Controllable Video World Model

author.name: Renlong Wu, Guanqiao Wang, Xuan Shang, Yin Hanming, Xiaoxiao Sheng, Tianyu Huang, Hui Li, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: MeteoVerse is a video world model with explicit weather control, jointly modeling observed and desired weather states so the model can preserve, introduce, or remove weather effects during scene evolution rather than leaving transitions implicit. Weather-controllable generation is relevant to simulation, autonomous driving, and world-model research. It extends world models beyond viewpoint and object dynamics to environmental conditions.

entry.title: CurvSpec: Adaptive Multi-Curvature Learning for Partial Relevant Video Retrieval

author.name: Zhen Liu, Letian Li, Jinpeng Wang, Shuzhao Xie, Yuzhi Huang, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses Partially Relevant Video Retrieval (PRVR), where the goal is to find a short moment in an untrimmed video matching a text query without temporal annotations. It identifies two challenges, signal dilution and fixed embedding geometry, and proposes CurvSpec, an adaptive multi-curvature learning approach that tailors the embedding space geometry to videos of different compositional complexity. The work matters because PRVR has a very low signal-to-noise ratio and current methods use rigid single-geometry spaces.

entry.title: SFE-VGGT: Source-Free VGGT Distillation for Event-Based Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Thai Duy Nguyen, Addison Lin Wang

entry.summary: SFE-VGGT distills geometric priors from the VGGT vision foundation model into the event-camera domain without paired RGB data, reconstructing surrogate frames directly from the target event stream as a frozen geometric teacher. It handles the imperfect, spatially varying supervision these surrogates produce. Removing the need for synchronized RGB-event pairs or depth annotations substantially broadens practical deployment of event-based depth estimation.

entry.title: Beyond Readability: Evaluating Task Information Recoverability

author.name: Yiwei Liu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper argues that direct visual readability and task-information recoverability are distinct quantities, since a target that cannot be decoded from a fixed observation may still be accessed through other recovery routes. It proposes an evaluation framework that makes the observation, query, target, and available knowledge explicit, and measures overlap between the success sets of different routes, such as direct optical recovery versus entity-linked recovery that uses residual visual evidence to identify the depicted entity and access its attributes via a knowledge resource. This reframing could improve how vision benchmarks and information-access tasks are evaluated.

entry.title: NHO: A Neural Hamiltonian Operator for Anchor-based Region Localization and Dense Correspondance

author.name: Jing Li, Yawei Luo, Xiangze Meng, Ying Li, Tieru Wu, Rui Ma

entry.summary: NHO learns a neural Hamiltonian operator whose localized eigenspace encodes both region support and intrinsic coordinates for dense non-rigid shape correspondence from sparse anchors. It parameterizes the Hamiltonian potential as an intrinsic neural field with reciprocal refinement between operator estimation and correspondence.

entry.title: Multi-task learning for the automatic grading of enlarged perivascular space burden using MRI

author.name: Jesse Phitidis, William N. Whiteley, Joanna M. Wardlaw, Miguel O. Bernabeu, Yajun Cheng, Xiaodi Liu, Junfang Zhang, Una Clancy, Stephen Makin, Roberto Duarte Coello, Susana Mu\~noz Maniega, Mark E. Bastin, Simon R. Cox, Maria del C. Vald\'es Hern\'andez

entry.summary: This work develops machine learning models to automatically grade enlarged perivascular spaces in brain MRI across basal ganglia and centrum semiovale regions, a marker linked to brain health. Its key novelty is training with imperfect, semi-automatically generated silver-standard labels instead of costly expert annotations.

entry.title: BeatDance: Generating Beat-Consistent 3D Dance with Hierarchical Spatial-Temporal Modeling

author.name: Xiaojian Shen, Dahu Shi, Jianrong Zhang, Hai Li, Hongwei Zhao, Dawei Zhang, Yunzhi Zhuge, Zhiliang Wu, Guanghui Yue, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: BeatDance is a diffusion-based music-to-3D-dance generation framework with Hierarchical Decoupled Attention that disentangles pose learning from temporal dynamics across short- and long-term dependencies, plus cycle-consistent learning for precise beat alignment. It targets synchronization accuracy that prior physically plausible methods lack.

entry.title: PrototypeNAS: Rapid Design of Deep Neural Networks for Microcontroller Units

author.name: Mark Deutel, Simon Geis, Axel Plinge

entry.summary: PrototypeNAS is a zero-shot neural architecture search method for selecting, compressing, and specializing DNNs to target microcontrollers without training many architectures from scratch, and it accounts for target-device resource constraints. This reduces the manual effort of deploying efficient inference across heterogeneous edge hardware. It matters for practical TinyML deployment.

entry.title: Quantum Fidelity Landscape-Guided Prior Calibration for Single-Circuit QGAN Image Generation

author.name: Xue Yang, Rigui Zhou, Dax Enshan Koh, Siong Thye Goh, Yitao Tang, ShiZheng Jia, Young-Wook Cho, Hongyu Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes pixel-level, end-to-end image generation with a single-quantum-circuit QGAN, avoiding the patch-based decomposition strategies common in NISQ-era quantum generative models. It provides theoretical analysis of how the quantum prior structurally matches the target data distribution in Hilbert space to guide prior calibration. This aims to improve global image consistency while reducing quantum resource overhead.

entry.title: Multimodal Detection of Higher-Order Behavioral Constructs: Self-Compassion in Structured Reflective Interaction

author.name: Siddhant Jain, Dimitra Tsovaltzi

entry.summary: This paper studies computational detection of self-compassion — a psychologically grounded but rarely modeled construct — from multimodal signals during structured reflective interviews in a technology-mediated training setting. It tackles the challenge of inferring latent, hard-to-label behavioral qualities from how people speak, move, and sound over time. The work bridges psychological theory and machine learning pipeline design.

entry.title: Where Does Randomness Matter in Neural Cellular Automata?

author.name: Fei Zuo, Jiaqi Shi, Yujing Liu

entry.summary: This work disentangles whether stochastic cell updates help learn useful rules in growing neural cellular automata versus whether randomness must persist at execution time. Through controlled experiments separating training and evaluation modes, it shows asynchronous training passes quality tests in 10/10 runs versus 3/10 synchronous runs and derives exact analytical results for a translation-invariant lattice case.

entry.title: Inferring Soil Friction Angle from Robot Foot-Ground Force Histories: A Bayesian Inverse Approach to Proprioceptive Soil Sensing

author.name: Dawei Xu, Zhijie Wang

entry.summary: The authors show that a soil's internal friction angle can be inferred from quadruped foot-ground force histories using a material-point-method continuum model, Gaussian-process surrogates, and Bayesian inversion. Matched-model experiments recover 14 off-grid friction angles with roughly 0.1 degree median error and well-calibrated credible intervals. This establishes a first step toward robots characterizing terrain strength proprioceptively, useful for off-world exploration and field robotics.

entry.title: Kinematic Nonlinear Spatio-Temporal Trajectory Warping for Contact-Rich Dexterous Manipulation Demonstrations

author.name: Hyojae Park, Arjun S. Lakshmipathy, Nancy S. Pollard

entry.summary: The authors present a method for repurposing existing contact-rich dexterous manipulation demonstrations by computing nonlinear spatio-temporal trajectory warps that respect waypoints, environmental barriers, and varied start/end configurations. Contact distributions are the key ingredient enabling reliable high-dimensional hand trajectory generation from a simple object-centric warp specification. This improves data reuse in dexterous manipulation, a domain where demonstrations are expensive.

entry.title: All You Need Is Low Fidelity: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real of Learned Robotic Fish Control

author.name: Liam Maloney, Simon Ramchandani, Mike Y. Michelis, Ronan Hinchet, Robert K. Katzschmann

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate that an intentionally low-fidelity, stateless quasi-steady fluid simulator suffices to learn a closed-loop controller for a soft tendon-driven robotic fish that transfers to hardware without tuning, with a staged pipeline grounding the simulator in two independent system identifications. The policy observes only signals measurable on hardware. This is a useful datapoint that simulation fidelity can be traded for careful domain grounding in soft robotics.

entry.title: Battery-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Aggressive Quadrotor Flight

author.name: Alejandro Sanchez Roncero, Olov Andersson, Petter Ogren

entry.summary: The paper trains RL controllers for aggressive quadrotor flight that exploit the extra thrust available as battery voltage changes, using a simulator coupling an identified load-transient battery model with rotor dynamics and firmware saturation. The policy receives filtered voltage at training and deployment while retaining the flight controller's voltage compensation and rate control.

entry.title: The Signed Geometry of One-Shot Recourse: On-Path Validity and the Signed-Curvature Criterion

author.name: Hazar Yueksel (Google)

entry.summary: Analyzes when closed-form one-shot algorithmic recourse steps succeed, proving to leading order that a step lands on the favorable side exactly when the path curvature of the classifier score is nonnegative. Empirical correlation of 0.985 across 80 models supports the criterion, and impossibility results show score-and-gradient-only rules cannot always be valid.

entry.title: Cheap and Powerful Tests for Supervised Subspaces: Per-Component Inference for PLS

author.name: Pawe{\l} Lenartowicz, Hubert Plisiecki

entry.summary: This work develops practical statistical tests for inference on supervised subspaces extracted by Partial Least Squares regression, framing inference as held-out OLS refits of the supervised span. The authors provide two tests — a Nadeau-Bengio corrected asymptotic t-test and a finite-sample-valid permutation test — both usable for per-component inference with interpretable bases like varimax. This fills a notable gap, since inference for PLS has traditionally been expensive, biased, or simply discouraged.

entry.title: Federated Clustering with Unknown Local and Global Cluster Cardinalities

author.name: Mitushi Goyal, Tarun S., Riddhanya Senapathi, Arun Raman

entry.summary: Proposes a two-phase federated clustering framework where neither the global cluster count K nor per-client local counts are known, removing an unrealistic assumption in prior work. Clients estimate local counts via Adaptive Split-Merge, a label-free BIC-driven Gaussian mixture procedure, and an aggregator like FedGEM consumes these estimates.

entry.title: The double descent and Runge phenomena in overparametrized polynomial interpolation

author.name: Jason Wein, Stephan Wojtowytsch

entry.summary: This note studies overparameterized polynomial interpolation in monomial, Chebyshev, and Legendre bases with minimum l2 (and l1 for monomials) coefficient norms, exploring the classical Runge phenomenon as an analogue of double descent in machine learning. It analyzes behavior for equidistant and Chebyshev data points with results largely independent of sampling details. The work connects classical approximation theory to modern overparametrization phenomena.

entry.title: A shape-similarity latent space for fluid interfaces: invertible reduced-order modelling of droplet morphology

author.name: Ali R. Hashemi, Mohammad R. Hashemi, Pavel B. Ryzhakov

entry.summary: The authors build a low-dimensional, invertible latent space for droplet interface shapes that is faithful to shape geometry rather than sampled coordinates, combining ideas from proper orthogonal decomposition, manifold learning, and elastic shape analysis. The goal is to reconstruct unobserved intermediate morphologies in fast droplet breakup experiments and sweep operating envelopes without expensive re-simulation. This enables scientific ML for fluid interface dynamics at microsecond timescales.

entry.title: How Much Do Reward Hackers Generalize?

author.name: Avi Brach-Neufeld

entry.summary: The post argues that discussions of chain-of-thought monitorability focus too narrowly on RL pressure, and that models might learn to avoid monitoring without ever being reinforced for it, depending on whether reward hacking has fully generalized to a terminal get-reward objective. It proposes an experiment inspired by the reported Hugging Face incident to test this, predicting that full generalization would break CoT monitoring even absent RL pressure. It engages with OpenAI's recently reported detection of a model exploiting DNS to escape a sandbox.

entry.title: SRJudge: Empowering Large Language Models with Selective Reasoning for Fine-Grained Knowledge Concept Tagging

author.name: Zhiwei Yang, Jiahua Yang, Huiru Lin, Xing Chen, Quanlong Guan

entry.summary: SRJudge is a three-stage Select-Reason-Judge framework for fine-grained knowledge concept tagging in educational content, addressing LLM struggles with very large candidate label sets. A fine-tuned small selector first narrows candidates to a top-K shortlist before LLM reasoning and judging. This reduces the decision-space dimensionality that typically degrades tagging accuracy.

entry.title: PowerMarketJax: A JAX Benchmark Suite for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Power Markets

author.name: Zhanhua Pan, Xin Qin, Xiao Liu, Zhilong Cao, Jianhong Wang, Dawei Qiu

entry.summary: PowerMarketJax is a JAX-based benchmark suite for multi-agent RL across five power market settings (day-ahead wholesale, real-time balancing, ancillary services, peer-to-peer auctions, local flexibility) with realistic clearing mechanisms and GPU-accelerated optimization. It overcomes the simplified clearing rules and CPU-bound solvers of prior MARL environments. This enables systematic study of bidding strategies and market behavior at scale.

entry.title: FIDAL: Diversity-Aware Federated Active Learning Under Real-World Distribution Shifts

author.name: David Due\~nas Gaviria, Shadi Albarqouni

entry.summary: FIDAL is an open-set federated active learning framework combining calibrated global-local evidential uncertainty, support-set diversity weighting, and adaptive OOD rejection to handle domain shifts and class imbalance in federated clinical settings. A per-client, per-round rejection gate uses a foundation-model Gaussian-coverage signal thresholded with Otsu's criterion to prevent irrelevant out-of-distribution samples from diluting labeled data.

entry.title: Spectral Reversal: Counteracting Singular Value Bias for Graph Prompting

author.name: Hanxu Yang, Yuhuan Zhao, Xiaodong He, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: The paper identifies spectral bias in pre-trained GNNs, where pre-training over-aligns representations with high-singular-value directions leaving low-energy directions under-explored yet informative. It proposes spectral reversal to exploit these underutilized directions for parameter-efficient graph prompting, improving adaptation of frozen graph encoders.

entry.title: FedHV: Low-Overhead Hypervolume Weighting for Federated Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Amirardalan Dehghanpour, Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: FedHV is a federated multi-objective optimization method that maps reference-relative objective slacks to closed-form inverse-slack weights, requiring each client to return only objective estimates alongside its update, adding just 2m auxiliary scalars versus the Theta(md) communication of prior approaches like FSMGDA. It handles heterogeneous data, partial participation, and communication constraints. This improves the practicality of multi-objective federated learning.

entry.title: Phenomenon-Graph JEPA: Label-Efficient Representation Learning for Contactless Cardiorespiratory Sensing

author.name: Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Nhi Nguyen, Mohammad Rakibur Rahman, Le Nguyen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Sasan Sharifipour, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: This work applies a JEPA with graph-structured objectives to learn representations from mmWave radar and RGB-D streams for contactless cardiac and respiratory monitoring, avoiding negative pairs and augmentation assumptions that are problematic for physiological signals. It enables label-efficient pretraining where labels require supervised acquisition sessions.

entry.title: Beyond Conservatism: Recoverability-Conditioned Exploration for Model-Based Imitation Learning

author.name: Xuanlin Chen, Ziyue Wang, Xunlan Zhou, Yuan-yih Shang, Qiang Wu, Shenghua Wan

entry.summary: RECON addresses model exploitation in model-based imitation learning by separating conservative policy optimization from targeted exploration: it conditions real-environment interaction on recoverability, sampling uncertain regions near the expert distribution that remain recoverable rather than task-irrelevant novel dynamics.

entry.title: The cost of useful natural gradient updates

author.name: Subhransu S. Bhattacharjee, Dylan Campbell, Rahul Shome

entry.summary: The paper constructs a four-state exponential family where different laws share initial gradient, scalar Fisher information, and natural gradient yet have disjoint useful-step sets, proving worst-case sample complexity of Theta(log(1/delta)/(p*eps^2)) to turn a natural-gradient direction into a useful finite update under a KL budget. This reveals fundamental information limits of natural gradient methods.

entry.title: EntroPack: Fast and Accurate Entropy-Coded Weight Compression at Arbitrary Bitrates

author.name: Hong Zhang, Zhongjie Duan, Yingda Chen

entry.summary: EntroPack is an entropy-coded weight compressor supporting arbitrary target bitrates without activation calibration or fine-tuning, combining row-normalized E8 lattice quantization with a conditional probability model of lattice coordinates. Sampled storage estimates enable quantization-resolution selection without repeated full-stream encoding.

entry.title: Distribution-Conditioned Task Routing for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Longhuan Xu, Zhipeng Zhou, Wei Ji, Chunyan Miao, Peilin Zhao, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the task-routing problem in class-incremental learning with parameter-efficient modules, where each input must be classified among all classes seen so far without a task label. The authors study training-free, inference-time calibration of routing, identifying three sources of routing error and proposing distribution-conditioned routing without retraining the learner or training a separate router. This fills an underexplored gap beyond standard catastrophic forgetting work.

entry.title: Single-Layer MeMo as a Randomized Hamming-Kernel Classifier

author.name: Alessandro Straziota

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical analysis of the recent MeMo language-model architecture, showing that its single-layer form with Gaussian random codes implements a multiclass classifier based on the positional Hamming kernel. The authors bound errors from context sketching and output decoding, characterize dependence on model and data parameters, and give margin-based recovery guarantees for the ideal prediction. This brings statistical learning theory to a new association-memory architecture.

entry.title: Learning Propagation Geometry from Message-Passing Feedback

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Kunyu Zhang, Xinwang Liu, Mengzhu Wang, Siyang Gao, Chang Tang, Nan Yin

entry.summary: The paper proposes GeoF, a recurrent graph neural network framework that jointly evolves node features and per-node symmetric positive-definite propagation geometry through message-passing feedback, with geometry initialized from structure-aware prototypes and parameterized in block log-triangular coordinates. Geometry determines neighborhood weights while frame transport maps transformed messages into local coordinates.

entry.title: Graph World Models for Constrained Epidemic Policy Planning

author.name: Yiqi Su, Rashed Shelim, Lingyi Wang, Walid Saad, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: EpiMind is a graph world model framework for constrained epidemic policy planning across regions, combining a graph-factored recurrent state-space model for policy-conditioned rollouts with graph-temporal ADMM optimization that enforces shared-resource feasibility. It reduces admission RMSE by 29 percent relative to graph-based baselines.

entry.title: Kernel-Based Steering of CLIP with Vision-Language Model Preferences

author.name: Sajjad Ghiasvand, Haniyeh Ehsani Oskouie, Sina Mansouri, Mahnoosh Alizadeh, Farzan Farnia, Ramtin Pedarsani

entry.summary: ASK transfers the similarity preferences of a large vision-language model into CLIP via kernel-based steering, learning from elicited pairwise judgments without access to teacher embeddings or new human annotations. Low-rank adapters update visual and text encoders while anchoring to frozen CLIP to preserve original capabilities.

entry.title: Taming the Greeks: Option Portfolios with Inductive Biases

author.name: Wee Ling Tan, Stephen Roberts, Stefan Zohren

entry.summary: An end-to-end deep learning framework for systematic options trading that embeds hedging behavior via differentiable penalties enforcing neutrality to selected portfolio-level risk exposures (Greeks). It operates directly on market data rather than RL-style simulated dynamics, combining performance-driven loss with risk-sensitivity constraints.

entry.title: Recursive LLM Degradation in Biomedical Question Answering: A Cross-Generation Study

author.name: Bibek Bhandari, Kshitij Lingthep

entry.summary: Using PubMedQA and two Qwen2.5 model sizes (0.5B and 3B), this study empirically compares recursive synthetic-data training against repeated use of original human data across four generations, evaluating on disease and chemical entity tasks with fixed seeds and evaluation sets. It examines the model-collapse-style feedback loop in a biomedical QA setting.

entry.title: From One-Shot Generation to Incremental Music Composition: Adapting a General-Purpose Instruction LLM for Persistent Symbolic Editing

author.name: Andr\'e Ricardo Ducca Fernandes, Jean-Pierre Briot, Simone Diniz Junqueira Barbosa1, H\'elio C\^ortes Vieira Lopes

entry.summary: The paper reframes LLM-based music generation as incremental editing of a persistent symbolic score, formulating composition as operation-aware state transitions over ABC notation with explicit preservation requirements. It implements two initialization variants and three editing operations (chord addition, inpainting, transposition) using a general-purpose instruction LLM. This shifts evaluation from one-shot complete outputs to iterative compositional workflows mirroring human practice.

entry.title: The Hidden Perception Constraint in Task-Aware Compression

author.name: Sahan Liyanaarachchi, Semih Akkoc, Sennur Ulukus, Aylin Yener

entry.summary: The paper uncovers perception constraints naturally present in task-aware compression, considering a setting where reconstruction is the primary task and classification is secondary, and analyzes how these constraints behave under varying levels of domain information. This extends rate-distortion-perception theory to multi-task compression settings. It is a theoretical contribution relevant to how neural compressors should be designed for downstream tasks.

entry.title: CoLMbo-SV: A Grounded Language Model for Explainable Speaker Verification

author.name: Massa Baali, Sarthak Bisht, Ziyue Qiu, Joseph Konan, Rita Singh, Bhiksha Raj

entry.summary: CoLMbo-SV connects a pretrained speaker encoder to a language model with explicit acoustic measurements to produce structured, explainable voice-comparison reports while retaining full verification accuracy beyond what is verbalized. The accompanying VoxReason dataset pairs recordings with measured acoustic properties. It addresses the transparency gap in high-accuracy but opaque speaker verification systems.

entry.title: NSV-Shift: A Contrastive Benchmark for Non-Speech Vocalization Understanding and Response Adaptation in Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Ziwei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces NSV-Shift, a contrastive benchmark where conversation pairs differ only in an embedded non-speech vocalization (laugh, sigh, etc.), testing whether speech-to-speech models perceive, interpret, and appropriately adapt responses to NSVs. A pilot of 22 human-verified pairs across five models shows models detect NSVs better than they interpret fine-grained emotion or adapt responses. The dataset and pipelines are publicly released.

entry.title: Temporal-Aware Fusion for Robust Outdoor LiDAR Localization

author.name: Minghang Zhu, Zhijing Wang, Yuxin Guo, Chen Liu, Yongshu Huang, Wen Li, Sheng Ao, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: TempLoc is a temporal-aware LiDAR relocalization framework that models sequential consistency across scans for robust outdoor 6-DoF pose estimation. It first predicts point-wise global coordinates and uncertainties per scan via a Global Coordinate Estimation module, then generates prior coordinates across frames to exploit spatio-temporal information that single-frame regression methods ignore. The approach targets robustness in dynamic or ambiguous scenarios.

entry.title: DSPO: Diversity-aware Subjective Policy Optimization for Robust Emotional Reasoning

author.name: Cheng Ye, Weidong Chen, Bingyan Xu, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: DSPO is a reinforcement learning framework for multimodal LLMs that handles the subjective, continuously distributed nature of human emotions, replacing deterministic hard-label supervision with diversity-aware objectives to reduce ungrounded emotional evidence and hallucination. It addresses a documented failure mode of standard RL algorithms in emotion reasoning. This extends RL post-training beyond objectively verifiable tasks.

entry.title: GA-EIRFS: A Geometry-Augmented Repeat-Factor Sampling Method for Long-Tailed LiDAR 3D Object Detection

author.name: Taufiq Ahmed, Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Daniel Herrera Castro, Sasan Sharifipour, Abhishek Kumar, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: GA-EIRFS refines repeat factor sampling for long-tailed LiDAR 3D detection by modulating class-frequency-based resampling with a geometry score combining point count, surface-normal entropy, and surface coverage, reflecting object observability rather than frequency alone. It is detector-agnostic, changing only frame-sampling probabilities, and improves mAP and NDS on nuScenes with CenterPoint and PointPillars.

entry.title: BCNav: Bearing-Conditioned Depth Policies for Sound Source Navigation

author.name: Yaozhong Kang, Jiang Wang, Takeshi Ashizawa, Benjamin Yen, Kazuhiro Nakadai

entry.summary: BCNav decouples acoustic sensing from navigation learning for sound source navigation: a direction-of-arrival estimator conditions depth-based policies, avoiding low-fidelity acoustic simulation and grid-based discrete action spaces. This closes the acoustic domain gap and kinematic gap that hinder real-world audio-visual navigation. It enables robots to respond to auditory events beyond their visual field in unknown environments.

entry.title: DROM: A Language-Guided Diffusion Framework for Multi-Skill Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Vincenzo Pomponi, Rocco Felici, Paolo Franceschi, Stefano Baraldo, Oliver Avram, Loris Roveda, Luca Maria Gambardella, Anna Valente

entry.summary: DROM is a language-guided diffusion framework that composes multiple manipulation skills in a single generative policy, using Dynamic Movement Primitives to augment small demonstration sets. Built on Motion Planning Diffusion with cross-attention conditioning, it reduces data collection needs while improving spatial generalization.

entry.title: Hierarchical Utility Calibration for Structured Multiclass Decisions

author.name: Futoshi Futami, Jerry Huang, Ichiro Takeuchi

entry.summary: This paper develops hierarchical utility calibration for multiclass prediction with meaningful label hierarchies, proving an exact decomposition of the utility gap into contributions from internal nodes of the label tree. The decomposition reveals cancellation effects between positive and negative node contributions that naive audits would miss. This improves reliability of downstream decision guarantees in domains like medicine and image classification.

entry.title: Why does Hacker Opus wirehead?

author.name: shawnghu

entry.summary: Analyzing Anthropic's recent reward-seeker training post, the author disentangles reward hacking terminology and examines why a model exhibited wireheading, terminally valuing the reward representation itself. Drawing on pre-LLM embedded-agency analyses of RL algorithms, the post explains conditions under which wireheading policies are explored and sustained because they genuinely achieve high reward. It connects classic RL theory to newly observed frontier-model behavior.

entry.title: DatalogBench: Evaluating Large Language Models on Text-to-Datalog Synthesis

author.name: Yuan Li, Hanyun Jiang, Guowei Tian, Chengpeng Wang, Peisen Yao

entry.summary: DatalogBench provides 136 text-to-Datalog synthesis tasks curated from existing Datalog artifacts, with execution-based grading against mutation-validated oracles. Across six LLMs and four prompting configurations, exact match peaks at only 68.4%, and auxiliary inputs like relation descriptions or examples help. It is the first systematic evaluation of LLMs on a logic-programming synthesis task relevant to program analysis.

entry.title: Measurement-Gated Provenance Attenuation for Frozen EEG Representations

author.name: Anuar Aimoldin, Yankai Chen, Ayana Mussabayeva, Nurdaulet Akhanov, Xue Liu

entry.summary: MGPA removes acquisition-site signatures from frozen EEG representations while preserving genuine biological and population differences, using paired measurement contrasts to define a gate outside which nothing is changed. Within the gate, the source score is moved to a value predicted by preserved coordinates.

entry.title: Sub-Model Short-Term Memory Convolutions for Keyword Spotting Systems on Device

author.name: Pawe{\l} Warlewski, Artur Czeczko, Artur Szumaczuk, Grzegorz Stefa\'nski, Szymon Klimaszewski

entry.summary: The paper applies the STMC framework to adapt a modular CNN keyword-spotting model for online, LSTM-like inference on resource-constrained edge devices such as wearables. It reports large reductions in power consumption and redundant computations while retaining CNN training stability and meeting accuracy, memory, and latency constraints. This targets the practical gap between voice-assistant demand and wearable hardware limits.

entry.title: Not Every Correction Helps: Gain-Guided Continual Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Youjia Zhang, Huiling Liu, Soyun Choi, Jaehong Yoon, Sungeun Hong

entry.summary: The paper proposes GAIN, a backpropagation-free continual test-time adaptation framework that decides whether and how strongly to apply corrections from accumulated target history, rather than relying on confidence or entropy alone. It addresses the problem that historical evidence becomes misaligned as the target distribution shifts. This offers an efficient, stability-aware approach to adapting models on streaming data.

entry.title: ThuRunel: Dynamic Decoupling for Structured Advisory Dialogue

author.name: Yuyan Chen

entry.summary: ThuRunel is an advisory agent for high-stakes two-phase domains such as medical aesthetics, legal consultation, and educational planning, formalizing a dynamic decoupling problem: deciding what to ask, when to stop, what to resolve autonomously, and what to escalate to specialists. It combines a finite-state belief management framework, a chain-of-thought teacher synthesis protocol, and learned generation adapters. The formalization of the escalation boundary problem is its most distinctive contribution.

entry.title: Accelerated surrogate dynamics for dynamical, stochastic system evolution

author.name: Marco Jochum, Ioannis Kouroudis, Gohar Ali Siddiqui, Taher Amine Hamzaoui, Manuel G\"o{\ss}wein, Alessio Gagliardi

entry.summary: Presents a machine learning surrogate framework for high-dimensional stochastic dynamical simulations, combining a variational approach with components designed to capture both short- and long-range effects and avoid drift. The goal is to reduce the prohibitive computational cost of dynamic simulations in scientific domains.

entry.title: Brain-SAD: A Brain-Inspired Safe Autonomous Driving Control Framework with Dynamic Fear-Oriented Constraint on Dual-Policy

author.name: Huan Rong, Chao Yin, Anouar Imel, Yijie Xia, Tinghuai Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a constrained RL framework for safe autonomous driving with dynamically varying constraints, motivated by a brain-inspired fear signal, replacing static state-to-cost mappings and fixed feasible-region projections. A dual-policy design adapts constraint dynamics during training and execution.

entry.title: Calibration-First Cross-Cohort Multimodal Temporal Learning for Transferable Asthma-Risk Forecasting

author.name: Taimoor Ahmad

entry.summary: CALIBRA is a calibration-first multimodal temporal framework for short-horizon asthma deterioration prediction with incomplete data, combining recurrent encoders for six data streams with a reliability-conditioned gate that suppresses stale or absent modalities. Gradient-reversal training discourages cohort-specific signatures and a shrinkage-based hierarchical logistic layer calibrates risk probabilities for cross-cohort transfer.

entry.title: Graph neural networks for sampling-invariant embeddings of organized signal sets

author.name: Martin Bauw (CMM), Santiago Velasco-Forero (CMM), Jesus Angulo (CMA)

entry.summary: This paper proposes GNN-based encoders that project heterogeneously sampled organized signal sets (ordered signals, range-cell grids, graph-structured sensor data) into a fixed-size vector space invariant to sampling differences. The representation enables topology-aware downstream processing without signal-processing constraints. It targets radar and sensor-network applications.

entry.title: Infrared Subtraction with Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Wenjie He, Xiaohui Liu, Yandong Liu, Zhan Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-assisted development of local infrared subtraction schemes in particle physics, building on projection to Born kinematics and EFT matching. Under human physics guidance, an LLM develops two implementations: one using a neural network for phase space projection and another using analytic construction with four-dimensional radiation integrals. It demonstrates human-AI collaboration in deriving technically demanding results in quantum field theory.

entry.title: Measuring trainable degrees of freedom in materials graph neural networks: a random-subspace intrinsic dimension analysis

author.name: Shehroz Ahmad Shoaib, Kangming Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces trainable-degree dependence as a complement to final predictive accuracy for characterizing materials graph neural networks. Using random-subspace intrinsic-dimension analysis, the authors train CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DimeNet++ in random parameter subspaces across six tasks and measure performance recovery as trainable degrees of freedom are restored. The recovery curves separate endpoint accuracy from the parameter efficiency required to achieve it, revealing distinctions accuracy alone misses.

entry.title: Think Before You Restore: Risk-Aware Manchu Manuscript Restoration with Stroke-Guided Attention

author.name: Mingqiu Liang, Dongdong Wang, Siyang Lu, Ting Huang, Yingjun Qi

entry.summary: SAGE-Restore is a selective restoration framework for historical Manchu manuscripts that first predicts patch-level repair probabilities from appearance and stroke-structural cues, then conditions candidate generation and pixel-level selection on that assessment. This avoids over-restoration of intact content, a common failure of generic restoration models.

entry.title: Designing a Boundary Negotiating Artifact for Collaborative Socio-Technical Sense-Making in AI Regulatory Sandboxes

author.name: Idoia Landa-Oregi, Tom Deckenbrunnen, Alessio Buscemi, Daniele Pagani, German Castignani

entry.summary: This paper addresses the socio-technical gap in AI Regulatory Sandboxes (AIRS), where legal frameworks leave interpretation to stakeholders without supporting tools. Using Research-through-Design, the authors iteratively develop a Boundary Negotiating Artifact to mediate shared meaning among stakeholders in regulatory sandbox processes. It matters because AI governance infrastructure often overlooks the practical sense-making needed for regulators and innovators to collaborate effectively.

entry.title: ResComEmb: Effective and Efficient Multimodal Embedding via Residual Homogeneity Compression

author.name: Zijing Cai, Yuzhe Wang, Jingxian Zhu, Fengbin Zhu, Richang Hong

entry.summary: ResComEmb is a trainable multi-vector multimodal embedding framework that encodes inputs at native dynamic resolution into global, intermediate, and fine-grained views, then applies a Residual Homogeneity Compression module to reduce within-granularity redundancy. It resolves the trade-off between single-vector compression (losing expressiveness) and long visual-token sequences (high storage cost). Relevant for retrieval and representation learning with MLLMs.

entry.title: Symmetry-quotient Flatness and Generalization

author.name: Taiki Miyagawa

entry.summary: This theory paper develops a symmetry-aware notion of flatness defined on quotient spaces of neural network parameters, showing a theorem-level chain: quotient linear stability implies quotient flatness, which implies input smoothness, and hence generalization. This addresses the well-known problem that standard flatness measures are not invariant under function-preserving symmetries like positive rescaling.

entry.title: STAR: Adaptive Spatial-Temporal Normalization for Unified Microservice Incident Management

author.name: Xinhua Miao, Linyu Zhu, Bowei Yang, Zhengong Cai

entry.summary: STAR is a representation learning framework for microservice observability data (metrics, logs, traces) that uses Temporal and Spatial Adaptive Normalization to handle non-stationary dynamics and heterogeneous service dependencies. It unifies anomaly detection, failure triage, and root cause localization in one self-supervised framework.

entry.title: Relational Compression: A Framework for Relational Fidelity in Constrained Representations

author.name: Yaniv Shulman

entry.summary: The paper formulates relational compression, asking what a compressed representation should preserve when the information of interest is in relationships rather than elements, and provides a common interface unifying graph summarization, spectral sparsification, similarity-preserving representation, and relational distillation. It positions selected methods within this framework while making their differing assumptions explicit. This is primarily a conceptual and unifying contribution.

entry.title: REALM: Regime-Switching, Explainable, and Activation-Induced Linear Models

author.name: Xiaoran Cheng, Sen Na, Jia Li

entry.summary: REALM is a mixture of local linear models whose regimes are induced by neural activation patterns: a deep teacher is distilled into a wide shallow student, whose binarized clustered activations define interpretable regimes with a linear model fit per cell. This preserves much of the teacher's predictive accuracy while yielding regime-level explainability of piecewise-affine ReLU networks.

entry.title: Topology-Adaptive Hyperbolic Graph Attention Networks Guided by the Hyperbolic Sombor Index

author.name: Haifang Cao, Boan Tao, Xiyuan Gao, Timing Li, Yu Wang, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: The authors introduce the Hyperbolic Sombor Index (HSO), a lightweight structural prior capturing degree stratification that indicates hierarchy in graphs. Building on it, HSO-GAT combines HSO-guided local curvature adaptation with attention-based message propagation, allowing node-wise geometric adaptation instead of shared curvature in hyperbolic graph neural networks.

entry.title: Editable Map-Conditioned Trajectory Generation for Human Mobility Simulation

author.name: Takayuki Mizuno, Shouji Fujimoto, Mikito Hiruki, Atushi Ishikawa

entry.summary: Formulates human mobility simulation as map-conditioned autoregressive generation where a road raster conditions a decoder emitting mesh-cell tokens at one-minute intervals, supporting held-out and locally edited maps without retraining. Trained on 87,400 smartphone trajectories from Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, using ResNet-50 visual-prefix and ViT cross-attention configurations.

entry.title: What Do Latent Predictive Vehicle Representations Retain? Measuring State, Geometry, and Local Response

author.name: Enzo Nicol\'as Spotorno, Josafat Leal Filho, Ant\^onio Augusto Fr\"ohlich

entry.summary: The paper proposes a measurement protocol for action-conditioned latent vehicle dynamics models, checking whether physical quantities (position, yaw, speed) are recoverable and whether predictions vary with commands as the real vehicle does. It argues that prediction error on latent targets alone measures neither property, which matters when latent world models are embedded in physically specified controllers. This improves evaluation of learned dynamics models for control.

entry.title: Learning When to Recur: Token-Adaptive Recursion for Imbalanced Ophthalmic Domain Incremental Learning

author.name: Nanxi Yu, Kang Li, Ye Du, Xiaowei Hu, Weihua Yang, Shujun Wang

entry.summary: ToRe is a rehearsal-free, parameter-efficient framework for ophthalmic domain incremental learning that uses token-adaptive recursion over frozen foundation models to handle both style-driven domain shift and severe class-imbalance-induced label distribution shift in clinical referral settings. It targets preserving diagnostic expertise as models sequentially adapt to new clinical domains. This is a specialized medical AI application of incremental learning.

entry.title: Over-the-Air Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Mobile Wireless Networks

author.name: Ming Xiang, Nicol\`o Michelusi, Yonina C. Eldar, Lili Su

entry.summary: The paper proposes FedOAG, a federated learning scheme using over-the-air computation that avoids the noise amplification of unbiased aggregation and the bias-sensitivity of partial contribution methods under heterogeneous fading channels. It targets scalable FL deployment in wireless networks.

entry.title: Efficient Message Passing for Partial Differential Equation Priors

author.name: Anna Kazachkova, Leonhard Hennicke, Rainer Schlosser, Ralf Herbrich

entry.summary: The authors solve PDEs via probabilistic inference on factor graphs, encoding governing equations as explicit factors and inferring approximate parameter posteriors with moment-matching message passing rather than posterior sampling or gradient-based optimization. Demonstrations include advection and semi-linear Fisher-KPP equations.

entry.title: ILP-BO: Integer Linear Programming-Based Black-Box Optimization

author.name: Hyakka Nakada, Shu Tanaka

entry.summary: ILP-BO reformulates kernel-based surrogate optimization in Bayesian optimization over discrete domains as an Integer Linear Programming problem, providing global-optimality guarantees in candidate selection that conventional heuristic acquisition maximization lacks. The approach targets expensive black-box functions with limited evaluation budgets.

entry.title: From Grey-Box to Green-Box: When can Physics-Informed Machine Learning Reduce Carbon Footprints in Structural Health Monitoring?

author.name: Daisy R. Bradley, Nathan A. Hinchliffe, Daniel J. Pitchforth, Matthew R. Jones, Elizabeth J. Cross

entry.summary: This work quantifies whether physics-informed grey-box models in structural health monitoring reduce computational carbon emissions relative to black-box learners, linking training data quantity, training time, and compute-related CO2. It offers a sustainability-oriented justification for physics-informed ML.

entry.title: Short-Length Code Designs for Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Deep Learning Approach

author.name: Muah Kim, Shuangyang Li, Tayyebeh Jahani-Nezhad, Rafael F. Schaefer, Giuseppe Caire

entry.summary: This paper proposes an autoencoder-based framework for ISAC waveform design in noncoherent short-blocklength settings, deriving a modified Cramer-Rao bound for multi-target delay estimation and analyzing ML decoding under correlated fading. The analysis reveals structural trade-offs that the autoencoder then jointly optimizes.

entry.title: ResDiffFRG: Residual Diffusion for Multiple Appropriate Facial Reaction Generation

author.name: Shizhe Liu, Jiayan Gu, Xiangyu Kong, Siyang Song

entry.summary: ResDiffFRG improves diffusion-based generation of multiple appropriate facial reactions in dyadic conversations by using residual diffusion with better-aligned initializations instead of denoising random Gaussian noise, simplifying the denoising trajectory. This addresses the one-to-many nature of human listener reactions for realistic human-agent interaction. It targets a specific but important affective computing task.

entry.title: SR4-Fit: A Unified Interpretable Rule-Based Machine Learning Framework for Informative and Trustworthy Decision-Making

author.name: Shyam Sundar Murali Krishnan, Dean Frederick Hougen

entry.summary: SR4-Fit extends rule-based interpretable modeling (building on RuleFit) using sparse relaxed regularized regression to improve the stability and predictive strength of intrinsically interpretable classifiers and regressors. It aims to close the perceived accuracy-versus-interpretability trade-off in high-stakes applications where post hoc explanations are unreliable.

entry.title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification

author.name: Mahesh Neupane, Pragya Dhungana, Pradip Khatri, Swechhya Baskota, Hariom Dhungana

entry.summary: This paper presents an empirical comparison of four contemporary probabilistic models for electricity demand forecasting, motivated by the growing variability introduced by renewable energy penetration and smart grid complexity. It argues that uncertainty-quantified forecasts are essential for reliable power-system planning, moving beyond deterministic point estimates.

entry.title: Deep kernel hedging

author.name: Jean-Loup Dupret, Donatien Hainaut, Edouard Motte

entry.summary: This paper combines deep learning with kernel methods for hedging in financial mathematics: the hedging functional is restricted to a reproducing kernel Hilbert space whose kernel is parameterized by a neural network embedding, with support for path-dependent information via signature features. The authors derive a generalized representer theorem and a random Fourier feature approximation for scalability. It targets derivative pricing and risk management with better inductive biases than pure deep learning.

entry.title: Beyond Site Agreement: Re-estimation for Brain Network Generalization

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Kunyu Zhang, Yanwu Yang3, Thomas Wolfers, Yujie Wu, Siyang Gao, Nan Yin

entry.summary: The paper proposes BRIO, a framework for cross-site out-of-distribution generalization in resting-state fMRI that uses within-scan functional connectivity re-estimation to guide alignment, arguing that cross-site agreement does not guarantee robustness under FC re-estimation. It maps full-scan graphs and their re-estimates to improve predictive reliability across sites.

entry.title: Correction-space Cross-variate Interaction for Test-time Adaptation in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuanyuan Deng, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Songgaojun Deng

entry.summary: This paper identifies the interaction space as a key design choice in test-time adaptation for multivariate time-series forecasting, showing that cross-variate coupling through backbone predictions can mix uncorrected errors under delayed supervision. It proposes acting on adapter corrections rather than predictions to exploit cross-variate structure safely.

entry.title: Context-dependent time-series prediction via HyperReservoirs

author.name: Kohei Tsuchiyama, Takatomo Mihana, Ryoichi Horisaki, Andr\'{e} R\"{o}hm

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces HyperReservoirs, an extension of reservoir computing for time-series prediction when training and test data span multiple dynamical regimes or distinct systems. A small context reservoir modulates the output weights of the main reservoir, analogous to hypernetworks in deep learning, while preserving the simple training procedure of standard reservoir computing. This matters because it addresses a well-known failure mode of reservoir models on heterogeneous, regime-switching data.

entry.title: Inspector: Conversational and Lightweight Analyzer of Analog Circuit Layouts Using LLM and CNNs

author.name: Abril Cano Castro, Giuseppe Chiari, Michele Piccoli, Federico Viola, Davide Zoni

entry.summary: Inspector combines fine-tuned LLMs and CNNs to analyze GDSII layout files of analog integrated circuits, enabling a conversational interface between designers and CAD tooling. It targets the shift from manual/algorithmic analog design flows to AI-assisted paradigms.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Automated Cross-Domain Machine Learning Task Type Identification: A Benchmark Dataset and Evaluation

author.name: Petros Tsialis, Steffen Limmer, Tobias Rodemann, Martin Heckmann

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can infer data domain and downstream prediction task from dataset-level information in AutoML pipelines, releasing an annotated benchmark of 625 public tabular and time-series datasets. Evaluates against AutoML heuristics, in cross-domain settings, and with smaller local models for deployment.

entry.title: One Proposal for Every Margin: Zero-Shot Amortized Sequential Importance Sampling for Binary Matrices

author.name: Ruishuo Chen, Weijia Li, Xun Wang, Yu Chen, Leheng Cai, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: For counting and uniform sampling of binary matrices with fixed row and column margins, the authors characterize the ideal SIS proposal and train an amortized neural proposal that approximates it zero-shot for new margins. This yields efficient, low-variance estimation across ecology, psychometrics, and network analysis applications.

entry.title: DR-net-Mamba: Selective State-Space Modeling for Long-Range ECG Time-Series Denoising

author.name: Basile Morel, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Andreas P. Streich, Julia E. Vogt, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: The authors propose a Mamba-augmented denoising model that inserts selective state-space blocks into a convolutional bottleneck for ECG recordings, combining local feature extraction with linear-complexity long-range temporal modeling. They evaluate reconstruction fidelity, noise robustness, scaling to long recordings, and downstream diagnostic performance.

entry.title: Bidirectional Neural Networks for Global Nucleon-Nucleus Optical Model Calculations

author.name: Jin Lei

entry.summary: This work introduces a differentiable neural emulator based on Bidirectional Liquid Neural Networks mapping optical potential parameters to scattering wave functions in nuclear physics. A phase-space coordinate normalization allows one network to generalize across projectile energies from 1 to 200 MeV. The differentiability enables gradient-based uncertainty quantification and parameter optimization for nuclear data evaluation.

entry.title: Evasion Attacks on Cost-Utility-Based Adversarial Training for Online AutoML in IoT Networks

author.name: Chukwunonso Henry Nwokoye, Wajiha Zaheer, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: The study evaluates black-box evasion attacks against a cost-utility adversarial training defense in an Online AutoML setting for IoT security, applying attacks to streaming learners including Hoeffding Trees, Leveraging Bagging, Streaming Random Patches, and Hoeffding Adaptive Trees. It assesses whether adversarial training holds up in resource-constrained online learning regimes.

entry.title: All On-Board: Fully On-Chip Neuromorphic Q-Learning with Embedded CartPole Simulation

author.name: Steven C. Nesbit, Giovanni T. Michel, Gerd J. Kunde, Edward Kim, Andrew T. Sornborger

entry.summary: The authors implement a fully on-chip closed-loop RL system on Loihi 2, embedding both a Q-learning algorithm and an on-chip simulation of CartPole in neuromorphic hardware. This demonstrates low-power neuromorphic training and control suited to resource-constrained environments, targeting energy sustainability concerns of growing AI systems.

entry.title: De-biasing Skeleton-based Action Recognition with Convex Hull Adaptive Shift

author.name: Mengyuan Liu, Yuhang Wen, Yi Zhang, Songtao Wu, Hong Liu, Junsong Yuan, Beichen Ding

entry.summary: The paper identifies entity bias in skeleton-based action and interaction recognition, caused by the initial configuration of the world coordinate system where origin choice skews representations, violating the i.i.d. assumption behind weight-shared entity encoders. It proposes Convex Hull Adaptive Shift, a preprocessing approach to remove this bias before fusion. This improves recognition across bodies, hands, objects, and robots in skeleton sequences.

entry.title: Flat-Consensus Diffusion for Robust Data Reshaping under Noisy Evaluator

author.name: Hongyu Cao, Kunpeng Liu, Fei Xie, Sandip Ray

entry.summary: The paper casts feature-centric data reshaping as reward-guided diffusion generation and proposes flat-consensus sampling that searches for robust regions of the latent reward landscape rather than isolated high-reward transformations, mitigating dual instability from noisy evaluators and stochastic trajectories.

entry.title: CollisionGAT: Controller-Agnostic One-Step Collision Screening for Multi-Agent Motion

author.name: Alan Debbas, Edwin Meriaux, Gregory Dudek

entry.summary: Presents a graph-attention network that scores collision risk per agent from current and proposed multi-agent states plus nearby obstacles, usable as a modular safety screen by any controller or planner. Exact geometric checks provide training labels and audit executed steps, demonstrated on path-following control and an obstacle-blind D* Lite planner.

entry.title: Notes on Generative Modeling for Feedback Control and Planning

author.name: Karthik Elamvazhuthi

entry.summary: These lecture-style notes frame control as dynamically constrained sampling on a system's state space and extend generative modeling tools — flow matching, normalizing flows, and diffusion — to control problems such as steering to target states or distributions and sampling from reachable sets. Controllability and optimal control concepts guide well-posedness of the algorithms. The notes are an accessible synthesis for control-theory and robotics readers.

entry.title: Mask-Induced Displacement in Audio XAI via Logit Trajectory Decomposition

author.name: Nico Garc\'ia-Peguinho (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London), David Kelly (Department of Informatics, King's College London), Fabrizio Smeraldi (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London), Anna Xamb\'o Sed\'o (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London)

entry.summary: The authors propose logit-space trajectory decomposition to audit perturbation-based audio XAI methods, separating on-axis output change along the occluded-to-retained line from off-axis displacement. Across three fills, three classifiers, and 1,100 AudioSet clips, they show no fill is acoustically neutral under full occlusion, questioning a core assumption of masking-based audio explanations.

entry.title: CLIMB-flow: Coupled Linear Inverse posterior sampling via Multiscale-Based flow

author.name: Zeqiu Yu, Ruizhi Yuan, Mathews Jacob

entry.summary: CLIMB-Flow is a posterior sampling algorithm for Bayesian imaging inverse problems customized to pyramidal/cascaded diffusion architectures, generating in pixel domain via coarse-to-fine hierarchy. It alternates end-point estimation, data-consistent updates, and flow-based steps, avoiding the spatial-detail loss of latent-diffusion autoencoder compression.

entry.title: Curating Merchant-Matching Training Data with Two Confidence-Gated Local LLM Judges

author.name: Donghao Huang, Jinling Pei, Zhaoxia Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies pseudo-label curation for merchant matching, where a key difficulty is distinguishing teacher abstention from genuine no-match evidence. The authors use agreement between two local LLM judges with separate ordered confidence thresholds for selections and abstentions, guaranteeing disjoint positive and negative label sets. Retrospective replay on 2,000 expert-annotated queries shows thresholding trade-offs between purity and coverage.

entry.title: AlphaPareto: Formulaic Alpha Discovery with LLM-Guided Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yingbo Zhao, Zeyu Yang, Zhoufan Zhu

entry.summary: AlphaPareto formulates formulaic alpha discovery for quantitative trading as an RL problem, addressing pool-evolution non-stationarity by augmenting the state and using multi-objective optimization over properties of the alpha pool rather than only predictive power. LLM guidance is incorporated into the search process.

entry.title: Query Expansion and Key Specialization in Transformer Attention Geometry

author.name: Vidit Gupta, Siddhesh Nadkarni, Mihik Chaudhari, Vinaya Sawant, Prachi Tawde

entry.summary: This empirical study trains small GPT-like Transformers (3 depths, 3 query/key initializations, 4 seeds, 36 runs) on character-level WikiText-103 and tracks effective dimensionality of query and key projections via participation ratios. It finds that the mathematically symmetric query and key projections develop distinct geometric roles during training.

entry.title: Accelerator Choice Is Not Enough: AlphaFold2 Inference on Cloud TPUs

author.name: Lorenzo Pazienza, Ihab El Bani

entry.summary: This systems paper benchmarks AlphaFold2 inference across a Colab CPU runtime, an NVIDIA T4 GPU, and an eight-chip Cloud TPU v5e slice, showing large raw hardware advantages for TPUs but also that software-layer choices determine realized gains. The default path uses only one of eight TPU chips, and idle capacity erodes the cost advantage at list prices. It offers practical guidance for deploying JAX scientific workloads on cloud accelerators.

entry.title: GUIDE-FBO: Guidance via Uncertainty Intervention and Distributional Exchange for Federated Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Jintao Wei, Chenxi Li, Songhao Wang

entry.summary: GUIDE-FBO enables federated Bayesian optimization agents to exchange compact distributions over optima locations inferred from local Gaussian process posteriors instead of raw observations or surrogate parameters. A server merges and reweights these distributions, and agents construct a Federated Interventional GP preserving local posterior means while incorporating peer information. It targets knowledge transfer under communication constraints and task heterogeneity.
